records.title: Using mosquitoes to vaccinate bats could curb the spread of deadly diseases
records.description: But scientists say there are practical and ethical challenges to overcome before the strategy could be deployed in real-world settings.

records.title: Photonic ‘ski jump’ steers light beam from silicon chip
records.description: Chip-based beam scanners use tiny electrically controlled cantilevers instead of moving mirrors to control the direction of light projected into free space.

records.title: A silicon chip that enables the creation of 4D cameras
records.description: The development of an affordable, low-power and scalable sensor to map the position and velocity of 3D objects in a dynamically evolving scene has so far proved difficult. An imaging system formed using integrated silicon photonic circuits has now been developed as an equivalent to a camera, but for 4D imaging.

records.title: Dynamics of circulating tumour DNA can guide treatment decisions for improved outcomes
records.description: A phase II trial shows that the risk of cancer recurrence as reflected by circulating tumour DNA can guide a risk-adaptive treatment strategy that improves participants’ survival compared with the current standard of care. Our biological insights can be translated into clinical decision-making — challenging the conventional fixed-course, therapeutic approach.

records.title: Statistics reach a ‘crisis point’: nations struggle with a critical lack of data
records.description: Some researchers are sounding the alarm over the official data sets that track crucial aspects of life in the United States, Argentina, the United Kingdom and India.

records.title: Universities have become property businesses. What does that mean for research?
records.description: In the United States, United Kingdom, Australia and Singapore, universities are operating as developers and landlords. Where does science fit in?

records.title: AI can ‘same-ify’ human expression — can some brains resist its pull?
records.description: Emerging evidence suggests that LLM outputs can shape the text and thoughts of human users.

records.title: A fellowship of the rings in plant defence
records.description: Infected plants assemble immune-protein complexes on cell membranes to induce defence responses and cell death. Some such complexes can form large ring-like clusters.

records.title: Child marriages plunged when girls stayed in school in Nigeria
records.description: Collaboration between researchers and religious leaders led to a cut in the likelihood of early marriage by 80%.

records.title: A fellowship of the rings in plant defence
records.description: Infected plants assemble immune-protein complexes on cell membranes to induce defence responses and cell death. Some such complexes can form large ring-like clusters.

records.title: Child marriages plunged when girls stayed in school in Nigeria
records.description: Collaboration between researchers and religious leaders led to a cut in the likelihood of early marriage by 80%.

records.title: Daily briefing: ‘Virtual cell’ simulates nearly every chemical reaction in the real thing
records.description: A new simulation models processes such as DNA replication and cell division in a virtual bacterial cell. Plus, China is giving science a billion-dollar spending boost and why national statistics are in trouble.

records.title: ‘Black rain’ in Tehran: what are the health effects?
records.description: Toxic smoke from burning oil depots has blanketed Iran’s capital after missile strikes.

records.title: Gut microbes affect cognition during ageing
records.description: As mice age, changes in the microorganisms in their guts contribute to cognitive decline by altering signalling between the gut and brain.

records.title: Marriage of adolescent girls in Nigeria reduced by 80% by ‘big push’ intervention
records.description: A locally tailored, big-push intervention to educate unmarried adolescent girls in 18 communities in northern Nigeria reduced rates of marriage from 86% to just 21%. Interventions that address complex, entrenched social problems from various angles simultaneously might be considerably more effective than smaller-scale, cheaper alternatives are.

records.title: Scientists revive activity in frozen mouse brains for the first time
records.description: ‘Cryosleep’ remains the preserve of science fiction, but researchers are getting closer to restoring brain function after deep freezing.

records.title: The dynamic basis of G-protein recognition and activation by a GPCR
records.description: Conventional and time-resolved cryo-electron microscopy reveal how NTSR1 dynamically engages and releases different G proteins, capturing over 20 intermediates and uncovering key mechanistic steps in GDP- and GTP-driven activation, subtype selectivity and distinct dissociation pathways.

records.title: A large-scale coherent 4D imaging sensor
records.description: A 4D imaging architecture using a large-scale, coherent LiDAR focal plane array comprising more than 0.6 million photonic components and associated electronics integrated on-chip can obtain coherent images at high frame rates over useful distances.

records.title: Capturing dynamic phage–pathogen coevolution by clinical surveillance
records.description: The acquisition of a parasitic anti-phage mobile genetic element, PLE11, showing potent anti-phage activity against cocirculating ICP1, and the subsequent evolution of ICP1 to escape this defense, are captured, revealing the molecular basis of the natural selection of a globally notable pathogen and its virus.

records.title: Multidimensional profiling of heterogeneity in supratentorial ependymomas
records.description: Individual supratentorial ependymoma tumour subgroups have two distinct progenitor-like cell states—neuroepithelial-like and embryonic-like—that are reminiscent of early human brain development and diverge in the extent of their neuronal or ependymal differentiation.

records.title: Structures of Marburgvirus glycoprotein and its complex with NPC1 receptor
records.description: Marburgvirus glycoprotein binds to the endosomal receptor NPC1 in a distinct orientation with higher affinity compared with Ebola virus glycoprotein, accompanied by fusion-relevant rearrangements, enabling more efficient viral entry.

records.title: Multimodal electron microscopy of halide perovskite interfacial dynamics
records.description: A multimodal in situ electron microscopy approach enables direct visualization of structural and chemical evolution in a working halide perovskite light-emitting diode with nanometre precision.

records.title: Lense–Thirring precessing magnetar engine drives a superluminous supernova
records.description: Observations of a nearby type I superluminous supernova showing oscillating light-curve bumps provide evidence of a centrally located magnetar in the wake of the explosion, surrounded by an infalling accretion disk undergoing Lense–Thirring precession.

records.title: Facile induction of immune tolerance by an interleukin-2–TGFβ surrogate agonist
records.description: A fusion protein designed to comprise IL-2 and a helminth-derived TGFβ mimic activates IL-2 and TGFβ signalling pathways in IL-2 receptor-expressing T cells and induces stable antigen-specific regulatory T cells in peripheral lymphoid organs.

records.title: Snapshots of the dynamic basis of NTSR1 G protein subtype promiscuity
records.description: Time-resolved cryo-electron microscopy during activation of Gα i1 βγ and Gα 11 βγ heterotrimers bound to NTSR1 enables isolation of multiple transient complexes along the activation pathway and reveals structural motifs that stabilize these intermediates.

records.title: Intestinal interoceptive dysfunction drives age-associated cognitive decline
records.description: Age-related microbiome changes increase medium-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria, driving GPR84-mediated myeloid inflammation, impaired vagal signalling and hippocampal dysfunction; targeting this gut–brain pathway restores memory in aged mice.

records.title: Assembly of helper NLR resistosome clusters upon activation of a coiled-coil NLR
records.description: SUMM2, a coiled-coil NLR, promotes the assembly of higher-order resistosome clusters to initiate cell death in plants.

records.title: A sorghum pangenome reference improves global crop trait discovery
records.description: A pangenome reference for the phenotypically diverse crop sorghum aims to help accelerate future efforts to breed crops that are better adapted to changing environments.

records.title: B cell imprinting in children impairs antibodies to the haemagglutinin stalk
records.description: Imprinting by influenza viruses can cause a deleterious shift of nearly the entire memory recall response against key, conserved epitopes.

records.title: Nanophotonic waveguide chip-to-world beam scanning
records.description: A monolithically integrated photonic ski-jump enables scalable, diffraction-limited 2D beam scanning from photonic chips, achieving ultrahigh spot rates, compact footprints and applications spanning displays, sensing and quantum photonics.

records.title: A big-push community intervention reduced rates of child marriage by 80%
records.description: A community-wide intervention in northern Nigeria reduced rates of child marriage from 79% to 14%, showing that bundled, big-push approaches can dramatically shift entrenched behaviours.

records.title: Immune evasive DNA donors and recombinases license kilobase-scale writing
records.description: INSTALL overcomes fundamental challenges for DNA delivery and integration methods by synergizing immune-stealth nucleic acids with recombinases to enable kilobase-scale integration strategies without viral vectors.

records.title: Natural maternal immunity protects neonates from Escherichia coli sepsis
records.description: Neonatal sepsis caused by Escherichia coli is associated with reduced transfer of pathogen-specific maternal antibodies and, in a mouse model, can be prevented by maternal preconceptual colonization with probiotic E. coli .

records.title: Ageing promotes metastasis via activation of the integrated stress response
records.description: Ageing reprograms the evolutionary trajectory of KRAS -driven lung adenocarcinoma, limiting primary tumour growth while promoting metastatic dissemination through epigenetic activation of the integrated stress response, and a therapeutic opportunity in older patients is revealed.

records.title: Risk-adaptive therapy guided by dynamic ctDNA in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
records.description: A clinical trial testing whether monitoring ctDNA clearance during treatment for nasopharyngeal cancer could be used to inform decisions about an individual’s subsequent therapeutic programme shows promising results.

records.title: Gene conversion empowers natural selection in a clonal fish species
records.description: Analysis of the asexually reproducing Amazon molly Poecilia formosa and its sexually reproducing progenitors Poecilia mexicana and Poecilia latipinna reveals that it maintains a divergent mutational landscape and has evaded functional mutational decay via gene conversion.

records.title: A mechanism to initiate emergency type 2 myelopoiesis
records.description: Myelopoiesis in response to a parasitic worm infection and the mechanism selective to this form of parasite are revealed.

records.title: Artificial general intelligence must be assessed in its scientific and societal context
Prevent pandemics through One Health commitments
How ‘Pele’s hair’ sprouts from erupting lava
records.description: Experiments with simulated magma show it can be pulled into long strands similar to those seen in lava tubes.

records.title: The ethical risks of open-access agreements being used for authorship leverage
Could flies sniff out contraband chemicals?
records.description: A suggestion that mutant insects could detect narcotics or explosive substances, and how ash seeds feature a screw propeller, in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: Privilege, power and vulnerability in science: precarious funding can prompt unethical ties
Live parrots were carried across the Andes before the Incas’ rise
records.description: Ancient DNA and other clues from feathers found in modern Peru hint that the ancient Ychsma culture imported birds from the distant Amazon.

records.title: Keep calm and be transparent: advice from scientists who retracted their papers
records.description: Retractions correct the scientific record, but they have stigma attached to them. Some in the research community want that to change.

records.title: How data can help to guide NIH funding policy
records.description: The US National Institutes of Health has troves of information on grant applications. Analysing it can assist with decision-making on issues such as equity.

records.title: Daily briefing: A daily multivitamin slows the signs of biological ageing
records.description: The daily supplement slows markers of ageing on two epigenetic ‘clocks’. Plus, the real science of skincare and the domino effect of fictional case studies involving opioids in breastmilk.

records.title: Forget SkinTok: the real science of skincare and why it matters for your health
records.description: Skip the complicated regimens and expensive products seen on social media. The science of skin is deep but the recommendations are simple.

records.title: Alcohol group migration by proximity-enhanced H atom abstraction
records.description: An editing method enables the migration of common alcohol functional groups to proximal sites with predictable stereo- and regiochemical outcomes.

records.title: Stop the use of AI in war until laws can be agreed
records.description: Researchers working on the most advanced AI models want rules to be drawn up to minimize the harm the technologies could cause. Their warnings need to be heard.

records.title: ‘Virtual cell’ captures the most-basic process of life: bacterial division
records.description: Researchers simulated nearly every molecule in a bacterial cell —and then watched it grow and reproduce.

records.title: From cancer to Alzheimer’s: could a renewed focus on energy transform biomedicine?
records.description: Including energy dynamics in research could improve our understanding of diseases and of the healing processes that sustain health.

records.title: Maximizing carrier extraction in hybrid back-contact silicon solar cells
records.description: Hybrid back-contact silicon solar cells using a multifunctional front layer for both light trapping and passivation enable the use of a thicker absorber, outperforming the 125-μm-thick silicon heterojunction devices, with a certified efficiency of 27.62%.

records.title: The world’s salt lakes are drying up, but solutions are hard to come by
records.description: An eclectic book asks how humans have shaped these ‘queer’ landscapes and how they can be restored.

records.title: Eight common errors I see in PhD applications and interviews, and how to avoid them
records.description: Convince a supervisor that you’re a great fit for their laboratory by preparing questions, honing your personal statement and showcasing strong team-player instincts.

records.title: How pollutants and poo paint a picture of past civilizations
records.description: A blend of chemistry and molecular-biology techniques are enabling archaeologists to mine ancient sediments for clues about the people who once lived there.

records.title: Daily briefing: Protein folding caught in real time
records.description: Scientists say they have made some of the first direct measurements of how long it takes an individual protein to fold. Plus, how AI is being used in warfare and how to avoid common mistakes when applying for a PhD.

records.title: How fast does a protein fold? Real-time technique captures the moment
records.description: Proteins assume complex 3D shapes even faster than does DNA, which is a simpler molecule.

records.title: How Congress can restore the independence of US science
records.description: Members must go beyond reinstating US government research spending and re-establish decentralized governance at the National Institutes of Health and other agencies.

records.title: Daily multivitamin slows signs of biological ageing
records.description: The supplement’s anti-ageing effect was greater in people who were already biologically older than their years.

records.title: My PhD student is stuck. How do I teach them perseverance and problem solving?
records.description: A new principal investigator wants to help PhD students to develop resilience and creativity in the laboratory without hovering or doing the work for them.

records.title: Monthly HIV-drug injections offer potent alternative to daily tablets
records.description: Long-lasting treatment suppresses HIV in people with mental illness and other conditions that make it challenging to adhere to standard treatments.

records.title: Briefing Chat: What Galileo’s scribbled margin notes reveal about his scientific journey
records.description: Nature staff discuss some of the week’s top science news.

records.title: Electric-vehicle batteries toughen up to beat the heat
records.description: Rising temperatures shorten battery life, but devices are improving fast enough to resist the ravages of climate change.

records.title: Peanut-processing microbes ward off dangerous allergic shock
records.description: Scientists identify bacteria that digest allergy-triggering compounds in peanuts, which can be life-threatening to those with allergies.

records.title: Modelling the cosmos and imagining a future without meat: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: The missing pieces of menopause science
records.description: Hormone therapy is back after decades in the shadows. But evidence gaps remain for treating perimenopause — often the most disruptive part of the menopause transition.

records.title: What a viral TikTok taught me about personal storytelling in science
records.description: The success of a student’s educational video made me rethink the ways that teaching can create moments of wonder that technology can’t replace.

records.title: Celebrate women in research and the networks that sustain them
records.description: On International Women’s Day, we celebrate technology pioneers and recognize the mentorship that is necessary to inspire the current generation and those of the future.

records.title: Climate change is speeding up — the pace nearly doubled in ten years
records.description: Earth is now warming at a rate of around 0.35 ºC per decade, fresh analysis finds.

records.title: Genetically modified pig liver keeps man alive until human organ transplant
records.description: First time the procedure has been performed on a living person.

records.title: Uncharted: understanding women’s health across the body
records.description: Disaggregating data by sex is a powerful way to help develop better diagnostics and treatments for women — but researchers say it’s not used enough.

records.title: Daily briefing: How koalas escaped a genetic bottleneck
records.description: Evidence from koalas suggest that even species pushed to the brink of extinction can recover lost genetic diversity. Plus, the first ‘half Möbius’ carbon-based molecule and a mathematician modelling Mexico’s drug cartels.

records.title: Cracked, but still there: the glass ceiling persists for senior women in science
records.description: To mark International Women’s Day on 8 March, Mangala Srinivas reminds junior colleagues that career success won’t protect you from gender-based bias.

records.title: Author Correction: Programmable 200 GOPS Hopfield-inspired photonic Ising machine
The first ‘AI societies’ are taking shape: how human-like are they?
records.description: Scientists are studying forms of ‘social’ interactions between artificial-intelligence agents. Will they find a fresh form of sociology, or merely a sophisticated mime act?

records.title: These brain cells clear proteins that contribute to Alzheimer’s
records.description: When specialized cells called tanycytes stop working, disease-causing tau proteins build up in the brain.

records.title: Daily briefing: How DNA testing can tell identical twins apart
records.description: Emerging forensic methods can differentiate between twin suspects in criminal cases. Plus, GLP-1 obesity drugs can help stave off addictions and scientists claim to have made a rare hexagonal diamond.

records.title: The Epstein scandal is a wake-up call — new rules are needed on links with rich donors
records.description: A systemic failure of oversight allowed the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein to curry favour with academia. Stronger governance is urgently needed.

records.title: Identical twins on trial: can DNA testing tell them apart?
records.description: In a French criminal trial, conventional DNA analysis couldn’t distinguish between twin brothers, but emerging scientific methods could help in such cases.

records.title: Inside Mexico’s stem-cell industry
records.description: Researchers in the country are calling for stronger regulation of treatments that many people make long journeys to receive.

records.title: How AI is shaping the war in Iran — and what’s next for future conflicts
records.description: Rapid technological development is prompting urgent discussions on regulating the use and procurement of artificial intelligence for military use.

records.title: Do obesity drugs treat addiction? Huge study hints at their promise
records.description: Study of 600,000 US military veterans shows that those who took anti-obesity medications were less likely to develop some complications of substance-use disorders.

records.title: First ‘half-Möbius’ carbon chain wows chemists
records.description: The looped molecule’s unusual shape could unlock strange physical properties.

records.title: High-rise transistors can be used to build space-saving circuits
records.description: Logical circuits have been built from nanosheet stacks of various transistors, which could make electronic devices faster and more compact.

records.title: How these koalas bounced back from the brink of extinction
records.description: Tracking DNA recombination offers hope for other species that have lost genetic diversity.

records.title: Women in science are not a ‘problem to be fixed’
records.description: Cordelia Fine wrote Patriarchy Inc to challenge two false visions of gender equality at work and offer a fairer future for the female workforce.

records.title: Heart surgery with quick-setting magnetic fluid could prevent strokes
records.description: Injectable fluid safely fills area in which blood clots can form, in animal trials — plus, strong evidence that an elusive form of diamond has been made in the lab.

records.title: Magnetic gel injected into the heart could stop strokes
records.description: The hydrogel-based plug blocks a part of the heart to cut stroke risk and was shown to be effective in rats and a pig.

records.title: Stress-hormone signalling protects spreading cancer cells from immune system
records.description: Metastasis occurs when cancer cells spread to other organs and escape elimination by the immune system. Analysis reveals that these cells resist killing by immune cells by harnessing stress-hormone signalling through the glucocorticoid receptor, suggesting a potential therapeutic target for preventing metastasis.

records.title: AI can write genomes — how long until it creates synthetic life?
records.description: The Evo2 genomic language model can generate short genome sequences, but scientists say further advances are needed to write genomes that will work inside living cells.

records.title: Magnetic fluid offers better seal in heart-plugging medical procedure
records.description: An injectable fluid has been used to close off part of the heart in animals — a potentially improved take on a procedure that prevents stroke in people with irregular heartbeats.

records.title: Funding from individual donors: lessons from the Epstein case
records.description: Universities need to establish and empower compliance teams to ensure adherence to ethical funding policies.

records.title: A genetic switch turns off parental behaviour and drives infanticide in male striped mice
records.description: Male parenting in mammals is highly variable, ranging from caring to neglectful and abusive. The brain and behaviour of the African striped mouse reveal that, in males, the social environment and expression level of the Agouti gene affect whether the animals will be hostile or caring towards pups.

records.title: Do wet or dry soils trigger thunderstorms? It depends on how the wind blows
records.description: Satellite data show that wind conditions affect the connection between soil moisture and thunderstorms, which could be used to inform forecasting.

records.title: Climate change and geopolitics threaten water supplies — but disaster is not inevitable
records.description: The Indus Waters Treaty withstood several armed conflicts and a huge loss of glaciers. It should serve as a blueprint for others.

records.title: Cancer blood tests are everywhere — here's why you should be cautious
records.description: Their makers claim they can detect dozens of cancer types — but some scientists say they could be missing many cancers or delivering the wrong diagnosis.

records.title: Skin cells boost distant antibody responses
records.description: How the skin enables immune defences is not fully clear. Now a pathway has been found in skin cells that boosts the production of antibodies to protect the whole body.

records.title: How a mathematician is cracking open Mexico’s powerful drug cartels
records.description: Rafael Prieto-Curiel explains how his models of organized crime could improve public safety in his home country.

records.title: Under pressure: the reality of Mexico’s research system
records.description: Researcher Oscar Xavier Guerrero Gutiérrez speaks out about the unstable conditions that Mexican scientists face — and what can be done to help.

records.title: Radiology AI makes consistent diagnoses using 3D images from different health centres
records.description: To meet the growing demand for radiology artificial-intelligence tools, a 3D vision–language model called Merlin was trained on abdominal computed-tomography scans, radiology reports and electronic health records. Merlin demonstrated stronger off-the-shelf performance than did other vision–language models across three hospital sites distinct from the initial training centre, highlighting its potential for broader clinical adoption.

records.title: Daily briefing: The return of the snail — the month’s best science images
records.description: The most jaw-dropping science images from February. Plus, whether cancer blood tests actually work and what we lose when we can’t see the stars.

records.title: Hunt for reactive metabolites uncovers unusual chemistry in a human pathogen
records.description: A workflow was developed to selectively capture bacterially produced compounds containing a reactive diazo chemical group. This enabled the discovery of two diazo-containing molecules from a bacterium that causes lung disease. Investigation of the bacterial synthesis of these molecules revealed an enzyme that constructs the diazo group, with broad synthetic applications.

records.title: All the world is staged
records.description: Exits and entrances.

records.title: Genome modelling and design across all domains of life with Evo 2
records.description: Evo 2 is an artificial intelligence-based biological foundation model trained on 9 trillion DNA base pairs spanning all domains of life that predicts functional properties from genomic sequences and provides a rich generative model for researchers in biology.

records.title: DICER cleavage fidelity is governed by 5′-end binding pockets
records.description: Cryo-electron microscopy and massively parallel assays shed light on the mechanism by which DICER, a key enzyme in the RNase III family, cleaves RNA at precise locations to produce small RNAs.

records.title: Limited thermal tolerance in tropical insects and its genomic signature
records.description: A survey of tropical insect populations and thermal tolerance limits indicates that species from lowland areas have low capacity to survive increased temperatures, and that thermal tolerance is limited by fundamental properties of protein architecture.

records.title: Shared neural substrates of prosocial and parenting behaviours
records.description: Mice with higher levels of parenting show more prosocial allogrooming towards stressed adults, and both behaviours share neural substrates in the medial preoptic area, suggesting that parenting circuitry may form an evolutionary foundation for adult-directed prosocial helping behaviour.

records.title: A metabolic alarmin from keratinocytes potentiates systemic humoral immunity
records.description: Farnesyl pyrophosphate—a mevalonate pathway metabolic intermediate—is an endogenous alarmin that enhances IgG antibody responses through keratinocyte-derived IL-6 and CCL20.

records.title: Bulk hexagonal diamond
records.description: The synthesis of millimetre-sized phase-pure hexagonal diamond, a polymorph of cubic diamond, by compressing highly oriented pyrolytic graphite under high pressures and temperatures is reported, providing new insight into the graphite-to-diamond transformation pathway.

records.title: Sea level much higher than assumed in most coastal hazard assessments
records.description: Meta-analyses on a global scale show that the measured coastal mean sea level is higher than assumed in most coastal hazard assessments.

records.title: A glucocorticoid–FAS axis controls immune evasion during metastatic seeding
records.description: Glucocorticoid receptor activation is a key driver of resistance of triple-negative breast cancer to both CD8 + T cells and natural killer cells during initial metastatic seeding.

records.title: The molecular basis of force selectivity by PIEZO2
records.description: PIEZO2 is intrinsically more rigid than PIEZO1, and disparate mechanical stimuli paradoxically evoke opposite conformational and gating responses in each channel.

records.title: Advancing operational global aerosol forecasting with machine learning
records.description: Reliable 5-day, 3-hourly forecasts of aerosol optical components and surface concentrations are obtained in 1 minute using a machine-learning-driven forecasting system.

records.title: Wind shear enhances soil moisture influence on rapid thunderstorm growth
records.description: Analysis of millions of events over sub-Saharan Africa shows that wind shear amplifies the impact of soil moisture in triggering rapidly developing thunderstorms.

records.title: Structural basis of RNA-guided transcription by a dCas12f–σ E –RNAP complex
records.description: Cryogenic electron microscopy reveals how dCas12f with σ E recruits RNAP to targeted DNA, initiating transcription at a fixed downstream distance, bypassing canonical −35 recognition and stabilizing the −10 element in an unusual manner.

records.title: Homologous recombination deficiency and hemizygosity drive resistance in breast cancer
records.description: Germline and somatic interactions define actionable genomic patterns driving acquired therapy resistance in breast cancer.

records.title: Exapted CRISPR–Cas12f homologues drive RNA-guided transcription
records.description: Specialized σ factors interact with nuclease-dead, CRISPR–Cas12f proteins to form potent, RNA-guided gene activation systems that function independently of fixed promoter motifs.

records.title: Wide-swath altimetry maps bank shapes and storage changes in global rivers
records.description: Observations of river channel geometry and monthly water storage changes for 126,674 river reaches worldwide are derived from the first water year of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography satellite mission.

records.title: Largest Silurian fish illuminates the origin of osteichthyan characters
records.description: New findings from articulated head and trunk material of Megamastax amblyodus yield previously unseen morphological details of a Silurian stem osteichthyan.

records.title: Precancerous niche remodelling dictates nascent tumour persistence
records.description: A study investigating the emergence of squamous tumours in the upper gastrointestinal tract of the mouse shows that an initial tumour stress response triggers fibroblasts to remodel the underlying stroma, creating a fibronectin-rich precancerous niche that supports tumour survival.

records.title: Jam-packed star system is most compact of its kind ever found
records.description: All four Sun-like stars would fit inside the area of Jupiter’s orbit.

records.title: Releasing open-weight AI in steps would alleviate risks
From the first telephone to videoconferencing in 100 years
records.description: Scientists of the 1970s look to the past and future of telecommunications, and a rainbow against a blue sky dazzles a reader, in this week’s peek at Nature ’s archive.

records.title: South Korea’s AI framework act focuses on rights and safety
Climate research is global — risks and responsibilities should also be distributed
Why ‘quantum proteins’ could be the next big thing in biology
records.description: Fluorescent proteins with a quantum upgrade could offer unprecedented views inside cells.

records.title: Author Correction: Healthy forests safeguard traditional wild meat food systems in Amazonia
US climate actions must continue, despite setbacks
records.description: The United States has slammed the brakes on legal routes to limit greenhouse gases. But cities, states and businesses can keep pushing for a cleaner environment.

records.title: My relationship with my PhD supervisor has become toxic — what do I do?
records.description: A graduate student in China has become seriously depressed after facing frequent verbal abuse.

records.title: How infighting led the Maya civilization to catastrophic collapse
records.description: Fresh archaeological evidence hints at what caused the disappearance of this thriving ancient Mesoamerican culture.

records.title: See raining iguanas and coral from the inside out — February’s best science images
records.description: The month’s sharpest science shots, selected by Nature ’s photo team.

records.title: Climate shocks, not just warming, threaten malaria control efforts in Africa
records.description: Climate change is expected to affect mosquito and parasite survival, reshaping malaria risk. But extreme weather could be a more immediate danger to disease control.

records.title: Daily briefing: Galileo’s notes discovered in the margins of an ancient book
records.description: Historians have discovered some recognizable jottings in a 400-year-old copy of Ptolemy’s The Almagest. Plus, tectonic plates might’ve started moving earlier than we thought and how fluorescent-protein labels can be used as quantum sensors.

records.title: Hey ChatGPT, write me a fictional paper: these LLMs are willing to commit academic fraud
records.description: Mainstream chatbots presented varying levels of resistance to deliberate requests for fabrication, study finds.

records.title: How can fast-evolving DNA retain a fundamental function in cell division?
records.description: In a dividing cell, chromosome pairs are pulled apart thanks to attachment sites called centromeres. Yeast genomes reveal key steps in how centromeres have evolved.

records.title: Going ‘beyond GDP’ should not mean sidelining the SDGs
records.description: The UN Sustainable Development Goals represent a carefully-crafted road map for future human and planetary prosperity.

records.title: Genetically encoded assembly recorder temporally resolves cellular history
records.description: The fluorescence-based protein assembly platform GEMINI is able to record the history of individual cells by leveraging a computationally designed protein assembly as an intracellular memory device.

records.title: The squeal of peeling tape, explained
records.description: Weak shock waves triggered by micro-cracks in the adhesive layer of tape cause it to screech when being unspooled from its roll.

records.title: Author Correction: Root microbiota drive direct integration of phosphate stress and immunity
Audio long read: Many people have no mental imagery. What’s going on in their brains?
records.description: People with aphantasia are offering brain scientists a window into consciousness.

records.title: The hidden lives behind China’s great Internet firewall
records.description: The country’s tightly controlled digital ecosystem is replete with human stories and acts of subtle resistance.

records.title: AI agents are ‘aeroplanes for the mind’: five ways to ensure that scientists are responsible pilots
records.description: As artificial-intelligence systems take on more of the scientific workflow, the central goal should not be complete automation, but designing platforms that preserve creativity, responsibility and surprise.

records.title: Earth’s oldest crystals suggest an early start for plate tectonics
records.description: The planet’s crust could already have been churning 3.3 billion years ago.

records.title: Daily briefing: Neanderthal dad, human mum was more common than the other way round
records.description: Ancient DNA evidence suggests that an imbalance in Neanderthal– Homo sapiens mating helped to shape the human genome. Plus, a look over China’s Great Firewall and what it means to reach for the Moon in a time of chaos.

records.title: ‘No one quite like her’: meet the female colleagues who inspire these award-winning women in science
records.description: To mark International Women’s Day, Nature asked winners of its awards programmes to nominate a colleague who brings out the best in them.

records.title: BCDX2–CX3 and DX2–CX3 complexes assemble and stabilize RAD51 filaments
records.description: Multiple complexes that contain various RAD51 paralogues involved in homologous recombination are revealed, highlighting the structural, functional and mechanistic importance of these complexes.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Pokémon turns 30 — how Pikachu and pals inspired generations of researchers
records.description: Nature staff discuss some of the week’s top science news.

records.title: Brain mysteries and Bronze Age diplomacy: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: Audio long read: Many people have no mental imagery. What’s going on in their brains?
records.description: People with aphantasia are offering brain scientists a window into consciousness.

records.title: The hidden lives behind China’s great Internet firewall
records.description: The country’s tightly controlled digital ecosystem is replete with human stories and acts of subtle resistance.

records.title: AI agents are ‘aeroplanes for the mind’: five ways to ensure that scientists are responsible pilots
records.description: As artificial-intelligence systems take on more of the scientific workflow, the central goal should not be complete automation, but designing platforms that preserve creativity, responsibility and surprise.

records.title: Earth’s oldest crystals suggest an early start for plate tectonics
records.description: The planet’s crust could already have been churning 3.3 billion years ago.

records.title: Daily briefing: Neanderthal dad, human mum was more common than the other way round
records.description: Ancient DNA evidence suggests that an imbalance in Neanderthal– Homo sapiens mating helped to shape the human genome. Plus, a look over China’s Great Firewall and what it means to reach for the Moon in a time of chaos.

records.title: ‘No one quite like her’: meet the female colleagues who inspire these award-winning women in science
records.description: To mark International Women’s Day, Nature asked winners of its awards programmes to nominate a colleague who brings out the best in them.

records.title: BCDX2–CX3 and DX2–CX3 complexes assemble and stabilize RAD51 filaments
records.description: Multiple complexes that contain various RAD51 paralogues involved in homologous recombination are revealed, highlighting the structural, functional and mechanistic importance of these complexes.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Pokémon turns 30 — how Pikachu and pals inspired generations of researchers
records.description: Nature staff discuss some of the week’s top science news.

records.title: Brain mysteries and Bronze Age diplomacy: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: Editorial Expression of Concern: The gene product Murr1 restricts HIV-1 replication in resting CD4+ lymphocytes
White House stalls release of approved US science budgets
records.description: The US Congress rejected sweeping cuts to science agencies. But the NIH, the NSF and NASA have had their spending slowed.

records.title: I will continue the fight for environmental justice in Black communities
records.description: Nicknamed the father of environmental justice, Robert Bullard argues that researchers in the field have more reason than ever to back up their work with action.

records.title: Pokémon turns 30 — how the fictional pocket monsters shaped science
records.description: The Japanese media sensation has inspired generations of researchers in fields as diverse as evolution, biodiversity and research integrity.

records.title: Is a ‘selfish gene’ making a Utah family have twice as many boys as girls?
records.description: Genealogy study claims first conclusive case of sex ‘distortion’ in humans — but not all researchers are convinced.

records.title: Daily briefing: This Utah family line might be evidence of ‘selfish genes’ in humans
records.description: Researchers claim to have found the first conclusive case of sex ‘distortion’ in people. Plus, stem cells could treat spina bifida and how 30 years of Pokémon has influenced science.

records.title: This compound enhances long-term memory of mice — but only in females
records.description: Acetate helps the female rodents form memories but is less effective in males.

records.title: Why an industry career move is a taboo topic in academia
records.description: Adam Levy investigates why researchers are sometimes reluctant to disclose their plans to colleagues.

records.title: Ultra-sensitive CAR T cells eliminate hard-to-treat tumours in mice
records.description: A proof-of-concept study opens up an avenue for treating solid tumours that express low levels of a target antigen.

records.title: UN creates new scientific AI advisory panel: what will it do?
records.description: The panel has been compared to the IPCC — the international panel whose research helped to shape landmark climate agreements.

records.title: Author Correction: Myocardial reprogramming by HMGN1 underlies heart defects in trisomy 21
Daily briefing: Stem-cell treatment strengthens people with age-related frailty
records.description: A single dose of stem cells can help older people with frailty build up their endurance. Plus, how to successfully make a career pivot and what ‘adulthood’ really means.

records.title: Health effects linger 20 generations after rats are exposed to fungicide
records.description: Scientists say the findings are a warning about the kinds of chemical that people are exposed to in the environment.

records.title: Neanderthal dad, human mum: study reveals ancient procreation pattern
records.description: Genomic analysis shows that interbreeding between female Neanderthals and male humans was less common than the opposite combination.

records.title: World-first stem-cell therapy shows promise for treating spina bifida in the womb
records.description: Six pregnant women participated in a small trial in which placenta-derived stem cells were applied to fetal spinal cords and the treatment was found to be safe.

records.title: The surprising science of squeaky sneakers
records.description: The mystery of why soft shoes squeak on hard floors may be solved, according to new research

records.title: How an exercise-activated enzyme helps to keep the brain young
records.description: A protein reinforces the blood–brain barrier, which becomes leaky with age.

records.title: How earthquakes and lightning help explain squeaky sneakers
records.description: High-speed footage reveals shoe squeaks can start with a tiny bolt of lightning — plus, evidence that a debated brain phenomenon exists in humans.

records.title: EU leaders should not rush to revamp green-hydrogen rules
records.description: Some policymakers think that climate-friendly policies are impeding the adoption of green hydrogen. They should ask scientists to review the evidence.

records.title: Stem cells provide a potent treatment for frailty
records.description: Elderly people with frailty, which affects up to one-quarter of over-50s, increased their endurance after a single dose of stem cells.

records.title: Reply to: Limitations of probing field-induced response with STM
We need a global assessment of avoidable climate-change risks
records.description: To understand the urgency of emissions reductions, policymakers and citizens need a full analysis of what is at stake.

records.title: The age of animal experiments is waning. Where will science go next?
records.description: Advances in organ and computer models are raising the prospect that some animal experiments could be eliminated. But there are still huge hurdles to overcome.

records.title: The protein carriers of hundreds of lipids have been identified
records.description: Different types of lipid molecule are transported around the cell by lipid-transfer proteins. Biochemical approaches have been adapted to measure which lipids are captured by the more than 130 known human lipid-transfer proteins, providing a valuable resource that reveals some principles of how these transporters work.

records.title: Flexible paths to multicellularity
records.description: Close relatives of animals can become multicellular if distinct individuals join together or if dividing cells remain attached. A species has been found to use both mechanisms.

records.title: Brains of ‘super agers’ are strong producers of new neurons
records.description: Older people with exceptional memory have a surprisingly high number of young neurons, study finds.

records.title: Environmental exposure trains the immune system to dampen allergic responses
records.description: Clean living conditions that lessen exposure to microorganisms are linked to an increase in allergies. Mouse data reveal how the environment affects allergic immune responses.

records.title: Scientists face fallout for past associations with Epstein
records.description: Jack Horner, who was a consultant for the Jurassic Park films, is among the researchers whose work or careers have been affected because of revelations from newly released documents.

records.title: Parkinson’s disease affects network of brain regions that controls whole-body action
records.description: Precision brain imaging of individuals with Parkinson’s disease reveals that the affected circuit is best characterized as a previously described network of brain regions called the somato-cognitive action network. Abnormally high connectivity in this network is associated with Parkinson’s disease and is normalized by effective pharmacological treatment and various brain-stimulation therapies.

records.title: The secret of squeaky basketball shoes
records.description: When shoes slide across a floor, wave-like deformations of the sole can generate squeaking. The pitch of the squeak depends on the rate at which deformations are generated.

records.title: The future perfect continuous passive and other transitive disorders of the mind
records.description: Grammar is destiny.

records.title: Sea-urchin spines generate electrical signals in flowing water
records.description: The spines of sea urchins can generate a voltage when water moves around them — a phenomenon that could be used to design underwater flow sensors.

records.title: Lipid nanoparticles engineered to target therapeutic RNA to the pancreas
records.description: A two-pronged strategy directs drug-delivering nanoparticles to the pancreas — and shows promise in animal models of serious pancreatic diseases.

records.title: Cavity-altered superconductivity
records.description: A new platform making use of hexagonal boron nitride interfaced with the molecular superconductor κ-(BEDT-TTF) 2 Cu[N(CN) 2 ]Br is demonstrated for realizing cavity-altered materials, confirmed by magnetic force microscopy and nano-optical measurements.

records.title: Compact deep neural network models of the visual cortex
records.description: Parsimonious deep neural network models can be used for prediction of visual neuron responses.

records.title: Echinoderm stereom gradient structures enable mechanoelectrical perception
records.description: Sea urchin spines show exceptional mechanoelectrical sensing from gradient structures and can be replicated in 3D-printed mimics for underwater sensing.

records.title: A membrane-bound nuclease directly cleaves phage DNA during genome injection
records.description: A widespread bacterial defence system called SNIPE is shown to localize to the cell membrane, where it identifies and cleaves the DNA of infecting phage as it is injected into the bacterial cell.

records.title: Vectorized instructive signals in cortical dendrites
records.description: Mice learning a neurofeedback brain–computer interface task show neuron-specific teaching signals in cortical dendrites, consistent with a vectorized solution for credit assignment in the brain.

records.title: Peripheral immune-inducer dendritic cells drive early-life allergic inflammation
records.description: Early-life exposure to allergens triggers a distinct local mode of dendritic cell activation in neonatal skin without requiring migration to lymph nodes, which shapes responses to allergens in later life.

records.title: Pancreatic-targeted lipid nanoparticles based on organ capsule filtration
records.description: Elucidation of fundamental pancreatic-targeted mechanisms enables the development of lipid nanoparticles for the precise delivery of nucleic acid therapeutics to the pancreas, highlighting their promising potential in the treatment of pancreatic diseases.

records.title: Squeaking at soft–rigid frictional interfaces
records.description: High-speed imaging reveals that the squeak of soft–rigid frictional interfaces, like sneakers sliding on a basketball court, arises from intersonic opening slip pulses—analogous to earthquake ruptures—that thin ridges on the rubber confine to repeat at a musical frequency.

records.title: Pivoting colloidal assemblies exhibit mechanical metamaterial behaviour
records.description: A method is described for the manufacture of pivoting colloidal assemblies comprising rotating diamond and rotating triangle geometries that show tunable folding and unfolding by thermal fluctuations and actuation by magnetic attractions.

records.title: Clonal-aggregative multicellularity tuned by salinity in a choanoflagellate
records.description: The choanoflagellate Choanoeca flexa forms motile and contractile cell monolayers purely clonally, purely aggregatively or through a combination of both processes depending on environmental conditions.

records.title: Convergent MurJ flippase inhibition by phage lysis proteins
records.description: A common mechanism of inhibition of the essential lipid II flippase MurJ by three distinct phage-encoded single-gene lysis proteins provides insights into potential new targets for antimicrobial development.

records.title: OR7A10 GPCR engineering boosts CAR-NK therapy against solid tumours
records.description: The identification of ‘boosters’ that drive gene overexpression directly in a CAR construct provides a simple and scalable strategy for developing effective CAR-NK cell therapies for solid tumours.

records.title: A disease model resource reveals core principles of tissue-specific cancer evolution
records.description: The Mouse Cancer Cell line Atlas (MCCA) provides major advances towards a mechanistic understanding of cancer genomes.

records.title: Rewiring an E3 ligase enhances cold resilience and phosphate use in maize
records.description: The E3 ubiquitin ligase NLA postively regulates cold tolerance and negatively regulates phosphate uptake in maize, and a genetically engineered variant of this enzyme leads to improved cold tolerance and enhanced phosphate uptake, improving yield in field trials.

records.title: Field-free full switching of chiral antiferromagnetic order
records.description: An Mn 3 Sn homo-junction enables efficient field-free full switching of chiral antiferromagnets with greatly reduced power consumption, advancing their potential for energy-efficient magnetic memory devices with advantages of ultradense integration and ultrafast speed.

records.title: Hydrofluorocarbon electrolytes for energy-dense and low-temperature batteries
records.description: A method using hydrofluorocarbon electrolytes for synthesizing alkanes with monofluorinated structures is described, yielding a pathway for manufacturing lithium-metal batteries able to achieve high energy density as well as operate at low temperature.

records.title: Argentine fossil rewrites evolutionary history of a baffling dinosaur clade
records.description: A skeleton of the alvarezsauroid Alnashetri cerropoliciensis —representing a highly complete alvarezsauroid skeleton from South America—provides evidence on the evolution of the peculiar anatomy and miniaturization within this unusual theropod dinosaur clade.

records.title: Coral microbiomes as reservoirs of unknown genomic and biosynthetic diversity
records.description: Reconstructing microbial genomes from 820 reef-building corals collected at 99 reefs across 32 islands throughout the Pacific Ocean highlights the importance of conserving coral reefs as vital reservoirs of molecular diversity.

records.title: CLCC1 promotes hepatic neutral lipid flux and nuclear pore complex assembly
records.description: CRISPR–Cas9 screening identifies CLCC1 as a factor that increases neutral lipid flux to prevent hepatic steatosis and promotes nuclear pore complex assembly by promoting membrane bending and fusion.

records.title: CLCC1 governs ER bilayer equilibration to maintain lipid homeostasis
records.description: Phospholipid scrambling at the endoplasmic reticulum is essential for establishing a dynamic equilibrium to maintain cellular homeostasis.

records.title: Functional dissection of complex trait variants at single-nucleotide resolution
records.description: Massively parallel reporter assays across five cell types identify thousands of causal, noncoding regulatory variants among 220,000 loci, revealing diverse regulatory mechanisms shaping complex traits and disease.

records.title: Uncovering origins of heterogeneous superconductivity in La 3 Ni 2 O 7
records.description: Wide-field quantum sensing shows μm-scale inhomogeneous superconductivity in high-pressure La 3 Ni 2 O 7 , linking local diamagnetic response to stress and stoichiometry and clarifying mechanisms that suppress or enhance superconductivity.

records.title: Human hippocampal neurogenesis in adulthood, ageing and Alzheimer’s disease
records.description: Mapping of neurogenesis in human hippocampi across ages and different cognitive abilities using multiomic single-cell sequencing reveals distinct signatures between cognitive preservation and decline.

records.title: Entanglement-assisted non-local optical interferometry in a quantum network
records.description: Entangled quantum memories are used in a quantum network of silicon–vacancy centres in diamond nanocavities to experimentally perform non-local phase measurements.

records.title: Author Correction: Global subsidence of river deltas
The Contributor Role Taxonomy tool must serve to record extent of authorship
Sewage systems waft more pollution into the air than reported
records.description: Wastewater treatment facilites and other infrastructure emit larger amounts of greenhouse gases than many nations report.

records.title: Treasures of scientific history could be hiding in plain sight
records.description: A reader calls for museum curators to look for historic scientific apparatus, and a landmark treaty aims to protect the Mediterranean from pollution, in our weekly dip into Nature ’s archive.

records.title: Defunding Chile’s climate research will undermine science and the region
Account for AI in the environmental footprint of scientific publishing

This ant species is composed of only queens — no workers or males
records.description: Temnothorax kinomurai queens survive by invading the nests of a related ant species and co-opting its workers.

records.title: Evidence alone won’t save biodiversity: the golden apple snail reveals an implementation gap
COVID’s origins: what we do and don’t know
records.description: Researchers summarize key insights from the world’s first comprehensive investigation into how a pandemic started.

records.title: Nuclear weapons testing is harmful — there’s no case for a restart
records.description: Scientific knowledge about the damaging effects of nuclear-weapons testing helped to end such tests. Those findings haven’t changed.

records.title: China is waging war on Alzheimer’s. What can its approach teach the rest of the world?
records.description: The country is facing a coming wave of dementia for its ageing population, and is investing in research into drugs, diagnostics and even surgery to prepare itself.

records.title: Daily briefing: COVID’s origins — what we do and don’t know
records.description: Most peer-reviewed evidence suggests an animal origin of SARS-CoV-2, but doesn’t indicate when or where the spillover occurred. Plus, how horses can make two sounds at once at the science jobs that might be overtaken by AI.

records.title: Scientists must step up to avert a nuclear breakout
records.description: The end of the US–Russia treaty to cap the number of nuclear weapons places the world at risk. Here’s what researchers can do.

records.description: The country is facing a coming wave of dementia for its ageing population, and is investing in research into drugs, diagnostics and even surgery to prepare itself.

records.title: Daily briefing: COVID’s origins — what we do and don’t know
records.description: Most peer-reviewed evidence suggests an animal origin of SARS-CoV-2, but doesn’t indicate when or where the spillover occurred. Plus, how horses can make two sounds at once at the science jobs that might be overtaken by AI.

records.title: Scientists must step up to avert a nuclear breakout
records.description: The end of the US–Russia treaty to cap the number of nuclear weapons places the world at risk. Here’s what researchers can do.

records.title: Dynamic antigen expression and cytotoxic T cell resistance in HIV reservoir clones
records.description: Insights into the vulnerabilities of HIV-1 reservoir clones to potent, sustained cytotoxic T cell pressure are revealed.

records.title: From Victorian voyages to vanishing maps: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: Why every scientist needs a librarian
records.description: Librarians can be key research partners who help to scour the literature, manage data and make science open.

records.title: AI tools can design genomes. Will they upend how life evolves?
records.description: Breakthroughs in computing are supercharging a field of science dedicated to building synthetic organisms from scratch.

records.title: Iron Age mass grave reveals unprecedented violence against women and children
records.description: Women and children moving through Europe became victims of mass violence.

records.title: First-of-a-kind stem-cell therapies set for approval in Japan
records.description: Regenerative medicines are headed for people with Parkinson’s disease or severe heart failure — but researchers are concerned about minimal clinical-trial data.

records.title: Whistle while you whinny: researchers identify two sounds straight from the horse’s mouth
records.description: The ability to make two distinct sounds at once is shared with human beatboxers and throat singers.

records.title: Historically Black US universities chase top research ranking
records.description: Howard University is reaping the rewards of becoming the first such institution to reach ‘R1’ status.

records.title: This AI can improve your peer review — and make it more polite
records.description: A system of five models helps peer reviewers to write more constructive comments, but it is not yet known whether this strengthens the papers that are being reviewed.

records.title: How big is the ‘motherhood penalty’? In Denmark, it adds up to $120,000
records.description: An analysis documents the cumulative income hit mothers incur — as well as the extent to which state aid can offset the loss.

records.title: Music is not a universal language — but it can bring us together when words fail
records.description: Societies, animals and even machines have music in common. Our varied experiences of it might tell us about the origins of language.

records.title: Super-sticky feet help a robot to climb the walls
records.description: An adhesive inspired by the foot pads of geckos allows a robot to scale both smooth and rough vertical surfaces.

records.title: Briefing Chat: How hovering bumblebees keep their cool
records.description: Nature staff discuss some of the week’s top science news.

records.title: Publisher Correction: PtdIns(3,5)P 2 is an endogenous ligand of STING in innate immune signalling
Gel helps mini spinal cords to heal from injury
records.description: Complex 3D structures of cells called organoids could be used to test treatments for spinal-cord damage that can lead to paralysis.

records.title: Author Correction: Natural behaviour is learned through dopamine-mediated reinforcement
Runaway black hole leaves a trail of stars
records.description: The supermassive object broke away from a nearby galaxy and is now racing through the intergalactic medium.

records.title: Why do curling stones slide across ice the way they do?
records.description: After a century of study, physicists have theories — but they’re still not 100% sure.

records.title: Five ways increased militarization could change scientific careers
records.description: Scholars working on defence, conflict and science funding consider the impact on research careers and budgets, highlighting five broad trends.

records.title: Are obesity drugs causing a severe complication? What the science says
records.description: The United Kingdom and Brazil have issued warnings about a possible link between GLP-1 weight-loss drugs and pancreatic inflammation, but the connection is murky.

records.title: Daily briefing: ‘Universal’ vaccine protects mice from multiple pathogens
records.description: A nasal-spray activates the innate immune system to protect against both pathogens and allergens in mice. Plus, how bigger military budgets could change the course of global science and a blood test that could predict the onset of Alzheimer’s disease.

records.title: AI is threatening science jobs. Which ones are most at risk?
records.description: Data-analysis and modelling positions are already becoming obsolete, but hands-on experimentalists can breathe easy for now.

records.title: Biotech investor set to lead US National Science Foundation
records.description: If confirmed, Jim O’Neill would be the first non-scientist or non-engineer to lead the agency, which is a big funder of US basic research.

records.title: ‘An AlphaFold 4’ — scientists marvel at DeepMind drug spin-off’s exclusive new AI
records.description: Isomorphic Lab’s proprietary drug-discovery model is a major advance, but scientists developing open-source tools are left guessing how to achieve similar results.

records.title: Daily briefing: Automated robot ‘scientists’ spark debate over the future of lab work
records.description: AI-controlled robots could automate simple tasks, but scientists say lab work still needs a human touch. Plus, a glass tile that can store terabytes of data and how service-dog trainers are using science to boost graduation rates.

records.title: Blood test holds promise for predicting when Alzheimer’s symptoms will start
records.description: The Alzheimer’s ‘clock’ could make it easier to treat the disease early, before memory problems appear.

records.title: Academia’s parent trap: the struggles faced by researcher mothers
records.description: How effective is the sector at supporting early career scientists hoping to start a family, including those who face fertility challenges?

records.title: Science journalism on the ropes worldwide as US aid cuts bite
records.description: Federal freezes to foreign assistance are affecting grants for investigative reporters everywhere — but especially in poorer countries.

records.title: ‘Universal vaccine’ protects mice against multiple pathogens
records.description: An innovative approach supercharges the innate immune system to provide a first line of defence against respiratory infections.

records.title: Host control of persistent Epstein–Barr virus infection
records.description: Using blood-based genome sequence data, non-genetic and genetic factors associated with control of Epstein–Barr virus during persistent infection are reported.

records.title: Author Correction: BCL6 enables Ph + acute lymphoblastic leukaemia cells to survive BCR–ABL1 kinase inhibition
Host control of persistent Epstein–Barr virus infection
records.description: Using blood-based genome sequence data, non-genetic and genetic factors associated with control of Epstein–Barr virus during persistent infection are reported.

records.title: Author Correction: BCL6 enables Ph + acute lymphoblastic leukaemia cells to survive BCR–ABL1 kinase inhibition
This chunk of glass could store two million books for 10,000 years
records.description: Microsoft unveils a laser-modified glass that could store huge amounts of data for millennia — plus, a trial of mRNA vaccines to prevent a form of breast cancer recurring.

records.title: This giant virus hijacks cells’ protein-making machinery to multiply wildly
records.description: A virus that is big enough to be seen under an ordinary light microscope co-opts its host’s systems with the help of potentially purloined genes.

records.title: How ‘skull drains’ keep the brain safe from damage and pathogens
records.description: Veins in the skull can rearrange their borders to accommodate patrolling immune cells, a strange behaviour called ruffling.

records.title: Mid-cycle update
records.description: Code of conduct.

records.title: How do autistic people age — and what does it mean for their health?
records.description: Most research on autism focuses on younger people, but some studies suggest older adults face increased risks — and perhaps benefits.

records.title: Microsoft team creates ‘revolutionary’ data-storage system that lasts for millennia
records.description: Researchers use mini plasma explosions to encode the equivalent of two million books into a coaster-sized device. The method could preserve research data for millennia with minimal storage costs.

records.title: AI offers way to image and assess clinical cell samples
records.description: The use of artificial intelligence in the clinic to image slides of cells enables the rapid assessment of cellular characteristics that might help with diagnostic decisions.

records.title: Stereospecific alkyl–alkyl cross-coupling of boronic esters
records.description: Stereospecific coupling of boronic esters catalysed by a copper acetylide complex provides simplification of the synthesis of chiral building blocks for complex molecules.

records.title: Turning on the ‘for you’ feed on X shifted political opinions, but turning it off did not
records.description: A field experiment shows that turning on the algorithmic feed on the social-media platform X in 2023 shifted political opinions to the right, whereas turning it off had no effect on political attitudes. The algorithmic feed led users to follow more right-leaning accounts, which they continued following when the algorithm was off.

records.title: Personalized mRNA vaccine induces strong, durable immunity in hard-to-treat breast cancer
records.description: In an experimental trial, a personalized mRNA vaccine was tested in 14 individuals with an aggressive form of breast cancer. It trained immune cells to target cancer-specific mutant proteins, inducing strong, lasting immunity. Ten participants remained disease-free. Analysis of relapses revealed resistance mechanisms, offering essential insights for future therapies.

records.title: AI succeeds in diagnosing rare diseases
records.description: An artificial-intelligence system uses clinical data, genetic information and literature searches to suggest diagnoses and provides the underlying reasoning.

records.title: Chip-scale device efficiently boosts light signals
records.description: Optical-amplifier devices that boost light signals are workhorses of modern technology, but shrinking them onto microchips requires impractically high power. An amplifier architecture has been developed that recycles its own ‘pump’ energy to achieve high performance at power levels ten times lower than those of previous designs, making low-power, chip-scale optical amplification practical.

records.title: Laser-written glass tablets can preserve data for millennia
records.description: An archive system that encodes information in modified optical properties of glass could be a fast, efficient way to store huge quantities of data.

records.title: Will self-driving ‘robot labs’ replace biologists? Paper sparks debate
records.description: AI-driven autonomous robots are coming to biology laboratories, but researchers insist that human skills remain essential.

records.title: Malaria is hindered by repression of a cell-cycle protein
records.description: A genetic variant that quashes cyclin D3 expression might have been selected for in a population on an island where malaria was once endemic.

records.title: Oysters build reefs with optimal geometries
records.description: Some species, including oysters, shape their habitat. However, the relationship between the 3D properties of their habitat and demographic processes is unclear. Experiments with systematically varying habitat units shed light on how specific combinations of geometric attributes influence oyster establishment and survival under predation.

records.title: Why China and Europe should collaborate to ‘defossilize’ the world’s carbon
records.description: The world needs non-fossil sources of carbon. It’s a no-brainer for nations working towards this goal to join forces.

records.title: Gene editing treats a mouse model of a neurodevelopmental disorder
records.description: An approach that specifically targets a single nucleotide corrected behavioural abnormalities in an animal model of Snijders Blok–Campeau syndrome.

records.title: Daily briefing: What we know about autism and ageing — and what we don’t
records.description: More adults are being diagnosed with autism than ever before, but we know very little about how the condition affects ageing. Plus, how hovering bees keep their cool and a call for nanoscientists to tackle the reproducibility crisis.

records.title: Giant energy storage and dielectric performance in all-polymer nanocomposites
records.description: A high-temperature immiscible blend of two dipolar polymers that self-assemble into three-dimensional all-polymer nanocomposites allows markedly enhanced dielectric and energy storage performances over a broad temperature range.

records.title: Rising atmospheric CO 2 reduces nitrogen availability in boreal forests
records.description: Nitrogen isotope tree-ring chronologies show that rising atmospheric CO 2 has reduced nitrogen availability in boreal forests in Sweden, suggesting that elevated atmospheric CO 2 is causing oligotrophication in boreal forests.

records.title: The natural architecture of oyster reefs maximizes recruit survival
records.description: Survival of reef-building oysters peaks at specific combinations of fractal dimension and height that reduce predation, showing how optimal three-dimensional habitat geometry can guide more effective ecosystem restoration.

records.title: Accurate predictions of disordered protein ensembles with STARLING
records.description: The deep learning model STARLING can generate accurate ensembles of intrinsically disordered regions of proteins using only protein sequence as input.

records.title: Practical lithium–organic batteries enabled by an n-type conducting polymer
records.description: An n-type conducting polymer with excellent mixed ionic and electronic transport enables a practical lithium–organic battery that exhibits a wide operating temperature range and excellent safety.

records.title: Individualized mRNA vaccines evoke durable T cell immunity in adjuvant TNBC
records.description: In a phase 1 trial, personalized mRNA vaccines tailored to individual tumour mutations in triple-negative breast cancer induced robust, long-lasting T cell responses and improved prognosis.

records.title: Reduced cyclin D3 expression in erythroid cells protects against malaria
records.description: Population-level analyses and in vitro experiments show that a specific genetic variant of cyclin D3 inhibits the growth of the malaria-causing parasite Plasmodium falciparum in erythrocytes, and suggest that its high frequency in Sardinia was driven by past endemic malaria.

records.title: Single-cell and isoform-specific translational profiling of the mouse brain
records.description: Post-transcriptional regulation of mRNA translation was explored using Ribo-STAMP and single-cell RNA sequencing to reveal cell-type-specific and isoform-specific translation patterns across hippocampal neuronal and non-neuronal cell types, highlighting functional differences between CA1 and CA3.

records.title: Roles of microtubules and LIS1 in dynein transport machinery assembly
records.description: Cryo-electron microscopy suggests a model in which microtubules, rather than adaptors in the cytoplasm, act as the primary platform for dynein–dynactin assembly, while LIS1 stabilizes low-microtubule-affinity intermediates near the pre-assembled complexes.

records.title: In vivo base editing of Chd3 rescues behavioural abnormalities in mice
records.description: In vivo base editing of a causative mutation that leads to the neurodevelopmental disorder Snijders Blok–Campeau syndrome restores protein dosage and ameliorates molecular and behavioural deficits in a humanized mouse model of the condition.

records.title: RYK is a GPNMB receptor that drives MASH
records.description: MASH is driven by the secreted GPNMB ectodomain, which binds hepatocyte RYK to activate ERK1/2 and promote lipid uptake and lipogenic programs; blocking the GPNMB–RYK axis prevented and treated MASH in preclinical models.

records.title: Highly dynamic dural sinuses support meningeal immunity
records.description: Microscopic imaging and biochemical studies show that sinuses in mouse and human form a highly dynamic surface that regulates fluid movement and immune cell surveillance via RAMP1-dependent regulation of smooth muscle contraction and RAMP2-dependent regulation of the sinus endothelial barrier.

records.title: Laser writing in glass for dense, fast and efficient archival data storage
records.description: An optical archival storage technology based on femtosecond laser direct writing in glass addresses the practical demands of archival storage.

records.title: Integrated photonics enabling ultra-wideband fibre–wireless communication
records.description: An integrated photonics scheme is presented for the manufacture of communication systems supporting the use of fibre and wireless infrastructures simultaneously, addressing the long-standing bandwidth mismatch between the two domains and demonstrating ultrahigh data rates.

records.title: Clinical-grade autonomous cytopathology through whole-slide edge tomography
records.description: This study presents a clinical-grade autonomous pipeline combining high-resolution whole-slide tomography, edge computing and artificial intelligence, achieving high accuracy in cervical cytology and enabling scalable and objective diagnostics.

records.title: A roadmap for evaluating moral competence in large language models
records.description: This Perspective offers a roadmap for tackling the challenges of the facsimile problem, moral multidimensionality and moral pluralism in large language models.

records.title: Nucleotide signals coordinate activation and inhibition of bacterial immunity
records.description: Biochemical and structural studies show that the bacterial dGTPase CloA is activated by virally produced dTTP and inhibited by 5′-triphosphothymidyl-3′5′-thymidine produced by its regulatory partner CloB, and thereby balances antiviral defence and immune-mediated toxicity.

records.title: Ancient co-option of LTR retrotransposons as yeast centromeres
records.description: Evolutionarily related ‘proto-point’ centromeres providing resolution to the evolutionary origins of point centromeres are identified in yeast, and comparison shows they evolved in an ancestor with retrotransposon-rich centromeres and that long-terminal-repeat retrotransposons are the genetic substrate.

records.title: Agouti integrates environmental cues to regulate paternal behaviour
records.description: Expression of agouti signalling protein in neurons in the medial preoptic area is increased by group housing and negatively associated with care, and overexpression of Agouti reduces care and enhances infanticide in previously tolerant mice.
