records.description: More than half of Gen Z now have a side gig. Are researchers among those seeking a second income?

records.title: AI can turbocharge scientists’ careers — but limit their scope
records.description: Artificial intelligence use can boost outputs, at the cost of research breadth — plus, solving the mystery of the Universe’s ‘little red dots’.

records.title: AI tools boost individual scientists but could limit research as a whole
records.description: Analyses of hundreds of thousands of papers in the natural sciences reveal a paradox: scientists who use AI tools produce more research but on a more confined set of topics.

records.title: Three tips for scientific writing: a guide for graduate students
records.description: Do you struggle with the blank page? These strategies could help.

records.title: Why is flu so bad this year? Highly mutated variant offers answers
records.description: A ferocious surge in influenza cases is linked in part to a variant that has not been dominant in the past few years — resulting in a waning of natural immunity.

records.title: LLMs behaving badly: mistrained AI models quickly go off the rails
records.description: Training large language models to write insecure code can cause them to exhibit seemingly aggressive behaviour when performing unrelated tasks.

records.title: Predicting the fate of tropical forests under intensifying heat
records.description: Intense droughts have caused water stress and elevated mortality for trees in the Amazon, foreshadowing the future of tropical forests as the climate changes.

records.title: Cancer might evade immune defences by stealing mitochondria
records.description: Hijacking the energy-producing organelles from immune cells seems to help tumours in mice to infiltrate lymph nodes.

records.title: How ageing harms the body’s response to raging infection
records.description: A gene that protects against sepsis in young mice raises the risk of death in older mice with the condition.

records.title: Ice age wolf pup’s stomach yields rare DNA from woolly rhino
records.description: A rare sample from a woolly rhinoceros reveals how the population changed in the lead-up to the species’ extinction.

records.title: Retraction Note: Antibodies against endogenous retroviruses promote lung cancer immunotherapy
Stretchy organic LED devices with an ‘exciplex’ state are highly efficient
records.description: Fully stretchable organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) have been limited by poor efficiency, in part because their elastic-polymer components hinder the harvesting of ‘triplet-state’ quasiparticles that can be converted into light-emitting states. Fully stretchable OLEDs with unprecedented efficiencies have been developed that recycle triplets in an elastomer-tolerant manner.

records.title: Daily briefing: Why ‘harmless’ germs can be deadly for some people
records.description: Rare immune errors can make usually harmless infections deadly in some people. Plus, the genetics of dogs’ floppy ears and a huge study on reasons for vaccine hesitancy.

records.title: US science in 2026: five themes that will dominate Trump’s second year
records.description: The outlook has brightened for federal science budgets, but political appointees are likely to have a big say in how that funding is spent.

records.title: Six steps to protect researchers’ digital security
records.description: Many US scientists have reported a rise in targeted harassment. Here are tools and tips to safeguard your cybersecurity.

records.title: Mysterious ‘little red dots’ could be black holes in disguise
records.description: Analysis indicates that the light from ‘little red dots’ is generated by young supermassive black holes obscured by dense clouds of gas.

records.title: Ageing rewires the body’s tolerance to infection
records.description: In life-threatening sepsis, the same signalling pathway that protects young mice from succumbing to organ dysfunction exacerbates damage and lethality in older animals.

records.title: Credit in research goes hand in hand with responsibility
records.description: Trust in science needs researchers, journals and institutions to correct the scientific record quickly and transparently when errors are found.

records.title: Genomic clues to the origin of eukaryotic cells
records.description: How did eukaryotic cells with complex architecture evolve from simpler prokaryotic cells? DNA analyses offer possible answers.

records.title: Beneath acid skies
records.description: Friends reunited.

records.title: Biosensors characterize the routes taken by receptors to different active states
records.description: A panel of fluorescently labelled G-protein-coupled-receptor proteins expressed in living cells has confirmed that, when bound by an activating ligand molecule, these receptors form different complexes with their G proteins. The activation trajectories induced by different ligands explain ligand-specific efficacies of G-protein activation and preferences for G-protein subtypes.

records.title: Memories of items and their contexts are encoded by separate groups of human brain cells
records.description: Human memory often needs to link specific items to the situation in which they feature. Brain recordings reveal that two distinct groups of neurons respond to stimuli and contextual information. These groups then cooperate to form flexible memories, rather than individual neurons encoding both signal types.

records.title: The infection enigma: why some people die from typically harmless germs
records.description: Millions of people worldwide carry genetic mutations that weaken their immune system.

records.title: Mosaic lateral heterostructures in two-dimensional perovskite
records.description: Colourful patterns in two-dimensional lead halide perovskites are created by letting them self-etch into tiny squares that can template epitaxial growth.

records.title: Dominant contribution of Asgard archaea to eukaryogenesis
records.description: A survey of the reconstructed gene set of the last eukaryotic common ancestor shows a consistent link between Asgard archaea and the origin of numerous, functionally diverse eukaryotic genes, demonstrating the dominant Asgard contribution to eukaryogenesis.

records.title: Microbiota-induced T cell plasticity enables immune-mediated tumour control
records.description: Molecular mimicry between a gut commensal and a tumour antigen forms part of an important mechanistic framework that can boost the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade therapy and restrain tumour growth.

records.title: Exciplex-enabled high-efficiency, fully stretchable OLEDs
records.description: Fabrication of fully stretchable organic light-emitting diodes incorporating an intrinsically stretchable exciplex-assisted phosphorescent layer along with MXene-contact stretchable electrodes is described, demonstrating high efficiency and mechanical compliance for applications in next-generation wearable and deformable displays.

records.title: Direct observation of the Migdal effect induced by neutron bombardment
records.description: Direct observation of the Migdal effect in neutron–nucleus collisions is reported, which resolves a long-standing gap in experimental validation.

records.title: Training large language models on narrow tasks can lead to broad misalignment
records.description: Finetuning a large language model on a narrow task of writing insecure code causes a broad range of concerning behaviours unrelated to coding.

records.title: Coherent nonlinear X-ray four-photon interaction with core-shell electrons
records.description: Using single broadband X-ray pulses from a free-electron laser on a gaseous neon target, coherent, nonlinear four-photon interactions with core–shell electrons is demonstrated, representing a strategy for multidimensional correlation spectroscopy at the atomic scale.

records.title: A foundation model for continuous glucose monitoring data
records.description: GluFormer, a generative foundation model, uses continuous glucose monitoring data to accurately forecast glycaemia-related health responses, particularly for long-term outcomes.

records.title: 3D-printed low-voltage-driven ciliary hydrogel microactuators
records.description: 3D-printed gel microcilia arrays printed by two-photon polymerization and composed of a soft acrylic acid-co-acrylamide hydrogel with a nanometre-scale network structure are shown to respond to low-voltage electrical stimuli within milliseconds, enabling dynamic individual control and non-reciprocal 3D motion.

records.title: Ligand-specific activation trajectories dictate GPCR signalling in cells
records.description: Different agonists produce equilibria of at least four distinct active states of the G-protein-bound M2 muscarinic acetylcholine receptor, each with a different ability to activate G proteins.

records.title: Disease tolerance and infection pathogenesis age-related tradeoffs in mice
records.description: Disease course and pathology an infection may cause can change owing to the structural and functional physiological changes that accumulate with age, but therapy can be tailored accordingly; disease tolerance genes show antagonistic pleiotropy.

records.title: Global subsidence of river deltas
records.description: Spatially variable surface-elevation changes across 40 global deltas using interferometric synthetic aperture radar are reported.

records.title: Enriching African genome representation through the AGenDA project
records.description: The Assessing Genetic Diversity in Africa (AGenDA) project shares their processes, including community engagement, obtaining ethics approvals, navigating legal compliance and developing a common governance framework.

records.title: Trapping of single atoms in metasurface optical tweezer arrays
records.description: Single strontium atoms are trapped in optical tweezer arrays generated via holographic metasurfaces, overcoming a critical barrier to realizing scalable neutral-atom quantum technologies.

records.title: A nowhere-to-hide mechanism ensures complete piRNA-directed DNA methylation
records.description: In mice, a SPOCD1–TPR-dependent ‘nowhere-to-hide’ mechanism is required for complete non-stochastic piRNA-directed LINE1 DNA methylation by preventing transposons from escaping surveillance within heterochromatin.

records.title: The ubiquitin ligase KLHL6 drives resistance to CD8 + T cell dysfunction
records.description: Integrating computational analyses of T cell exhaustion and mitochondrial fitness atlases with in vivo CRISPR screens has identified KLHL6 as a dual-negative regulator of both exhaustion differentiation and mitochondrial dysfunction, highlighting its potential as a target to enhance anti-tumour immunity.

records.title: N 1 -Methylpseudouridine directly modulates translation dynamics
records.description: N 1 -Methylpseudouridine enhances the translation of synthetic mRNAs, independently of innate immunity.

records.title: Little red dots as young supermassive black holes in dense ionized cocoons
records.description: The highest-quality JWST spectra reveal that little red dots are young supermassive black holes shrouded in dense cocoons of ionized gas, where electron scattering, not Doppler motions, broadens their spectral lines.

records.title: Ultra-high-throughput mapping of genetic design space
records.description: CLASSIC is a high-throughput genetic profiling platform that combines long- and short-read next-generation-sequencing modalities to quantitatively assess pools of constructs of arbitrary length containing diverse genetic part compositions.

records.title: Language model-guided anticipation and discovery of mammalian metabolites
records.description: Chemical language models trained on known metabolites can identify previously unknown metabolites from mass spectrometry-based metabolomics data with high accuracy.

records.title: CFAP20 salvages arrested RNAPII from the path of co-directional replisomes
records.description: CFAP20 has a key role in rescuing RNA polymerase II complexes that have arrested during DNA transcription, limiting the accumulation of R-loops and preventing collisions between the transcription and replication machinery.

records.title: An electrically injected solid-state surface acoustic wave phonon laser
records.description: A completely solid-state, single-chip, microwave-frequency surface acoustic wave phonon laser can generate coherent phonons from thermal noise or resonantly amplify injected phonons using only a direct current bias field.

records.title: Predictive coding of reward in the hippocampus
records.description: Calcium imaging of mouse hippocampal neurons while mice learn a reward-based task over several weeks provides insight into the evolution of the hippocampal reward representation during extended periods of experience.

records.title: Artificial intelligence tools expand scientists’ impact but contract science’s focus
records.description: Artificial intelligence boosts individual scientists’ output, citations and career progression, but collectively narrows research diversity and reduces collaboration, concentrating work in data-rich areas and potentially limiting broader scientific exploration.

records.title: Sub-zero Celsius elastocaloric cooling via low-transition-temperature alloys
records.description: A compression-based, regenerative elastocaloric cooling device using low-transition-temperature tubular NiTi units in a cascaded configuration, which show superelasticity and substantial entropy changes, allows the construction of a sub-zero Celsius refrigeration system without refrigerant gases.

records.title: Polyamine-dependent metabolic shielding regulates alternative splicing
records.description: Polyamines prevent the action of kinases on acidic phosphorylatable motifs in spliceosomal proteins, thus providing a mechanism for metabolite-mediated regulation of alternative splicing in cells.

records.title: No world-changing discoveries without biodiversity
Don’t assume that women’s low retraction rates reflect male ‘boldness’
Should the Loch Ness Monster have a scientific name?
records.description: A debate over a potential newly discovered species, and a tip for buying good sherry in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: AI writing tools could lead scholars from low-income countries to erase their own voices
AlphaFold can help African researchers to do cutting-edge structural biology
How to improve vaccine uptake: a huge study offers clues
records.description: An analysis of more than one million people in the UK found that two-thirds of people who were vaccine-hesitant during the COVID-19 pandemic went on to get vaccinated.

records.title: Daily briefing: Same-sex sex is a normal part of some primates’ lives
records.description: Same-sex sexual behaviour could help some primates cope with complex social hierarchies. Plus, new clues as to where birds came from and the US Environmental Protection Agency will stop including human health in cost–benefit analyses.

records.title: Do their ears hang low? The genetics of dogs’ adorable floppy ears
records.description: Scientists are just beginning to understand the signals that determine the length of dogs’ ears.

records.title: How did birds evolve? The answer is wilder than anyone thought
records.description: Discoveries in Jurassic rocks reveal that birds were adept fliers earlier than scientists realized.

records.title: AI can spark creativity — if we ask it how, not what, to think
records.description: Studies aiming to maximize human creativity demonstrate that people work best when buoyed up by others who show them new ways to innovate.

records.title: The academic community failed Wikipedia for 25 years — now it might fail us
records.description: Artificial-intelligence systems are feeding on Wikipedia without giving back, and academic indifference is threatening the survival of what is arguably the most widely used reference work on the planet.

records.title: Developing super-tortillas to address malnutrition in Latin America
records.description: Mexican food scientist Raquel Gómez-Pliego works to improve the nutritional value of foods through microbial fermentation.

records.title: Ancient ‘snowball’ Earth had frigidly briny seas
records.description: Ocean temperatures well below freezing in Earth’s deep-past glacial phases imply some very salty waters.

records.title: Same-sex sexual behaviour can help primates to survive — and reproduce
records.description: Bonds between same-sex individuals help apes and monkeys to manage conflict and strengthen alliances, especially in dry habitats and predator-rich landscapes.

records.title: US scientists push back as Trump eyes Greenland
records.description: An open letter organized by US-based researchers who work in Greenland opposes any takeover of the territory.

records.title: Fresh starts: how to thrive when you leave academia
records.description: Do your New Year resolutions include a plan to leave higher education? These researchers explain how to reinvent your career.

records.title: ‘We’re humans — brilliant and a mess’: Wikipedia founder Jimmy Wales on trust and optimism
records.description: Twenty-five years after its launch, the online encyclopedia now competes with chatbots — but its creator still has faith in humans when it comes to sourcing facts.

records.title: AIs are biased towards some Indian castes — how can researchers fix this?
records.description: Benchmarks reveal how artificial-intelligence systems reinforce discriminatory social hierarchies.

records.title: Daily briefing: The neural circuit that can make it hard to start a difficult task
records.description: A ‘motivation brake’ in our brains makes taking that first step towards a task less appealing. Plus, US scientists have signed an open letter in solidarity with Greenland and what Wikipedia can teach us about trust.

records.title: Student mental health is in crisis — here’s how to help
records.description: Universities, governments, academics, health-care providers and students must work together to ensure timely access to suitable mental-health support.

records.title: This shapeshifting polymer was inspired by octopus skin
records.description: A new octopus-inspired polymer can change colour and texture on command.

records.title: Getting to the (square) root of stock-market swings
records.description: A huge data set has confirmed a long-theorized relationship between the size of stock trades and the impact on prices.

records.title: Disappearing ‘planet’ reveals a solar system’s turbulent times
records.description: What was originally thought to be a planet orbiting the Fomalhaut star was probably just the fallout of a wild collision.

records.title: To infinity and beyond Earth’s pale blue dot: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: Daily briefing: Fusion reactor pushes plasma past crucial limit
records.description: A Chinese reactor has jumped a hurdle that’s held nuclear fusion back for decades. Plus, astronauts are being evacuated from the International Space Station and AI chatbots in therapy make claims of abuse.

records.title: ‘Coming out as a transgender scientist made me the best teacher I’ve ever been’
records.description: Shannon Bros and K Wilson outline how academia can better support LGBTQ+ researchers, launching a podcast series about workplace topics that are often off limits.

records.title: AI models were given four weeks of therapy: the results worried researchers
records.description: Chatbots put through psychotherapy report trauma and abuse. Authors say models are doing more than role play, but researchers are sceptical.

records.title: Can’t get motivated? This brain circuit might explain why — and it can be turned off
records.description: Scientists have uncovered a way to manipulate the brain pathway in monkeys that puts the brakes on motivation.

records.title: NASA won’t bring Mars samples back to Earth: this is the science that will be lost
records.description: A Congressional bill restores funding for most NASA space-science missions, but there is no money for returning samples already collected on the red planet.

records.title: We need to talk about salaries in science
records.description: Academia too often has a ‘passion first, money second’ culture. Overcoming this mindset is crucial for building a happy career.

records.title: Chinese nuclear fusion reactor pushes plasma past crucial limit: what happens next
records.description: Breaking the plasma density limit brings researchers a step closer to viable fusion reactors.

records.title: Author Correction: Structural insights into BCDX2 complex function in homologous recombination
Putting immune cells into ‘night mode’ reduces heart-attack damage
records.description: Drugs that limit the activity of cells called neutrophils could make heart attacks less severe without compromising the immune system.

records.title: Huge Chinese cell atlas reveals surprising immune variation among peoples
records.description: A giant functional atlas of immune cells in a Chinese cohort reveals crucial differences from European and Japanese data sets.

records.title: Daily briefing: Octopus-inspired synthetic ‘skin’ changes appearance on demand
records.description: A new material can switch from matte to shiny and display a variety of other effects as required. Plus, humans were using poison arrows 60,000 years ago and the quest to authenticate a da Vinci drawing using DNA.

records.title: Will mpox go global again? Research shows it’s evolving in curious ways
records.description: Analyses of monkeypox virus clades currently in circulation provide clues to how the virus managed to spread worldwide in 2022 — and how it might go global again.

records.title: A mysterious ancient fingerprint and a lemon-shaped planet — the stories you’ve missed
records.description: We highlight some Nature Briefing stories from the end of 2025, including: a seismic detector made from a telecom cable, and how self-heating plants attract pollinators.

records.title: Oldest known poison arrows show Stone Age humans’ technological talents
records.description: Traces of a toxic chemical found on 60,000-year-old arrowheads hint at advanced planning by Palaeolithic hunters.

records.title: The complex role of nutrients in cancer spread
records.description: An in-depth analysis of nutrient availability across mouse tissues reveals their influence on the spread of cancer to other organs.

records.title: Ultra-low-density exoplanets observed around a young star
records.description: Measurements of the masses of exoplanets orbiting a young star have identified a system of low-density ‘super-puff’ planets.

records.title: Of all the quarries: Casablanca fossils reveal African ancestors of Homo sapiens
records.description: Surprising fossil finds in a Moroccan quarry reveal 773,000-year-old hominin specimens that are close to the ancestor of modern humans.

records.title: Daily briefing: How 400-year-old sharks keep their vision sharp
records.description: Greenland sharks are surprisingly eagle-eyed, even in old age. Plus, a call to ‘defossilize’ chemistry and the best books to help shape your science career.

records.title: Octopus-inspired ‘synthetic skin’ changes colour and texture on demand
records.description: A material that can switch its appearance, cephalopod-style, could have future applications in robotics or display technology.

records.title: Electrochemical defluorinative Matteson-type homologation
records.description: A new Matteson-type homologation method inserts carbon units into boronic esters using electrochemistry.

records.title: How viral RNAs escape a host mechanism that controls translation
records.description: A long-standing question has been how viral RNAs that use genetic codes different from those used in human cells can still drive efficient viral protein production during infection. It emerges that the sequences of 5′ untranslated regions in viral RNAs drive codon-usage-independent translation by blocking mRNA circularization, enabling viruses to evade the host’s codon-usage control of translation.

records.title: Chronic pain could be eased by uncoupling the sensory and emotional experiences
records.description: Researchers identify the neurons involved in the emotional distress associated with pain, and design a genetic approach that could soothe suffering without opioid drugs.

records.title: Exotic quasiparticles glimpsed in graphene
records.description: Bilayer graphene has been used to observe robust interference patterns consistent with the presence of fractionally charged quasiparticles known as non-Abelian anyons. Demonstrating and controlling this interference is a crucial step towards harnessing these elusive quasiparticles as building blocks for fault-tolerant quantum computers.

records.title: A way to identify the biological basis of gene–trait associations
records.description: Genetic-association studies have identified many genetic variants that are associated with complex traits. However, in most cases, the biology underlying the association is unknown. Integrating experimental gene-perturbation and genetic-association data sets could reveal the mechanisms underlying complex traits.

records.title: ‘I rarely get outside’: scientists ditch fieldwork in the age of AI
records.description: In the race to embrace new technologies, some ecologists fear their field is losing touch with nature.

records.title: A troubleshooting guide to your flat-pack planet
records.description: World-making tips and tricks.

records.title: Blood protein thwarts deadly fungal disease
records.description: Low levels of albumin, a protein found in blood, are associated with poor clinical outcomes for people with the fungal disease mucormycosis.

records.title: A framework for addressing racial and related inequities in conservation
records.description: This Perspective proposes a new framework to support the inclusion of Black, Indigenous and people of colour in conservation initiatives.

records.title: A hidden diversity of ceratopsian dinosaurs in Late Cretaceous Europe
records.description: New results indicate that rhabdodontids and the previously described Ajkaceratops are actually distinctive European ceratopsians, a group better known from Asia and North America.

records.title: A young progenitor for the most common planetary systems in the Galaxy
records.description: A nine-year transit-timing campaign has measured the extremely low masses and densities of four large planets orbiting the young star V1298 Tau, which are now predicted to contract and form a typical compact super-Earth and sub-Neptune system.

records.title: Surface optimization governs the local design of physical networks
records.description: Analysis of the local branching geometries of several physical networks shows violations of predictions of length and volume minimization, leading to the hypothesis that estimating the material cost requires accounting for the full three-dimensional geometry.

records.title: RNA-triggered Cas12a3 cleaves tRNA tails to execute bacterial immunity
records.description: Cas12a3 nucleases constitute a distinct clade of type V CRISPR–Cas bacterial immune systems that preferentially cleave the 3′ tails of tRNAs after recognition of target RNA to induce growth arrest and block phage dissemination.

records.title: Plastic landmark anchoring in zebrafish compass neurons
records.description: Using two-photon microscopy with a panoramic virtual reality setup, how head direction cells in larval zebrafish integrate visual landmarks and optic flow to track orientation is revealed.

records.title: An expanded registry of candidate cis -regulatory elements
records.description: The existing ENCODE registry of candidate human and mouse cis -regulatory elements is expanded with the addition of new ENCODE data, integrating new functional data as well as new cell and tissue types.

records.title: High-voltage anode-free sodium–sulfur batteries
records.description: A new architecture based on high-valence sulfur/sulfur tetrachloride cathode chemistry is described for manufacturing high-voltage anode-free sodium–sulfur batteries, demonstrating promise for applications in grid energy storage and wearable electronics.

records.title: Climate change shifts the North Pacific storm track polewards
records.description: An observation-based storm-track proxy shows that the winter North Pacific storm track has shifted substantially polewards, suggesting regional impacts on precipitation and warming patterns, with implications for temperature variability and extreme events.

records.title: Prefrontal neural geometry of learned cues guides motivated behaviours
records.description: The dorsomedial prefrontal cortex encodes the value, salience and valence of learned stimuli along distinct neural dimensions, and the geometry of these representations shapes motivated behaviours in mice.

records.title: Bidirectional CRISPR screens decode a GLIS3-dependent fibrotic cell circuit
records.description: Integrated single-cell and spatial data analysis, combined with bidirectional CRISPR screens, identify the transcription factor GLIS3 as a key driver of chronic inflammation and fibrosis and a potential marker of disease severity in patients with ulcerative colitis.

records.title: Soft biodegradable implants for long-distance and wide-angle sensing
records.description: A soft, biodegradable, wireless sensing device can monitor pressure, temperature and strain over long distances (up to 16 cm), maintaining accuracy across varying positions and angles.

records.title: Early hominins from Morocco basal to the Homo sapiens lineage
records.description: New hominin fossils from the Grotte à Hominidés at Thomas Quarry I (ThI-GH) in Casablanca, Morocco, dated to around 773 thousand years ago are similar in age to Homo antecessor , yet are morphologically distinct.

records.title: Genetic switch between unicellularity and multicellularity in marine yeasts
records.description: Myb1 functions as a switch-like regulator of state transitions in Hortaea werneckii , whereby its expression and degradation are coupled to nutrient conditions, stabilizing unicellular or multicellular growth.

records.title: Insights into DNA repeat expansions among 900,000 biobank participants
records.description: Human genetic variation influences instability of DNA repeats that commonly expand as we age.

records.title: Pulse heating and slip enhance charging of phase-change thermal batteries
records.description: A strategy based on the design of a composite coating that enables slip-enhanced close-contact melting inside sealed phase-change thermal batteries to improve charging rates enables high-performance thermal energy storage over a wide range of temperatures.

records.title: Neuro-epithelial circuits promote sensory convergence and intestinal immunity
records.description: Specific pain-sensing nociceptors and chemosensory tuft cells form a circuit to promote type 2 immune responses in the intestine.

records.title: Nutrient requirements of organ-specific metastasis in breast cancer
records.description: How the complex interplay between multiple nutrients within the microenvironment dictates potential sites of metastatic cancer growth is explored.

records.title: Towards fibre-like loss for photonic integration from violet to near-infrared
records.description: Germano-silicate used as a building material for integrated photonics circuits substantially reduces optical losses, approaching levels comparable to those in optical fibres.

records.title: Aharonov–Bohm interference in even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states
records.description: This study reports coherent Aharonov–Bohm interference, including statistical phase contributions, in a Fabry–Pérot interferometer at two even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states in high-mobility bilayer-graphene van der Waals heterostructures is reported.

records.title: Soft photonic skins with dynamic texture and colour control
records.description: Inspired by dynamic textural modulation in cephalopod skin, polymer films whose colour and surface texture can be dynamically and independently controlled are developed and demonstrated using standard electron-beam patterning tools.

records.title: Mitochondrial transfer from glia to neurons protects against peripheral neuropathy
records.description: Mitochondria that are transported from satellite glial cells in dorsal root ganglia to peripheral sensory neurons through tunneling nanotube-like structures provide protection against peripheral neuropathy.

records.title: Intratumoural vaccination via checkpoint degradation-coupled antigen presentation
records.description: An intratumoural vaccination chimera reprograms tumour cells into an antigen-presenting state with restored anti-tumour immunity.

records.title: Systematic analyses of lipid mobilization by human lipid transfer proteins
records.description: Systematic characterization of human lipid transfer proteins in complex with their lipid partners reveals the relevance of these interactions for lipid metabolism, identifies mechanisms that contribute to lipid binding selectivity and provides a rich resource for the study of these proteins.

records.title: An ancient DNA perspective on the Russian conquest of Yakutia
records.description: Yakut communities, with Trans-Baikal admixture during the Mongol expansion, preserved genomic diversity and oral microbiomes despite the Russian conquest, which introduced cereals, pathogens and Christianity, whereas marital practices preserved low consanguinity except in one late case of traditional shamanism.

records.title: Mimicking opioid analgesia in cortical pain circuits
records.description: The anterior cingulate cortex encodes affective pain behaviours modulated by opioids; targeting opioid-sensitive neurons through a new chemogenetic gene therapy replicates the analgesic effects of morphine, providing precise chronic pain relief without affecting sensory detection.

records.title: Distinct neuronal populations in the human brain combine content and context
records.description: Single-neuron recordings in humans reveal largely separate content and context neurons whose coordinated activity flexibly places memory items in context.

records.title: A mechanical ratchet drives unilateral cytokinesis
records.description: Division of embryonic cells with an incomplete contractile ring occurs by a ratchet mechanism with repeated cycles of cytoplasmic stiffening, which stabilizes the contractile actin band, and fluidization, which enables band ingression.

records.title: Albumin orchestrates a natural host defence mechanism against mucormycosis
records.description: Albumin selectively inhibits Mucorales growth through the release of bound free fatty acids.

records.title: Small persistent humid forest clearings drive tropical forest biomass losses
records.description: A bookkeeping approach shows that disturbed tropical humid forests experienced net aboveground carbon loss during 1990–2020, primarily driven by small but persistent deforestation clearings owing to persistent land-use conversion without forest regrowth.

records.title: ipRGC properties prevent light from shifting the SCN clock during daytime
records.description: The inability of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells to shift the circadian clock in the suprachiasmatic nucleus during daytime is caused by light-dependent depolarization block of these cells.

records.title: Evidence accumulation from experience and observation in the cingulate cortex
records.description: Humans and monkeys integrated experiential and observational evidence during a two-player task, and the anterior cingulate cortex combined the information sources into a unified neural belief representation that explains behavioural asymmetries.

records.title: Stress controls heterochromatin inheritance via histone H3 ubiquitylation
records.description: A histone ubiquitin-dependent regulatory hub governs stimulus-dependent heterochromatin propagation, with important implications for understanding mechanisms governing rapid changes in the epigenetic landscape in physiology and disease.

records.title: Oral 4′-fluorouridine rescues nonhuman primates from advanced Lassa fever
records.description: Treatment with 4′-fluorouridine (also known as EIDD-2749) in an African green monkey ( Chlorocebus aethiops ) model of Lassa disease resulted in complete clearance of infectious virus in a high proportion of cases and prolonged survival to the pre-determined study end-point in all cases.

records.title: The poetic life and death of a glow-worm
records.description: A peek behind the scenes at the zoo reveals animal escapades, and a glow-worm shines in a mild midwinter, in our weekly dip into Nature ’s archive.

records.title: Rethink how we build AI to enable effective climate-change mitigation
These women helped to shape quantum mechanics — it’s time to recognize them
records.description: An astute book redresses our collective perception of a field that became known as ‘boys’ physics’.

records.title: Daily briefing: The human cells in our bodies that aren’t genetically ours
records.description: ‘Microchimeric’ cells passed from your mother can challenge basic tenets of immunology. Plus, an experimental cancer vaccine that uses blood ‘cleaned’ with ultraviolet light and the evidence for trying ‘Dry January’.

records.title: Pandemic PhDs: graduates anxious, but optimistic, about the future
records.description: Five early-career scientists from around the world share how lingering COVID-19 pandemic shadows and ripples from US academic disruptions have affected them.

records.title: Sunyaev–Zeldovich detection of hot intracluster gas at redshift 4.3
records.description: Detection of hot intracluster gas in SPT2349−56 with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array provides new insights into early cluster formation.

records.title: Author Correction: Repulsions instruct synaptic partner matching in an olfactory circuit
Author Correction: Rewiring an olfactory circuit by altering cell-surface combinatorial code
Science in 2026: what to expect this year
records.description: More refined AI models, advancements in human gene editing and the continuing impact of the Trump Team on science — we run through what to look out for over the next 12 months.

records.title: The climate is in crisis — here’s four things we can do
records.description: More needs to be done to combat climate change, but what? We discuss some big ideas to rein in emissions.

records.title: Architecture of a portal complex embedded in the poxvirus core
As El Niño builds, studies of extreme marine heatwaves must start now
records.description: Researchers must track warming oceans and use the knowledge gained to inform strategies for sustaining fisheries and communities that depend on them.

records.title: The psychology of imaginary friends — and why they are good for kids
records.description: Children often conjure up invisible pals to keep them company. A psychologist delves into the reasons why.

records.title: Chinese scientist sacked after child died in gene-editing trial
records.description: Institutions and other researchers involved have also been reprimanded.

records.title: Is the sixth great extinction imminent? Scientists must draw on natural history for clues
records.description: A lack of crosstalk between research disciplines is hampering scholars’ ability to fully examine how people have altered Earth’s biodiversity.

records.title: Number of international students arriving in US plunges — worrying scientists
records.description: Decline in the number of students from China and India are driving the trend, which researchers say could slow the progress of US science.

records.title: Chinese graduate students are now choosing to stay closer to home
records.description: Malaysia, Hong Kong and Macau are the new hot destinations for students.

records.title: Accept all changes
records.description: It’s the end — or is it?

records.title: This AI ‘mechanic’ can peer inside the black box of other neural networks
records.description: Being able to target and debug systems could improve artificial-intelligence safety and utility.

records.title: Is the climate totally cooked? What the data say
records.description: In the first of our new podcast series, a Nature reporter looks for reasons for hope in the face of overwhelming climate anxiety.

records.title: Found: a protein that drives ageing without unleashing inflammation
records.description: Aged mice engineered to lack granzyme K have improved heart and liver function and less kidney damage.

records.title: This little brown mushroom is laced with a hallucinogen — and lethal toxins
records.description: A Florida fungus might combine the psychedelic compound psilocybin with deadly chemicals to defend itself against hungry animals.

records.title: Who needs sex? Kelp reproduce asexually when no mate is nearby
records.description: Insights into the reproductive modes of brown algae could help in the fight to protect them in warming climate.

records.title: Author Correction: SLAMF6 as a drug-targetable suppressor of T cell immunity against cancer
Record-breaking Ebola outbreak: phone data reconstruct first weeks of spread
records.description: The Bundibugyo virus strain was circulating for weeks before its detection in May, but was missed owing to surveillance failures, testing gaps and funding cuts, researchers say.

records.title: Massive atlas of brain region linked to a host of diseases is the most detailed yet
records.description: A global team profiled nearly 26 million brain cells from the basal ganglia to build a cross-species reference database that will help to understand conditions from Parkinson’s disease to addiction.

records.title: RSV vaccines slash infections: data show jabs’ staggering success against dangerous virus
records.description: Vaccines and monoclonal-antibody injections are cutting hospitalizations linked to the respiratory virus.

records.title: Daily briefing: Are one-person firms the future of biotech?
records.description: Researchers are debating whether small, AI-enabled biotech companies are the future of drug discovery. Plus, even microplastics still reach the wildlife furthest from humanity and an upgrade to AlphaGenome.

records.title: Novel CRISPR therapy is poised to gain first FDA approval to alter genes inside the body
records.description: Current gene-editing treatments require removal of a participant’s cells, a complex and costly approach.

records.title: Rattlesnakes have personalities too — to venomous effect
records.description: A snake’s defensiveness might affect how much venom it produces in a laboratory test.

records.title: Iconic first image of black hole holds up to scrutiny
records.description: Picture produced by fresh analysis of the data that yielded the first-ever image of a black hole outputs the same, ring-like shape.

records.title: Too dry for cacti: extreme droughts could push iconic species to extinction
records.description: Analysis reveals these plants face severe habitat loss across the Americas — plus, researchers test a new way to diagnose obesity.

records.title: Getting a grasp on the global wildlife trade
records.description: A study reports that about 107,000 species are traded worldwide, legally or illegally — more than double a previous estimate.

records.title: Efficient catalyst-controlled C–H arylation of arenes
A guide to Nature Index tables
records.description: Information on the methodology used in the ranking for the 2026 Nature Spotlight: Energy.

records.title: Even giant anteaters in remote Brazil have microplastics in their blood
records.description: Mapping the movements of wildlife across the Amazon and other regions to their exposure to human activities can inform protection initiatives.

records.title: Microplastics change the colour of the sea near the Great Pacific Garbage Patch
records.description: The waters around the zone of floating debris appear greener and bluer on account of high levels of tiny bits of plastic.

records.title: Salty grains in Saturn’s outermost ring formed from the slow freeze of plumes from the moon Enceladus
records.description: One of Saturn’s rings consists of a diverse population of icy and rocky grains, each with a distinct composition. How this came about might now have an explanation.

records.title: Daily briefing: Should old, bad science be culled from the literature?
records.description: AI tools that summarize scientific literature are picking up decades-old flawed papers — should they be retracted? Plus, the first image of a black hole holds up to scrutiny and how the Artemis II mission might have disrupted GPS.

records.title: Cacti are severely threatened by drought in a warming world
records.description: Forecasts of the effects that climate change will have on biodiversity typically rely on long-term climate averages while excluding extreme events. Projections that include severe drought predict that a majority of the 993 cactus species assessed will see large losses of suitable climatic area: more than 25% of species could lose at least 80% of it by 2100.

records.title: Extraordinary materials shaped by the principles of complex networks
records.description: Network science has inspired the design of materials that spread out their deformation when a force is applied, have tunable stiffness and can control vibrational waves.

records.title: DeepMind’s ultra-powerful AI for genome mapping wows scientists
records.description: AlphaGenome 2 can predict the types of cell in which a DNA variant is likely to act.

records.title: Proteins that form the nuclear pore barrier move like liquids
records.description: Nuclear pores control molecular traffic into and out of the cell nucleus. Measurements in living cells, together with molecular-dynamics simulations, show that flexible protein chains that form the selectivity barriers of nuclear pores are highly mobile, and that a sugar modification and the carrier protein importin-β help to preserve this dynamic state.

records.title: How to avoid aliens and live
records.description: Silence is golden.

records.title: Earth’s early history told by 3.9-billion-year-old rocks from northern China
records.description: Ancient rocks in northern China reveal that by 3.95 billion years ago, surface-altered oceanic crust had been buried rapidly to depths greater than 50 kilometres and partly melted. This crust was derived from a mantle reservoir that had been left behind when the crust separated from the early mantle as early as 4.3 billion years ago.

records.title: Biotech innovations are an opportunity to limit climate change
records.description: Agricultural biotechnology once found itself in opposition to environmental science. Now it could reduce the impact of food systems on global warming and biodiversity loss.

records.title: How I balance my life as a professional surfer and a university researcher
records.description: Cliff Kapono shares his advice on ways to navigate and grow two different careers.

records.title: Hideki Shirakawa obituary: chemist who showed that plastics can conduct electricity
records.description: Nobel prizewinner’s accidental discovery led to new forms of materials, light-emitting diodes and solar cells.

records.title: Give biologists the space to be curious, not just better tools
records.description: Technology is making biological studies more powerful than ever. But people are the real force behind discovery.

records.title: Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery’s future?
records.description: A promising biotechnology company developed an approach that might treat a rare disease — but its sole employee didn’t do all the work.

records.title: Move over BMI: new obesity definition is better for predicting your health
records.description: A fresh approach considers waist circumference, rather than just weight and height, providing a more accurate classification.

records.title: New culprit in early Alzheimer’s: blood–brain barrier blocks protective proteins
records.description: The brain relies on crucial proteins to maintain neurons. This system is disrupted in mice with neurological disease.

records.title: AI’s energy paradox: will the AI boom strain energy systems or be the source of solutions?
records.description: Ginelle Greene-Dewasmes is leading a community of interdisciplinary specialists exploring how to make the energy use of artificial intelligence net-positive.

records.title: Retractions of old papers are on the rise: when should bad science be culled?
records.description: Decades-old papers are increasingly being pulled from the literature, bringing a host of challenges.

records.title: Author or just ‘acknowledged’? How women are not gaining full credit for research
records.description: An analysis of who is more likely to get authorship than acknowledgement highlights the influence of a researcher’s gender and status.

records.title: Engineered bacteria are weaning farms away from synthetic fertilizers
records.description: Scientists are editing microbes to supply more nitrogen to staple crops.

records.title: Proposed approach for diagnosing obesity outperforms old method
records.description: A framework for diagnosing obesity that was proposed in 2025 incorporates waist circumference and related measures and distinguishes clinical from preclinical obesity on the basis of obesity-induced organ dysfunction. In an international multi-cohort study of 844,108 adults, this framework outperformed conventional body-mass-index-based criteria in diagnosing obesity and stratifying mortality risk.

records.title: Personal incentives for public officials drove a drop in China’s fertility
records.description: Once the promotion prospects of bureaucrats became tied to birth targets, the country’s one-child policy became more effective. Can the state now reverse this effect?

records.title: Can green technologies deliver energy security in an unstable world?
records.description: As global energy markets grapple with a period of sustained political volatility, researchers are digging deep for solutions.

records.title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart
records.description: Structural and biochemical studies show that the CMG helicase directly recruits PRIMPOL for leading-strand repriming, enabling replication fork restart and limiting post-replicative DNA gaps.

records.title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China
records.description: Stronger bureaucratic incentives under China’s one vote veto policy intensified enforcement of the one-child policy, accounting for nearly half of China’s fertility decline during the 1990s.

records.title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
records.description: A large-scale data analysis assesses the Lancet Commission’s proposed diagnostic framework for obesity, finding that this framework, in which BMI is combined with other criteria, such as waist circumference and organ function, is more useful than classifications based on BMI alone.

records.title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss
records.description: TDP-43 loss induces a predegenerative state in which neurons remain structurally intact and suffer a substantial breakdown in synaptic communication; a therapeutic strategy is found that corrects UNC13A cryptic splicing by using splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides.

records.title: NRF2 is a mechanosensitive checkpoint for NLRP3 inflammasome activation
records.description: The stiffness of the extracellular matrix is identified as a pivotal factor that influences activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in vitro and in vivo.

records.title: Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion
records.description: An electrolyte framework that harnesses anionic chemistry to coordinate the interfacial microenvironment and molecular interactions enables reversible four-electron iodine conversion in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes, and is validated in metal–iodine batteries.

records.title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
records.description: IL-1β from neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby brown adipocytes in a low-UCP1 state; cold temperature reduces IL-1β via sympathetic nerves, leading to transition to a high-UCP1 state and increased thermogenesis, while higher temperatures have the opposite effect.

records.title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis
records.description: Single-cell epigenetic analyses reveal a conserved epigenetic signature across patients that may help identify those at increased risk for disease relapse in breast cancer.

records.title: A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2′,3′-cNMP produced by insect effectors
records.description: The rice RNA-binding protein NIB1 detects 2′,3′-cyclic nucleotide products from insect saliva RNase, forming nuclear condensates that recruit EDS1 to activate defence, revealing a conserved messenger-based immune pathway in plants.

records.title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
records.description: Flexible tidal turbine blades with passive trailing-edge deformation match the energy yield of active pitch-controlled blades while reducing fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third, lowering maintenance complexity.

records.title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
records.description: Analysis of a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, China, reveals a composition suggesting a low-temperature altered basaltic source, that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean, was most likely transported to mantle depths through a transient subduction event and partially melted to produce the trondhjemite.

records.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
records.description: Microplastic burdens in Brazilian tapirs and anteaters rise with human-modified land use and proximity to development, however animals in remote habitats also carry microplastics, showing that landscape change and individual space use jointly shape wildlife exposure.

records.title: Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice
records.description: A distinct physical nuclear state acquired by embryos at the beginning of life supports the initiation of the zygotic transcription program.

records.title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
records.description: Experiments in mouse models show that immunoglobulin A in the gut lumen has a role in regulating the turnover of colon epithelial cells and reduces the susceptibility of mice to colorectal cancer.

records.title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
records.description: The somatic evolutionary histories of haematopoietic cells in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia diagnosis show that the clonal dynamics of blood comply with a set of simple evolutionary rules.

records.title: Scale-rich network-based metamaterials
records.description: A network-science-based framework that embeds network heterogeneity into mechanical metamaterials is used to produce scale-rich metamaterials that exhibit properties inaccessible to traditional single-scale systems.

records.title: The molecular basis of replication fork restart via repriming by PRIMPOL
records.description: PRIMPOL is recruited to stalled forks through an interaction with the replicative helicase CDC45–MCM2–7–GINS, facilitating primer handover from PRIMPOL to the high-fidelity polymerase ε, minimizing mutagenic DNA synthesis.

records.title: Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer
records.description: A novel therapeutic modality enforces non-native androgen receptor (AR)–p300/CBP interactions to collapse AR transcriptional programs, producing super-inhibitory, lineage-selective suppression of metastatic prostate cancer and establishing domain-alteration chimeras as a broadly applicable therapeutic strategy leveraging induced proximity.

records.title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores
records.description: Nuclear pore proteins maintain a fluid, spatially organized barrier through coordinated molecular interactions, explaining how cells achieve selective transport and reconciling competing models of pore structure.

records.title: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti
records.description: Severe drought and warming will substantially increase the loss of suitable climatic area for cactus species.

records.title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high- κ dielectrics
records.description: A transferable single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric enables high-quality interfaces with two-dimensional semiconductors, yielding near-ideal switching, low hysteresis and ultra-low-power complementary transistors and inverters.

records.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
records.description: An imaging algorithm using closure-invariant formalism and diffusion-based reconstruction applied to supermassive black hole very long baseline radio interferometry datasets enables independent recovery of the ring-like shadow and mass that is free from the usual calibration and imaging assumptions.

records.title: Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity
records.description: Inhibition of mitochondrial protein import can enhance tumour immunogenicity by promoting mitochondrial DNA release.

records.title: Metasurface waveguides for all-day augmented reality glasses
records.description: An all-day-wearable augmented reality glasses prototype using a dual-layer metasurface-based waveguide and three matched grating patterns achieves a 30° field of view in an 8 × 8-mm 2 two-dimensional eyebox while maintaining high luminance efficiency.

records.title: PhD funding mechanisms should protect the right to disagree with supervisors
A practically perfect plesiosaur
records.description: A very well preserved ancient marine reptile and a Latin poem that describes an optical phenomenon, in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: Chile’s postdoc rules risk driving talent away
Students need AI-free spaces to learn core skills
Why your physics project needs an anthropologist
records.description: Picking a site for an observatory should be about more than science. Humanities scholars have a crucial role in responsible siting.

records.title: California votes to give record $8.4 billion to medical research
records.description: The cash infusion, earmarked for immunology studies, is the largest ever for science authorized by a US public vote — but it has drawn criticism.

records.title: Daily briefing: Where academic freedom is declining — and where it’s on the rise
records.description: Academic freedom is deteriorating globally, but has soared in a few countries in recent years. Plus, testimony from a member of a year-long simulated Mars mission and how key fungal networks could save Mongolia’s iconic grasslands.

records.title: How microbes can secure the critical minerals the world needs
records.description: To sustain supplies of key metals, policymakers should support the infrastructure needed to deploy mining biotechnologies on a large scale.

records.title: Mongolia’s iconic grasslands are in crisis — invisible fungi could help save them
records.description: Clues suggest that underground fungal networks might be key to reviving degraded land and preserving plant biodiversity.

records.title: PhDs worldwide are having a shake up — why now?
records.description: Government-supported initiatives around the globe aim to change the PhD, with the goal of providing fresh talent to the private sector.

records.title: The public trusts scientists with AI — more than it does anyone else
records.description: Public confidence in scientists’ use of generative artificial intelligence remains high, but that trust comes with conditions.

records.title: Metascience should be a source of evidence, not a means of control
records.description: The field has captured the interest of politicians. There are positives — but governments must not misuse the data.

records.title: Some people are resistant to dementia — here’s what their genes can teach us
records.description: For years, researchers have studied people with a genetic predisposition to Alzheimer’s and other dementias. They might have even more to learn from those who don’t get the disease.

records.title: He spent a year on ‘Mars’: NASA science officer emerges from mock mission
records.description: Engineer Matthew Montgomery, who has just finished a 378-day simulated Mars mission, talks about what it was like to be out of contact with the rest of humanity for a two-week blackout.

records.title: The super El Niño is more than a climate shock – it’s a health one, too
records.description: Food shortages and disease outbreaks are to be expected and need to be addressed together.

records.title: How to make failure your friend and teacher in science
records.description: Apprentices develop expertise after doing monotonous tasks repeatedly and learning from their mistakes. Scientists are no different, argues Ruth Morgan.

records.title: Carlo Rovelli says fundamental physics is overrated
records.description: The theoretical physicist unpacks the need for more humility in science and whether artificial intelligence could ever become conscious.

records.title: COP31 kicks off as planet faces imminent overshoot of 1.5 °C climate target
records.description: Scientists say governments must commit to carbon dioxide removal if world is to bring temperatures back down to safer limits.

records.title: Author Correction: Histone H3 trimethylation at lysine 36 guides m 6 A RNA modification co-transcriptionally
AI has transformed maths — this is how we got here
records.description: The story of how maths came to run the world, and created the artificial-intelligence models that might surpass human mathematicians.

records.title: How academic freedom is changing around the world — by the numbers
records.description: Nature reports on five countries where academic freedom has either plummeted or soared in recent years.

records.title: Daily briefing: The ‘overshoot COP’ kicks off
records.description: The COP31 climate conference begins, with ‘climate overshoot’ a key talking point. Plus, the surprising benefits of ‘pink noise’ and the role of AI chatbots to support men’s mental health.

records.title: What postdoc ads ask for and what they leave unsaid
records.description: Looking for a postdoc while raising four children made one thing clear to Wenhuan Xu: many adverts describe the ideal applicant much more clearly than they describe the job itself.

records.title: Medicinal plants, lessons from mushrooms and the power of smell: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: Cholera bacterium’s good deed: inspiring a glue with rare properties
records.description: An adhesive that binds strongly even under water was inspired by a protein made by a feared pathogen.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Meet the snakes that cartwheel away from trouble
records.description: Nature staff discuss an acrobatic reptile defence strategy — plus, evidence of fossilized dinosaur blood cells.

records.title: Cholera bacterium’s good deed: inspiring a glue with rare properties
records.description: An adhesive that binds strongly even under water was inspired by a protein made by a feared pathogen.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Meet the snakes that cartwheel away from trouble
records.description: Nature staff discuss an acrobatic reptile defence strategy — plus, evidence of fossilized dinosaur blood cells.

records.title: Preprint platform offers to pay researchers to review papers, but questions remain
records.description: A reviewer can earn US$200 through XSci’s scheme if they deliver their work within five days.

records.title: Daily briefing: Ancient cave art found hiding in plain sight
records.description: Rock-art in a Spanish cave dates back 26,000 years. Plus, flexible working policies can end up saddling academic mothers with more work and the origins of Celtic and Germanic languages.

records.title: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering
These AI agents design your perfect robot-powered lab — and run it for you
records.description: A team of artificial-intelligence agents simulates a laboratory of robots and instruments to ensure that the physical workspace functions smoothly and then directs that workspace’s operations.

records.title: ‘Mathematics is more than a mechanical process’ — why I think the field will survive OpenAI’s disruption
records.description: Artificial intelligence could take the field into new territory, but researchers must create the rules and institutions that keep humans at its centre.

records.title: ESC (DC) 2
records.description: Security issues.

records.title: The palaeo cave art that hid in plain sight for 26,000 years
records.description: Hundreds of engravings were spotted in a widely visited cave — and some include signs of animation.

records.title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch
Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China
The surprising reason women in academia do more parenting than men
records.description: Policies designed to keep women in the workforce could be entrenching gendered parenting roles.

records.title: Daily briefing: Toothbrush zaps bacteria to clear plaque
records.description: The manual toothbrush cleans by generating a bacteria-killing electrical charge. Plus, what ‘historic’ US mid-term results mean for science and a genetics lab run by AI-powered robots.

records.title: Spider snooze stages
records.description: How similar are vertebrate and invertebrate sleeping behaviours? An analysis of spiders offers insights about how sleep evolved.

records.title: Why not to wait even a few minutes before fleeing a tsunami
records.description: Simulation shows that hesitating can be the difference between making it to safety and not.

records.title: Toothbrush zaps bacteria with electricity that’s made when bristles move
records.description: Innovative polymer could give the manual toothbrush its first radical redesign in more than 1,000 years.

records.title: First-of-its-kind planetary wreckage holds clues to our Solar System’s fate
records.description: Astronomers spot an unprecedented double disk of debris around a dead star.

records.title: A guide to Nature Index tables
records.description: Information on the methodology used in the ranking for the 2026 Nature Spotlight: Neuroscience.

records.title: Ancient DNA charts spread of Celtic and Germanic languages
records.description: Genomes from thousands of ancient individuals show how migrations helped shape Celtic and Germanic languages — plus, how the brain may regulate emotions differently than we thought.

records.title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer
The oracle of the second quadrant
records.description: It all adds up.

records.title: X-ray stopwatch can measure durations of just attoseconds
records.description: The duration of short ångström-wavelength X-ray pulses, which lasted merely 170 attoseconds, has finally been measured accurately. The optical system designed for precision pulse duration metrology can be used as a ‘stopwatch’ to measure the rapid motion of electrons inside atoms and molecules, too.

records.title: Is social media changing children’s brains? Here’s what the science says
records.description: Some countries are introducing sweeping social-media bans for young people, but the impact of screen time is still under investigation.

records.title: ‘Historic change’: what the 2026 US mid-term election results mean for science
records.description: Researchers hope that US lawmakers will push back against the Trump administration’s science policies — but there are limits to what Congress can do.

records.title: How a once-controversial idea is advancing understanding of Parkinson’s disease
records.description: The disease is thought to be divided into two subtypes, depending on where it originates in the body — the gut or the brain.

records.title: Rise of Germanic and Celtic languages is written in ancient DNA
records.description: Thousands of genome sequences identify human migrations that might have spread early forms of these tongues around Europe.

records.title: AI agents enter the ‘wet lab’
records.description: An AI system coordinates laboratory instruments to conduct multi-step molecular-biology experiments with limited human intervention.

records.title: How the brain protects itself from Parkinson’s disease
records.description: Brains are resilient. Harnessing their self-protective mechanisms might help to prevent or slow the progression of this neurodegenerative condition.

records.title: Daily briefing: See a tardigrade shed its skin
records.description: Enjoy the month’s best science images. Plus, an outbreak of anthrax in African hippos and the places where biodiversity drops after humans leave.

records.title: Clearing the way for a transformative stem-cell treatment for Parkinson’s disease
records.description: Most Parkinson’s therapies aim to reduce the motor-control symptoms that the disease triggers. But stem-cell transplants in the brain could alter the disease at a more fundamental level.

records.title: Progress accelerates in Parkinson’s treatments
records.description: Researchers are reporting encouraging results for a disease that affects millions of people worldwide.

records.title: Ecosystems depend on people: don’t abandon them
records.description: It might seem counterproductive to put more people in nature, but sometimes human activity nurtures biodiversity.

records.title: See a tardigrade shed its skin — October’s best science images
records.description: The month’s sharpest science shots, selected by Nature ’s photo team.

records.title: Fruit, flies and getting frisky: how food odours trigger sexual arousal
records.description: Males of a Drosophila species that thrives on a particular fruit need the smell of food to begin courtship. This environmental cue acts on defined mating circuits in the brain.

records.title: Six highlights from Parkinson’s disease research
records.description: Targeting a new network, addressing gait issues and other advances from recent studies.

records.title: Cutting-edge technique uncovers how the spine’s shock absorbers bear load
records.description: An exciting imaging approach reveals how discs of soft tissue in the spine respond to compressive force at the micrometre and nanometre scales.

records.title: Epileptic seizures nearly vanish after people receive experimental gene therapy in their brains
records.description: A clinical trial in three people tested a combination of gene-laden viruses and a drug.

records.title: A death sentence for ‘sloppy’ cancers
records.description: The process of making protein from RNA can go awry in cancer cells. This malfunction might be harnessed to create an effective gene-therapy tool that targets tumours.

records.title: Faint exoplanets detected using computational approach to remove glare from stars
records.description: An image-processing framework for detecting exoplanets directly has been developed. The technique overcomes the telescope-stability barrier that has limited previous methods, reveals fainter exoplanets than other approaches can detect and could make imaging exo-Earths easier for future observatories.

records.title: People’s social networks can be unintentionally reshaped during randomized interventions
records.description: A re-examination of a randomized controlled trial for a health-advice intervention reveals ripple effects and altered relationships in communities in rural Honduras.

records.title: Fine-tuning brain stimulation to fight Parkinson’s disease
records.description: Neuroscientists are developing a new type of brain implant that will decode every movement and symptom of people with this neurodegenerative condition, seeking better ways to ease symptoms.

records.title: Mysterious anthrax outbreak kills hippos in Africa — raising concerns for human spread
records.description: The latest cases, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, come as the country grapples with ongoing Ebola and cholera outbreaks.

records.title: Why nature collapses when people leave the countryside
records.description: For decades, conservation has worried about the risks of too many people. In some places, depopulation is the real threat.

records.title: Could chemicals contribute to Parkinson’s?
records.description: Researchers and advocates point to pollutants as a trigger for the neurodegenerative condition.

records.title: Replacing the neurons that Parkinson’s destroys
records.description: After decades of work, researchers have begun trialling transplants of dopamine neurons into people with the neurodegenerative disease — with early signs of success.

records.title: Why are we conscious? Nature investigates the theories
records.description: Scientists have yet to reveal how the human brain produces the subjective experience we perceive as consciousness, but research has pushed the field in exciting directions.

records.title: Infrared image detectors grown directly on read-out chips
records.description: A film of lead sulfide — an infrared-sensitive semiconductor — has been grown directly on a circuit that can read out the material’s electrical signal through an approach called monolithic in situ integration. This brings material growth and electronic integration together into a single step. The resulting image sensor shows high sensitivity for infrared wavelengths.

records.title: A two-dimensional reticular triaxial molecularly woven fabric
records.description: A two-dimensional reticular triaxial woven network material is constructed by incorporating C 3 -symmetric macrocycles into a triangular weave pattern, enabling an extra topological dimension to be used for the construction of functional materials.

records.title: Accelerating commercialization and deployment of indoor photovoltaics
records.description: Recent progress in photovoltaics has been investigated to translate state-of-the-art cells in the laboratory into deployable products suited to real indoor conditions, focusing on wide-bandgap absorbers, reduced non-radiative voltage losses and reshaping module design.

records.title: In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs
records.description: Using high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double knockout screening, synergistic gene combinations to improve CAR-T cell therapy are revealed.

records.title: Observation of prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting
records.description: A programmable neutral-atom quantum simulator is used to explore quench dynamics in spin models with up to 180 qubits, revealing prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting.

records.title: Ecological and social cues orchestrate concerted courtship in Drosophila
records.description: In Drosophila erecta , food odours initiate male sexual arousal, which is subsequently reinforced by the visual motion of other courting flies, creating a multisensory mechanism that synchronizes courtship in groups when conditions are favourable for reproduction.

records.title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations
records.description: AutoDNA is an artificial intelligence (AI)-native autonomous biomolecular engineering laboratory targeting multi-objective experiments across diverse instruments, realizing the co-evolution of AI and the automation system within an end-to-end multi-user framework.

records.title: Multimodal X-ray imaging reveals hierarchical fibre mechanics
records.description: The X-ray visualization platform TomoSAXS, demonstrated here on intervertebral spinal discs, can visualize nanoscale to macroscale mechanics in intact biological organs and fibrous materials.

records.title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
records.description: Using deuterium as a proxy for hydrogen, atom probe tomography provides experimental evidence for interstitial hydrogen in solid solution across different FCC phases, consistent with theoretical predictions of hydrogen affinity, revealing hydrogen partitioning in structural alloys.

records.title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity
records.description: Multi-omic analyses of cells from patients with glioblastoma (GB) provide insight into the role of non-genetic cellular plasticity in disease progression, showing that state stability in GB cells is controlled by a network of interacting activators and repressors.

records.title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
records.description: A high-throughput CRISPR-interference platform allows the mapping of interactions between essential genes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis , revealing many previously unknown genetic interactions and providing insight into gene function and drug–target relationships that could enable the development of new therapies for tuberculosis.

records.title: Conjugation-regulated self-assembled molecules for tandem solar cells
records.description: Rationally engineered molecular spatial conjugation is used for the formation of highly ordered, conformal self-assembled molecules, enabling the fabrication of high-performance perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.

records.title: Hard X-ray attosecond metrology
records.description: Metrology techniques are developed to characterize and control attosecond hard X-ray pulses, directly measuring a 170-attosecond duration and enabling ultrafast studies of electronic dynamics in quantum systems.

records.title: Cancer-selective gene circuits via intrinsic ribosomal frameshifting
records.description: Codon-pair-dependent ribosomal frameshifting is a feature of translational dysregulation in cancer cells.

records.title: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics
records.description: Genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals are analysed, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which alternative archaeological and linguistic models for the origin and spread of Celtic fit reconstructed demographic histories.

records.title: Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling
records.description: Longitudinal tracking of endothelial cells shows they can adapt to loss of VEGFR2 and form new functional vessels, challenging conventional views of the essential role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and providing insight into resistance to anti-VEGF therapies.

records.title: The neural basis of flavour–nutrient learning
