records.description: A dopamine pathway to the basolateral amygdala is necessary for associating nutrients with flavours.

records.title: Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells
records.description: Nectin-4 is identified as a pivotal host entry receptor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of rubella virus.

records.title: Aggression experience and observation drive shared behavioural and neural changes
records.description: Aggression experience and observation recruit a brain-wide network of excitatory, inhibitory and valence signals, and changes to this activation pattern predict a shared adaptive behaviour-control policy in a new aggression context.

records.title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism
records.description: Gene network analysis shows how mutations in diverse genes associated with autism spectrum disorder can converge to exert shared effects, with X-linked transcription factor ZFX emerging as a key protective factor in the female brain.

records.title: The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity
records.description: Continental-scale uplift and subsidence associated with long-wavelength dynamic topography due to mantle convection drove the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity.

records.title: Twist-angle-dependent quantum phase diagrams in moiré bilayer MoTe 2
records.description: Twist-angle-dependent studies of moiré bilayer MoTe 2 reveal a transition from fractional topological states to correlated insulators and superconductivity, linking topology, symmetry breaking and magnetism in moiré quantum materials.

records.title: An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
records.description: structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model pre-trained on 21 million sequence–structure pairs, learns multimodal representations that improve secondary and tertiary structure prediction, functional inference and zero-shot generalization across diverse RNA families.

records.title: Synergy in viral–bacterial co-infection expedites algal bloom demise
records.description: Viral–bacterial synergy accelerates algal bloom collapse by enhancing virus-induced mortality, driven by Alteromonas chemoattraction and co-infection, revealing a previously unrecognized mortality agent that influences oceanic carbon cycling .

records.title: A conserved flowering-time module underlies double-season cropping
records.description: The genomic footprints of 80 years of modern breeding in China are traced using representative cultivars, demonstrating how precision genome editing can be used to reconstruct adaptive modules for climate-resilient crop design.

records.title: Microbiome-wide PheWAS links gut microbial SNVs to health and exposures
records.description: Gut microbial single-nucleotide variants across 10,781 individuals reveal 940 associations that link strain-level genetic variation to 69 host traits, with structural analyses pinpointing host phenotype-associated variants, providing a base pair-resolution resource for mechanistic hypothesis generation.

records.title: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory underlies glioblastoma heterogeneity
records.description: A deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma is generated, pairing transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling, and tracing glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity to a stereotyped and spatially patterned trajectory of cancer cells.

records.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
records.description: A new physics-based method combining the use of automatic differentiation to optimize millions of model parameters with a flexible physical model is described for starlight subtraction from real, on-sky coronagraphic images to greatly improve sensitivity.

records.title: Whence dragons?
records.description: The ecology and evolution of winged legendary beasts, and monkeys that show their behinds to their buddies, in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: Research bonuses need clear and fair rules

Universities must measure learning, both with and without AI assistance
China should share the evidence behind animal-testing alternatives openly
Historic Marburg outbreak hints at long-term viral hideout
records.description: Sequencing of Marburg virus collected during Ethiopia’s first outbreak suggests that the pathogen is lurking in East and Central Africa.

records.title: Will AI grant reviews make science more conservative?
records.description: Researchers are questioning whether outsourcing decisions about research funding to artificial intelligence will reduce scientific novelty.

records.title: Trump’s executive order on women’s health feels like déjà vu
records.description: Previous US administrations fell short on promised improvements to women’s-health research — here’s what real change will take.

records.title: Cities are changing — and architects must adapt
records.description: Climate change is reshaping urban environments. Architect Carlo Ratti tells Nature that technology offers solutions, but citizens must get the final say.

records.title: How democracy depends on science — and must protect it
records.description: Verified information from trusted experts is crucial to help the public and governments navigate rapid changes and increasing complexity.

records.title: Chinese doctoral students in clinical medicine can graduate without a thesis — more degrees to follow
records.description: Postgraduate students studying professional medicine degrees can qualify with a ‘practical achievement’.

records.title: This cholesterol drug promised to be a game-changer. Why did it flop in the clinic — and is there still hope?
records.description: Physicians were excited about several therapies that slash levels of lipoprotein(a) — an important cardiovascular risk factor. One major trial failed to show a benefit, and now scientists are scrambling to work out what that means.

records.title: Biotech firms are meant to pay to use Earth’s genetic data. They’re not.
records.description: Global leaders at the COP17 biodiversity summit complained that companies using public genetic data are not paying into a voluntary fund to protect nature.

records.title: Daily briefing: Why science is the backbone of democracy
records.description: Seven leading researchers set out three pillars by which science enables democracy. Plus, how researchers are probing neurons like never before and a debate over fossilized red blood cells.

records.title: Why we’re setting up an institute for radically broad thinking
records.description: The scale of today’s challenges demands a fresh approach — across all disciplines. Here’s how we’re making space for researchers to generate new ideas.

records.title: US social sciences face existential crisis after NSF cuts
records.description: The US National Science Foundation is a major funder of economics and archaeology research but in 2026 awarded no new grants in those disciplines.

records.title: Nature awards recognize inspiring women in science
records.description: This year’s winners are a materials scientist and a champion of women’s science education. They — like all those shortlisted — are driven by the desire to support others.

records.title: Author Correction: mTORC1 drives cell-autonomous astrocyte reactivity in tuberous sclerosis

records.title: Daily briefing: ‘A triumph of scientific self-correction’

records.title: Earth’s resources sustain humanity — but they come at a high price
records.description: Two books explore the damage caused by our unsustainable extraction of raw materials.

records.title: What tech entrepreneurs can teach scientists about failure
records.description: Start-up founders routinely talk about their failed companies. Academia could learn from them, says Mary Ryan.

records.title: Iranian scientists in the United States face major upheaval
records.description: Pressures due to the continuing US–Iran conflict are mounting as early-career researchers endure frozen immigration status, employment limbo and families caught in the war.

records.title: Five overlooked steps to identify new epidemics, fast
records.description: Current measures to track emerging epidemics have a key limitation: they don’t work if the disease causes unusual or unexpected symptoms.

records.title: Meet Neuropixels: how probes that track hundreds of brain cells at once are revolutionizing neuroscience
records.description: From rodents to humans, tools that enable large-scale, single-cell neuronal recordings are exposing the inner workings of the brain.

records.title: In Indonesia, PhD students blow the whistle on bad supervision
records.description: The nation plans to boost the number of doctoral candidates, but some early-career researchers warn of systemic challenges, including poor-quality supervision.

records.title: How researchers debunked ‘race science’: ‘a triumph of scientific self-correction’
records.description: An account of how nineteenth-century studies aiming to find a biological basis for human races were dismantled by good scientific practices — although their effects are still felt today.

records.title: ‘A perfect scientist, a perfect mum’: researchers mourn two biologists’ deaths in Spanish train crash
records.description: Scientists pay tribute to Marta Shahbazi Alonso and Tamara González Costa, who died on their way to a developmental-biology meeting.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Dog years: could longevity science extend your pets' lives?
records.description: Nature staff discuss the emerging field of pet longevity — plus, a researcher decides not to care about their student reviews. Are they wrong?

records.title: Author Correction: Rh 3+ stabilized in KRh@MFI catalyses regioselective hydroformylation

records.description: Researchers say his portrayal of the Star Trek character represented curiosity, thoughtfulness and an effort to understand others.

records.title: Daily briefing: How Captain Picard inspired today’s scientists
records.description: Researchers pay tribute to actor Patrick Stewart. Plus, what the US mid-term elections might mean for science and why ancient people never settled in the centre of the lush ‘Green Arabia’.

records.title: Somewhere over the transcontinental burrito tunnel
records.description: Pipe dreams.

records.title: I built the UK government’s metascience unit — here’s what countries need to know
records.description: To find evidence-backed ways to improve grant-funding processes, metascientists need freedom and money to experiment, as well as leaders who are willing to make change.

records.title: Record-breaking retraction: scholarly publisher pulls 1,400 conference papers on one day
records.description: Announcement by IEEE follows publication of a study showing the retracted papers are linked to paper mills.

records.title: Are dinosaur fossils hogging top journals? Analysis sparks debate over ‘charismatic’ finds
records.description: Fossils of dinosaurs, mammals and other glamorous species are over-represented in high-profile titles, suggests a study of thousands of palaeontology papers.

records.title: Even stupendous black holes can’t explain dark matter
records.description: The theoretical objects would have left a larger imprint on cosmic radiation if they were a source of the invisible force pulling together the galaxies.

records.title: Daily briefing: The three red flags of suspicious journals
records.description: These warning signs suggest a journal might be engaging in dubious publishing activities. Plus, the brain clears out faulty neurons at birth and whether a giant ‘sunshade’ could cool Earth.

records.title: How the US mid-term elections could shake up science
records.description: A Democratic victory in Congress could halt the Trump administration’s controversial grant-review plan and curb some of its funding actions.

records.title: Switchable Chlorine Atom Transfer Radical Reactions

Why did ancient humans avoid this lush paradise
records.description: A new expedition into the Rub’ al Khali desert finds no evidence of ancient human settlement.

records.title: This Arabian desert was once a lush paradise. Why did ancient humans avoid it?
records.description: Expedition revealed that water wasn’t enough for human settlement — plus, proposals to block sunlight get serious.

records.title: Accounting of Africa’s water reveals a management gap
records.description: A map of Africa’s water demand reveals that the scarcity of water is only part of the problem facing the continent — management is a separate challenge.

records.title: The brain liquidates billions of mutant neurons around the time we’re born
records.description: Faulty neurons can contribute to various neurological conditions, but researchers have uncovered a system that might clean them up.

records.title: Daily briefing: The big push to personalize psychiatry
records.description: A data-driven approach could match treatments to individuals with more precision. Plus, funders in Europe are backing preprint-led publishing and whether professors should care about student evaluations.

records.title: What students think about my teaching doesn’t matter. Am I wrong?
records.description: A jury weighs in on whether teaching assessments are popularity contests or an important tool.

records.title: How personalization and psychedelics are revitalizing psychiatry
records.description: Fresh ideas are welcome in a discipline in which progress is rare — provided they are applied rigorously.

records.title: Lactate takes a shortcut into mitochondria to power the heart
records.description: A cellular fuel called lactate is channelled directly into energy-generating organelles in heart muscle, defying the prevailing view about lactate transport.

records.title: Clues about complex life come from freshly cultivated archaea
records.description: Two archaeal strains that belong to a lineage closely related to the ancestor of eukaryotic cells (complex cells with membrane-bound organelles) have been brought into culture. Their simple internal organization, elaborate surface structures, microbial partnerships and protein-dependent lifestyle provide clues about how eukaryotic cells arose.

records.title: Preprint-centric publishing model gets major boost
records.description: European funders put weight behind emerging ‘publish, review, curate’ approach for preprints.

records.title: These three red flags could unmask dodgy journals
records.description: As poor publishing practices proliferate, scholarly databases are under pressure to ensure the titles they list are reputable.

records.title: Is research funding now a lottery? Elite funder ERC swamped by applications
records.description: A marked rise in submissions for the European Research Council’s grants is pushing down success rates.

records.title: Dengue comes back even in vaccinated people — new clues
records.description: Researchers help to answer a question dogging the development of improved vaccines against the mosquito-borne disease.

records.title: The grand plan to transform psychiatry — by personalizing mental-health care
records.description: Could a blood sample, a brain scan and a look at your phone data transform how your psychiatrist treats you?

records.title: Could a giant sunshade in space ‘solve global warming’? Scientists are taking the idea seriously
records.description: Some say the concept is complete fantasy, but a detailed analysis suggests that the falling cost of rocket launches might make it feasible in a few decades.

records.title: An unexpected function of a cell-cycle enzyme might explain the toxic effects of its inhibitors
records.description: A previously unknown mechanism required for cells to start proliferating has been identified. A combination of mathematical modelling and cell-based experiments shows that the enzyme WEE1 switches off a protein-degradation complex to allow cell proliferation to start, with implications for WEE1 inhibitors currently in trials for cancer treatments.

records.title: Meta-study sparks questions about what it means to be good at regulating emotions
records.description: A first-of-its kind consortium reveals a lack of correlation between behavioural and neural measures of a person’s emotional regulation.

records.title: How the pandemic changed trust in science — in four charts
records.description: The largest analysis of its kind reveals the public’s changing relationship with science and the people who do it.

records.title: Genetic variants that alter gene regulation in specific cell types are closely tied to disease
records.description: Single-cell profiling of nearly 2,000 people brings scientists closer to understanding the link between genetic variation, gene expression and health.

records.title: Ribbon made of carbon pentagons and heptagons has metallic properties
records.description: Ribbons that are composed exclusively of five- and seven-carbon rings have metal-like electron transport and conductance. The ribbons can be synthesized by linking previously inaccessible chains of paired five-membered rings, providing a route to making highly conducting carbon nanoribbons.

records.title: Where have all the saucers flown?
records.description: Missed encounters.

records.title: The shifting sands of research independence: why mid-career scientists crave security
records.description: A project to improve understanding of an often-neglected group in academia aims to help its members to navigate career uncertainty.

records.title: Stone and water governed early human settlement of the desert
records.description: A geoarchaeological survey of the Rub’ al Khali (the Empty Quarter of Arabia) and spatial modelling of the Arabian Peninsula suggest that human settlement tracked the co-occurrence of water and stone suitable for making tools, rather than water alone.

records.title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury
records.description: A subset of necrotizing enterocolitis in infants is mediated specifically by the Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin.

records.title: Tandem repeat variation shapes immune cell type-specific gene expression
records.description: Whole-genome sequencing and cell-level gene expression measurements show that length variation in tandem repeats in the human genome contributes to cell type-specific differences in gene regulation and expression, as well as the architecture of complex traits.

records.title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking
records.description: Computational simulations of a neural network based on fly connectomes identify a three-neuron circuit that is organized to produce leg motor rhythms for walking.

records.title: Narrow carbon pentaheptite nanoribbon as a covalent metal
records.description: Planar carbon pentaheptite nanoribbons are synthesized by laterally fusing polypentalene chains transformed from pre-synthesized polycyclooctadiene chains, suggesting a possible route towards carbon quantum wires.

records.title: Molecular underpinnings of rheumatic diseases and emerging therapeutic concepts
records.description: Improved molecular insights into inflammatory rheumatic diseases are enabling better disease control and advancing the field towards achieving durable remission and eventual cure.

records.title: Subcycle videography of Landau–Zener–Majorana transitions in graphene
records.description: An experimental concept enabling attosecond-precision, subcycle band-structure videography covering the entire first Brillouin zone is demonstrated and used to visualize the lightwave-driven electron motion of Landau–Zener–Majorana transitions in graphene.

records.title: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory
records.description: Dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory.

records.title: T and B cells recognize splicing-derived neutrophil neoantigens in lupus
records.description: In systemic lupus erythematosus, aberrant splicing in neutrophils generates novel peptides that are presented on MHC I, driving CD4 + and CD8 + T cell activation, clonal expansion and IgG autoantibody responses, establishing neoantigen-driven autoimmune immunity.

records.title: Rare and common genetic variants shape single-cell immune gene expression
records.description: Phase 1 of TenK10K takes single-cell RNA sequencing and matched whole-genome sequencing data from 1,925 individuals, enabling detection of associations for common and rare genetic variants, the latter of which have been uncharacterized in their impact on cell-specific gene expression.

records.title: Tracing the spread of Germanic languages using ancient genomics
records.description: Analysis of newly sequenced and previously published ancient human genomes identifies migrations associated with the spread of the Germanic language group, from its arrival in Scandinavia 4,000 years ago, through to its diversification during the historical period.

records.title: Emotion regulation capacity lacks a shared neural signature
records.description: Sensorimotor and amygdala activation, but not canonical prefrontal control circuits, indicate emotion regulation capacity.

records.title: Tumour assembloids recapitulate tumour–CAF–T cell crosstalk in renal cancer
records.description: Tumour assembloids, which model components of human renal cell carcinoma, including cancer cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts and tumour-infiltrating immune cells, are used to identify an essential pathway that mediates heterogeneous therapeutic responses.

records.title: MCT1-dependent mitochondrial lactate import sustains cardiac metabolism
records.description: In mouse myocardium, glucose oxidation persists in the absence of the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier, with mitochondrial MCT1 importing lactate into mitochondria and LDHB oxidizing it to pyruvate and NADH, sustaining cardiac energetics and preventing stress-induced heart failure.

records.title: Eukaryotes’ closest relatives are internally simple syntrophic peptidotrophic archaea
records.description: Cultures reveal conservation of cell structure, physical symbioses and anaerobiosis across Heimdallarchaeia (the archaeal lineage that branches closest to eukaryotes) and other Promethearchaeota.

records.title: Monolithically and in situ integrated PbS infrared imagers
records.description: A method for growing infrared image sensors directly from solution using raw materials by monolithic in situ integration of high-performance semiconductor PbS photodetectors on readout integrated circuits is described, yielding films with excellent electronic properties.

records.title: Time-reversal-symmetry-breaking spin injection from a compensated magnet
records.description: Experiments show that altermagnetic Mn 5 Si 3 generates spin currents despite zero net magnetization, demonstrating a central prediction of altermagnetic spintronics.

records.title: A single-molecule spin–photon interface
records.description: A triplet carbene molecule in a tailored crystal provides a stable single-molecule spin–photon interface with millisecond coherence, advancing chemically engineered molecular qubits for quantum networking.

records.title: Presynaptic homeostasis mediated by exocytosis of a SNARE protein
records.description: Experiments show that when subjected to high-frequency stimulation, excitatory neurons exhibit a presynaptic form of homeostatic plasticity mediated by the exocytosis of v-SNARE protein VAMP7 and the resulting inhibition of P/Q-type calcium channels.

records.title: Spatial and sectoral water demand assessment for the African continent
records.description: Africa-wide water demand analysis across six sectors in 2020 shows that in specific regions of northern and southern Africa, the current water demand exceeds water availability.

records.title: Alzheimer’s disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation
records.description: A multi-ancestry study of Alzheimer’s disease identifies new risk loci and potential drug targets, implicates microglia and neurons, and reveals a larger common-variant contribution than previously estimated.

records.title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk
records.description: Single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling identifies cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific genetic effects that link non-coding variants to immune disease risk.

records.title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers
records.description: Pharmacological inhibition of the m 7 G methyltransferase METTL1 in vivo impairs tumour growth and substantially prolongs survival in multiple mouse cancer models of different tissue origin.

records.title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk
records.description: Single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling identifies cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific genetic effects that link non-coding variants to immune disease risk.

records.title: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers
records.description: Pharmacological inhibition of the m 7 G methyltransferase METTL1 in vivo impairs tumour growth and substantially prolongs survival in multiple mouse cancer models of different tissue origin.

records.title: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin
records.description: Loss of function of canonical BAF induces gain of CTCF and cohesin binding that alters 3D genome architecture and reprograms transcription.

records.description: Therapy pioneered by Chinese biotechnology firm HuidaGene showed promise in animals but caused a fatal reaction in a child.

records.title: Why pharma firms are betting billions on psychedelic drugs despite setbacks
records.description: Regulatory pushback stalled the field. But researchers are optimistic about mind-altering drugs as potential treatments for depression and mood disorders.

records.title: Revered NASA spacecraft is about to perish in flames — astronomers are mourning
records.description: A failed rescue mission means that the Swift observatory will fall into Earth’s atmosphere next week, but it leaves behind a massive archive of data for scientists to explore.

records.title: Could measuring immune health reshape medical care?
records.description: Finding practical ways to analyse the state of a person’s immune system could guide treatment decisions and create opportunities for disease prevention.

records.title: Mysterious flickering brain signals could help to unlock secrets of consciousness
records.description: Monkeys’ brain activity flips 15 times per second between patterns linked to objects of which the monkeys are aware and patterns for objects outside their awareness.

records.title: Global climate body fights for survival: why the IPCC must be saved

records.title: Can scientists reliably tell if a novel is written using AI?

records.title: Evolutionary ‘game-changer’: weird armoured amphibian lived in ancient seas
records.description: The creature’s armour cladding probably enabled it to tolerate the salty seas of the Late Triassic.

records.title: The Selfish Gene , 50 years on — it’s time for an update
records.description: A focus on the gene alone has become outdated. Books that capture the complexity of life deserve centre stage.

records.title: Mentoring a lab colleague? Share your ‘CV of failures’ with them
records.description: Melanie Stefan became a ‘poster child of failure’ after writing an article about it. Now she urges senior colleagues to be more open about career setbacks.

records.title: Brazil election: many scientists relieved as Lula wins surprise victory
records.description: Scientific organizations in Brazil had rallied around Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who defied expectations to defeat his opponent in a run-off.

records.title: Sleep declines in rural communities after electricity arrives
records.description: Scientists tracked the changing sleep patterns of Indigenous people in Argentina who gained access to mains electricity — and smart phones.

records.title: Surprise! White dwarf stars come in a rainbow of colours

records.title: To heal sick cities, scientists and residents must work together

records.title: An AI tool improves weather forecasts up to a month ahead

records.title: Teen depression and anxiety predicted by childhood brain development

records.title: Using AI to offer personalized health advice

records.title: Global emissions slow — but world hurtles towards 2 °C of warming

records.title: Huge mapping study reveals how your brain tracks what your body is feeling
records.description: Signals in the insula region, deep in the brain, can make people feel hot, tingly and nauseous.

records.title: Plastics embedded with enzymes degrade readily in the sea
records.description: Embedding enzymes that break down ester bonds into compostable polyesters enables rapid and complete biodegradation even in microbe-scarce environments. This method is effective in marine sites ranging from coastal sea water to the deep sea, and could therefore contribute towards solving the global plastic pollution problem.

records.title: This is what the mysterious Denisovans looked like
records.description: Archaeologists identified skull fragments from China as belonging to this group of ancient human relatives.

records.title: Can plants defend coasts against storms?
records.description: Salt-marsh plants can protect inland areas against huge waves — but seemingly only up to a point, and big storms cause progressive damage.

records.title: Worms live longer in cool conditions thanks to a muscle-derived molecule
records.description: In nematodes, a metabolite induced by the cold links low temperatures to a body-wide signal that promotes longevity. This signalling system is also seen in human cells.

records.title: Daily briefing: How tech billionaires are changing science funding

records.title: Cave stalagmites document global patterns in monsoon rainfall over the past 450,000 years
records.description: A 450,000-year stalagmite record of rainfall in the Amazon Basin , combined with existing Asian records, shows that the global monsoon system has oscillated regularly, strengthening in one hemisphere while weakening in the other. However, during intervals of warmth and warming climate, monsoons in both hemispheres failed for millennia.

records.title: Large-scale single crystals printed layer by layer
records.description: A 3D-printing method has made single crystals of metals and alloys in complex shapes and up to one metre in length, as needed for advanced technological applications.

records.title: A single antimatter particle in a cage opens door to ‘revolutionary’ physics
records.description: Physicists trap and cool down positron for months to measure its ‘magnetic moment’ with extraordinary precision.

records.title: Robert Williamson obituary: geneticist who mapped genes for muscular dystrophy and cystic fibrosis
records.description: Researcher and policy adviser who championed tests and treatments for genetic diseases.

records.title: Fabric user interface can be worn on your sleeve — and machine-washed
records.description: Touch-sensitive, light-emitting yarn can turn everyday clothing into washable, bendable user interfaces with dynamic graphics and versatile computing functions.

records.title: How tech billionaires are disrupting biomedical science
records.description: Money from the world’s increasingly prosperous technology entrepreneurs has been flooding into biomedical research. Is it changing how science is done?

records.title: How a new wave of science philanthropists can have the greatest impact
records.description: Tech entrepreneurs are bringing an engineer’s eye to research funding. They must be open about their findings to reap maximum benefit.

records.title: Multimodal precision diagnostics in clinical xenotransplantation
records.description: Now that hyperacute rejection of pig xenografts can be reliably prevented, subtler immune-mediated graft injuries have emerged that conventional diagnostics often miss; a multimodal precision diagnostic framework is proposed to detect these injuries earlier, guide personalized immunosuppression and inform future gene editing strategies.

records.title: The contribution of salt marshes to wave attenuation during extreme storms
records.description: Salt marsh platforms resist erosion under extreme waves, but vegetation damage reduces wave attenuation; substantial wave attenuation by vegetation is mainly limited to low-energy marsh coasts with waves below 1 m.

records.title: Zeolite-catalysed olefin carbonylation based on tuning spatial confinement
records.description: The use of zeolites with an appropriate pore structure combined with a high CO/olefin ratio is shown to catalyse olefin carbonylation and produce primary and secondary carboxylic acids as the main products.

records.title: Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis
records.description: A multi-tissue signalling system links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans.

records.title: WEE1 opposes APC/C CDH1 activity to promote S phase entry
records.description: Experimental and modelling data indicate that WEE1 promotes re-entry of quiescent cells into the cell cycle, potentially explaining the toxic side effects of WEE1 inhibitors in cancer therapies.

records.title: A single archaeon couples long-chain fatty acid oxidation to methanogenesis
records.description: Methanoglobus dolicholipophagus AA-75 is a thermophilic archaeon isolated from a Chinese petroleum reservoir that converts methanol into methane, carbon dioxide and acetate, and uses saturated and unsaturated fatty acids to produce methane.

records.title: An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root
records.description: An environment-regulated state is identified across multiple cell types at the root tip, revealing a shared dichotomy between cells with and without this state.

records.title: CD51 delineates functionally distinct astrocyte subtypes in neural circuits
records.description: CD51 + astrocytes promote synapse formation in the developing cortex, circuit plasticity in the hippocampus and circuit remodelling after stroke.

records.title: Persistent neuronal stress signalling underlies Angelman syndrome phenotypes
records.description: Genetic and proteomic analyses in human neurons and mouse models of Angelman syndrome (AS) show that loss of the ubiquitin ligase UBE3A leads to an overabundance of asparagine synthetase, and that this is linked with many AS phenotypes.

records.title: Structural basis for protocadherin-1 recognition by New World hantaviruses
records.description: The structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike defines the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition.

records.title: GRP75-dependent SIMPA mediates inter-organellar quality control
records.description: Proteotoxic stress drives formation of GRP75-dependent protein aggregates that signal through mitochondria–ER contact sites to activate targeted quality-control pathways, enabling selective clearance of damaged proteins and preserving mitochondrial integrity.

records.title: Programmable design of functional proteins from natural language
records.description: Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter artificial intelligence model, designs functional proteins from natural-language descriptions, demonstrating experimentally validated activities and improved CO 2 -fixation product yields without iterative optimization.

records.description: The structure of PCDH1 bound to the ANDV spike defines the structural determinants of hantavirus–receptor recognition.

records.title: Programmable design of functional proteins from natural language

records.title: Octupole-driven spin torque switching of antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions
records.description: All-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions can display both a large TMR and a reciprocal switching effect, octupole-driven spin-transfer torque, enabling nanoscale magnetic memory and potentially room-temperature terahertz spintronic devices.

records.title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts
records.description: Fifteen years of atmospheric CO 2 measurements show that the Amazon carbon sink is weakening, with fires, deforestation and climate stress driving increasingly high carbon emissions.

records.title: The proteome of Middle Pleistocene Xujiayao and common Denisovan morphology
records.description: Denisovans from the Xujiayao and other East Asian sites are morphologically distinctive, with a low cranial profile with near-parallel lateral walls, a massive supraorbital torus, a flat zygomaxillary region and weak prognathism.

records.title: Functional architecture of the human insula
records.description: A functional architecture of the human insula links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience.

records.title: Touch-sensing digital pixel fibre enables interactive garment GUI
records.description: Multifunctional digital fibres integrate display, touch sensing, computation and multimodal input–output, enabling flexible, washable garments with interactive graphical interfaces and wireless multimedia capabilities.

records.title: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators
records.description: Climate-driven drought and prey decline triggered lynx predation on raptors, reducing raptor fitness and abundance and producing cascading effects across lower trophic levels.

records.title: Additive manufacturing of ultralong and architected single crystals
records.description: A free-form additive manufacturing method that uses alternating and pulsed heat inputs is described for fabricating metre-tall, centimetre-diameter single crystals of Ti-6Al-4V, as well as hard-to-process refractory metals, including W, Mo, Nb and MoNb alloys.

records.title: Enzyme-embedded polyesters for accelerated biodegradation in the deep sea
records.description: Near-complete deep-sea degradation of enzyme-embedded compostable polyesters shows that thermal enzyme embedding greatly accelerates breakdown across marine environments while preserving material performance, offering a promising strategy to mitigate persistent ocean plastic pollution.

records.title: The anatomy of a personal health agent
records.description: A multi-agent framework that coordinates data science, medical reasoning and health coaching over longitudinal wearable and clinical data to provide holistic personal health support is described.

records.title: Is it ‘moon-stroke’, or a chill?
records.description: An explanation for the injurious effect of sleeping in the moonlight, and a proponent of all-electronic televisions, in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: Bundle water safeguards into critical-mineral licences
Nobel-prizewinning breakthroughs can emerge from neglected organisms
Conservation planning should follow animal clocks
Europe and the rest of the world must come up with an answer to US science strategy
Butterfly wing patterns make motion hard to read
records.description: Movement can expose camouflaged prey, yet whether colour patterns help moving prey to avoid capture is a long-standing puzzle. Butterfly wings might offer an answer.

records.title: Nature ’s job-satisfaction survey highlights the changing geography of science
records.description: A higher proportion of scientists in China and India report feeling optimistic about the future than in the United States and several European countries.

records.title: Will this sleep-disorder drug be the next big blockbuster?
records.description: Orexin agonists have been approved for the treatment of a type of narcolepsy, yet they could also treat conditions across the health spectrum.

records.title: Daily Briefing: Tiny doses of LSD seem to boost cognition
records.description: The drug improved the ability to focus — but only in women. Plus, US climate scientists are facing a deluge of public-records requests and why a sleep-disorder drug might be the next big blockbuster.

records.title: Can a human survive in a whale’s belly? The science behind the thriller Whalefall
records.description: Nature spoke with marine and anatomy specialists about the ‘modern-day Jonah’ film. Warning: spoilers ahead.

records.title: It’s time to teach peer review as a core research skill
records.description: Preprint journal clubs offer a scalable way to make peer-review training a routine part of scientific education.

records.title: Vast new fossil record challenges story of Earth’s ‘big five’ mass extinctions
records.description: An artificial-intelligence model trained on nearly four million fossils suggests that three of the extinction events might have happened more gradually than previously thought.

records.title: China picks first researchers for 15-year mega grants
records.description: Scientists start with a five-year grant that could be extended for another ten years.

records.title: Body-clock disruptions contribute to one in four cases of depression, suggests large study
records.description: Evidence grows for ‘circadian depression’, but more evidence is needed to change diagnosis and treatment guidelines.

records.title: Nepal’s disaster is an urgent wake-up call
records.description: Record-breaking avalanches and floods are signs of things to come. Scientists must evaluate and respond to growing risks in mountain regions.

records.title: Toxic chemicals in fentanyl revealed by speedy technique
records.description: Chemical fingerprinting charts the rises and declines of specific adulterants in illicit supplies of the drug.

records.title: Light and mirrors move large quantum computers closer to reality
records.description: Scientists improve photon-collecting device that could be used to connect multiple quantum-computing arrays.

records.title: Audio long read: How to stay smart in the age of AI — the science of critical thinking
records.description: Although worries are growing about AI's potential to blunt reasoning skills, research has uncovered ways to keep the brain sharp.

records.title: US government probe into postdoc visas worries scientists
records.description: The administration says that the universities being investigated are using the visas to undercut wages for US nationals, but researchers say that restricting international applications could harm science.

records.title: Microdosing LSD shows some cognitive benefits — but only for women
records.description: Different effects of low-dose psychedelics on sustained attention in women and men deserve further investigation.

records.title: How pregnancy reshapes the brain throughout life
records.description: Neuroscience is mapping changes in the brain during pregnancy. What they mean for future health is yet to be pinned down.

records.title: Climate scientists face deluge of public-records requests about fossil-fuel studies
records.description: A Nature investigation identified more than 30 requests since 2024 to US universities in a campaign questioning climate attribution science.

records.title: ‘Fiercely stubborn’: the US scientists continuing their research amid funding cuts
records.description: Researchers working on climate change, diversity, transgender health and international aid have turned to lawsuits, private donors and alternative topics to keep their projects going.

records.title: Experienced researchers ‘disrupt’ less than rookie scientists — but their ideas last
records.description: Researchers have found a link between a scientist’s experience and and whether their ideas have a lasting influence.

records.title: Three reasons why AI is not conscious and perhaps never will be
records.description: Large language models can mimic thought and feeling with uncanny skill. But evidence from neuroscience suggests that intelligence alone is not enough for subjective experience.

records.title: Author Correction: Long-read sequencing reveals pre-meiotic gene conversion in sperm
How to compare and strengthen research systems
records.description: Analysing national research systems by using open-access data and new methods can help countries to learn from each other.

records.title: Why failure is a taboo topic in science
records.description: Failure is one of the best teachers we have. So why is nobody talking about it?

records.title: Daily briefing: How to rebuild science from ruin
records.description: Researchers in New Orleans share lessons from the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina. Plus, budding cryptographers are using AI to crack historical codes and an enzyme that keeps cognition sharp with age.

records.title: Lessons from Katrina: how to rebuild academia from the ground up
records.description: More than 20 years after Hurricane Katrina, universities in New Orleans have learnt what it takes to rebuild from ruin — including what gets in the way.

records.title: Cortex-wide imaging in naturally behaving mice with 1-gram wireless mesoscopes
Briefing Chat: An invisible tattoo that appears under UV light – and then disappears
records.description: Nature staff discuss a new ink that could be useful for medical tattooing — plus, an insight into why small dogs live longer than big ones.

records.title: The pianist who never played
records.description: A note to self.

records.title: Daily briefing: We’re close to reaching a 30% land-conservation target
records.description: More land for conservation is positive, but doesn’t necessarily protect biodiversity, say researchers. Plus, say goodbye to the leap second and how the Inca empire lasted longer than we thought.

records.title: IceCube just won a Nobel prize. Protect astroparticle physics projects with the same potential
records.description: Building the Nobel-prizewinning neutrino experiment was a big risk. To continue its success, scientists — and funders — need to stay bold.

records.title: Memory stays strong in old age when this brain enzyme is active
records.description: Data from mouse brains and 13 human brains show a link between levels of a lipid-degrading enzyme and cognitive resilience.

records.title: Unprecedented atlas explores mitochondria across the tree of life
records.description: The mitoproteomes of five parasites and a plant hold medical potential — and reignite the question of just when the mitochondrion evolved.

records.title: PhD students who write dissertations with AI less likely to stay in academia
records.description: US PhD graduates who used artificial intelligence were more likely to work in industry.

records.title: History’s long-secret codes are being cracked by amateurs using AI
records.description: Cryptographers’ inboxes are being flooded with requests to validate cipher solutions.

records.title: Is AI eroding PhD students’ critical thinking and analysis skills?
records.description: An expert panel debates the impact of artificial intelligence on doctoral programmes.

records.title: World’s timekeepers upend how they adjust time to avoid catastrophic ‘negative second’
records.description: A conference of 69 governments has voted to abolish the leap second immediately and replace it with a leap hour.

records.title: Orangutan mothers arrange play dates for their babies
records.description: Solitary primates spend energy and time travelling to patches of forest for get-togethers.

records.title: Daily briefing: Bleached corals revived by healthy neighbour’s touch
records.description: Ghostly white corals are fully restored in eight weeks by contact with a healthy counterpart. Plus, arXiv is capping submissions per researcher and four good news stories to brighten your day.

records.title: Nearly half of reef-building corals face elevated relative risk of extinction
Give me the good news: four science stories to brighten your day
records.description: Drugs that can reverse multiple sclerosis in mice and a new species of penguin are just the beginning.

records.title: Margaret Hamilton obituary: computer scientist who pioneered software engineering and helped us get to the Moon
records.description: Programmer whose forward-thinking and reliable code helped to save the Apollo 11 mission.

records.title: ArXiv versus AI slop: will capping preprint submissions work?
records.description: Major preprint platform tightens its rules to curb a surge of submissions, including those generated by artificial-intelligence tools.

records.title: This is why butterflies are so hard to catch
records.description: High-speed camera footage reveals the visual tricks butterflies use to evade predators.

records.title: Growing plane and ship traffic degrade the air of western North America
records.description: Pollution from transport across the Pacific Ocean is raising ozone levels above a region whose own emissions have dropped.

records.title: The world is closer to a major conservation target than scientists thought
records.description: Analysis suggests number of protected areas is hugely underestimated but biodiversity is still in peril — plus, a huge study looking at the health effects of brown fat.

records.title: Becoming real
records.description: An endless blessing.

records.title: Lay of the land: terrestrial conservation efforts cover a wider area than thought
records.description: Governments around the world have pledged to conserve 30% of the terrestrial realm by 2030, but official data suggest that the target is barely halfway to being met. A combined global and national-level data set now shows that up to 27% of land area is conserved, but gaps in ecological representation remain.

records.title: Will my lack of country-specific grants limit my chances of employment abroad?
records.description: A researcher in Latin America seeks advice on the best way to present themselves when applying for faculty positions in Europe and North America.

records.title: A guide to the Nature Index
records.description: A description of the terminology and methodology used in this supplement, and a guide to the functionality that is available free online at natureindex.com.

records.title: Nature Index reveals the four countries to watch in biomedical engineering
records.description: These nations are making their distinct mark in the field through specialization and collaboration.

records.title: Is this idea from AI or humans? A detector claims it can tell
records.description: A tool called IdeaLens helps to judge whether concepts — rather than just writing — in scientific papers are AI-generated.

records.title: Some Jurassic period birds were flightless
records.description: The fossil discovery of an early avian ancestor in China reveals that flightless birds lived alongside the known flying species.

records.title: Catalytic transfer of carbon atoms enables spirofusion of C–C σ -bonds
records.description: A rhodium-catalysed method is developed for constructing complex spirocyclic structures by inserting a single carbon atom into C–C bonds, forming four new bonds through sequential activation.

records.title: Large blind test of methane-detecting satellites lends credibility to emissions data
records.description: Twelve methane-sensing satellites were tested for their accuracy in measuring controlled-release events in the Arizona desert over a year-long blind test. Many were found to detect and quantify releases accurately, with instruments purpose-built for methane sensing performing best.

records.title: Daily briefing: China’s extraordinary rise in science
records.description: Explore China’s efforts to grow its scientific and technological might. Plus, how butterflies trick the eye and what could be the oldest shipwreck ever found.

records.title: China’s AI research is booming: what it’s like to be on the front line
records.description: China trains more AI talent than any other country. Nature spoke to analysts and scientists about how AI research there compares to the United States.

records.title: Protecting nature means valuing biodiversity
records.description: Appeals for extra money are failing. Fundamental changes are needed to safeguard the planet for future generations.

records.title: ‘Incredible’: bleached corals thrive within days when touching healthy neighbour
records.description: A coral fragment can form a tissue bridge with a dying counterpart — and provide it with crucial microalgae.

records.title: Alveolar stem cells go beyond making gas-exchange cells to repair damaged airways
records.description: Alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells are the stem cells of the lung’s air sacs and are responsible for maintaining alveolar structure and gas exchange. A study that tracked AT2 cells shows that, after injury to the airway, they can also migrate between lung compartments and become bronchiolar cells to help repair damaged airways.

records.title: Hydrogels and MRI: meet three biomedical engineers reshaping health care
records.description: Researchers are making great advances across medical disciplines, using a wide range of tools and processes.

records.title: How early tetrapods got their neck
records.description: As fish evolved into four-limbed creatures, their skull separated from their shoulders to form a neck. Now we learn that this early neck was surprisingly rigid.

records.title: Overlooked brown fat in our bodies linked to wide range of health benefits
records.description: Massive study of more than 100,000 people finds surprising connection between ‘good’ body fat and improved mental health.

records.title: Smartwatch health data are piling up. How can doctors keep pace?
records.description: To harness the full value of wearable devices for monitoring and diagnosing medical conditions, protocols must be established.

records.title: Smartwatch health data are piling up. How can doctors keep pace?
records.description: To harness the full value of wearable devices for monitoring and diagnosing medical conditions, protocols must be established.

records.title: China’s extraordinary rise in science and how it will change the world
records.description: The nation is on a trajectory to lead the world in science, a development that will reshape technological advancement, innovation and the balance of global power.

records.title: Evidence for multi-Li + clustering in lithium-ion battery electrolytes
records.description: Machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations, spectroscopy, electrochemical data and quantum-chemical calculations reveal previously unstudied multi-lithium-ion complexes without bound anions, improving understanding of lithium-ion-battery functionality at the atomic level.

records.title: Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates
records.description: A globally representative sample of 25 countries and territories indicates that conservation areas cover 26.81% of the land, much closer to the 30% by 2030 target than officially reported.

records.title: Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism
records.description: A tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist recapitulates IL-10’s potent suppression of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells while avoiding stimulation of T cells.

records.title: Elp1 is required for myeloid differentiation and brain repopulation
records.description: Primary cultured haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells are used to analyse the molecular mechanisms of brain myeloid differentiation, and this platform enabled the identification of elongation factor ELP1 as an important regulator of this process.

records.title: Modelling mouse embryogenesis from chemically induced totipotent stem cells
records.description: A mouse embryo model derived from chemically induced totipotent-like stem cells progresses through key developmental milestones, including gastrulation, embryonic axis formation, haematopoiesis and early organogenesis.

records.title: Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K
records.description: The mechanical properties of medium-entropy alloys at 20 K show a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition.

records.title: Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor
records.description: Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy shows that the fractional spin-1/2 end states of molecular Haldane chains couple differently to a superconducting condensate depending on whether the chain contains an even or odd number of spin-1 triangulene units.

records.title: Capillary-selective vasodilation through myosin inhibition halts ischaemic cascades
records.description: R (+)2501 reverses capillary no-reflow by relaxing pericytes, restoring microvascular perfusion and improving survival in animal models of myocardial infarction and acute kidney injury.

records.title: Evaluating space-based methane detection through a one-year blind test
records.description: A year-long single-blind study shows that multiple satellites can accurately detect and quantify methane point-source emissions.

records.title: De novo design of cysteine proteases
records.description: De novo-designed enzymes use an activated cysteine nucleophile to hydrolyse polypeptide backbones in a sequence-dependent manner.

records.title: Computational design of metalloproteases
records.description: RFdiffusion methods are used to de novo design proteins with water-activating zinc-based active sites adjacent to a peptide substrate binding pocket, yielding highly active, programmable proteases with potential applications in therapeutics, biotechnology and bioremediation.

records.title: Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas
records.description: Longitudinal genomic analyses in patients with astrocytoma or oligodendrioglioma suggest that these two types of tumour differ in the mechanisms by which they become resistant to treatment, with astrocytomas accumulating copy-number alterations and chromosomal instability markers but oligodendrogliomas acquiring new driver mutations.

records.title: Rh 3+ stabilized in KRh@MFI catalyses regioselective hydroformylation
records.description: DFT investigations combined with spectroscopic and catalytic studies of disrupted subnanometric Rh 2 O 3 clusters show that Rh + centres in a zeolite-based catalyst are blocked with N-containing molecules, whereas Rh 3+ sites are stabilized, allowing hydroformylation reactions with enhanced regioselectivity and efficiency.

records.title: Targeted stimulation of motor cortex ensembles drives learned movements
records.description: Optogenetic stimulation of motor-cortex neuron ensembles shows that precisely timed activity in the primary motor cortex can generate learned neural patterns and movements, demonstrating an active role in skilled motor control.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat
records.description: Artificial intelligence-enabled quantification and analyses of brown adipose tissue (BAT) activity uncover links between BAT and a healthier metabolic profile along with lower rates of psychiatric disease, and can identify pharmacologic agents that could be repurposed to activate this tissue in humans.

records.title: Early tetrapod neck mobility modelled using an extant analogue
records.description: Biomechanical analysis of several early tetrapods using sturgeon as an analogue revealed that early tetrapods had limited neck mobility despite separation of the head and shoulders.

records.title: Intrinsic physicochemical activity at microplastic–water interfaces
records.description: Commodity microplastics exhibit intrinsic physicochemical activity at water interfaces, manifested by spontaneous generation of reactive oxygen species, challenging the prevailing paradigm of plastic inertness, with implications for human health and the environment.

records.title: Hidden reaction pathways inform additive engineering for perovskite LEDs
records.description: Resolution and control of the hidden solution-phase chemistry of 5-aminovaleric acid added to perovskite precursor solutions is described for producing films with a near-unity mean peak photoluminescence quantum yield and near-infrared perovskite LEDs with enhanced external quantum efficiencies.

records.title: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks
records.description: A randomized controlled trial involving a health-education intervention in rural villages in Honduras shows that the intervention changed social network connections, including not only health-related connections but also friendships and financial ties.

records.title: Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning
records.description: The AI framework probabilistic bias correction is shown to correct weather forecast errors 2 to 6 weeks ahead and boost forecast skill, making it promising for improved extreme-weather prediction.

records.title: Jurassic flightless bird reveals early ecological diversity of avialans
records.description: A fossil bird from the Upper Jurassic Zhenghe Fauna of southeastern China contemporary with Archaeopteryx and that clearly could not fly sheds new light on the ecological diversification of early-diverging avialans.

records.description: Spin-sensitive tunnelling measurements provide converging evidence of two-dimensional d -wave altermagnetism in KV 2 Se 2 O, establishing helical edge modes as a tool for atomic-scale spin sensing in quantum materials.

records.title: Selective catalytic oxidation of polyethylene surfaces
records.description: Interfacial catalytic functionalization of solid polyethylene selectively converts methylene units into ketones to enhance its surface properties without compromising critical bulk traits.

records.title: Award-winning microscopy image disqualified over AI use
records.description: The incident has prompted discussions about the use of artificial intelligence in scientific imagery.

records.title: Author Correction: Timing and trajectory of BCR::ABL1 -driven chronic myeloid leukaemia
