records.description: Better career support and more funding stability is needed to retain this invaluable group of scientists.

records.title: Economics Nobel awarded for work on stabilizing economies in crisis
records.description: Laureates share award for their research that builds on the theories that contributed to governments intervening during the COVID-19 pandemic.

records.title: Beyond the solvent fog: watching molecules dance in the crowd
records.description: A technique called time-resolved X-ray liquidography has been used to shed precision light on the steps involved in a classic chemical reaction.

records.title: What does a PhD pay? Data reveal huge gaps across Europe
records.description: Earnings come in a combination of scholarships and salaries and vary widely between countries, an analysis by international federation Eurodoc reveals.

records.title: Hidden signals in sleep can predict future health
records.description: From a single night of sleep, AI tools can uncover physiological patterns linked to disease and mortality that are missed by conventional sleep measures.

records.title: I told ChatGPT to ‘continue’ — it went too far
records.description: An ambiguous instruction caused the chatbot to send three e-mails from Ying Zhao’s connected account. The incident advanced Zhao’s project, but showed that chatbots need limits.

records.title: Daily briefing: Visit a huge climate experiment in the Amazon rainforest
records.description: Step into the rainforest with climatologist David Lapola. Plus, watch an ‘invisible’ tattoo be revealed by ultraviolet light and explore PhD remuneration across Europe.

records.title: Does the decline of book reading mark the end of rational thinking?
records.description: Smartphones and artificial intelligence are undermining our ability to follow a complex argument, with grave consequences.

records.title: Antiviral immunity via telomerase-like reverse transcription in bacteria
Private, offline and yours: how to search the literature with local AI systems
records.description: Concerns about privacy, reproducibility and cost are prompting scientists to use models on their computers rather than in the cloud.

records.title: Breaking down nerve-cell scaffold relieves chronic pain in mice
records.description: Results could help researchers to develop painkillers that are safer and more effective than existing treatments.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Top researchers are being misled by sham academic societies
records.description: Nature staff discuss a network of organizations that have been building their ranks through deceptive practices.

records.title: Chimp and gorilla brains resist weight loss with age — unlike human brains
records.description: The relatively short lifespans of non-human great apes might explain why their brain mass is maintained in later life

records.title: The life of Darwin and the science of clouds: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: Watch this invisible tattoo appear under UV light
records.description: The ink could be useful for medical tattooing, but more tests are needed before it is widely available.

records.title: An experiment to glimpse the future Amazon — in pictures
records.description: David Lapola is testing a big climate-science unknown: how will the forest cope as atmospheric carbon dioxide continues to rise?

records.title: Publisher Correction: Sleep chart of biological ageing clocks in middle and late life
Daily briefing: Rogue ‘jumping genes’ age bigs dogs faster than little ones
records.description: Epigenetic genes accumulate faster in big dogs. Plus, what’s know about reports of plague in Russia and the legacy of software engineer Margaret Hamilton.

records.title: Five movements from the edge of the singularity
records.description: Change is in the air.

records.title: Author Correction: Histone readers MLLT1 and MLLT3 concentrate AID to confer locus specificity
Editorial Expression of Concern: Maternal gut bacteria promote neurodevelopmental abnormalities in mouse offspring
Women are talking about menopause — health systems must listen
records.description: In the Arab world, lack of training, research and discussion about menopause is hampering care. Three changes can help.

records.title: US proposes $100,000 charge for international students to do postgraduate work
records.description: Suggested change to immigration rules would choke off a crucial STEM talent pipeline, policy specialists say.

records.title: How to build a mouse: embryo development captured in stunning detail
records.description: Gene-editing technologies enabled researchers to trace the cell-by-cell development of a single fertilized mouse egg to a late-stage embryo.

records.title: Woody ‘blankets’ are being deployed on Arctic permafrost to reduce carbon emissions
records.description: A start-up company is testing whether stabilizing areas of rapidly eroding permafrost can prevent greenhouse-gas emissions.

records.title: Daily briefing: Mathematicians up in arms over OpenAI’s preprint deluge
records.description: OpenAI has released 700 preprints tackling maths problems. Plus, a gut microbe could protect against cardiovascular disease and the value of silent meetings.

records.title: Will AI scoop your science? Some researchers see a gloomy future
records.description: Scientists worry that increasingly capable large language models will beat them to discoveries.

records.title: Plague scare: what scientists know, and what Russia won’t say
records.description: Unverified rumours swirl around the death of a Siberian laboratory technician. Nature talks to a biosecurity specialist to unpack the fallout.

records.title: Big dogs age faster than little ones — rogue ‘jumping genes’ might be to blame
records.description: Study of almost 900 dogs from roughly 120 breeds finds that rapid ageing of large canines is linked to changes in the epigenome.

records.title: UAE completes Arab world’s first solo space probe – and sets course for an asteroid
records.description: Device will be launched on a craft built jointly by the United Arab Emirates and the United States. Some researchers say it could be the last mission constructed with outside help.

records.title: A guide to Nature Index tables
records.description: Information on the methodology used in the ranking for the 2026 Nature Spotlight: Infectious diseases.

records.title: NASA releases trove of Moon data from historic Artemis II flight
records.description: Annotated images and more collected by the four astronauts could inform missions to the lunar surface.

records.title: How we ditched presentations and embraced silence in our lab meetings
records.description: Swapping to a system in which lab members read memos quietly before team discussions helped to create an open culture.

records.title: Blend
records.description: Identity crisis.

records.title: Semiconductors pushed into insulator territory
records.description: A material that was previously assumed to be an electrical insulator has been shown to be a semiconductor, with potential uses in electronics and optics.

records.title: Genome accessibility reveals disease risk that gene expression misses
records.description: Most disease-associated genetic alterations do not affect the genes themselves, but instead change how strongly they are expressed, often by modifying genome accessibility. Gene expression and accessibility have now been analysed simultaneously in 10 million immune cells from 1,108 people, linking disease-associated changes in accessibility to gene expression.

records.title: Nuclear clocks tick for the first time
records.description: Ultraprecise clocks that use transitions in atomic nuclei to keep time show promise as a next-generation time standard and for probing fundamental physics.

records.title: Retrofitted LLM can count the letter ‘i’s in ‘artificial intelligence’
records.description: Most LLMs cannot reliably evaluate text on the level of individual letters. A technique called byteification retrofits existing models to enable it.

records.title: Why sound, strong science alone isn’t enough in pandemic preparedness
records.description: Comparable data are key to protecting the world from the next epidemic, says bioengineer Polina Brangel.

records.title: ‘When prevention disappears, infections rise’: can the world still end AIDS?
records.description: The United Nations’ deadline for eliminating HIV/AIDS as a public-health threat is unlikely to be met. But medical, political and social advances have raised hopes that longer-term success is still possible.

records.title: The science of superintelligence and why AI is still a useful word
records.description: President Donald Trump wants to replace ‘artificial intelligence’ with ‘Super Intelligence’ — but there are questions about whether we’re there yet.

records.title: Gut microbes that trace ancient human journeys
records.description: The Indigenous African Hadza and South American Tsimane share gut microorganisms that shed light on human dispersals and microbial losses in industrialized societies.

records.title: An early predecessor to mammals could swim, suckle and swallow
records.description: A fossil of an early ancestor of mammals from the Jurassic period reveals a mammal-like throat passage (pharynx) and throat bones (hyoids). It fills a gap in our knowledge about throat features in the animals from which modern mammals evolved their ability to swallow as adults and suckle milk as babies.

records.title: Daily briefing: Chemistry Nobel goes to mirror-molecule researchers
records.description: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai have won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Plus, the biggest success stories in cancer survival and one of the biggest debates in neuroscience.

records.title: Can your brain grow new neurons? How researchers are solving a century-old puzzle
records.description: Scientists have debated for decades whether the human brain sprouts new neurons throughout life. What would it mean if it could — and how much evidence is enough?

records.title: Australia’s bush fires got worse after British colonization — this is why
records.description: The suppression of Indigenous burning practices probably spurred the growth of flammable forests.

records.title: Why we must advocate for proper care on the frontlines of the Ebola outbreak
records.description: As the Bundibugyo virus public-health crisis continues to evolve, physician Richard Kojan is finding ways to care for people with the infection and helping relatives to visit loved ones safely.

records.title: Revealed: how this common gut microbe protects against heart disease
records.description: Intestinal bacterium secretes a molecule that reduces cholesterol production, according to a mouse study.

records.title: OpenAI posts 700 maths preprints online: mathematicians are up in arms
records.description: The firm used an unreleased model to tackle hundreds of high-profile problems.

records.title: How to control where semiconductor crystals start growing
records.description: Semiconductor crystals grow from tiny nuclei, but the position of these nuclei is difficult to control precisely and can affect the crystal’s properties. An approach using ‘etching flux’ has now been developed that constrains the position at which a nucleus forms, enabling spatially programmable growth of large single crystals of semiconducting material.

records.title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of how ‘handed’ organic molecules can emerge
records.description: Prize goes to two chemists who probed why life favours one mirror-image molecule over another.

records.title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of how ‘handed’ organic molecules can emerge
records.description: Prize goes to two chemists who probed why life favours one mirror-image molecule over another.

records.title: Observation of relativistic bond weakening in seaborgium hexacarbonyl
records.description: Gas chromatography analysis of compounds formed by the superheavy element seaborgium shows that the hexacarbonyl complex Sg(CO) 6 exhibits lower first bond dissociation energy than the lighter chemical homologue W(CO) 6 , owing to relativistic bond weakening effects.

records.title: RNA catalysis emerges from dynamic structural ensembles
records.description: RNase P RNA forms shifting active and inactive conformers whose catalytic activity depends on Mg 2+ -driven tertiary-interaction dynamics, which are modulated by binding of accessory proteins.

records.title: A thorium-229 optical nuclear clock with feedback loop
records.description: A thorium-229 nuclear clock is realized by stabilizing a continuous-wave laser to the 148-nm nuclear excitation with a rapid feedback loop based on absorption spectroscopy.

records.title: Structural basis for regulating lipopolysaccharide transmembrane transport
records.description: Structures of the protein machinery in Gram-negative bacteria that transports lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the cytoplasmic membrane to the outer leaflet of the outer membrane reveal how conformational changes in response to the presence of LPS promote its transport.

records.title: A nuclear clock synchronized to 229 Th
records.description: A nuclear clock synchronized to 229 Th establishes laser-addressed nuclei as operational clock references and 229 Th:CaF 2 as a stable, reproducible solid-state platform for compact nuclear clocks and nuclear quantum sensors.

records.title: Hydrogen bonding in water under extreme confinement
records.description: A new technique allows direct nanoscale observations of the vibrational response of water confined inside carbon nanotubes, revealing that high degrees of confinement disrupt the hydrogen bond network through a fluctuating and highly-dispersed molecular state.

records.title: Alveolar stem cells transdifferentiate to drive bronchiolar regeneration
records.description: Identification of a cross-compartmental cellular mechanism for bronchiolar epithelial repair informs therapeutic strategies for airway injury.

records.title: Experimental observation of critical topology
records.description: Experimental evidence indicating that critical gapless topological states can be characterized by the entanglement spectrum and wavefunctions is presented, demonstrating persistence of topology at phase boundaries and extension to higher-dimensional systems.

records.title: Prehistoric global migration of vanishing gut microbes with humans
records.description: Microbial species disappearing from industrialized populations have evolved with humans over millennia and migrated worldwide with them—this may have consequences for human health.

records.title: A preinvasive regulatory T cell axis for lung cancer interception
records.description: An effector regulatory T cell circuit is identified that can be monitored in blood samples to track the development of lung cancer, and blockade of this immune network in the preinvasive setting can intercept tumorigenesis to reduce tumour incidence and size.

records.title: Mechanism of spliceosome termination
records.description: A coordinated sequence of RNA helicases and associated factors dismantles normal and defective spliceosome complexes to enable intron degradation and ensure accurate gene expression.

records.title: A 7-eV bandgap semiconductor based on silicon-doped α-(Al x Ga 1− x ) 2 O 3
records.description: Suboxide molecular-beam epitaxy is used to grow silicon-doped α-(Al x Ga 1− x ) 2 O 3 films with bandgaps exceeding 7.0 eV, enabling the fabrication of a Schottky diode and a field-effect transistor with colossal-bandgap channels.

records.title: Overcoming key challenges in the evolutionary transition to multicellularity
records.description: This Review synthesizes an evolutionary framework for understanding the key stages, challenges and microevolutionary processes through which single cells evolve into functionally integrated multicellular organisms.

records.title: tRNA dosage regulates lineage dependency and resistance in prostate cancer
records.description: A tRNA-specific regulatory pathway is associated with codon biology, lineage transitions and therapy resistance in prostate cancer.

records.title: A chiral superlattice route to spin-split topological antiferromagnetism
records.description: A chiral superlattice in collinear antiferromagnetic UOTe generates large Berry curvature and spin-polarized currents, enabling anomalous Hall effects and advancing chiral quantum materials for spintronics.

records.title: Dynamics of human cardiogenesis and its disruption in trisomy 21
records.description: Single-cell and spatial multiomics are combined to define niches in the developing human heart, revealing pacemaker-cell organization, cardiomyocyte maturation and compaction, and developmental perturbations associated with trisomy 21.

records.title: Australia’s current wildfire crisis linked to colonial land-use change
records.description: A 1,000-year lake-sediment record from southeastern Australia shows that colonial disruption of Indigenous cultural burning transformed open woodland into dense, flammable forest, priming the landscape for today’s climate-driven wildfires.

records.title: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes
records.description: Byteification is a general method for retrofitting large language models to operate over bytes such that they approach the capabilities of subword-based systems and may be better for scientific data.

records.title: Spatially deterministic nucleation of 2D semiconductors by etching flux
records.description: Etching-flux-mediated single-centred nucleation of two-dimensional semiconductors is used to deterministically localize a single nucleation event, expanding semiconductor deposition from controlling where materials grow to controlling where and how crystals can begin to form.

The Solar System could die one billion times earlier than thought
records.description: Modelling suggests that the planets’ orbits will become destabilized inside one billion years once the Sun starts to shed mass.

records.description: A satisfying congruence between genetics and cell-biology findings, and experiments at altitude with a rotating device that measures radiant energy, in this week’s peek at Nature ’s archive.

records.title: Preprints must not leak sensitive research information

records.description: ‘Rivers in the sky’ helped to keep an expanse of water roughly as big as Portugal ice-free.

records.title: AI could undermine scientific independence in subtle ways

records.description: Nature reporter Davide Castelvecchi reflects on covering the fast-moving field of astronomy honoured by the Nobel physics award.

records.title: Rising numbers of Asian and African PhD students choose to study in China
records.description: International students explain the advantages and challenges that come with pursuing a doctoral degree in China.

records.title: How digital breakdowns affect supply chains — and endanger the global economy
records.description: When supply chains fail, it’s often because of energy, computer or data-network failures. Addressing these requires a way to make interdependencies visible.

records.title: Daily briefing: Physics Nobel for founder of neutrino-hunting observatory
records.description: Francis Halzen has won the Nobel Prize in Physics for his work in founding the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. Plus, a call to prevent a privacy crisis driven by smart glasses and has flu season come early?

records.title: Strong evidence that ‘baryon junctions’ give proton its identity
records.description: A conserved property of protons and neutrons is carried not by their constituent particles but by structures that mediate the force between them.

records.title: Why smart glasses are about to create a major privacy crisis
records.description: As AI wearables become discreet, cheap and mainstream, they risk normalizing non-consensual recording in everyday spaces.

records.title: Cells, who needs them? Biochemists turn to proteins in a tube
records.description: Scientists are using cell-free transcription and translation systems to synthesize proteins, design biology-based sensors and develop synthetic cells.

records.title: Circular DNA exposes a weakness in cancer cells
records.description: Repetitive sequences make extrachromosomal DNA vulnerable to breaks, which could be exploited for therapy — but might also promote tumour evolution.

records.title: Flu season could kick off ‘incredibly’ early — what scientists are watching
records.description: Cases in the Northern Hemisphere are cropping up weeks early, and they are dominated by a virus with a concerning mutation.

records.title: Nobel physics prize awarded for detection of cosmic neutrinos
records.description: Francis Halzen wins this year’s award for his work on a neutrino observatory at the South Pole that has helped to unlock mysteries of the Universe.

records.title: Brain organoids grafted into cortex-free mice will advance human brain research
records.description: Cell-based models of the human cortex transplanted into mice produce neurons that are inaccessible in vitro , and could enable scientists to link brain injury to behaviour.

records.title: How to mobilize the agile science needed in a crisis
records.description: Two reports highlight the changes needed in academia to facilitate the fast, collaborative, responsive and inclusive research that aids global decision makers.

records.description: Nature ’s senior biology reporter Ewen Callaway reflects on today’s prize for optogenetics — which scientists have anticipated for years.

records.title: The top cancer success stories of the past 50 years, by the numbers
records.description: Outcomes have improved drastically in the United States for some forms of the disease, but those for others continue to lag.

records.title: Daily briefing: Medicine Nobel prize goes to optogenetics
records.description: Three pioneers of optogenetics have won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Plus, the funniest nature photography and the physics behind a new science-fiction novel.

records.title: Medicine Nobel awarded for brain ‘switch’ that controls neurons with light
records.description: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel win the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their work on optogenetics, which has revolutionized neuroscience.

records.title: How big tech is building a military–industrial complex in the age of AI
records.description: Two books explore how warfare is being reshaped, with influence shifting from states to tech giants.

records.title: AI biohazard hype must not divert attention from the real risks we face now
records.description: Twenty-five years after the US anthrax attacks, fears around AI are distracting people from seeing what’s needed to stay safe: a strong, regulated life-sciences sector.

records.title: Location, location, location: how to edit genes only in the cells you want
records.description: Gene-editing CRISPR enzymes controlled by light and sound target tissues of interest.

records.title: ‘Learning about physics changed my life’: author Hernan Diaz on his new novel Ply
records.description: The Pulitzer-Prize-winning author joins us to talk about his time visiting CERN and communicating quantum physics in fiction.

records.title: How to respond to hate speech without fuelling it further
records.description: Psychologist Mirta Galesic discusses an increase in hateful comments online, and the science-backed way to react.

records.title: Stunning fossil shows dinosaurs’ distinctive path to flight
records.description: A fossil from a previously undiscovered species with feathery limbs, unearthed in China, adds to evidence that dinosaurs and birds evolved flight more than once.

records.title: Nature has rights — it is time the world recognized them
records.description: Existing legal frameworks have not halted planetary crises. Recognizing the rights of nature could offer a different path.

records.title: Daily briefing: Can you name every female Nobel laureate?
records.description: Test yourself on your science Nobel knowledge. Plus, how butterfly markings mislead the eye and how to respond to hate speech without fuelling it further.

records.description: Take Nature ’s quiz on female Nobel laureates in physics, chemistry and physiology or medicine.

records.description: One small study in Iran swayed meta-analyses in favour of antidepressant use in children, researchers say.

records.description: Advocates say that delivering lectures and presentations al fresco can energize students and provide them with a complete experience.

A black hole’s jets have a halo effect
records.description: Observations confirm jets’ expected effect on the gas cloud that surrounds a galaxy.

records.title: Can pancreatic cancer be stopped in its tracks? Radical tactic raises hopes
records.description: With prospects for new treatments at an all-time high, researchers are looking for ways to boost survival by treating the disease early.

records.title: ‘Vibe coding’ makes the dictionary: AI terms recognized by Merriam-Webster
records.description: ‘Agentic’, ‘prompt engineering’ and other technical terms are among the 1,400 entries added to the online catalogue of the iconic lexicon.

records.title: The ‘missed disease’ that affects 190 million: endometriosis drug shows early promise
records.description: Modified medication targets the cells implicated in the condition’s tell-tale lesions.

records.title: Gaze into the cosmos and through the eyes of a bee — September’s best science images
records.description: The month’s sharpest science shots, selected by Nature’ s photo team.

records.title: Daily briefing: The sky as you’ve never seen it — the month’s best science images
records.description: Coloured stripes across the sky and a crab caught in jellyfish tentacles are among this month’s sharpest science shots. Plus, a ‘speech clock’ could determine how fast you’re ageing and how invasive plant species are displacing farmers in Africa.

records.title: Battle of the Anthropocene: allegations re-ignite row over proposed geological epoch
records.description: Researchers say that a vote to reject the epoch violated procedure and call for transparency.

records.title: These optical illusions are why butterflies are so hard to catch
records.description: High-speed footage of takeoffs reveal that the butterfly markings mislead the eye, making them harder to catch.

records.title: Who’s the loudest of them all? The bare-throated bellbird vies for the prize
records.description: The bellbird’s extra-large gape helps it to achieve pneumatic-drill-level volume.

records.title: Is exposomics the key to making personalized medicine a reality?
records.description: Scientists say tailored disease treatments require a comprehensive assessment of a person’s lifelong environmental exposures.

records.title: Daily briefing: How to save corals from the El Niño
records.description: Scientists are trying to help coral reefs survive record ocean temperatures. Plus, the aftermath of a deadly attack on Ukraine’s National Academy of Sciences and whether it’s OK to dodge small talk.

records.title: The super El Niño is cooking coral reefs — can lullabies and probiotics save them?
records.description: Researchers are trying everything they can to help coral reefs to survive severe heat stress from climate change, including playing sounds underwater.

records.title: This award-winning microscopy image used AI — igniting controversy in a prestigious competition
records.description: Researchers say that using artificial-intelligence tools to visualize scientific images can become problematic when models misrepresent the underlying data.

records.title: 2D semiconductor aims to turbocharge development of high-performance electronics
records.description: An ultrathin semiconductor that conducts electricity using positively charged ‘holes’ might clear the way for next-generation electronic devices.

records.title: Elena, Aris, Marcus: AI-generated ‘ghosts’ are polluting the scientific literature
records.description: The overuse of certain names has revealed the scale of fake experts on academic publishing platforms, say researchers.

records.title: Tuberculosis treatment has advanced — now we need to stop drug resistance dragging us backwards
records.description: The next major advancement in TB might not be a new drug, but a better understanding of how and why resistance to medicines emerges.

records.title: Sugar amplifies antibiotic disruption of gut microbes
records.description: People who underwent stem-cell transplantation and ate sugar-rich food had disrupted communities of gut microorganisms during antibiotic treatment.

records.title: How did Earth get its water? Inside the extreme machine seeking answers
records.description: The Z machine in New Mexico generates shockwaves that can simulate conditions deep inside our planet.

records.title: Harmful tau spreads like self-propagating prion proteins
records.description: Structural studies support the idea that fibrillized tau protein, a feature of neurodegenerative disorders, acts as a prion-like template to induce misfolding in healthy tau.

records.title: Beware sham scientific societies: the research community must be more vigilant
records.description: As AI content makes bad actors harder to spot, scrutiny of organizations must increase without reducing trust.

records.title: AI ‘speech clock’ assesses how fast you’re ageing from your voice
records.description: The pitch and emotional content of your speech are important predictors of accelerated ageing, researchers find.

records.title: The buck stops with me
records.description: A note to self.

records.title: Secret watermark labels proteins as ‘made by AI’
records.description: An innovative safeguard could help to flag proteins devised by artificial-intelligence tools such as AlphaFold, but the digital marker can be erased.

records.title: Pipework problems when cancer spreads to an area bordering the brain
records.description: Analysis of cancer growing adjacent to the brain reveals that bone-eroding cells interfere with lymphatic drainage vessels and hinder anti-tumour immune responses.

records.title: How to spend $25 billion on science: OpenAI’s staggeringly rich research charity gets under way
records.description: Jacob Trefethen, who leads life sciences at the OpenAI Foundation, speaks to Nature about the organization’s ambition to cure disease.

records.title: I turn up late to meetings to dodge small talk. Am I wrong?
records.description: A jury weighs in on whether a latecomer is simply using their time efficiently or disrespecting their colleagues.

records.title: Restoring hearing in people with a rare form of deafness
records.description: How a decades-long quest led to the first gene therapy for deafness caused by a mutation.

records.title: Sugar-rich foods exacerbate antibiotic-induced microbiome disruption
records.description: Avoiding a diet rich in simple sugars during treatment with antibiotics may mitigate microbiota disruption.

records.title: Type 2 immune history trains lung macrophages for viral disease tolerance
records.description: Type 2 inflammation trains nerve- and airway-associated macrophages to confer disease tolerance against lethal influenza by limiting immunopathology and promoting tissue repair without enhancing viral clearance.

records.title: Global mangrove distribution on the open coast is controlled by waves
records.description: A process-driven mangrove presence or absence model using 20 years of open-source wave data shows that wave conditions are critical in determining where mangroves grow worldwide.

records.title: X-ray liquidography decodes complex motions in azobenzene isomerization
records.description: Time-resolved X-ray liquidography films the structural changes of azobenzene during trans -to- cis isomerization in solution with atomic-level precision.

records.title: Histone readers MLLT1 and MLLT3 concentrate AID to confer locus specificity
records.description: By being restricted to target regions by MLLT1–MLLT3 occupancy, activation-induced deaminase activity is able to avoid most off-target mutagenesis during B cell somatic hypermutation.

records.title: Carbene transfer from thianthrenium ylides for cyclopropanation
records.description: Thianthrenium ylides can be used as a general platform for metal–carbene generation and transfer, including cyclopropanation, σ -bond insertion and sigmatropic rearrangements.

records.title: An amygdala to anterior hypothalamic circuit gates stress sensitivity
records.description: The anterior hypothalamic nucleus regulates negative valence in the brain, highlighting a new pathway that controls sensitivity to stressful events and signposting approaches to identify new circuit interactions relevant to mental health.

records.title: Dynamic protrusions mediate crawling motility in Asgard archaea
records.description: Anoxic live-cell imaging shows actin-dependent crawling motility and dynamic protrusions in Asgard archaea, providing insights into cellular innovations that may have contributed to eukaryotic evolution.

records.title: Osteoclasts intercept meningeal lymphatic paths for dural metastasis
records.description: Osteoclast-derived angiopoietin-2 in the dura mater impairs lymphatic vessel function and weakens anti-tumour immunity against dural metastases, which offers new therapeutic approaches to restore meningeal lymphatic function through selective osteoclast targeting.

records.title: γδ T cell receptor dependencies define a unique immunosurveillance modality
records.description: Tissue-resident γδ T cells mount rapid, innate-like stress responses that require γδ T cell receptor signalling, revealing lineage-specific receptor dependence that underpins their conserved roles in immunosurveillance and informs therapeutic deployment.

records.title: Spatiotemporal clonal architecture of the newborn mouse forebrain
records.description: Clonal barcoding across the newborn mouse forebrain reveals developmental principles whereby glutamatergic neurons and astrocytes remain locally derived, whereas widely dispersed GABAergic (γ-aminobutyric acid-producing) lineages link neurons with oligodendrocyte precursor cells.

records.title: Scalable decision-making for games of imperfect information
records.description: Ataraxos, an AI for the board wargame Stratego, establishes a design pattern for reinforcement learning and search that is effective under large amounts of hidden information, a longstanding desideratum of the field of strategic decision-making.

records.title: Evolution of terrestrial anatomy revealed by a derived stem tetrapod
records.description: New anatomical evidence reclassifies Westlothiana as an aquatic stem tetrapod, showing that terrestrial limb adaptations evolved mosaically in transitional amphibious environments before crown tetrapods emerged.

records.title: Butterfly wing patterns in flight create powerful illusory motion cues
records.description: Butterfly wing patterns and flight dynamics work in tandem to create powerful visual illusions that confuse predators, potentially representing one of the most successful visual defence strategies in moving animals.

records.title: Self-aligned optical microcomb emerging between octave-separated lasers
records.description: An architectural inversion shifts integrated optical frequency comb generation from outward broadening around a central pump to filling the spectrum between two octave-separated pumps through a self-aligned parametrically driven cavity soliton, enabling robust self-referencing for future deployable on-chip frequency and time metrology.

records.title: Function-preserving watermarking of AI-generated proteins
records.description: SynthIDBio watermarks AI-generated protein sequences and structures while preserving function, enabling provenance detection and offering a proof-of-concept tool for biosecurity and information integrity.

records.title: A TBK1/ULK1 signalling axis couples lysosomal stress to TFEB activation
records.description: Proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses of lysosomes identify a nutrient-independent regulatory arm of mTORC1 signalling that mediates lysosomal adaptation to stress and whose deregulation underlies tumorigenesis in follicular lymphoma.

records.title: A two-hit mechanism triggers autoimmune hair loss
records.description: Immune dysregulation and physiological neural activation converge to trigger autoimmune alopecia.

records.title: Strange and beautiful creatures spotted on the Challenger expedition
records.description: A genus of soil-dwelling beetle discovered in Italy, and a glimpse at the wonders of the deep sea, in our weekly dip into Nature ’s archive.

records.title: PhD training should encourage ethical dissent
Biodiversity protection must include language preservation
Emissions after the Paris accord made Europe’s heatwaves more severe
records.description: A heatwave in 2025 would have been one-third of a degree cooler without the greenhouse gases released since 2015.

records.title: Patents alone won’t unlock critical-mineral supply chains
The cost of lost labour on a warming planet
records.description: Researchers quantify the economic damage caused by climate-change-related heat stress on the global workforce.

records.title: Why AI-authorship debates miss a deeper shift in how scholarly knowledge is produced
AI-powered medical devices must be tested in real-world settings
records.description: Tools that inform clinical decision-making require rigorous assessments equivalent to processes used to approve drugs and self-driving cars.

records.title: AI can widen science — but only if institutions stop rewarding the already measurable
records.description: Funders, journals and universities must reward the creation of new scientific terrain, not just the efficient mining of old ground.

records.title: Daily briefing: Vaping has ‘alarming’ risks for children
records.description: Vaping in childhood comes with bigger health risks than we thought. Plus, chemists can’t seem to ditch hazardous solvents and whether apocalyptic claims about AI are a dangerous distraction.

records.title: Chinese-owned science journal created to rival the best
records.description: Newly launched Vita is part of a broader government plan to give China a bigger say in what counts as high-quality science.

records.title: Author Correction: Proteasome-guided haem signalling axis contributes to T cell exhaustion
A new chapter in targeting kinase enzymes in cancer
records.description: Inhibitors of tyrosine kinase enzymes have been a cornerstone in precision cancer treatments. Now, targeted protein degraders could reshape therapeutic options.

records.title: Lab-grown brain organoids: time for international oversight
records.description: Researchers in the field are right to focus on biosafety, ethics and the involvement of patient groups and the public.

records.title: How to put people first in cyberspace
records.description: Digital technologies increasingly shape everyday life. Computer scientist Francine Berman tells Nature that stronger safeguards are required to protect the public interest.

records.title: Daily briefing: Old hearts ‘de-age’ in younger people
records.description: Epigenetic 'clocks' suggest that transplanted organs adjust to the host's biological age. Plus, a new biography of Stephen Hawking and how sham societies are misleading star researchers.

records.title: China now leads the world in trials for next-gen CAR-T therapies
records.description: China tests these therapies faster than the rest of the world but regulatory changes could slow the progress.

records.title: Stephen Hawking biography explores an ‘exceptionally clear, uncluttered mind’
records.description: An elegant account of the physicist’s unusual life story highlights the relationships that inspired him.

records.title: Bigger than CRISPR? A guide to the latest genome editors
records.description: Gene-editing techniques could soon allow researchers to replace entire genes and engineer complex cellular circuits — if the systems can be delivered safely into cells.

records.title: Vaping in childhood has bigger health risks than we’d thought
records.description: Use of e-cigarettes makes it more likely that young people will experience mental-health disorders and take up smoking. Governments must act.

records.title: Old hearts age backwards: transplanted organs adjust to host’s biological age
records.description: Tracking the biological age of grafted organs suggests that donor pools could be expanded to boost organ availability.

records.title: Paid to peer review: firms are paying researchers to assess manuscripts for journals
records.description: Freelance peer-review jobs through third-party companies raise practical and ethical questions.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Why scientists made papyrus scrolls, then burnt them
records.description: Nature staff discuss a technique that could help researchers read charred Herculaneum scrolls — plus, a biodegradeable, edible battery.

records.title: Why science wouldn’t exist without alchemy, curiosity and great writing: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: Anthropic’s AI biolab finds ‘CRISPR-like’ DNA in viruses. What’s next?
records.description: The detection effort enlisted roughly 950 AI agents, which spent more than 21 hours combing through DNA sequence databases.

records.title: Chemists struggle to ditch hazardous solvents — even after decades of ‘green’ efforts
records.description: Laboratories are still using dangerous and carbon-intensive liquids much more often than environmentally friendly ones, according to a 40-year survey of patents.

records.title: Nepal’s floods expose issues with climate-disaster funding — firmer policies are needed fast
records.description: The UN’s climate loss and damage fund needs to consider how to make decisions about finance fairly and quickly, without disadvantaging low-resource nations.

records.title: Exclusive: Sham scientific societies are misleading star researchers
records.description: A Nature investigation reveals a network of organizations that have been building their ranks through deceptive practices.

records.title: OpenAI’s research chief talks of ‘cultural reset’ after wild few weeks
records.description: Mark Chen discusses how the Hugging Face cybersecurity incident prompted a pivot to safety — and giving AI models a sense of ‘taste’.

records.title: AI bots are flooding researchers with requests for money and time
records.description: Many scientists use artificial intelligence in their work, but agents are increasingly soliciting researchers for collaborations.

records.description: A new project aims to generate chromosome-level genomes for all living bat species. Plus, AlphaFold has a new pandemic preparedness portal and security risks of AI.

records.description: A new project aims to generate chromosome-level genomes for all living bat species. Plus, AlphaFold has a new pandemic preparedness portal and security risks of AI.

records.title: Bumblebees don’t mind a little plastic in their honeypots
records.description: Insects show off their adaptability by incorporating unfamiliar construction materials to build honey-storage vessels.

records.title: Youthful fans of YouTube sports videos stick to the sofa
records.description: University students who are highly motivated to watch sports online do not report higher participation in exercise.

records.title: GLP-1 drugs fail to help some people lose weight — scientists are on a quest for answers
records.description: Understanding why some people see no benefits from potent anti-obesity medications could lead to new therapies and personalized weight-loss regimens.

records.title: AI system helps lab devices ‘talk’ with each other — streamlining research
records.description: Platform allows disparate machines to communicate and to be controlled by an artificial-intelligence agent.

records.title: AI agent hacks government website for first time: why this breach matters
records.description: An OpenAI agent accessed secure data on an Australian health-care website, but the incident wasn’t reported for months.

records.title: Daily briefing: Will AI really be the death of us all?
records.description: Nature unpacks why AI companies are calling for a slowdown. Plus, the best clock ever and a new, unusual phase of boron.

records.title: AlphaFold ‘goes viral’: database adds protein complexes of common viruses
records.description: AI predictions could help with pandemic preparedness, but they will need experimental confirmation.

records.title: Author Correction: Large recoverable elastic energy in chiral metamaterials via twist buckling
Bank accounts reveal the fingerprints of abusive financial control
records.description: Analysis of anonymized banking data could help inform strategies to support victim-survivors of financial abuse — plus, how opposing forces within the Earth can alter the length of a day.

records.title: Competition heats up in the regenerative-medicine ranks
records.description: The United States leads, but China poses strong competition, according to the latest Nature Index data.

records.title: Huge hoard of metal bars hints at vast Iron Age trade
records.description: One-tonne cache of iron is the largest ever found — and enough to make roughly 500 swords.

records.title: Brain lipids are organized into zones — and reorganized during pregnancy
records.description: A map of fats across the whole mouse brain reveals a spatial architecture that differs from that seen in gene-expression and protein atlases.

records.title: Efficient yet stable large perovskite solar modules made using surface treatment
records.description: Non-uniformities in the layer of passivator molecules, which are used to fix defects and protect the surface of perovskite material in solar cells, can limit the durability of the resulting modules. Large modules treated instead with chemically stable lead carboxylate passivators were efficient, reliable and had a higher yield than did commercial silicon modules.

records.title: Landmark map of human brain’s gene activity holds clues to Alzheimer’s disease and more
records.description: The atlas of gene expression in the prefrontal cortex was created using samples from almost 1,500 donors of all ages — from infants to centenarians.

records.title: How to stay smart in the age of AI: the science of critical thinking
records.description: There is growing concern that AI can blunt memory and reasoning. But science shows ways to keep the brain sharp.

records.title: Vast cellular gene-expression atlas could transform how scientists understand brain ageing and disease
records.description: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing captures molecular changes in the prefrontal cortex across the lifespan and in health and disease.

records.title: The human skeleton’s unique adaptations relied on gene regulatory changes
records.description: Variants in genes involved in the production of extracellular matrix molecules could have enabled the skeletal adaptations that distinguish humans from other great apes.

records.title: Gravitational forces inside Earth drag some decades out — and make others fly by
records.description: Variations in day length that occur on multidecadal timescales are caused by gravitational coupling between Earth’s inner core and its solid mantle.

records.title: A guide to the Nature Index
records.description: A description of the terminology and methodology used in this supplement, and a guide to the functionality that is available free online at natureindex.com.

records.title: How do I rekindle my motivation for earning my PhD?
records.description: An early-career researcher has hit a roadblock. Here’s how they can persevere in their studies.

records.title: Best clock ever: timekeeper based on lutetium atoms wows researchers
records.description: The device is a step towards redefining the second using a new generation of ultra-accurate devices.

records.title: A widespread agricultural practice is an unexpected CO 2 sink
records.description: ‘Liming’ to reduce soil acidity has long been considered a carbon dioxide source, but in North America’s largest river basin, it has resulted in net capture of atmospheric carbon.

records.title: Conifer trees can prosper half a world away from their usual home
records.description: Northern Hemisphere trees planted in the Southern Hemisphere can thrive, displaying increased stem growth and physiological signals linked to reduced stress.

records.title: Genome project opens the next chapter for studying bat evolution
records.description: A landmark collection of bat genomes reveals fresh clues about the evolution of one of the world’s most unusual groups of mammals.

records.title: What is needed for regenerative medicine to flourish?
records.description: Although the field’s breakthrough research has the potential to save lives, it requires a more in-depth and equitable foundation of research.

records.title: Surprising protein links dietary restriction to increased lifespan in flies
records.description: A fruit-fly protein thought only to store amino acids in fact responds to nutritional deficiency in both development and adulthood, resulting in lifespan extension.

records.title: The courier
records.description: A special delivery.

records.title: The gene-regulatory evolution of the human skeleton
records.description: Massively parallel reporter assays and human–ape hybrid skeletal cells are used to study the evolution of human cis -regulatory elements (CREs), revealing how differences in CREs have shaped the composition of human skeletal tissue.

records.title: The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases
records.description: Emerging infectious disease outbreak risks are ubiquitous worldwide, and highest in landscapes where people, livestock and fragmented natural ecosystems coexist, but detection and data on outbreaks are currently limited by inequalities in healthcare access.

records.title: Gravitational torque drives multidecadal variations in length of day
records.description: Multidecadal fluctuations in Earth’s length of day are shown to be driven by gravitational torque and resisted by electromagnetic and topographic forces, improving our understanding of the material properties and dynamics of Earth’s deep interior.

records.title: Single-nucleus transcriptome-wide association study of human brain disorders
records.description: Single-nucleus transcriptomics across diverse populations is used to explore how genetic risk for brain disorders affects specific cell types, revealing previously hidden gene–trait associations and conserved, cell-type-specific mechanisms.

records.title: Lu + optical frequency references with accuracy verified at the 19th digit
records.description: Two independent 176 Lu + single-ion optical clocks achieve fractional frequency uncertainties near 10 −19 and agree at 5.7 × 10 −19 , advancing precision timekeeping.

records.title: Sequence-encoded hexagonal lattices in multichannel peptide nanofibrils
records.description: Nine-residue peptides can encode discrete interaction motifs that direct the formation of hexagonal pores, which hierarchically tile into laterally expandable multichannel nanofibrils with defined topology.

records.title: Banking records reveal characteristics of financial abuse
records.description: An analysis of UK banking data reveals that people who reported being victim-survivors of financial abuse experience worse financial outcomes compared with a control group.

records.title: Hepatocytes promote liver metastasis of pancreatic cancer by providing serine
records.description: Metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in the liver that lack the enzyme necessary to synthesize serine can reprogram hepatocytes to produce this amino acid, thus promoting tumour growth and survival.

records.title: A design approach for bitopic kinase inhibitors
records.description: Detailed analyses of ligand choice, linkage vector and linker length enabled the development of bitopic inhibitors of ABL1 and EGFR kinases, including an ABL1 inhibitor with enhanced activity against resistance mutations and reduced off-target toxicity.

records.title: A methanogen hydrolase reveals the structure of archaeal peptidoglycan
records.description: ArmA from Methanobrevibacter smithii , a dominant member of the human gut microbiome, is identified and characterized as a glycosyl hydrolase specific for cleaving the cell wall of methanogens, revealing an unsuspected chemical structure of archaeal peptidoglycan that includes a previously unidentified sugar.

records.title: Reference genomes and fossils revise bat family phylogeny and biogeography
records.description: An updated phylogeny of bats is presented, based on new genome assemblies and many ancient fossils and including all known bat families.

records.title: mTORC1 drives cell-autonomous astrocyte reactivity in tuberous sclerosis
records.description: Reactive astrocytes emerge as a primary consequence of TSC2 loss in tuberous sclerosis complex, implicating glial dysfunction as a primary driver of pathogenesis and highlighting the astrocytes as potential therapeutic targets for tuberous sclerosis complex-related neuropathology.

records.title: Targeting ZMYND8 unleashes IL-2 signalling to override T cell exhaustion
records.description: ZMYND8 suppresses IL-2R–STAT5 signalling by inhibiting p300-mediated transcriptional activation of Il2ra to enforce CD8 + T cell terminal exhaustion, and its deletion boosts effector-like states and markedly enhances antiviral and antitumour immunity.

records.title: Anomalous metal and superconducting phases in rhombohedral graphene
records.description: Observations of rhombohedral graphene on a WSe 2 substrate at varying temperature, magnetic field and current indicate the presence of regions of gate space with zero-resistance superconductivity alongside others with finite saturation resistance.

records.title: Lifespan single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the human prefrontal cortex
records.description: The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex exhibits non-linear, cell-type-specific transcriptional trajectories characterized by dynamic remodelling during development, relative stability in midlife and selective molecular reactivation in late adulthood.

records.title: Agricultural liming is a carbon sink in the Mississippi River Basin
records.description: Century-scale records of agricultural liming and anthropogenic acidity inputs for the Mississippi River Basin show that agricultural liming has acted as a net carbon sink over the past century.

records.title: Stacking-induced direct band gap in CVD-grown 1H MoS 2 bilayers
records.description: Atomically aligned 1H bilayer MoS 2 exhibits a direct band gap, enhanced excitonic emission and stronger valley polarization, establishing its potential for advanced optoelectronic and valleytronic applications.

records.title: TRAM promotes Toll-like-receptor-free myddosome signal transduction
records.description: TRAM is a regulator of myddosome assembly through dissociating MyD88 from the TLR–TIRAP complex to enable myddosome maturation and durable downstream signal transduction.

records.title: Lsp2 links mTORC1 to TOP mRNA translation and lifespan in Drosophila
records.description: In Drosophila , the protein Lsp2, which is induced by dietary essential amino acids, is a key physiological effector of mTORC1, and mutant flies that lack the Lsp2 gene exhibit reduced translation of TOP mRNAs and improved longevity.

records.title: Lsp2 links early-life diet to adult translation and lifespan in Drosophila
records.description: Isotope tracing is used to determine the fate of larval dietary amino acids in adult flies, and identifies Lsp2 as a key regulator of translation and lifespan that forms the molecular basis of the effects of early-life protein restriction.

records.title: The lipidomic architecture of the mouse brain
records.description: A spatial lipidomic atlas of the mouse brain reveals more than 500 biochemical territories that mirror cell types and connectivity, capture oligodendrocyte heterogeneity and ventricular zonation, and are remodelled during pregnancy.

records.title: Single-cell atlas of transcriptomic vulnerability across brain disorders
records.description: A population-scale single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex provides a perspective of the transcriptomic landscape in neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric disorders, and offers potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

records.title: MMEJ repair of breaks at TA repeats maintains ecDNA and cancer fitness
records.description: Stability of extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) relies on microhomology-mediated end joining at fragile TA-rich sites, with FANCM suppressing break formation, suggesting that Polθ disruption may destabilize ecDNA and sensitize ecDNA-driven tumours to therapeutic intervention.

records.title: A quadruped robot designed to complete a marathon on a single battery charge
records.description: RAIBO2, an energy-efficient quadruped robot, completed a full marathon in 4 hours, 19 minutes and 52 seconds on a single battery charge, achieving a total cost of transport of 0.25 that surpasses the human benchmark of 0.37.

records.title: Neuronal detection of social actions directs collective escape behaviour
records.description: Collective escape in Danionella cerebrum arises from visual detection of rapid, biologically realistic motion of other fish, with midbrain and thalamic neurons encoding social offsets that enable fish to infer danger from others’ behaviour.

records.title: Organic two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures
records.description: Sequential on-water-surface assembly enables layer-by-layer stacking of two-dimensional polymers to create both lattice-matched and controlled lattice-mismatched van der Waals heterostructures with defined lattice registry, stacking sequence and thickness.

records.title: The mutational dynamics of the Arabidopsis centromeres
records.description: Centromeres in Arabidopsis thaliana evolve through frequent insertions and deletions of repeat units and increased rates of point mutations driven by homology-directed repair, a mutation spectrum that is sufficient to generate and maintain large homogenized tandem-repeat blocks.

records.title: Chiral oxazolidinones via biocatalytic aziridination of unactivated alkenes
records.description: A biocatalytic aziridination and ring-expansion cascade enables direct, enantioselective synthesis of clinically relevant and discovery-stage chiral oxazolidinones from simple alkenes.

records.title: Biosecurity must protect human functional capacity
Why insects need their own protected areas
A global safety net for climate-risk intelligence is urgently needed
What happens in Vegas: one lecturer’s hunt for a projector
records.description: Misadventures at a scientific meeting in Nevada, and ponderings on the idea that physical objects exist only as perceptual phenomena, in our weekly dip into Nature ’s archive.

records.title: Dust in the wind is on the decline
records.description: The global decrease in atmospheric dust might be affecting Earth’s temperature.

records.title: About to give your first lecture? Read this first
records.description: Ten researchers and faculty members share what surprised them when they began teaching — and what they wish they had known before walking into the room.

records.title: Watch scientists decipher burned scrolls without unrolling them
records.description: By making and burning their own papyrus, researchers have come up with a method that might help to read glowing text from unopened scrolls from Herculaneum.

records.title: This super-cold microscope could spur a quantum revolution
records.description: The instrument, which operates near absolute zero for hours, will soon ship to a few labs. Researchers are thrilled.

records.title: Daily briefing: The mystery of the ‘little red dots’
records.description: Theories abound about the identity of these enigmatic objects in space. Plus, meet a nation’s favourite goth robin and discover benefits associated with a low-sugar babyhood.

records.title: Why AI companies can’t be trusted to self-regulate
records.description: From aviation to banking, high-risk industries are subject to independent oversight and meaningful penalties. AI companies should be no exception.

records.title: Hundreds of ‘free’ academic journals have started charging fees
records.description: A study tracking diamond open-access journals has found an increase in titles switching to other publishing models — especially over the past few years.

records.title: All the ways a cell can die — and why the variety matters
records.description: Scientists are poking holes in established ideas about how cells live and die, and are harnessing these discoveries to fight diseases from cancer to autoimmune conditions.

records.title: Nepal floods pose biggest test yet for UN climate loss and damage fund
records.description: Countries should not have to wait months to receive relatively small grants for responding to the immediate impact of extreme weather.

records.title: The worst El Niño in recorded history is brewing — here’s how governments must prepare
records.description: From southern Africa to the Amazon, the risks are mounting and the window for action is rapidly closing.

records.title: Will AI really kill us all? The science behind the hype
records.description: Nature examines whether the technology might spell the end for humans, and why AI companies are calling for a slowdown.

records.title: Six principles for supporting academic freedom in universities
records.description: Many academics are concerned about threats to independent enquiry in higher education. Here’s how it can be protected while taking legitimate concerns into account.

records.title: Losing your way of life to climate change matters — and we need a way to measure it
records.description: Climate losses extend beyond property and income. Policymakers need ways to assess what people value, experience and ultimately stand to lose.

records.title: Edible batteries power medical devices in the body
records.description: The tiny power sources, tested in pigs, dissolve inside the digestive tract after several months.
