records.description: The tiny power sources, tested in pigs, dissolve inside the digestive tract after several months.

records.title: China punishes prominent academics exposed by research sleuth
records.description: Several scientists investigated for research-integrity violations by video-blogger ‘Student Geng’ have now faced disciplinary measures. The penalties are part of a misconduct crackdown on 31 research teams.

records.title: AI co-scientists are revolutionizing how research is done
records.description: Artificial-intelligence systems can generate hypotheses, design experiments and analyse data — but humans still need to decide what makes sense.

records.title: How do I change labs gracefully during my PhD?
records.description: A scientist in training seeks help in finding a new adviser without damaging existing working relationships.

records.title: ‘Epigenetic’ editing is here: gene-tagging technique banishes hepatitis B virus
records.description: The technique uses chemical tags to shut down viral DNA lurking in a host’s genome.

records.title: Daily briefing: The first new cat species described by science in a century
records.description: Leopardus tilcayo is smaller than a housecat and covered in leopard-like spots. Plus, the brain might spawn from two types of precursor cell and how to maintain the foundations of human flourishing in a climate crisis.

records.title: Chemist-aligned retrosynthesis by ensembling diverse inductive bias models
records.description: RetroChimera, a deep learning retrosynthesis model, improves prediction accuracy, particularly for rare and challenging reactions.

records.title: Cognitive resilience helps to predict Alzheimer’s dementia
records.description: The trait could explain why symptoms vary in severity between people with similar brain pathology.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Evidence mounts for hidden chambers beyond Tutankhamun's tomb
records.description: Nature staff discuss data that could point to Nefertiti’s burial place — plus, the implant that translates brain activity into speech and gestures.

records.title: Daily briefing: How to turn a paper into an AI agent
records.description: A new tool is designed to help researchers interact with published papers. Plus, promising news for an RNA-based treatment for ALS and how psychoactive drugs might have shaped pre-Incan culture.

records.title: Europe pushes for space independence amid geopolitical rifts
records.description: The European Union is easing its reliance on US space infrastructure — and seeking to grow its satellite and launch operations.

records.title: How research funding took me out of the lab and into leadership
records.description: Landing two large grants caused Anna Sandak to take on a managerial role in her team and made her reflect on what it means to contribute to research.

records.title: First for RNA therapy: man with rare motor-neuron disease improves after treatment
records.description: Gene-targeting treatments could be used to treat other people with rare forms of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

records.title: How to make a brain: new experiments challenge existing picture
records.description: Research also uncovers an efficient way to grow hindbrain cells from stem cells — a difficult feat.

records.title: Chinese companies doubled down on science after US tech restrictions
records.description: Affected Chinese companies adjusted their sources of knowledge to stay competitive.

records.title: Mercury is shrinking with age — faster than thought
records.description: Impacts by space objects have obscured some of the evidence of the planet’s contraction over the past 4.5 billion years.

records.title: Schoolhouse meals serve up an income bump
records.description: Modelling shows a link between feeding programmes and higher potential earning in five African nations.

records.title: How fast are you ageing? Ask AI
records.description: A new system will help scientists to refine large language models for longevity research and clarify ‘biological’ age.

records.title: Exclusive: New evidence for hidden chambers beyond Tutankhamun’s tomb
records.description: Geophysical survey yields ‘tantalizing’ data that could point to Nefertiti’s burial place — but it’s too early to draw definitive conclusions.

records.title: Take a risk or play it safe? Neuronal tug-of-war helps the brain decide
records.description: Using a video game involving bombs and treasure chests, researchers show how neural activity flickers between two regions of the frontal cortex when the brain weighs up a tricky decision.

records.title: How a team of AIs discovered a promising lung-cancer drug
records.description: Researchers developed a ‘virtual biotech’ made up of as many as 37,000 agents reporting to a ‘chief scientist’.

records.title: Author Correction: Genomic deletion of malic enzyme 2 confers collateral lethality in pancreatic cancer
Daily briefing: Fresh evidence for hidden chambers at Tutankhamun’s tomb
records.description: Scans support the idea that as-yet-unexplored chambers might hold the remains of the Egyptian queen Nefertiti. Plus, mathematical controversy and beautiful ctenophores.

records.title: Who gets credit in the AI era? OpenAI maths bombshell sparks debate
records.description: Controversy around OpenAI’s claim to have solved the Navier–Stokes problem highlights how researchers could be inadvertently sharing — and absorbing — ideas through chatbots.

records.title: Why most stars don’t have outbursts like the Sun’s
records.description: A strong magnetic field can disrupt a star’s ability to produce the fountains of matter called coronal mass ejections.

records.title: Transplanted human brain-tissue takes root in mice without a cortex
records.description: Extensive cellular integration might provide platform for in vivo testing of new therapies — plus, the AI tool that turns papers into ‘virtual corresponding authors’.

records.title: Marine bacteria cooperate to break down complex algal carbohydrates
records.description: Marine algae produce sulfated carbohydrates called fucoidans that are chemically too complex for any bacteria to digest alone. Instead, marine bacteria split the task between them in a modular fashion: some strains degrade the molecular backbone, whereas others remove the side branches.

records.title: Antimatter: coming soon to a lab near you?
records.description: Antiprotons have been transported by road at CERN. This advance might one day enable laboratories outside the site to use antimatter in their experiments.

records.title: Molecular computation that rolls energetically downhill
records.description: A DNA-based computer that operates by relaxing to thermodynamic equilibrium has been demonstrated on ten molecular programs, which completed computations in as little as one minute. Some programs were rerun using distinct inputs up to 25 times and others were scaled up to 100-bit computations — although this slowed them down substantially.

records.title: Daily briefing: Asgards — the microorganisms that might have begat us all
records.description: Explore the origins of all complex life, boggle at award-winning microscopy and learn that stomach bugs send protective immune cells rushing from gut to brain.

records.title: Turning scientific research papers into interactive AI agents
records.description: Scientific knowledge is mostly stored in static papers. An automated framework called Paper2Agent can now transform each paper into an active artificial intelligence agent — a virtual corresponding author that answers questions, applies the paper’s methods to new data, and collaborates with other paper agents. This makes research easier to reproduce, reuse and extend.

records.title: Is it safe to use consumer wearable devices for research?
records.description: Wearable technology is a boon for studying health behaviours, but it comes with some thorny ethical concerns, says researcher Wuyou Sui.

records.title: Nearly one in seven young, male white voters in the US support white nationalism
records.description: Three national surveys reveal how factors such as gender, age, political alignment and income are correlated with support for white nationalism in the United States.

records.title: Map of brain ‘microproteins’ could offer new clues to Alzheimer’s disease
records.description: Researchers detect more than 1,000 overlooked microproteins in human brain tissue, including some that are altered in Alzheimer’s disease.

records.title: I who have never known trees
records.description: Lost connections.

records.title: Virus-like particles observed assembling in real time
records.description: Scientists have long dreamt of being able to track and analyse each step in the assembly of a virus’s protein shell. An ingenious experiment shows how this can be done.

records.title: Development of a random background to understand ligand optimization
records.description: An approach to improve efficiency and establish a background expectation for ligand potency optimization is described.

records.title: Developmental xenocortication using human-derived organoids in mice
records.description: Xenocortication with human neurons enables circuit- and behaviour-level analysis of neurodevelopment in mice.

records.title: Mitochondrial fission factor senses and governs ferroptosis
records.description: The mitochondrial–peroxisomal fission adaptor MFF is identified as a selective pro-ferroptotic mediator, and the newly developed MFF–SPARK sensor enables high-content screening of ferroptosis-sensitizing compounds and the discovery of upstream regulators of MFF.

records.title: Reimagining research papers as interactive and reliable AI agents
records.description: Paper2Agent converts research papers into interactive artificial intelligence agents by turning manuscripts, code and data into model context protocol-based tool-invoking systems that reproduce original results, answer new scientific queries and collaborate to generate novel insights.

records.title: Electroluminescent photoresists extending lithographic scaling to OLEDs
records.description: Electroluminescent photoresists synthesized via atom transfer radical polymerization can be directly patterned by ultraviolet and electron-beam lithography, and used to fabricate monolithic, multicolour organic-light-emitting-diode micro-pixel arrays.

records.title: Inflection points and transitions in Alzheimer’s disease
records.description: Alzheimer’s disease reflects phase-specific shifts in molecular, cellular and network states triggered at biological thresholds, with amyloid-induced tau phosphorylation marking a key inflection point that explains symptom–pathology dissociation.

records.title: Continuous-wave laser absorption spectroscopy of the thorium-229 nucleus
records.description: Absorption spectroscopy of thorium-229 nuclear excited states in a thorium-doped calcium fluoride crystal demonstrates a path towards a much more efficient way to build a highly stable and robust solid-state optical nuclear clock.

records.title: Mutational constraints on RSV F and its neutralization by antibodies
records.description: How respiratory syncytial virus mutations affect antibody neutralization is defined, and a biophysical model of the mechanism is provided, to show how Fab potency and epitope specificity combine to determine the effects of viral mutations on antibody neutralization.

records.title: Evolution and heterogeneity of lethal metastatic bladder cancer subtypes
records.description: A rapid autopsy programme provides valuable resources to enable detailed molecular and genetic analyses of the temporal evolution of aggressive histological subtypes and therapy resistance in metastatic bladder cancer.

records.title: Topographic structure and function of locus coeruleus noradrenaline neurons
records.description: Dorsal and ventral noradrenergic neurons in the locus coeruleus form topographic subpopulations whose projection patterns and activity encode choice switching, reward-prediction errors and disregard of reward-predictive cues, supporting flexible learning behaviour.

records.title: Overmassive black holes and little red dots naturally form in simulations
records.description: Observations from the JWST reveal an unexpectedly abundant population of little red dots and overmassive black holes in the early Universe, which are confirmed by their formation in fully cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulations.

records.title: A retinoic acid autoregulatory loop governing prefrontal–motor arealization
records.description: MEIS2 , encoding a transcription factor linked to intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, is a key hub of a retinoic-acid-associated gene regulatory network.

records.title: Road transport of trapped antiprotons
records.description: Researchers demonstrate successful road transport of trapped antiprotons, establishing a practical method for moving antimatter to quieter laboratories and substantially improving future tests of matter–antimatter symmetry.

records.title: Transcriptional activation of plant immunity by salicylic acid
records.description: A mechanistic basis for how the hormone salicylic acid promotes transcriptional activation during plant immune responses is described.

records.title: Rapid patient-specific neural networks for X-ray to volume registration
records.description: xvr makes pan-anatomical 2D/3D rigid registration accessible to broad clinical and research communities.

records.title: Heterogeneous photonic integration of single-crystalline nanomembranes
records.description: A framework consisting of advanced epitaxy and layer lift-off techniques uses heterogeneous photonic integration of single-crystalline nanomembranes to infuse desired functionalities into silicon and silicon nitride photonics, demonstrating ultraefficient electro-optical and magneto-optical modulation.

records.title: Molecular-level observation of the self-assembly of a virus-like particle
records.description: Using mass photometry combined with a single-molecule trapping method allows real-time monitoring of the assembly of individual virus-like particles with molecular resolution, enabling observation and quantification of their self-assembly pathways and dynamics.

records.title: Mechanisms of transcriptional regulation by salicylic acid receptors
records.description: Deciphering a dual receptor pathway of salicylic acid signalling in plants offers a comprehensive view of salicylic acid-mediated defence gene activation, triggering transcriptional activation through NPR1 and relieving transcriptional repression by NPR3 and NPR4.

records.title: Targeted genomic integration and rearrangement using prime assembly
records.description: Prime assembly enables RNA-guided integration of medium-to-large DNA sequences in human cells without requiring double-strand breaks or cell cycle progression, and supports exon recoding, transgene insertion and megabase-scale rearrangements.

records.title: Sex without crossovers mimics clonal reproduction in Rhynchospora tenuis
records.description: Rhynchospora tenuis undergoes obligate, genome-wide achiasmy in both male and female meiosis.

records.title: Scalable near-real-time Bayesian phylogenetics for outbreaks with Delphy
records.description: Delphy makes near-real-time and scalable Bayesian phylogenetics possible for growing viral outbreaks, enabling public health bodies anywhere to analyse and react to their own data with state-of-the-art accuracy and minimal friction.

records.title: Author Correction: Obesity rise plateaus in developed nations and accelerates in developing nations
Electrically controllable superconducting memory effect in UTe 2
records.description: Observations of a memory effect in the p -wave superconductor candidate UTe 2 , which can be controlled by varying the strength and duration of the electrically applied stimuli, are described.

records.title: Cohesin reshapes replication fork contacts to aid fork slowing and reversal
records.description: Cohesin-mediated loop extrusion limits sister-fork coupling and tethers nearby replication forks under replication stress, promoting fork reversal and slowing fork progression to safeguard genome stability.

records.title: Assessing biological degradation of non-hydrolysable synthetic polymers
records.description: The evidence for biological degradation of non-hydrolysable synthetic polymers is critically evaluated to propose best-practice principles for experimental design that should promote reproducibility and impact across this field.

records.title: Identification of broadly tumour-reactive γδ TCRs from multiple myeloma
records.description: A machine-learning algorithm, PreGame, is developed to identify tumour-reactive γδ T cells from single-cell CITE sequencing data, and expansion of this cell population can be used as a biomarker of therapeutic response.

records.title: Predictors and prevalence of support for white nationalism in the United States
records.description: Explicit support for white nationalism is uncommon overall, but higher among young white men, disadvantaged and politically disaffected white people, conservatives, Republicans, and those with primarily online friendships.

records.title: A thermodynamically favoured molecular computer
records.description: Scaffolded DNA Computer performs diverse computations while thermodynamically relaxing towards equilibrium, demonstrating simplicity, reusability, speed, robustness and scalability of the approach by running 10 programs, including parity, multiplication and 25-bit addition.

records.title: A wake-up call: diversify global research funding
Why Nepal floods resulted in a disaster even after satellites spotted danger
The geometric genius of René Descartes
records.description: The achievements of a visionary mathematician, and a trip to the National Air and Space Museum in Washington DC, in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: Make AI traceable before it shapes global climate assessments
Why the NIH must resist the metrics trap
Global inequality panel is a chance for research to change lives
records.description: The scientific panel is welcomed. It must now invite all interested researchers to participate.

records.title: CRISPR crops are coming to Europe — why bolder would be better
records.description: For farmers and consumers to reap the benefits, guidelines for farming gene-edited plants must be implemented with careful thought.

records.title: Underground hydrogen could spur a green-energy revolution — if companies can find it
records.description: Firms are racing to drill for hydrogen in hopes of finding a dirt-cheap green-energy source.

records.title: Cities and countryside are intimately linked — green initiatives must recognize that
records.description: Urban areas depend on resources from the land that surrounds them. Managing regions in their entirety is the best way to avoid rural decline.

records.title: Daily briefing: Reading for pleasure linked to big brain benefits
records.description: Evidence that reading for fun is related to structural brain changes, improved mental health and reduced risk of cognitive decline. Plus, go prospecting for clean-burning hydrogen gas underground and discover the oldest galaxy ever seen.

records.title: Author Correction: Erythropoietin receptor on cDC1s dictates immune tolerance
‘Stomach bugs’ send protective immune cells rushing from gut to brain
records.description: Voyaging gut-derived immune cells ‘remember’ past stomach infections in mice.

records.title: Quality control of glycogen through direct ubiquitylation by RNF213
records.description: Cryo-electron microscopy and functional studies of the E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF213 show that sugar ubiquitylation can trigger autophagy, identifying a mechanism for quality control of biomolecules and facilitating future research into glycogen storage diseases.

records.title: The roots of astrology, the mysterious nature of time and more: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: How is climate change affecting conifers and their ability to sequester carbon?
records.description: Fresh evidence reveals that the interplay of several factors could affect the ability of these trees to grow.

records.title: The pet trade puts reptiles and amphibians at risk: close legal gaps now
records.description: Patchy legislation means that animals are routinely taken from their natural habitats and sold in other countries. Fresh national and international measures could help to stop this exploitation.

records.title: Science philanthropy is rising in Brazil ― upending a long tradition
records.description: Philanthropists are stepping up support for research in a country where scientists have relied on the government alone for funding.

records.title: ‘Multifunctional’ brain implant translates speech and gestures in real time
records.description: A neural device uses artificial intelligence to read brain activity for intended words and gestures simultaneously.

records.title: UK universities are on the brink — what is their greatest source of stress?
records.description: Nature asked eight leaders in higher education what they thought about the state of UK institutions. Here’s how they answered.

records.title: Fraud sealed the fate of controversial zoologist Paul Kammerer — 100 years on, his ideas deserve revisiting
records.description: After an eventful life in the limelight, the discovery of a manipulated specimen preceded the biologist’s death. Questions about his findings remain.

records.title: Daily briefing: How this year’s super El Niño is different
records.description: Climate change makes the event difficult to predict. Plus, signs of success from an early trial of an osteoporosis therapy and how to safeguard reptiles and amphibians from illegal trafficking.

records.title: Drug firms’ secret data supercharge AI protein models
records.description: An AI system trained on more than 20,000 protein structures from pharmaceutical companies outperforms AlphaFold-like models that use only public data.

records.title: Encoded and non-genetic protein variants expand the human functional proteome
records.description: Alternative genetic and non-genetic proteoforms detected in unrelated individuals reflect natural diversity in the human population.

records.title: The super El Niño is already wreaking havoc: here’s what’s in store
records.description: The extreme weather of this year’s mega El Niño could look different from past events.

records.title: Briefing Chat: The Bunsen burner myth that turns out to be just hot air
records.description: Nature staff discuss an AI tool that can assess the impact of 9 billion mutations — plus, how the Bunsen burner’s reputation for sterilization might be based on tradition alone.

records.title: NSF moves to overhaul funding approach in line with White House priorities
records.description: The major funder of basic science has not said how its new initiatives will be funded — but staff worry that streamlined approach will further squeeze cash for core sciences.

records.title: People trust scientists seen to be ‘on their side’, UK study finds
records.description: Politics and personal values influence people’s confidence in scientists, according to a report.

records.title: El Niño goes viral — and scientists learn what makes people care about the climate
records.description: Evoking emotions is more likely to prompt people to engage with climate efforts than are data alone.

records.title: Successful early-career scientists rely on network of mentors
records.description: Large networks are particularly beneficial to researchers in under-represented groups.

records.title: Osteoporosis affects millions: could modified cells rebuild their bones?
records.description: Small trial hints at regenerative potential of bone-seeking marrow cells.

records.description: Large networks are particularly beneficial to researchers in under-represented groups.

records.title: Osteoporosis affects millions: could modified cells rebuild their bones?
records.description: Small trial hints at regenerative potential of bone-seeking marrow cells.

records.title: Daily briefing: Skeleton teeth show evidence of the earliest known habitual drug use
records.description: Traces of the psychoactive compound arecoline suggest that two people regularly sucked on psychoactive betel nuts. Plus, what motivates people to take action on climate change and the promise of nasal vaccines.

records.title: The neurons that can put a brake on a nervous-system cancer
records.description: Drugs that imitate the effect of GABAergic neurons slow the growth of tumours called gliomas in mice.

records.title: Distant sensors announced a fearsome tsunami’s birth
records.description: Seismic data pinpoint the collapse of an underwater volcano, and reveal how the eruption triggered a destructive tsunami.

records.title: Rivers deliver unexpectedly high loads of microplastics to the sea
records.description: Intense rains coupled with poor waste management cause big spikes in pollution.

records.title: Daily briefing: Text-message tutoring keeps kids learning when schools close
records.description: Twenty-minute phone calls from tutors improved children’s maths learning during emergency school closures. Plus, Denisovans made excellent deer hunters and Beatles puns are here, there and everywhere in scientific literature.

records.title: AI researchers reckon with the $1.5 million ‘academia tax’
records.description: Academics explain that their research freedom beats the increased salary they would get in the corporate sector, but emerging hybrid models might allow them to get the best of both worlds.

records.title: Author Correction: The molecular basis of force selectivity by PIEZO2
Phone tutoring boosts math scores when schools are forced to close
records.description: Evidence suggests that regular calls can keep kids learning when schooling is disrupted — plus, why a familiar world map may be about to change.

records.title: How AI is changing PhD programmes: join our free webinar
records.description: Learn how artificial intelligence can hone your research skills as well as the potential pitfalls of relying too heavily on it.

records.title: Bacteria recruited to treat cancer
records.description: Anticancer drugs could be manufactured and delivered by modified microorganisms.

records.title: Ruins of ancient Asian city show engineering prowess and organization
records.description: The 5,000-year-old city of Liangzhu has mounds, dams and city walls built in a challenging waterlogged site.

records.title: In the basement of miniaturized relics
records.description: Thinking small.

records.title: AI model predicts which breast-cancer drugs work best
records.description: Model trained on millions of protein measurements can gauge drug effectiveness in tissue samples taken from people with triple-negative breast cancer.

records.title: Why the super-fun Ig Nobel prizes bring serious value to science
records.description: Awards that celebrate humour, curiosity and irreverence are a balm in hard times.

records.title: These six advances could change how drugs are delivered
records.description: Medication triggered by your circadian clock, self-assembling delivery systems based on DNA and other highlights from studies and trials.

records.title: DNA-editing ‘pencils’ probe early human development
records.description: A genome-rewriting approach known as adenine base editing offers a precise way to investigate gene function in early human embryos.

records.title: Popular open-science platform to stop hosting data and code amid funding concerns
records.description: Changes to the Open Science Framework’s policies will come into effect in November, forcing researchers to reconsider their workflows.

records.title: Special delivery: bacterial couriers are smuggling drugs into cancers
records.description: Microorganisms that deliver treatments to tumours could make chemotherapy, radiotherapy and immunotherapy safer and more effective.

records.title: Daily briefing: OpenAI claims a huge maths breakthrough
records.description: The AI giant claims to have solved one of maths’ trickiest problems, but questions swirl over should get the credit. Plus, an atlas of every single DNA letter mutation in humans and why more bioengineered microorganisms aren’t making it out of the lab.

records.title: Uniform film formation helps tandem solar cells work better for longer
records.description: When making mixed-halide perovskite films for use in solar cells, bromide-rich domains crystallize faster than iodide-rich ones do, leading to defects. Adding a molecule tuned to bind selectively to bromide-bound lead synchronizes the crystallization rates, yielding uniform films, better operating stability and a more-efficient perovskite–organic tandem.

records.title: Use AI as a sparring partner, not an oracle
records.description: As artificial-intelligence tools become crucial collaborators in science, universities must teach students to challenge such systems and assess their ability to do so.

records.title: Who were the Denisovans? Rich trove of fossils and tools paints new picture
records.description: Objects found in a cave in southwestern China suggest that these enigmatic ancient humans were accomplished hunters.

records.title: Combined satellite and news data capture unseen aspects of war
records.description: Records of war extracted from news reports have shaped what researchers know about violence. Satellite images could transform that understanding — if access stays open.

records.title: Drug-delivering particles aim to breach the blood–brain barrier
records.description: The inability to get drugs into the brain has impeded the treatment of cancer and neurodegenerative diseases for decades. Techniques based on nanoparticles and exosomes are vying to provide a solution.

records.title: Phone-based tutoring improves learning during school closures
records.description: One-to-one phone sessions substantially increased students’ numeracy test scores in low- and middle-income countries that experience emergencies that disrupt schooling.

records.title: Medicines do no good if people don’t take them
records.description: Health psychologist Rob Horne explains why medication non-adherence is such a problem, and how behavioural science can help to address it.

records.title: Hello Equal Earth: what the UN’s new world map will change
records.description: What the UN vote to ditch the Mercator projection means for education, navigation and public perception.

records.title: Why we need an International Panel on Inequality
records.description: Disparities in income and wealth are growing. A scientific assessment process can give governments the information they need to tackle them.

records.title: Pick up the phone! Phone calls with tutors keep kids learning when schools shut down
records.description: The low-cost intervention was trialled in five countries during the COVID-19 pandemic.

records.title: Phone-call tutorials improve learning cost-effectively during education emergencies
records.description: Across five randomized trials in India, Kenya, Nepal, the Philippines and Uganda, weekly 20-minute mobile-phone-call tutorials produced large learning gains for primary-school children during school closures caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. Governments can keep children learning through societal shocks using this approach, which combines low-cost, high-access mobile-phone technology with high-quality tutoring targeted to each child’s learning level.

records.title: A good drug is useless if it misses its target
records.description: The best medicines go exactly where they’re needed in the body— and nowhere else.

records.title: The Einstein test: what happens when AI tries to rediscover relativity?
records.description: Scientists are probing whether language models trained on historical data can reproduce creative breakthroughs.

records.title: Electric charge makes drops of water more destructive
records.description: In many real-world settings, water droplets can become slightly charged as they slide across solid surfaces. This charge has been found to enable water droplets to damage protective coatings more easily than uncharged droplets do, and to cause the underlying metal to corrode.

records.title: ‘Superdark’ protein looks like a G-protein-coupled receptor — but shows unconventional behaviour
records.description: Mining millions of AI-predicted structures reveals an evolutionarily conserved protein that resembles a receptor family member but functions differently.

records.title: Oddball fossils suggest that the first insects were a mixed bunch
records.description: As the most diverse class of animals, insects have dominated terrestrial ecosystems for the past 320 million years. However, the origins of this successful group have faded into the abysses of geological time. A collection of fossils reveals the unusual body plans and evolutionary experiments that could have contributed to the success of insects.

records.title: Drug delivery gets subcellular
records.description: Therapies that target mitochondria and other organelles are being put to test in the clinic.

records.title: Breaking timescales with generative sampling of conformational transitions
records.description: A generative committor-guided path-sampling framework reconstructs rare biomolecular transition pathways and reveals the underlying thermodynamics and kinetics without using predefined collective variables or brute-force sampling, at an acceptable computational cost.

records.title: Within-family effect of ancestry on complex traits in a Mexican population
records.description: This study uses a within-family design to identify significant ancestry differences in complex traits such as height and type 2 diabetes in a genetically diverse population from Mexico City.

records.title: Neocortical long-range inhibition promotes cortical synchrony and sleep
records.description: In mice, a sparse population of sleep-active long-range inhibitory neurons in the neocortex promote widespread cortical synchronization and sleep, revealing a cortical mechanism that contributes to the regulation of sleep.

records.title: An operational perturbation proteomics-based virtual cell model
records.description: Temporal protein-abundance measurements from systematically perturbed breast cancer cell lines were generated to develop ProteinTalks, a virtual cell model that functions as an operational tool for diverse drug discovery tasks.

records.title: PLA2G2D in tumour-draining lymph nodes regulates anti-tumour immunity
records.description: A specific population of macrophages that express high levels of the enzyme PLA2G2D in tumour-draining lymph nodes is associated with poor prognosis in patients, and inhibiting PLA2G2D improves anti-tumour immunity in mouse models.

records.title: Foaming photopolymers as a high-resolution biomimetic printing platform
records.description: Deep-foam photolithography uses light-controlled polymer foaming to create high-resolution, multifunctional microstructures with tunable optical, wetting and fluid-handling properties for advanced manufacturing applications.

records.title: Advancing conflict research and response through satellite-derived data
records.description: Integrating satellite-derived war-damage data with text-based fatality records through improvement, enrichment and fusion mitigates limitations inherent in each source, revealing complex violence dynamics beyond fatality-centric paradigms, as case studies from Ukraine and Myanmar illustrate.

records.title: Denisovans from southwestern China and their subsistence strategies
records.description: Evidence from Bianfu Cave shows specialized hunting, expedient stone-tool production and extensive bone use of Denisovans, providing new insights into their ecology, behaviour and cultural legacy in eastern Asia.

records.title: Highly efficient base editing at PCSK9 and normal human embryo development
records.description: In contrast to Cas9-induced DNA double-stranded breaks, base-editor-induced lesions are efficiently repaired in early human embryos.

records.title: A serpin–myeloid axis in pancreatic cancer heterogeneity and immune evasion
records.description: SERPINE1 and SERPINB2-driven fibrin-rich niches locally programme immunosuppressive macrophages and exclude T cells, enabling spatially organized immune evasion in pancreatic ductal carcinoma.

records.title: Mobile education builds resilience during shocks in five countries
records.description: Remote phone-based targeted tutoring in five countries produced large, cost-effective learning gains during school closures, outperforming text messaging and working effectively when delivered by governments or non-governmental organizations to strengthen education resilience.

records.title: Ancient proteins identify various Denisovan remains from Southwest China
records.description: Identification and proteomic analysis of bone fragments and teeth from an excavation in Southwest China provide insight into the evolution and phenotype of Denisovans and fill a geographical gap in their documented distribution.

records.title: Predicting genome-wide functional constraints with GPN-Star
records.description: GPN-Star, a genomic language model with a phylogeny-aware architecture for whole-genome alignment data, is shown to be a scalable and flexible tool for genetic variant effect prediction across species.

records.title: Imaging cellular activity across all organs reveals body-wide circuits
records.description: An imaging system developed to record cellular activity throughout the whole body of zebrafish captures cellular organ dynamics and identifies multiple distributed circuits.

records.title: TRI-611, a selective, brain-penetrant molecular glue degrader of ALK
records.description: TRI-611 induces the degradation of ALK fusion proteins via a previously undescribed CRBN recruitment motif, and its preclinical anti-tumour activity highlights TRI-611 as a potential new way of treating ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer.

records.title: Anodic Pd membrane H 2 extraction enhances thermochemical dehydrogenation
records.description: An electrochemical cell with molten hydroxide and a Pd membrane actively extracts H 2 and thereby boosts ammonia and methylcyclohexane conversion, while also delivering purified H 2 ready for use.

records.title: Integrated signatures define mutational processes in prostate cancer
records.description: Eight integrated mutational footprints collectively explain the mutational processes in 85% of primary prostate cancer genomes.

records.title: Put patients at the centre of medical AI governance
Nepal disaster is a wake-up call to take compound climate risks seriously
Sideline vested interests to reform China’s research
Limit bets on clinical-trial outcomes being placed on prediction markets
The Kelvin scale’s creator William Thomson made many scientific advances
records.description: A physics pioneer who provided a new way to describe temperature, and the value of studying fossilized tracks in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: Author Correction: Contrasting roles of histone 3 lysine 27 demethylases in acute lymphoblastic leukaemia
The World Bank is right to prioritize reproducibility
records.description: The development bank and others are starting to publish and verify the raw data and code accompanying their research-based reports and papers. Other agencies should do the same.

records.title: China’s fast-track clinical trials are in the spotlight after child deaths
records.description: A new government policy seeks to balance innovation and safety.

records.title: Two children died from gene therapies in China: where the field goes next
records.description: Strengthened laws should help to ensure future deaths are quickly disclosed to the public, but China’s reputation for such research is at risk.

records.title: Why this neuroscientist is taking the plunge into science advocacy
records.description: As funding cuts reshape the US research landscape, Stefano Cataldi is turning towards policy and advocacy work to defend science.

records.title: A data leak shut a top research biobank: lessons from the recovery
records.description: UK Biobank is imposing new safety measures after a security incident, but safeguarding biomedical data while enabling researcher access remains a challenge.

records.title: OpenAI claims huge maths breakthrough on a famed ‘Millennium Problem’
records.description: The company says it has cracked the physics of fluids using artificial intelligence, solving one of the toughest puzzles in mathematics.

records.title: Daily briefing: Gene-therapy deaths put spotlight on trials in China
records.description: The deaths of two children in separate gene-therapy trials could have a profound effect on China’s biomedical industry, say researchers. Plus, an AI system has formalized Fermat’s last theorem and the impact of Nancy Grace Roman.

records.title: ‘Mother of Hubble’: how Nancy Grace Roman ushered in a new era of astronomy
records.description: The scientist honoured by the newest telescope in space spearheaded a pioneering programme as NASA’s first chief astronomer.

records.title: How countries can grow without impoverishing future generations
records.description: Governments should invest to develop all types of capital, and not just income, to improve the lives of future citizens and to protect the planet.

records.title: Probing the proteome at cellular scale
records.description: Rapid technological advances are allowing researchers to identify thousands of proteins in individual cells, revealing the hidden mechanisms underlying development and disease.

records.title: The secret life of a cell-cycle gatekeeper of breast cancer
records.description: A newly discovered function for the protein Rb explains why inhibiting cell division can enhance the signalling mediated by the oestrogen receptor that drives breast cancer.

records.title: Author Correction: AhR inhibition promotes axon regeneration via a stress–growth switch
Daily briefing: Bunsen burners don’t waft bacteria away from workbenches
records.description: A new study could fuel debate about whether the Bunsen burner still has a place in the modern lab. Plus, the United States is shifting a huge swathe of biomedical research to the military and boat-bashing orcas are just having a good time.

records.title: Author Correction: A mouse brain stereotaxic topographic atlas with isotropic 1-μm resolution
Isaac Newton’s remarkable year — and the plagiarism accusations that followed
records.description: A deep dive into Newton’s major work, Principia Mathematica , reveals his hate of hypotheses and a habit of courting controversy.

records.title: Anthropic AI ‘formalizes’ proof of Fermat’s last theorem — a milestone for mathematics
records.description: Claude produced a 13-million-line, computer-checked proof of the famed conjecture in just 11 days.

records.title: Briefing Chat: How 1,000 pairs of buried underpants helped measure soil health
records.description: Nature staff discuss the winners of the 2026 Ig Nobel prizes — plus, the isolated energy flash that could be the first glimpse of dark matter.

records.title: Super-precise optical clocks in four nations tick in harmony
records.description: Comparison using signals sent over fibre-optic cable tests agreement between seven devices spread across Europe.

records.title: Body parts used for ancient Egyptian artworks traced to surprising source
records.description: Coffin decorations and wall paintings were made with tissue from a broad range of organisms.

records.title: Daily briefing: Psilocybin blocks side-effect of chemotherapy in mice
records.description: Two doses of psilocybin completed prevented debilitating neuropathy in mice. Plus, a new direction for ‘time’s arrow’ and this year’s fun and thought-provoking Ig Nobel prizes.

records.title: Tropical cyclones could be predicted with an extra day’s warning, thanks to an AI model
records.description: The track and intensity of tropical cyclones can be predicted with high accuracy using an AI model, which has the potential to protect lives if shared responsibly worldwide.

records.title: Ada Yonath obituary: Crystallographer who overcame ‘impossible’ challenge of mapping the ribosome
records.description: Nobel laureate persisted despite widespread derision and revolutionized structural biology by protecting fragile crystals.

records.title: Revealed: inside the US military’s plan to tap huge sums from the NIH
records.description: An agreement paves the way for hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of projects to be transferred from the NIH’s institute for infectious diseases to the Department of Defense.

records.title: Bunsen burners’ reputation for sterilizing workplaces flames out
records.description: Study shows that the venerable device does not waft bacteria away from workbenches, as is often assumed.

records.title: Immune therapy engineered inside the body eases multiple sclerosis
records.description: Results from a small trial suggest a modified virus can instruct the immune system to wipe out disease-causing cells.

records.title: Ketone homologation via palladium-catalysed decarboxylative rearrangement
records.description: A Pd(II)/Pd(IV)-catalysed concerted semi-pinacol rearrangement preserves stereochemistry, improves migratory selectivity and avoids hazardous diazo reagents, enabling efficient carbon-skeleton editing in natural-product synthesis.

records.title: Magic-mushroom compound blocks a severe side effect of chemotherapy in mice
records.description: Study shows that psilocybin acts on nerves to prevent the painful condition called peripheral neuropathy.

records.title: Buried underpants and a new definition of kissing win 2026 Ig Nobel prizes
records.description: The awards highlight weird, funny and improbable research that also makes you think.

records.title: Nations expanding their research programmes impose sweeping penalties for malpractice
records.description: India, Peru and Vietnam are rolling out policies that limit opportunities for scientists who fall foul of research-integrity guidelines.

records.title: Daily briefing: GLP-1 obesity drugs slow signs of ageing in mice
records.description: Mice on GLP-1s also performed better on cognitive tasks than those on a calorie restricted diet . Plus, satellite images showed early warning signs of glacier collapse near the Nepal–Tibet border and the impact of people saying fewer words aloud.

records.title: Author Correction: Endocannabinoids facilitate reward engagement through retrograde gain control
Audio long read: Could mending damaged DNA prolong life?
records.description: Researchers are hunting for ways to enhance DNA repair with the hopes that this will keep people healthier for longer.

records.title: Satellite images before Nepal disaster showed warning signs
records.description: Images revealed the accelerated movement of a glacier–rock mass just days before it collapsed and triggered a deadly flash flood.

records.title: Blood cells replace the immune cells of the ageing human brain
records.description: At birth, the brain contains its own immune cells, called microglia, that are thought to persist throughout life without being replaced by cells from outside the brain. Studies that trace cell lineage now show that these cells are replaced by circulating immune cells during ageing, revealing a previously unappreciated interaction between the brain and the rest of the body.

records.title: Weight-loss drug slows ageing in female mice
records.description: In one inbred strain of laboratory mice, late-life treatment with a GLP-1 drug extends lifespan. This effect might be more than just a consequence of calorie restriction.

records.title: Aquatic invertebrates contribute substantially to global nutrient supplies
records.description: An analysis of the nutritional content of aquatic invertebrate species suggests that their global production is a rich source of nutrients that are crucial for human health. The work provides a foundation for better recognition of these valuable invertebrate nutrients and incorporate them into conservation, management and policy efforts.

records.title: UN finally admits global warming will shoot past 1.5 ºC climate limit
records.description: Earth will breach a long-standing target before the end of the decade, report says.

records.title: City of slop
records.description: Home is where you end up.

records.title: When do infections lead to long COVID? Scientists close in on triggers and treatments for post-viral syndromes
records.description: Hundreds of millions of people have long-term conditions as a result of an infection. Researchers are working out how to help them.

records.title: Peruvian ice has preserved a global methane record
records.description: The first record of global methane in the tropics, collected from the summit of the mountain Nevado Huascarán in Peru, fills a crucial gap in historical methane data sets. It improves our understanding of the contribution of tropical sources to the past and current global methane distribution.

records.title: Anxious or outgoing? Huge study links ‘Big Five’ personality traits to genetic variants
records.description: Researchers identify more than 1,200 personality-linked genetic variants, with effects largely independent of family background.

records.title: Can GLP-1 drugs slow ageing? Mouse study shows promise
records.description: Older female mice given an anti-obesity medication lived longer and in better health than did mice not taking one.

records.title: The death of Jason Arday must prompt deep reflection
records.description: Universities and media organizations need to scrutinize their roles in the events that led to this tragedy.

Landmark pancreatic cancer drug shows potential against lung cancer too
records.description: Results bolster hopes that the drug daraxonrasib could prove effective against a variety of tumours.

records.title: Antimatter ‘tag’ used to detect elusive particle decay
records.description: A long-underexplored test of particle-physics theory has been revived. This method uses quantum entanglement to infer the presence of undetectable particles.

records.title: NASA’s Roman telescope holds promise far beyond mapping the invisible Universe
records.description: Discovery flourishes when instruments, ideas and people come together in unpredictable ways.

records.title: Self-driving cars make mistakes, and now users can see why
records.description: An autonomous-vehicle system that directly explains its decisions in a way that can be interpreted by humans could improve driving safety.

records.title: Biomarkers that predict improved outcomes after perioperative immune-based therapy for lung cancer
records.description: Comprehensive exploratory analyses of biomarkers were done in the phase III CheckMate 77T study of pre- and post-surgical treatment with the immunotherapy nivolumab in individuals with surgically resectable non-small-cell lung cancer. The analyses indicate that pre-surgical clearance of circulating tumour DNA, among other markers, is associated with improved clinical outcomes with nivolumab.

records.title: Say hello to the next generation of lobsters — August’s best science images
records.description: The month’s sharpest science shots, selected by Nature ’s photo team.

records.title: Designing physics experiments with artificial intelligence
records.description: Artificial intelligence in physics experimental design is explored on the basis of searching for optima over a vast space of hardware configurations and proposing entirely new experimental layouts, rather than tuning a handful of parameters.

records.title: Creating bottom-up RNA transfer vehicles from synthetic protein assemblies
records.description: Synthetic virus-like protein architectures designed by artificial intelligence show superior ability to deliver RNA into cells, compared with their naturally occurring counterparts, by overcoming the evolutionary constraints limiting viral evolution.

records.title: Late-life semaglutide treatment slows ageing and extends lifespan in female mice
records.description: Semaglutide treatment for 3 months in female mice improved physiological function, attenuated hallmarks of ageing and modulated nutrient sensors and conserved genetic regulators of ageing.

records.title: Robust inference and correlates from genetic associations with personality
records.description: The genetic architecture of personality is robustly generalizable, minimally confounded and widely relevant to human experience.

records.title: Exploring baryon semileptonic decays through polarization and entanglement
records.description: Polarization and quantum entanglement measurements of baryon semileptonic decay greatly enhance single-event sensitivity, and combined with lattice quantum chromodynamics calculations enable determination of the | V us | element of the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa matrix, providing an independent test of the standard model.

records.title: Atmospheric CH 4 plateau sustained by NO x emission rise and southward shift
records.description: The atmospheric methane plateau can be explained by tropical hydroxyl radical enhancement primarily driven by a global rise and spatial redistribution of nitrogen oxides emissions towards developing regions and the oceans.

records.title: Pines grow faster and are more drought resilient in the Southern Hemisphere
records.description: Non-native conifers from the Northern Hemisphere grow faster and are more drought resistant and resilient in the Southern Hemisphere, where they seem to escape the growth–stress-tolerance trade-off.

records.title: Rewiring the ribosome to translate proteins encoded in its own RNA
records.description: Bacterial ribosomes can synthesize proteins encoded within their own RNA.

records.title: Molecular mechanisms and pathogenesis of MASH
records.description: This Review highlights the state of the art of molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying MASH pathogenesis and its transition to hepatocellular carcinoma.

records.title: Explainable deep learning improves human mental models of self-driving cars
records.description: Concept-Wrapper Network, a concept-based explanation approach deployed on a real autonomous vehicle, improves drivers’ ability to understand and predict its behaviour.

records.title: Current therapeutic landscape and future treatment perspectives of MASH
records.description: The therapeutic landscape and advances in biomarkers for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis are reviewed.

records.title: The nutritional value of invertebrate aquatic foods
records.description: Aquatic invertebrates are exceptionally nutrient dense, supplying the equivalent annual vitamin B 12 and selenium requirements for over 5 billion people.

records.title: Intracellular complement factor H protects neurons during CNS inflammation
records.description: CFH is a key mediator of neuronal resilience across the central nervous system in mice and humans.

records.title: Probing far-from-equilibrium dynamics of electrical double layers
records.description: A new framework combining experimental and computational methods to track ions and water present at an electrode interface allows the molecular structure and evolution of electrical double layers far from equilibrium to be discovered.

records.title: Structure and operating principles of a monkeypox virus replisome
records.description: During replisome assembly of monkeypox virus, the hexameric helicase–primase E5 undergoes large-scale conformational changes that allow two of its primase domains to interact with the polymerase F8 thumb domain and A22 subunit, activating the helicase–primase.

records.title: Savannah grass growth in dry conditions is boosted by increased CO 2 levels
records.description: Analysis of 70 experiments and 32 years of field observations shows that increasing the amount of carbon dioxide enhances the growth of the C 4 group of grasses when water is limited. These findings challenge the assumption that C 4 grasses respond weakly to changes in carbon dioxide level, and reveal an overlooked driver of change across the world’s savannahs.

records.title: Systems vaccinology and the architecture of human immunity
records.description: A review of the current state of the field of systems vaccinology discusses the challenges in translating insights into clinical and regulatory practice.

records.title: Ultrafast and reference-free sequence discovery in single-cell data
records.description: Malva enables ultrafast, reference-free searching of raw single-cell sequences across millions of cells, transforming static transcriptomic atlases into dynamic resources for understanding the functions of sequences.

records.title: Cell-type-specific eQTLs underlie the genetic architecture of complex traits
records.description: Single-cell RNA-sequencing shows that cell-type-specific expression quantitative trait loci drive much of complex trait heritability, highlighting cell-type-specific gene regulation as key to linking genetic variants with traits.

records.title: Amphibious stem-insect sheds light on colonization of land
records.description: Restudy of a challenging fossil using cross-polarized light imaging and phylogenetic reconstruction identifies Chosha praecursor , a probable early-diverging insect, helping to bridge the longstanding ‘hexapod gap’ in the fossil record.

records.title: 3D bulk-resolved g -wave altermagnetic order parameter in CrSb
records.description: Quantum oscillation measurements map the g -wave altermagnetic order parameter in CrSb, establishing it as a prototypical unconventional magnet with momentum-dependent spin splitting.

records.title: Tidal tomography reveals a thermal anomaly beneath Mars’s crustal dichotomy
records.description: Analysis of tracking data from Mars orbiters reveals time-variable gravity field behaviour reflecting the structure underlying the Martian crustal dichotomy and indicates the preservation of a 200–400 °C thermal anomaly in the present-day mantle below the southern highlands.

records.title: Synergistic degradation of fucoidans in the ocean
records.description: Efficient degradation of fucoidans depends on complementary bacterial guilds that cooperatively break backbone and side-chain sugars, revealing a conserved, globally relevant mechanism that shapes marine carbon cycling.

records.title: A binding-to-release strategy for targeted anticancer drug delivery
records.description: A binding-to-release drug conjugate strategy enables targeted payload release without cellular internalization, improving tumour specificity, efficacy and expanding therapeutic targets beyond conventional drug conjugates.

records.title: Critical zone processes limit alkalinity export from natural basaltic systems
records.description: Observations from natural volcanic watersheds demonstrate attenuation of alkalinity fluxes along the complete reactive pathways from soil to river that lead to reductions in exported alkalinity, indicating the limiting effects of critical zone processes.

records.title: Aberrant excitatory neuronal ERBB4 promotes Alzheimer’s disease pathology
records.description: Neuroinflammation alone may be dispensable for early synapse loss in Alzheimer’s disease.

records.title: Video reconstruction of variable VLBI observations with neural fields
records.description: The kine neural reconstruction algorithm produces high-resolution, time-continuous very long baseline interferometry videos, enabling direct measurement of instantaneous plasma velocities and detailed kinematic analysis of relativistic astrophysical jets.

records.title: Endocannabinoids facilitate reward engagement through retrograde gain control
records.description: A key role for retrograde neuromodulatory signalling in motivated behaviour is shown through dynamic endocannabinoid release within a thalamostriatal circuit that regulates behavioural engagement during reward seeking.

records.title: Primate-specific regulation of the human glycosphingolipid gatekeeper UGCG
records.description: Cryogenic electron microscopy structures of full-length human UGCG, the gatekeeper that dictates the scale and composition of glycosphingolipid diversity, are reported, showing that it uses a metal-independent catalytic mechanism driven by an arginine network.

records.title: Granule cells reorient cortical trajectories to separate contexts
records.description: Simultaneous imaging of premotor cortex and cerebellar granule cells in mice learning two skills in parallel shows that trajectories generalize in cortex but coherently reorient apart in granule cells, supporting generalization and separation between contexts.

records.title: Long-read sequencing reveals pre-meiotic gene conversion in sperm
records.description: Single-molecule long-read sequencing of human sperm reveals variation in recombination across donors and that a substantial fraction of non-crossover gene conversions arises before meiosis, distinct from PRDM9-driven recombination and associated with fragile sites.

records.title: Infrared absorption spectroscopy of a single polyatomic molecular ion
records.description: Non-destructive single-molecule absorption spectroscopy is achieved by detecting photon recoil from a trapped molecular ion, enabling single-photon-sensitive measurements of molecular vibrational transitions.

records.title: Spontaneously charged water drops induce corrosion
records.description: Experiments have shown that spontaneously charged water drops can damage coatings on metal surfaces, leading to corrosion of the metal.

records.title: Hidden volcanoes hint at Moon’s turbulent past
records.description: A pair of massive shield volcanoes have been pinpointed by lunar spacecraft.

records.title: To shield the fetus, link a protein to these drugs
records.description: Adding albumin to popular antibody-based medicines helps to block their passage through the placenta.

records.title: Astronaut vest cuts radiation exposure in half
records.description: Tests on uncrewed NASA mission showed garment could spare astronauts the worst effects of solar storms.

records.title: These trees are making air quality in cities worse
records.description: They release compounds that contribute to ozone emissions, and rising temperatures could exacerbate the problem.

records.title: Exclusive: NSF set to issue lowest number of new grants in four decades
records.description: The US science-funding agency is withholding $1 billion of its budget so that the money can go to a special White House project.

records.title: Moderna cancer vaccine stops melanoma returning: what’s next for personalized treatments?
records.description: Promising trial results suggest cancer vaccines work and could be used to target other tumours.

records.title: Daily briefing: People older than 100 have more cancer-killing cells
records.description: Killer T cells might help people to live to extraordinarily old ages. Plus, the longest-lived brain organoids so far and how mass genome-screening programmes for newborns might work.

records.title: Investors’ sneak peak: can this AI tool spot the science that will lead to patents?
records.description: The approach could speed up investment decisions, but researchers say it has flaws.

records.title: Staggering 90% of biomedical papers now show signs of AI help
records.description: The figure, which is much higher than previous estimates of large-language-model use, is for papers published in December and archived in PubMed.

records.title: Virus deploys a ‘loose cannon’ enzyme to overpower bacterial defences
records.description: Viruses that infect bacteria must either evade or counter the defence systems of their host. The viral kinase enzyme T7K has been found to phosphorylate nearly all bacterial proteins, but its specificity for DNA-binding proteins enables it to disable defence systems that target nucleic acids.

records.title: South Africa’s scientists must register with official body or risk prison, according to draft law
records.description: Many researchers are unaware of an upcoming law that will require them to register with a regulatory body, as is the case for engineers and health-care professionals.

records.title: How do people live beyond 110? Abundance of cancer-killing cells might be key
records.description: Research on people 110 years and older reveals an immune system that continues to adapt.

records.title: Psychedelics tune the brain to the environment
records.description: Rather than just scrambling neural activity, the psychedelic substance psilocybin also reorganizes brain dynamics so as to align with a person’s context and experiences.

records.title: Screening babies’ genomes could save lives. Here’s how it would work
records.description: Massive genomic newborn-screening studies are under way all over the globe. But questions about scalability, feasibility and net benefit remain.

records.title: Rudolph A. Marcus obituary: theoretical chemist who explained how electrons jump between molecules
records.description: His calculations explain the efficiency of batteries and solar cells.

records.title: AI tool lets researchers ‘vibe code’ in the quantum realm
records.description: An autonomous AI agent can write and execute quantum computing code, but it sometimes needs a human touch.

records.title: Reply to: Artefacts in single-cell mtDNA analyses misinform phylogenies
Computational ‘gym’ trains AI models to control turbulence
records.description: The HydroGym computational environment teaches agents strategies for fluid-flow control that can be applied to scenarios they have not encountered before.

records.title: Delisted
records.description: Called to account.

records.title: Human organoids that mimic brain development grown for years in lab
records.description: Models of how the brain changes over time could help researchers to understand how diseases affect the organ later in life.

records.title: Activity of solar-driven polymer catalysts unleashed to produce a potential green fuel
records.description: Engineering of polymer crystals has vastly increased the activity of these materials as catalysts for producing hydrogen fuel from water, using only sunlight.

records.title: Artefacts in single-cell mtDNA analyses misinform phylogenies
The Antarctic ice sheet has gained mass — but probably not for long
records.description: Since 2020, snowfall has largely counterbalanced the melting of the Antarctic ice sheet. The atmospheric effect that causes this has been identified — and it’s temporary.

records.title: Daily briefing: How 3D printers are changing lab work
records.description: Printing custom lab tools can be cheaper than buying them. Plus, South African scientists might soon have to register with a regulatory body and what an exoskeleton-powered future might look like.

records.title: Functional role of skull lymphoid structures in CNS immunosurveillance
records.description: Functional lymphoid structures within the skull bone marrow enable central nervous system immunosurveillance and shape immune responses to brain disease.

records.title: Observation of conformal field theory spectra in a quantum simulator
records.description: Measurements on an array of optically trapped neutral atoms at a quantum phase transition provide a direct observation of the universal excitation spectrum predicted by conformal field theory.

records.title: Wake-activated neuronal populations that regulate sleep drive
records.description: Whole-brain activity mapping, targeted cell manipulations and electrophysiology in mice identify wake-activated neuronal populations that are crucial for sleep drive and can persistently reduce daily sleep amount.

records.title: Evidence for vacuum-enhanced superconductivity in NbSe 2
records.description: Vacuum fluctuations provide an important new way to control material properties non-invasively and can enhance superconductivity, which is shown by an increase in the critical temperature of superconducting NbSe 2 , a layered transition-metal dichalcogenide.

records.title: Increasing CO 2 levels fertilize C 4 grass production
records.description: By combining a meta-analysis of CO 2 enrichment experiments with three decades of southern African savanna observations, an increase in biomass production by C 4 grasses under rising CO 2 levels in water-limited environments is revealed.

records.title: A global atmospheric methane record from a tropical ice core
records.description: A 2,000-year Peruvian ice core record of atmospheric CH 4 concentrations contains the first historical global CH 4 record from the low latitudes, and implementation of a four-box model indicates higher equatorial CH 4 strength than previous estimates from polar-only records.

records.title: Family genetic designs in MoBa provide insights into health and functioning
records.description: The Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study demonstrates how family-based genomic data can disentangle direct genetic effects from confounding, improving studies of health and human development.

records.title: Asymmetric prefrontal representations for leader–follower dynamics
records.description: Mice spontaneously form leader and follower roles during cooperation, and the medial prefrontal cortex encodes these role dynamics and an egocentric social value map of the partner’s position.

records.title: Atomic-scale double-slit interferometry with a focused electron probe
records.description: Double-slit interferometry at the atomic scale is demonstrated using scanning transmission electron microscopy to provide evidence of interference fringes generated with a focused electron beam encountering two silicon atomic columns separated by 1.36 Å.

records.title: Synthesis of pyrroles from isoxazoles by an O-to-C skeletal edit
records.description: A one-pot skeletal-editing reaction replaces isoxazole oxygen with carbon to form challenging pyrroles, enabled by an N -propargylic enaminone intermediate and a computational model predicting reaction outcomes.

records.title: Human brain organoids record the passage of time over multiple years
records.description: Human brain organoids were developed for over five years in culture to demonstrate that brain cells can continue to mature and record the passage of time, following human-specific endogenous programs, even outside the context of the organism.

records.title: Multiyear tropical warm pool warming drives slowdown in Antarctic mass loss
records.description: Recent Antarctic ice mass gain was linked to a recurrent atmospheric teleconnection, but this recurs about once per decade in observations and historical simulations so does not yet reflect a global-warming-driven moistening of Antarctica.

records.title: The HydroGym reinforcement learning platform for fluid dynamics
records.description: HydroGym offers over 60 standardized reinforcement-learning flow-control environments and demonstrates zero-shot transfer to a 3D wing, cutting local skin friction by 38% and exploration costs by four orders of magnitude.

records.title: An Icelandic pangenome reference
records.description: Newly developed methods enable construction of Icelandic haplotypes and mapping of population-scale short reads to a pangenome by reducing reference bias and improving discovery in low-mappability regions, revealing many novel variants, including pathogenic alleles.

records.title: Psychedelics align brain activity with context
records.description: The psychedelic psilocybin reorganizes brain activity into structured, context-aligned patterns that integrate internal and external processing, providing a neural basis for the felt continuity between self and world, elucidating how the psychedelic state translates into psychological change.

records.title: Discovery of a star sensitive to the spin of Sagittarius A*
records.description: The discovery of the fast-orbiting star S301 near Sagittarius A* offers a promising new probe of the central black hole spin of the Milky Way through relativistic orbit measurements.

records.title: Safety and security of large language models in healthcare
records.description: The Review examines rapid LLM adoption in clinical care, outlining emerging security and safety risks across development stages, key protective layers, clinically relevant threats and current mitigation responsibilities in a single integrated framework.

records.title: Pervasive phosphorylation by phage T7 kinase disarms bacterial defences
records.description: The T7 bacteriophage deactivates bacterial defence systems through T7K phosphorylation of nearly all host and phage proteins during infection.

records.title: A biased allosteric modulator is a molecular glue for β 2 AR dimerization
records.description: AP-7-168, an optimized derivative of a β-arrestin-biased negative allosteric modulator of the β 2 -adrenergic receptor (β 2 AR), functions as a molecular glue to stabilize β 2 AR homodimerization.

records.title: Heatwaves expose weak links in food systems

records.title: Will you be wearing an exoskeleton in ten years? The tech that could change how we move
records.description: Robotic supports were once designed for clinical use, but researchers are now developing cheaper, smaller devices aimed at everyone — from people with ageing knees to 20-somethings seeking to climb mountains.

records.title: Mathematics holds the secret to ‘ladder-proof’ knitting

records.title: Daily briefing: ‘Too hot to sleep’ is harmful to your health

records.title: NIH proposes major revamp of how it scores research grant proposals
records.description: Proponents argue that the current system creates a false sense of precision, but critics fear that the change could increase political interference.

records.title: Five ways 3D printing is improving lab work
records.description: As 3D printers become cheaper and easier to work with, researchers are finding new ways to incorporate the technology in their studies.

records.title: A revolutionary stem-cell therapy must proceed responsibly to achieve its full potential
records.description: It is 20 years since induced pluripotent stem cells shook biomedicine. Public trust must be retained now that clinical trials are well under way.

records.title: How the Middle East can become a hub for sustainable aviation fuels
records.description: Building on the region’s oil infrastructure, investment funds and shipping corridors, Gulf nations can thrive in the clean-energy economy.

records.title: Positional isomerization of pyridine through nitrogen transposition
records.description: Pyridine positional isomerization can be enabled by controlled reorganization of the heteroaromatic core through sequential nitrogen insertion and deletion.

records.title: Too hot to sleep? How heatwaves at night affect our health
records.description: As climate change ramps up, scientists must urgently understand how night-time heat makes it harder for our bodies to rest and recover.

records.title: Daily briefing: Narcolepsy drug could kick off an Ozempic-style moment for the brain

records.title: Universities must stop protecting bullies — or more people will leave science

records.title: Why AI systems are most useful as designers of new scientific tools

records.title: Programmable remodelling of carbon–nitrogen connectivity in amines
records.description: Tertiary benzylamines can be transformed from static scaffolds into programmable platforms for molecular diversification through catalytic remodelling of their C–N bonds.

records.title: Defect passivation and optical management of triple-junction solar cells
records.description: A passivating molecule and optimized light management enable perovskite/perovskite/silicon triple-junction solar cells to achieve certified efficiencies up to 32.22%, advancing scalable high-performance photovoltaics.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Anthropic rolls out new AI watermark — will it make a difference?

records.title: Ultrafast temporal engineering of optical properties using terahertz light

Bow shocks reveal how a dying star returns matter to interstellar space
records.description: Deep imaging of ionized gas in the Helix Nebula uncovers many curved shock waves around a dying Sun-like star. These ‘bow shocks’ are produced when ejected shells of stellar material break up and race outwards. Their changing shapes imply that the shell fragments are being stripped, shredded and mixed into interstellar gas over roughly 10,000 years.
