records.description: High sea surface temperatures are expected to weaken ocean carbon sinks and damage coral reefs.

records.title: No single rule explains how climate affects carbon storage in tropical forests
records.description: Ecologists have long wondered why some tropical forests store more carbon than others. A global satellite survey offers an explanation.

records.title: Trump wants MMR vaccine split up: the science behind why it’s a bad idea
records.description: Numerous studies have shown that separating childhood jabs will delay protection and increase costs for families.

records.title: Agentic profiles for effective AI governance
records.description: A framework comprising four dimensions—autonomy, efficacy, goal complexity and generality—is proposed for characterizing AI agents, supporting the construction of agentic profiles for the effective governance of different AI agents.

records.title: Cascading continental-scale floods across Europe in 1342–1343
records.description: Tracing cascading continental-scale medieval megafloods across Europe indicates that current flood management is unprepared for such sequences, highlighting the urgent need for proactive flood risk management strategies that account for unusual series of extreme flood events.

records.title: Lead carboxylates passivation for metre-scale perovskite solar modules
records.description: Chemically stable lead carboxylates are used as surface passivators for engineered perovskite films to manufacture metre-scale solar modules that can achieve record-high certified efficiencies, as well as passing all IEC 61215 reliability tests.

records.title: Rb-driven transcription limits its tumour-suppressive effects in breast cancer
records.description: CDK4/6 inhibition redirects Rb chromatin occupancy to activate oestrogen-responsive genes, counteracting its own ability to maintain therapeutic cell-cycle arrest.

records.title: Procognitive restoration of PV neuron plasticity in neurodevelopmental disorders
records.description: Expression of Meis2 in hippocampal parvalbumin-expressing interneurons in an adult mouse model of neurodevelopmental disorders rescues experience-dependent plasticity, improves memory and network function and suppresses seizures.

records.title: A gas-enshrouded and gas-reddened black hole at cosmic dawn
records.description: Observations of an unusual cosmic-dawn source illuminate how early supermassive black holes may have grown rapidly in a gas-enshrouded state; such enshrouded black holes may lie at the heart of the 'little red dots'.

records.title: Towards an equitable future of global photovoltaic waste recycling
records.description: Global photovoltaic waste will reach 297–402 million tonnes by 2060, and regionally adapted recycling strategies and international cooperation will be needed to provide equitable and scalable PV waste circularity.

records.title: Luminescent-reaction-enabled super-resolution imaging
records.description: A new chemistry-based super-resolution imaging framework is described, enabling 3D, laser-free, highly sensitive and ultralong-term imaging of live cells which overcomes the limitations in spatiotemporal resolution associated with reaction-based imaging methods.

records.title: Degree-of-polarization modulation for high-dimensional optical computing
records.description: By engineering the statistics of light at the micrometre scale using phase-only spatial light modulators, both the state and degree of polarization become spatially programmable, enabling direct encoding of information in a high-dimensional space.

records.title: Neural basis of compositional control
records.description: Behaviour of human participants in a prey-pursuit task reflects dynamic blending of goal-specific control policies, with hippocampus estimating latent states, anterior cingulate cortex orchestrating policy switches and orbitofrontal cortex supplying value-based contextualization rather than driving continuous policy updating.

records.title: Structural mechanism governing the directionality of bridge recombination
records.description: Cryo-electron microscopy structures show how IS621 bridge recombinase mediates DNA excision, explaining its natural preference for insertion and informing the design of programmable bridge-editing technologies.

records.title: Species intraspecific variation drives tropical forest drought resistance
records.description: Substantial intraspecific variation, together with species turnover, drives coordinated shifts in drought resistance such as increased embolism resistance and wider stomatal safety margins in drier forests.

records.title: Numerous bow shocks in the outer Helix Nebula
records.description: Shocks in the eastern outskirts of the Helix Nebula, detected in Hα emission with the MOTHRA telescope, provide evidence for the recycling of fragmented stellar ejecta into the surrounding gas.

records.title: Maternal influences on infant gut microbiome and health
records.description: The maternal gut microbiome is a predictor of infant eczema.

records.title: Evidence for the first globular cluster stellar stream beyond the Milky Way
records.description: Deep Hubble Space Telescope imaging of the ultra-diffuse galaxy UGC 9050-Dw1 reveals an extragalactic globular cluster stream, with analysis and modelling probing the rich dark matter content of the host galaxy.

records.title: Heterogeneous climatic controls on tropical-forest biomass
records.description: An analysis of the relationships between aboveground biomass and various climatic factors in three major regions of tropical forest shows that understanding the complex interactions between climate, topography and soils is crucial to predict how climate change will affect carbon storage capacity.

records.title: Superconducting 2D cuprate with a single CuO 2 plane
records.description: A high-quality, pristine monolayer cuprate superconductor with a single CuO 2 plane is fabricated and used to identify two quantum critical phenomena emerging between the Mott insulating phase and the superconducting phase.

records.title: In vivo genome-wide CRISPR screens of human T cells in solid tumours
records.description: An in vivo model that is able to recover human T cells from solid tumours can identify targets to help improve CAR T cell antitumour activity.

records.title: Biomarkers of nivolumab benefit in resectable non-small cell lung cancer
records.description: Potential predictive biomarkers of perioperative nivolumab therapy benefit in non-small cell lung cancer are identified from evaluable participants in the CheckMate 77T trial.

records.description: Dyna-1 was trained on missing data from nuclear magnetic resonance depositions and predicts µs–ms dynamics, often linked to biological function, including enzyme catalysis and ligand binding.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Is DNA repair the secret to a long life? Whales and mole rats offer tantalizing hints
records.description: Nature staff discuss how animal studies are starting to uncover how DNA repair could prolong life, and how COVID-19 can reawaken dormant viruses.

records.title: Universal vaccine for pneumococcal disease moves closer to reality
records.description: Targeting shared proteins could help to control bacterial subtypes that current vaccines do not protect against.

records.title: Pumas are drivers’ guardian angels
records.description: Vehicles are less likely to smash into deer on the road where the big cats are on patrol.

records.title: How a steady drip-drip can erode the hardest stone
records.description: Measuring the deformation of a surface hit by a falling droplet offers insights into water’s erosive power.

records.title: Heatwaves have killed millions. Here’s how scientists tally lives lost
records.description: Two very different methods are used to estimate the human toll of heatwaves such as those now hitting parts of Asia and Europe.

records.title: AI agents are checking the scientific literature — and spotting decades-old errors
records.description: The technology is proving adept at finding faults in decades-old papers and reference databases.

records.title: Scientists up in arms about cuts to UK physics and astronomy
records.description: Funding is being terminated for projects including a future CERN experiment and the iconic Lovell Telescope.

records.title: Levitating sensor for magnetic fields could detect ultrafaint brain activity
records.description: The device’s simple design could rival much more complex alternatives in biophysics research — and could even be used to search for dark matter.

records.title: Operational tropical cyclone forecasting with AI
records.description: An AI forecasting system called WeatherNext Cyclones can predict the track, intensity (maximum wind speed) and size of tropical cyclones with an accuracy gain over leading operational models comparable to a decade of progress in numerical forecasting.

records.title: Junk plastic turns into high-value commodity with chemistry trick
records.description: Researchers untangle the chemistry behind turning PVC into high-grade motor lubricant — plus, how engineered yeast can help make a cancer drug.

records.title: Junk plastic turns into high-value commodity with chemistry trick
records.description: Researchers untangle the chemistry behind turning PVC into high-grade motor lubricant — plus, how engineered yeast can help make a cancer drug.

records.title: James Bond, not Bond James: why scientific publishing must respect name order
records.description: Databases and submission systems are often inflexible. Can’t publishers do more on author names?

records.title: Can empty space interact with light — and even change its properties?
records.description: Observations of a magnetized stellar core indicate that in an ultra-strong magnetic field, empty space can polarize light.

records.title: Maps of chromosomal regions crucial for cell division reveal high diversity
records.description: Centromeres are regions of chromosomes that are required for cell division. Complete sequence characterization of centromeres from a diverse group of 65 individuals reveals dynamic and rapid patterns of mutational change, providing information about centromere evolution and function.

records.title: Exclusive: the science papers that patents cite the most
records.description: Nature reveals the studies that are mentioned most often in patent filings — and why.

records.title: More muscle, less belly fat: mutations to a gene are linked to wide-ranging benefits
records.description: Analysis of one million diverse genomes yields mutations associated with lower risk of diabetes, heart disease and other ‘cardiometabolic’ conditions.

records.title: First poo transplant to treat food allergy in people has ‘exciting’ results
records.description: Existing treatments for food allergy are limited.

records.title: COVID can wake up a slew of dormant viruses inside you
records.description: Reactivation of typically harmless anelloviruses, in particular, seems to be linked with developing long COVID, study finds.

records.title: Switching off the FNIP1 gene protects against metabolic disease
records.description: A study of more than one million people shows that rare genetic variants that disrupt the FNIP1 gene are associated with a favourable metabolic profile and a roughly 60% lower risk of cardiometabolic disease than the general population. Silencing genes in the FNIP1 pathway in mice induces fat breakdown and reproduces the metabolic benefits associated with the variants in humans.

records.title: The recovered notes of Professor Alborough
records.description: Time for a break.

records.title: Neanderthal gene makes some modern humans taller and more muscular
records.description: The ancient genetic variant is most common in people of South and East Asian ancestry.

records.title: Why science must reinforce its social contract
records.description: Questions of public trust can be addressed only through better communication and research that meets society’s interests.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Progressive plasticity during colorectal cancer metastasis
Editorial Expression of Concern: Tumour exosome integrins determine organotropic metastasis
An expanded codebook of human transcription factor DNA-binding specificity
records.description: Results from a panel of assays that analyse different aspects of DNA sequence specificity reveal more than 100 new motifs to aid the characterization of putative human transcription factors.

records.title: Thermally evaporated perovskite/silicon tandems via formamidinium eutectic
records.description: A formamidinium-based eutectic enables low-temperature perovskite evaporation, producing efficient, scalable and durable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells with minimal efficiency loss over large areas.

records.title: Ubiquitous Kelvin–Helmholtz instabilities driving plasma mixing on the Sun
records.description: High-spatial-resolution observations of the solar photosphere reveal a far more complex and dynamic solar scene than previously observed and show that ubiquitous Kelvin–Helmholtz instabilities drive plasma mixing on the Sun.

records.title: ZFP36L2 orchestrates stress-adaptive plasticity in regeneration and cancer
records.description: The RNA-binding protein ZFP36L2 mediates stress-adaptive plasticity in intestinal regeneration and colorectal cancer metastasis.

records.title: In situ particle-to-fibre transformation of hydrogels for 3D printing
records.description: A three-dimensional printing method transforms hydrogel particles into aligned microfibres during extrusion, creating structural anisotropy to accelerate muscle tissue regeneration.

records.title: Amygdala astrocyte primary cilium mechanisms contribute to stress behaviours
records.description: Amygdala astrocyte primary cilia are disrupted during stress, and their restoration leads to improvements in stress-related behaviour in mice.

records.title: The Virtual Tissues foundation model resolves spatial proteomics across scales
records.description: Virtual Tissues (VirTues), a foundation model for spatial proteomics that captures tissue organization across scales, supports marker reconstruction, cell segmentation and typing, niche annotation, spatial biomarker discovery and patient stratification across heterogeneous panels and datasets.

records.title: Virus reactivation in acute and long COVID-19
records.description: Chronic reactivation of distinct herpesviruses and anelloviruses occur during acute and long COVID-19, and track with disease severity, inflammation and outcomes, revealing immune signatures with prognostic potential.

records.title: Uncovering the mechanism of female restitution in sugarcane hybrids
records.description: Female restitution in interspecific sugarcane hybrids between Saccharum officinarum and Saccharum spontaneum arises from second division restitution, as haplotype-resolved F 1 genomes reveal duplicated, partially recombined maternal chromatids and distinctive recombination signatures, resolving its meiotic mechanism and enabling breeding strategies to accelerate crop improvement.

records.title: Pseudogap in a Fermi–Hubbard quantum simulator
records.description: A cold-atom quantum simulator reveals the pseudogap metallic state in the Hubbard model, mapping its phase diagram and advancing understanding of doped Mott insulators and high-temperature superconductivity.

records.title: Membranolytic peptide programs immunogenic cell death for cancer therapy
records.description: The synthetic-acid-responsive membranolytic peptide aMP C16 -CA 5 0 induces immunogenic membranolytic cell death in tumour cells, robustly potentiating immune checkpoint blockade therapy.

records.title: A tumour-derived organoid biobank maps cancer gene dependencies
records.description: A clinically annotated multi-omic organoid resource with matched tumour samples from 256 patients across 5 cancers maps gene dependencies, reveals subtype-specific vulnerabilities and uncovers treatment-driven changes, expanding mechanistic insight and models for precision oncology.

records.title: DCAF11-dependent molecular glue degrader activated by glutathionylation
records.description: M12 is a metabolically activated molecular glue that recruits diverse proteins to DCAF11 for ubiquitin-mediated degradation, revealing a glutathione-dependent mechanism that broadens targeted protein degradation across multiple substrates.

records.title: A cholinergic hub in the nucleus accumbens gates opioid-reward learning
records.description: Cell-type-specific opioid blockade in accumbal cholinergic interneurons abolishes morphine-reward learning without impairing analgesia and decouples morphine-evoked dopamine elevations from acetylcholine dips, suggesting pro-cholinergic strategies to limit early opioid reward acquisition.

records.title: Vacuum birefringence and the polarized X-ray emission from a radio magnetar
records.description: Polarization measurements of the magnetar 1E 1547.0−5408 provide strong evidence that vacuum birefringence shapes X-ray propagation, offering an important observational test of quantum electrodynamics in extreme magnetic fields.

records.title: An ancient mitochondrial program tunes translation to haem availability
records.description: An evolutionarily conserved mitochondrial haem-sensing mechanism that predates the emergence of haemoglobin-based oxygen transport could have therapeutic value in iron deficiency disorders.

records.title: FNIP1 variants are associated with favourable metabolism in 1 million humans
records.description: The FNIP1 pathway has a role in human energy metabolism, and its inhibition is a potential therapeutic strategy in cardiometabolic disease.

records.description: Sustaining the region’s strong position in the life-sciences sector will require investment and education in bioengineering.

records.title: Privacy risks from medical AI tools are not shared equally
records.description: Privacy attacks can reveal whether someone’s medical data was used to train an AI model. People who differ from the majority are the most vulnerable to such attacks.

records.title: NSF rolls out ‘industry PhD’ programme — joining a global trend
records.description: The US pilot programme will provide financial support for four years to more than 250 students, who will gain industry experience.

How I explore trauma through ‘cinematic neuroscience’
records.description: Combining scientific research and artistic expression helped neuroscientist Shaira Berg to find her niche.

records.title: Could mending damaged DNA prolong life?
records.description: Inspired by long-lived animals — and human centenarians — researchers are hunting for ways to enhance DNA repair and extend healthspan.

records.title: The three-and-beyond-body problem: juggling kids, travel and careers in academia
records.description: The issues faced by scientist-couples can be multiplied once they start a family, making conference travel a logistical trial.

records.title: Sickle-cell disease linked to prematurely aged stem cells in mice
records.description: A combination of drugs restores stem-cell function in mouse models of the blood disorder.

records.title: Venus’s rift valleys could be its secret to staying active
records.description: The nature of geological dynamics on Venus are fiercely debated — the planet’s steep rift valleys could be evidence of ongoing tectonic activity.

Plans for nuclear-powered merchant ships must confront risks
records.description: Vessels propelled by atomic reactors have low emissions but create other hazards that need clear regulations.

records.title: Cancer-fighting antibodies with a one-two punch take aim at tumours
records.description: Bispecific antibodies, which bind to two targets, are sweeping into the clinic and are prompting even more elaborate versions.

records.title: Science-backed tips on how to avoid distractions
records.description: Struggling to stay focused in the lab? Attention researchers offer some advice.

records.title: ‘A waste of time for all of us’: caught in the crossfire of the peer-review wars
records.description: Review mills — researchers who write fake referee reports with coercive citation requests — are setting off a war in academic publishing. What happens to those caught in the middle?

records.title: Gasdermin D-mediated delivery of caspase inhibitors to suppress pyroptosis
records.description: Covalent, membrane-impermeable caspase inhibitors exploit transient GSDMD pore formation to enter pyroptotic cells, selectively blocking caspase-1 and caspase-11-driven pyroptosis and IL-1β and IL-18 release, enabling targeted suppression of inflammatory pathology in vivo.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Orcas smashed a sunfish to bits — researchers aren’t sure why
records.description: Nature staff discuss a massive survey of insects in the Amazon, and unusual orca behaviour caught on video.

records.title: The physics of fizz: why some bubbles are louder than others
records.description: A high-speed camera and underwater microphones help scientists to investigate a puzzle about bubbles.

records.title: Brains of male and female mice recover differently from ketamine
records.description: Specialized immune cells found in the brain, known as microglia, reach out to neurons in female mice that were given a dose of ketamine anaesthetic.

records.title: The power of ignorance and peering into the Milky Way: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: Meat allergy is on the rise — what scientists want to know
records.description: The allergy is caused by ticks, but researchers have much to learn about it.

records.description: Research suggests that the combination of incentives to publish and the use of large language models will lead to more papers, but they will be less refined.

records.description: Researchers are looking for ways to extract the metal from underground reservoirs that use less water in the process.

records.title: Fires in Europe are breaking records: here’s what the future holds
records.description: Countries such as Spain and France can expect fire regimes more like those of California as climate change favours hot, dry conditions, scientists suggest.

records.description: New discoveries at famous archeological site add to mystery of ancient human culture.

records.title: How silicon-chip technology is being re-engineered for quantum computing
records.description: Two demonstrations of silicon-based quantum processors tackle the engineering challenges of building scalable quantum computers.

records.title: Quantum meets capitalism: how to pair long-term bets on technology with commercial speed
records.description: Quantum computing exists because governments funded risky bets. Capitalism can carry it the rest of the way — if quantum scientists are supported.

records.title: Papers with open peer-review reports are less likely to be retracted
records.description: Researchers say that transparent publishing practices could be associated with research quality, but more evidence is needed.

records.title: A guide to the Nature Index
records.description: A description of the terminology and methodology used in this supplement, and a guide to the functionality that is available free online at natureindex.com.

records.title: Polio will come roaring back if the task of eradicating it isn’t finished soon
records.description: Eliminating polio is within reach — if countries see it as an essential public-health priority.

records.description: A lost world.

records.title: Electric dipoles go sideways in thin ferroelectric film
records.description: Coupling between horizontal and vertical electric polarization enables an unconventional ferroelectric material to be controlled using standard device geometry.

records.title: Can long COVID be prevented? Two drugs finally show promise
records.description: Rigorous trials suggest the treatments reduce the risk of long-term disease after coronavirus infection.

records.title: Three rising stars of nanoscience and nanotechnology
records.description: The smallest building blocks are enabling next-generation solutions.

records.title: Daily briefing: Ice-age art hints at how humans flourished
records.description: Tiny bird figurines hint at the sophistication of Europe’s earliest Homo sapiens . Plus, open peer-review reports are less likely to be retracted and a mission to fly over dangerous ‘fire clouds’.

records.title: How fruit flies track the edge of odour plumes
records.description: Ants and bees are known to use spatial memories to navigate to fixed locations, such as a nest. Virtual-reality experiments in which Drosophila fruit flies follow fictive odour plumes now show that these insects use components of a similar memory-guided navigational toolkit to track the edge of a plume towards its source.

records.title: This AI Raygun can shrink and supersize proteins — opening the door to easy editing
records.description: The model can modify existing proteins using a probability approach.

records.title: Intestinal stem cells count to eight divisions to maintain cell ratios
records.description: In the fly gut, stem cells keep the balance of cell types by undergoing eight rounds of cell division to form absorptive cells, then one round to form secretory cells.

records.title: How mosquitoes are conquering the world — in four charts
records.description: Mosquito-borne diseases are breaking records as climate change and other human influences allow the insects to expand their range.

records.title: How mosquitoes are conquering the world — in four charts
records.description: Mosquito-borne diseases are breaking records as climate change and other human influences allow the insects to expand their range.

records.title: To help children with rare diseases, we must solve drug delivery
records.description: Nanoparticle technologies hold promise for delivering gene therapies to children with few treatment options.

records.title: The first known cephalopod was only a millimetre long and lived about 520 million years ago
records.description: The locomotion of modern cephalopods, such as squid and cuttlefish, relies on buoyancy control achieved mainly by a specialized structure called a siphuncle. The discovery of fossils of Eoceras — a millimetre-sized cephalopod with a siphuncle — suggests that the group had already emerged in the early Cambrian, around 520 million years ago.

records.title: Amazonian earthwork survey indicates ancient population was much larger than thought
records.description: Aerial laser-scanning data reveal that, from ad 100 to ad 300, an area spanning less than 3% of the Greater Amazonia region probably supported between 1.25 million and 3 million people and contained more than 20,000 human-made earthworks. These findings call for a re-evaluation of the density of pre-colonial Amazonian populations and the influence these civilizations had on present-day tropical soils and forests.

records.title: Relatively few Black people benefited in the 1930s and 1940s from mortgages backed by the US government
records.description: Newly digitized mortgage records from 38 US states reveal the profound racial inequality of two mortgage programmes during the 1930s and 1940s. These loans, supported by the Federal Housing Administration and the Veterans Administration, were mainly responsible for the emergence of a US society that idealized home ownership. However, Black households were systematically excluded from receiving such loans. By contrast, immigrants received mortgages proportional to their number.

records.title: Artificial algal blooms could remove atmospheric carbon — but can they be used responsibly?
records.description: Adding iron to the ocean to stimulate carbon-absorbing phytoplankton could have ecological consequences that reach far beyond the intervention site.

records.title: Relapsed childhood cancers show genomic scars left by previous therapy
records.description: Whole-genome sequencing of hundreds of childhood tumours, enriched for pretreated, relapsed and metastatic samples, shows that cancer therapies, especially platinum-based ones, are associated with rapid acquisition of distinctive patterns of DNA damage. These mutational signatures are linked with worse outcomes and could be used to track relapses and guide treatment decisions.

records.title: Underdog ‘spin qubits’ leap forward in race to a useful quantum computer
records.description: Four independent research teams report big advances in devices built with the underestimated quantum-bit technology, including lower error rates.

records.title: Obituary: Susumu Tonegawa, Japan’s first Nobel prizewinner in physiology or medicine
records.description: Fearless molecular biologist who revealed the workings of antibodies and memories.

records.title: The piezochiral effect
records.description: The piezochiral effect, a new member of the family of strain-responsive functionalities alongside piezoelectricity and piezomagnetism, is introduced, enabling control of chirality through mechanical strain, with future applications in photonics, spintronics, biosensing and quantum information.

records.title: 40,000-year-old bird carvings provide clues to how ice age humans flourished
records.description: Newly discovered figurines point to skills that might have helped shape early humans’ expansion across Europe.

records.title: The dark horse of biology: how RNA is becoming a nanotool maker’s dream
records.description: Scientists are harnessing its ability to fold, switch and reorganize itself to create a new generation of cellular technologies.

records.title: Diverse bacterial pattern recognition receptors sense the core phage proteome
records.description: Systematic analysis of prokaryotic STAND NTPases — relatives of animal and plant immune receptors — uncovers diverse antiviral sensors that detect most of the core structural and replicative proteins of bacteriophages.

records.title: Mitochondrial metabolism and epigenetic crosstalk drive SASP
records.description: In senescent cells, mitochondria-derived acetyl-CoA promotes histone acetylation and increases chromatin accessibility at inflammatory gene loci. Inhibition of SLC25A1 attenuates these effects, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting mitochondrial metabolism and its epigenetic crosstalk to delay age-related functional decline.

records.title: Alternating CO 2 and bicycloalkane copolymerization to circular polyesters
records.description: A simple organic catalyst enables direct alternating copolymerization of CO 2 with bicycloalkanes to produce high-performance polyesters that can be selectively depolymerized and recycled in a closed-loop lifecycle.

records.title: Avalanche-like intercalation and intraparticle correlations in graphite
records.description: Operando optical microscopy shows avalanche-like lithium deintercalation (intercalation) processes as the dilute stages of graphite are emptied (filled), showing how local disorder governs phase-transition dynamics and ion transport in lithium-ion battery electrodes.

records.title: Sequential reading of a stepwise-shortened peptide immobilized on nanopore
records.description: A nanopore-based ‘chop and measure’ method sequences peptides at single-amino-acid resolution by using enzymatic digestion to progressively shorten the N terminus one residue at a time, together with repetitive N-terminus re-reading.

records.title: Perpendicular switching of polarization in layered ferroelectrics
records.description: Perpendicular switching of the polarization state in the layered ferroelectric Bi 4 Ti 3 O 12 is demonstrated by means of trilinear coupling, allowing manipulation of the in-plane polarization component with an out-of-plane electric field.

records.title: New-deal mortgage programmes benefited white borrowers disproportionately
records.description: New data on homebuying loan records around the Second World War in the USA, linked to race and immigration status, show that Black borrowers were disproportionally excluded from mortgage programmes.

records.title: Weight-four parity checks in a spin-shuttling architecture
records.description: A silicon spin-qubit device comprising a shuttling bus for transporting qubits is used to achieve parity checks up to weight four, highlighting the feasibility and benefits of incorporating shuttling into semiconductor quantum processors.

records.title: Enzymatic glycosylation and amidation reshapes polyene bioactivity
records.description: Pathways to previously undescribed polyenes, including unusual enzymes that introduce more sugars onto polyene scaffolds, are discovered, and their accessibility through clean and efficient fermentation and potential for safe use as antifungal treatments is described.

records.title: A digitally controlled silicon quantum processing unit
records.description: A silicon quantum processing unit executes high-fidelity multiqubit circuits, with all time-varying control signals generated by a digitally programmed cryogenic complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor controller and delivered to the low-noise, exchange-only qubit device through a high-density superconducting ribbon cable.

records.title: A global view of human centromere variation and evolution
records.description: Complete sequencing of more than 2,000 centromeres from diverse humans reveals structures and elevated mutation rates that shape the evolution of these critically important regions.

records.title: Rational design of disordered proteins for sequence–function investigation
records.description: GOOSE enables the design and testing of thousands of disordered protein region sequences to reveal distinct sequence-to-function relationships.

records.title: In situ structure of the poxvirus portal complex
records.description: Cryo-electron tomography uncovers the structure of a conserved hexameric ‘portal complex’ that spans the core wall in vaccinia virus, and shows how it is associated with viral functions such as assembly, mRNA release and genome uncoating.

records.title: Plasmonic metamaterial time crystal
records.description: A plasmonic metamaterial driven at terahertz frequencies achieves strong, ultrafast temporal modulation and shows a transition to the photonic time crystal regime with reduced plasmonic losses.

records.title: Earliest siphuncle-bearing cephalopod from the early Cambrian
records.description: Early Cambrian Eoceras shaanxiense gen. et sp. nov. preserves septa and a segmented tube resembling a primordial siphuncle, extending cephalopod origins and revealing early assembly of chambered shells used for buoyancy regulation.

records.title: Octahedral-coordinated Co 3 O 4 for water electrolysis in acid
records.description: A new trigonal-phase Co 3 O 4 manufactured using a vacuum-mediated molten-alkali mechanochemical method is described, demonstrating edge-shared octahedral coordination and achieving lower overpotential than spinel-type Co 3 O 4 in the acidic oxygen evolution reaction, with reduced dissolution of cobalt.

records.title: In situ structures of plant photosystem supercomplexes
records.description: The cryo‑EM structure of the Oryza sativa photosystem II–light harvesting complex II supercomplex in its native membrane reveals the intact plant photosystem architecture, retaining physiologically relevant proteins and lipids that are otherwise lost during purification.

records.title: Photocatalytic water splitting by 2D polymer with out-of-plane carrier flow
records.description: A strategy using polymeric carbon nitride crystals induces out-of-plane carrier migration by means of internal electric fields applied on facet-selective nanofilms placed on polymer photocatalysts, increasing the apparent quantum efficiency for overall water splitting.

records.title: Climate benefit and ecological cost trade-offs for ocean iron fertilization
records.description: A process-rich global biogeochemical model is used to determine the trade-offs between carbon dioxide removal efficiency and ecosystem impacts in ten ocean ocean biomes following ocean iron fertilization.

records.title: Over 20,000 precolonial earthworks in the Southwest Amazonia
records.description: Using canopy-penetrating LiDAR data, the northern part of southwestern Amazonia appears to contain as many earthworks as previously estimated for the whole of Amazonia.

records.title: Miniaturizing and modifying natural proteins with Raygun
records.description: Probabilistic sequence encoding from language model embeddings within a generative AI framework enables protein miniaturization, modification and augmentation while maintaining native architecture and functional integrity.

records.title: Cretaceous zhelestid mammals are zalambdalestoids
records.description: New Mongolian fossil evidence shows zhelestids were not placental-like herbivore relatives, but a dental variant within Zalambdalestoidea, with distinctive molars alongside zalambdalestid skull and limb traits.

records.title: Intestinal stem cells count self-renewal divisions to switch multipotency
records.description: In Drosophila , cell fate switching in adult intestinal stem cells is determined through an epigenetic mechanism in which these cells count divisions, switching from producing enterocytes to producing an enteroendocrine mother cell every ninth division.

records.title: The past and future impact of climate change on childhood malaria in Africa
records.description: Climate and econometric modelling reveal that human-induced climate change is shifting the burden of childhood malaria in Africa.

Values in science go beyond politics
Deserts face unprecedented flash flooding
It’ll grow on you: live fungi formed into sustainable fashion
records.description: Textile made from fungal filaments can repair itself and is biodegradable.

records.title: Why some wool is wavy
records.description: How crimps form in the coats of sheep, and the history of the word ‘ionosphere’, in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: Wildfires rampaged across Europe in the dying days of the Triassic
records.description: Infernos ravaged continental expanses of ferns during mass extinction of land and sea animals.

records.title: Conversational AI: align commercial incentives with public interests
Fertility clinics are offering young mitochondria in controversial fertility technique
records.description: Researchers are alarmed that the procedure, which has not been rigorously studied, is being advertised by clinics around the world.

records.title: Skin cancer spreads between catfish in a freshwater lake
records.description: The discovery of a transmissible melanoma in a freshwater catfish raises questions about the disease’s origin, mode of transmission and broader impact on the species.

records.title: When physicians and AI work together, who is accountable? How to lay out medical liability
records.description: A staging system based on how big a role AI has in patient care can help to identify who is responsible in cases in which care fails.

records.title: First volunteer gets Ebola vaccine — three months after the outbreak began
records.description: The University of Oxford has already vaccinated its first clinical-trial participant. The study’s lead scientist, Teresa Lambe, tells Nature how the team was able to move so fast.

records.title: Daily briefing: Why all living cells emit a faint glow
records.description: The emission of ‘biophotons’ could be a cell’s way of communicating with its neighbours. Plus, a ‘timer’ in the brain that tracks sleep and who is accountable when physicians and AI work together.

records.title: First mission to fly through monstrous ‘fire clouds’ is about to take off
records.description: The towering formations appearing over severe wildfires in France and Oregon loft smoke so high they have global consequences.

records.title: Medical AI has a measurement problem
records.description: The development of two medical AI assistants highlights an unnerving challenge: as the technology races ahead, what is the best way to evaluate what works?

records.title: All living things emit a faint glow. Could this light be useful?
records.description: Ultra-weak ‘biophotons’ might be used to diagnose disease, or could even represent a new signalling mechanism in cells.

records.title: Led by the nose: a queen’s scent shapes naked mole rat society
records.description: Naked mole rats live in colonies characterized by having a single breeding queen. It emerges that a queen-associated chemical helps to maintain this reproductive hierarchy.

records.title: Consciousness research is having an AI moment. Will the hype help the field?
records.description: The idea of AI sentience is drawing more focus to consciousness science. But some researchers aren’t sure that’s a good thing.

records.title: Entangled dual-site migration through boracycle rearrangement
records.description: Entangled dual-site migration is enabled by a process termed the borinane rearrangement—a lead-and-follow movement of a borinane ring along the carbon backbone.

records.title: Daily briefing: The town heated by one big battery
records.description: A sand battery can keep Pornainen, Finland, toasty for up to a week in winter. Plus, UK physics facilities face a funding threat and examine MAHA health claims under the microscope.

records.title: The existential choice facing UK physics facilities: commercialize or close
records.description: The national synchrotron source, a laser facility and a particle accelerator are under threat of closure unless cash is found.

records.title: ‘Timer’ in the brain tracks sleep — and predicts awakening
records.description: Chemical tags on proteins could provide a biomarker for sleep deprivation, mouse studies suggest.

records.title: When should you treat a fever? Evolution holds the answer
records.description: Understanding natural selection can improve medical treatments, social policies and crop yields.

records.title: How to prevent AI from harming mathematics
records.description: Mathematicians must urgently recognize AI’s impacts on their field — and act swiftly to mitigate threats.

records.title: Researchers are building computers that run on brain organoids — but have neglected a major ethical issue
records.description: People who give tissue samples for biomedical research might have no idea that their cells are being used for biocomputers.

records.title: Bizarre CRISPR enzyme kills cancer cells by shredding their DNA
records.description: Early tests suggest the protein can be aimed at targets with tumour-causing mutations.

records.title: White House rolls out AI funding — and signals a new era for US science
records.description: Chief US science adviser calls for a shake-up in funding while handing out grants to accelerate research with AI.

records.title: Daily briefing: The science of The Odyssey
records.description: The tale gives us glimpses of the medicine and technology of the Homeric world. Plus, this year’s El Niño is set to be the largest on record and the boom in languages at the dawn of farming.

records.title: What The Odyssey reveals about ancient science — from botany to psychiatry
records.description: From intelligent ships to clues about eclipses, Homer’s The Odyssey reveals how Bronze Age Greeks understood the world.

records.title: Could small-team science be dying out?
records.description: The proportion of one- and two-author papers in the Nature Index is shrinking rapidly, as science done by big teams continues to surge.

records.title: International PhD students to face strict limits on time in the US
records.description: Trump administration takes action to address ‘forever students’.

records.title: Breathalyser can tell if you are burning fat from a single exhalation
records.description: The compact device can measure when the body is in ketosis and could help people to manage weight loss.

records.title: How does Make America Healthy Again hold up against scientific scrutiny?
records.description: Researchers share their views on the US health policy spanning topics from vaccines to nutrition.

records.title: Humanity spoke thousands of languages at the dawn of farming — now many of them are lost
records.description: A shift from nomadic lifestyles could have triggered linguistic diversity before it then declined rapidly.

records.title: Daily briefing: Orcas smash sunfish to smithereens
records.description: The dolphins might be helping their young eat, or just having fun. Plus, the beauty and skill of scientific illustration and a crash course in quantum computing.

records.title: This El Niño is set to be the largest on record by a ‘mind-blowing margin’
records.description: Forecasters predict that the monster climate pattern will combine with global warming to push global temperatures in 2027 to new heights.

records.title: Rising stars of mathematics awarded prestigious 2026 Fields Medal
records.description: Two of the four are the first Chinese-born winners of the prize since 1982.

records.title: What counts as a moon? Huge ‘exosatellite’ sparks debate
records.description: Discovery of a distant Jupiter-mass object could pave the way for detection of exomoons — plus, a rare transmissible cancer found in catfish.

records.title: How do quantum computers work?
records.description: Recent breakthroughs suggest usable devices could be here in a decade.

records.title: A radical approach to making C-glycoside molecules
records.description: A platform for synthesizing highly desirable C-glycoside molecules from sugar has been developed that uses glycosyl sulfonyl hydrazides as readily accessible free-radical precursors. The strategy enables targeted formation of carbon–carbon bonds across carbohydrate scaffolds and with specificity for the desired 3D arrangement of atoms.

records.title: Eyes upturned towards infinity
records.description: Stars in our eyes.

records.title: Here’s what’s next for the Artemis II astronauts
records.description: Newfound fame has proved to be stellar for some astronauts but harder for others. Will NASA’s popular crew need some space?

records.title: How to use AI to make a graphical abstract in minutes
records.description: Artificial intelligence is a democratizing force for those without graphic-design experience, as long as it is used conscientiously.

records.title: ‘Good design takes mastery’: scientific illustrators sketch out AI’s future
records.description: Nature talks to five artists about their approaches to communicating science visually.

records.title: AI identifies interactions in CRISPR complexes to improve specificity of DNA editing
records.description: AlphaFold3 predictions of the molecular contacts made by a genome-editing enzyme have been used to improve the enzyme’s selectivity for target DNA sequences.

records.title: Background genetics and new mutations interact to direct cancer evolution
records.description: Rerunning tumour evolution in mice shows how cancer develops after DNA damage and reveals that background genetics and acquired mutations interact to shape genome stability and selection. This provides experimental evidence that genetic ancestry has an important role in setting the trajectory of cancer evolution.

records.title: Air conditioning is not enough to keep people cool — can scientists find an alternative?
records.description: Advances in materials allow buildings to be cooled as temperatures rise.

records.title: Three tips to avoid AI image mistakes in science
records.description: Artificial-intelligence tools can be useful for brainstorming and creating graphics, but they can introduce errors. If you’re going to use them, here’s how to avoid problems.

records.title: Fly neurons carry a molecular ‘timestamp’ that encodes their birth order
records.description: A single-cell gene-expression atlas of the fly nerve cord mapped onto its wiring diagram has uncovered a simple shared gene-expression code. The code enables neurons to carry a molecular memory of the order of their birth from a parent cell, and shapes their diversity.

records.title: Geomagnetic storms caused by solar wind might be more extreme than previously thought
records.description: The severity of geomagnetic storms — magnetic disturbances in Earth’s outer atmosphere — is widely understood to reach an upper limit as the strength of the solar wind increases. But this upper limit is an illusion that results from uncertainty in the measurement of solar-wind strength as the true value regresses towards the mean.

records.title: The heart has a ‘little brain’ — and it protects against stress
records.description: A subset of cardiac neurons keep the heart from malfunctioning in stressed mice.

records.title: Polio should have been eradicated by now. What’s plan B?
records.description: Amid funding cuts and political barriers, researchers are asking whether the campaign can ever succeed, and what to do next.

records.title: Daily briefing: Can the world finally eradicate polio?
records.description: Some researchers think the current eradication strategy is outdated. Plus, goats hurt their brains when they butt heads and what scientist will never hand over to AI.

records.title: Rare contagious cancer discovered in wild catfish
records.description: Transmissible tumours have been found in only a few types of animal, but there might be many more out there.

records.title: Celebrating Nature ’s covers — past, present and future
records.description: Nature ’s iconic front page uses inspiration, creativity and ingenuity to unite science and technology with art and design.

records.title: Regional drivers and contributors to changes in life expectancy across Asia
records.description: Life expectancy in Asia has increased substantially since 1990, but the gains have varied considerably across regions and countries. The main causes and risk factors have been identified, highlighting regions in which preventable deaths are concentrated.

records.title: Structures and inhibition of the Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever virus polymerase
records.description: Structural studies of Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) polymerase reveal the structural basis of CCHFV RNA synthesis and highlight druggable sites for designing both nucleoside antivirals and non-nucleoside antivirals.

records.title: CRISPR–Cas regulates expression of embedded anti-phage defence systems
records.description: CRISPR–Cas systems transcriptionally tune diverse innate defences using CRISPR RNA-like guides to balance antiviral protection with fitness, and hyperactivate these defences when compromised, establishing a layered bacterial ‘immunity guard’ network.

records.title: Non-epitaxial perovskite polariton laser diode operating under direct current
records.description: By integrating a solution-grown perovskite microplate with chemically inert single-walled carbon nanotube electrodes and embedding them into an optical microcavity, the new microdevices can achieve polariton lasing under a constant direct current at 8 K.

records.title: Prior therapy defines mutation profiles in childhood cancer at relapse
records.description: Chemotherapy, particularly with platinum-based drugs, is associated with substantial, rapidly detectable mutagenesis in childhood cancers, tripling private signatures and doubling mutation burden, highlighting therapy-induced tumour evolution and opportunities for safer, de-escalated treatment.

records.title: Structural basis of the RNA-editing cascade in trypanosome mitochondria
records.description: Cryo-electron microscopy sheds light on the architecture of the Trypanosoma brucei mitochondrial editosome and reveals how this assembly mediates mRNA editing through the insertion and deletion of uridine nucleotides.

records.title: Insulator-free topological photonic multi-lane highways
records.description: An insulator-free topological waveguide architecture comprising four inequivalent photonic valley half-semimetals arranged in a parallel, cyclic configuration and stacked very close to one another demonstrates robust, multi-lane, unidirectional light transport with 100% spatial efficiency.

records.title: Planetary-mass exosatellite detected around the substellar companion of a star
records.description: Radial velocity measurements provide evidence for a Jupiter-mass exosatellite orbiting the brown dwarf companion CD-35 2722 B, a promising detection of an exomoon-like object.

records.title: Tertiary lymphoid structures harbour stem-like tumour-specific T cells
records.description: Renal cell carcinoma tumours containing tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are enriched for exhausted CD8 + T cells, including tumour-specific clonotypes with stem-like progenitor features and reduced terminal exhaustion.

records.title: Electronic-resonance enhanced molecule for perovskite solar cells
records.description: In a self-assembled monolayer molecule with a donor–acceptor–donor structure, the electronic resonance increased the negative charge density at the acceptor-anchoring group, improving the certified efficiencies of rigid and flexible perovskite solar cells.

records.title: Prior therapy defines mutation profiles in childhood cancer at relapse
records.description: Chemotherapy, particularly with platinum-based drugs, is associated with substantial, rapidly detectable mutagenesis in childhood cancers, tripling private signatures and doubling mutation burden, highlighting therapy-induced tumour evolution and opportunities for safer, de-escalated treatment.

records.title: Structural basis of the RNA-editing cascade in trypanosome mitochondria
records.description: Cryo-electron microscopy sheds light on the architecture of the Trypanosoma brucei mitochondrial editosome and reveals how this assembly mediates mRNA editing through the insertion and deletion of uridine nucleotides.

records.title: Insulator-free topological photonic multi-lane highways
records.description: An insulator-free topological waveguide architecture comprising four inequivalent photonic valley half-semimetals arranged in a parallel, cyclic configuration and stacked very close to one another demonstrates robust, multi-lane, unidirectional light transport with 100% spatial efficiency.

records.title: Planetary-mass exosatellite detected around the substellar companion of a star
records.description: Radial velocity measurements provide evidence for a Jupiter-mass exosatellite orbiting the brown dwarf companion CD-35 2722 B, a promising detection of an exomoon-like object.

records.description: Renal cell carcinoma tumours containing tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are enriched for exhausted CD8 + T cells, including tumour-specific clonotypes with stem-like progenitor features and reduced terminal exhaustion.

records.title: Electronic-resonance enhanced molecule for perovskite solar cells
records.description: In a self-assembled monolayer molecule with a donor–acceptor–donor structure, the electronic resonance increased the negative charge density at the acceptor-anchoring group, improving the certified efficiencies of rigid and flexible perovskite solar cells.

records.title: A vector-based strategy for olfactory navigation in Drosophila
records.description: Using a virtual reality system, experiments in Drosophila show that flies use memory mechanisms to navigate along the boundary of an odour plume and track the source of a smell.

records.title: Precise DNA base editing using AlphaFold3-based contact modelling
records.description: ContactSeek is an AlphaFold3-driven model that can improve the precision of genome-editing tools.

records.title: AI-redesigned starting points and outcomes enhance protein evolution
records.description: A workflow using artificial intelligence-redesigned starting points to evolve enzymes with improved properties compared with those evolved from natural proteins is established.

records.title: The planktonic microbiome of the Great Barrier Reef
records.description: The Great Barrier Reef Microbial Genomes Database compiles prokaryotic, viral and eukaryotic genomes from seawater collected from the Great Barrier Reef, providing a rich resource for the study of marine microbial communities and ecosystem research and management.

records.title: A global molecular code for birth order and neuronal identity in Drosophila
records.description: A high-resolution developmental transcriptional atlas of the Drosophila melanogaster nerve cord identifies a shared transcriptional code that records neuronal birth order and organizes neuronal diversity.

records.title: Subnuclear genome compartmentalization controls bivalent chromatin activity
records.description: Knowledge of the spatial location of a gene is necessary to understand its epigenomic regulation.

records.title: Non-Gaussian statistics of the order parameter across a phase transition
records.description: Single-atom measurements show non-Gaussian order-parameter fluctuations and critical scaling across a continuous phase transition, highlighting the importance of full statistical distributions in understanding universality.

records.title: Imaging of nanoscale polar textures in quantum paraelectric SrTiO 3
records.description: Cryo-STEM reveals that SrTiO 3 forms periodic polar nanodomains below 105 K, but these fragment below 40 K, linking quantum paraelectricity to nanoscale polar ordering and disordering.

records.title: Exceptional brain and ecological diversity in the earliest snakes
records.description: A well-preserved fossil snake from the Late Cretaceous of Brazil shows early ecological and brain shape disparity in the group.

records.title: Brown bullhead catfish melanoma represents a novel transmissible cancer
records.description: Whole-genome sequencing analysis of tumour and matched non-tumour host tissues of the brown bullhead catfish reveals a type of naturally occurring transmissible cancer.

records.title: Semiconducting and magnetic lanthanide MXenes from intercalated halides
records.description: A bottom-up synthesis strategy creates lanthanide MXenes (Ln 2 CT 2 ) that combine semiconducting behaviour with ferromagnetism, offering a promising new class of two-dimensional materials for spintronic applications.

records.title: RNA synthesis and substrate analogue inhibition in the CCHFV polymerase
records.description: Structural insights into the Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever virus polymerase reveal how the virus replicates.

records.title: Efficient and precise programmable DNA knock-in without double-strand breaks
records.description: Kilobase-scale nickase-targeting (KNIT) editing enables single-nick-based DNA insertion across genomic loci and cell types, supporting insertion of DNA fragments exceeding 10 kb, with high efficiency and minimal unwanted off-target effects.

records.title: Mapping drivers of life expectancy change in Asia from 1990 to 2023
records.description: Using the Global Burden of Disease Study data across Asian countries and territories, life expectancy trends and the effects of cause-specific mortality and risk factors on changes in these trends are analysed.

records.title: Genetic background sets the trajectory of experimental cancer evolution
records.description: Experimentally replaying tumour evolution in divergent mouse strains reveals the importance of interactions between genetic ancestry and acquired cancer-driving mutations in shaping the earliest stages of cancer development.

records.title: Are boldness and belligerence related?
records.description: Different types of aggression in stickleback fish, and a pillar of light seen at sunset, in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: Faintest planet ever spotted from Earth has been hiding in plain sight
records.description: Method used to discover an exoplanet called β Pictoris d might reveal other very dim exoplanets.

records.title: Moving floors keep buildings from swaying with the wind
records.description: A construction design inspired by traditional Japanese pagodas could help to keep modern towers safe.

records.title: Oil and gas drilling is shifting to the deep sea — here’s what is at stake
records.description: Technologies are taking the search for fossil fuels to the deepest parts of the ocean. Engineers must keep ecological risks manageable.

records.title: New hope in the fight against cachexia — cancer’s deadly co-conspirator
records.description: Scientists are getting closer to understanding the wasting and fatigue that often accompanies cancer. Treatments could be on the horizon.

records.title: Ten years of mapping gene expression in tissues
records.description: Spatially resolved transcriptomic technologies continue to enhance understanding of development and disease through a feedback loop involving academia and industry.

records.title: Seven ways endurance sports have taught me to be a better researcher
records.description: The ‘24-hour rule’ and other tips from sport can improve lab life.

records.title: Does China’s latest AI model finally equal US rivals? What scientists think
records.description: ‘Kimi K3’ can match or outperform cutting-edge models, says Moonshot AI. But its large size might limit uptake.

records.title: Don’t let AI steal all the joy: what scientists won’t give up to chatbots
records.description: Nature asked readers of the Nature Briefing what they like about their job and don’t want to hand over.

records.title: Daily briefing: Baby T. rex were tiny but deadly
records.description: Tyrannosaurus rex of any size were not to be messed with. Plus, the first genetic clues for borderline personality disorder and a step closer to understanding the wasting that often accompanies cancer.

records.title: Detailed maps of European wetlands reveal overlooked patches of ecosystems
records.description: Satellite images have been analysed by a machine-learning algorithm to produce high-resolution maps of wetland environments — a boon for conservation efforts.

records.title: Why some trees never come back after rainforests are cleared
records.description: Tree diversity is lower in regenerated forests than in old forests — even after 120 years of regrowth.

records.title: Daily briefing: How to nail an industry interview
records.description: Careers coaches shed some light on multi-stage interviews for roles in industry. Plus, a man’s ability to make sperm has been restored by a testicular-tissue transplant and the deadly toll of a ‘disease of the built environment’.

records.title: Smuggling charges against NIH virologists trigger political uproar
records.description: Other researchers say that non-infectious viral samples in luggage posed no risk, but might have violated import rules.

records.title: The science of foresight: how to future-proof your research
records.description: Anticipating from the start the various ways a research programme can succeed or fail can avoid problems later. Here’s how to do it.

records.title: Huge study finds first genetic clues for borderline personality disorder
records.description: Largest genetic analysis of the condition so far finds 11 linked locations in the human genome.

records.title: My job interviews for industry positions are going nowhere. How do I make myself stand out?
records.description: A postdoc researcher trying to move into an industry role wants help gaining traction and making it past the first interview stage.

records.title: Briefing Chat: Sweet! Elusive sugar molecules found in space
records.description: Nature staff discuss the discovery of a four carbon ‘true sugar’ in interstellar space — plus, a formula inscribed on a wall reveals a Maya mathematician’s name.

records.title: Wearable sensors on the face are invisible to the eye
records.description: Electrodes that measure brain waves and more cannot be seen or felt.

records.title: Daily briefing: Naked mole rat queens use a smell to stay on top
records.description: Just one chemical is enough to maintain the status quo in naked mole rat colonies. Plus, the hunt for the origins of a cyclosporidia outbreak and whether it’s possible to end poverty without economic growth.

records.title: AI is set to completely transform cybersecurity — here’s how researchers must prepare
records.description: As automated tools accelerate both the discovery and the exploitation of software vulnerabilities, organizations must redesign their defences and workflows to keep pace.

records.title: A global capital for AI safety is emerging — and it’s not in Silicon Valley
records.description: The United Kingdom is gaining influence through its growing AI-safety ecosystem.

records.title: US politicians push agencies to restrict research collaboration with China
records.description: Republicans and Democrats worry about research theft and exploitation — but don’t agree on how to solve the problem.

records.title: CRISPR gets a power boost from AI-designed ‘molecular scissors’
records.description: Researchers used artificial intelligence to design functional CRISPR enzymes not seen in nature.

records.title: Will making ‘replication studies’ easier to find help science self-correct?
records.description: Project on peer-review platform Pubpeer aims to make replication studies more visible.

records.title: ‘Explosive diarrhoea’ outbreak grips US: how researchers are hunting its source
records.description: Cases have hit record levels, and scientists are racing to pinpoint where the Cyclospora parasite entered the food supply.

records.title: The simple chemical that lets queen naked mole-rats 'rule'
records.description: The mechanism behind these strange mammals' extreme social structure has been a long-standing puzzle.

records.title: ‘Holy grail’ of naked mole-rat research reveals how queens rule
records.description: The simple chemical that keeps a mole-rat queen atop her throne — plus, how people approach new games.

records.title: Relapse
records.description: Restore previous version?

records.title: How to end poverty and protect Earth: inside the debate tearing up economics
records.description: The idea of prosperity without growth is gaining traction among researchers. So why are many economists sceptical?

records.title: Improvements in educational opportunities go hand in hand with innovation
records.description: The first longitudinal regional atlas of intergenerational educational mobility shows that the subnational regions of Europe in which individuals’ educational opportunities are least dependent on the educational background of their parents tend to have the most innovation, as shown by the number of patents.

records.title: Beyond lithium: how sodium-ion batteries could change the world
records.description: Batteries based on sodium ions are entering mass production. Some researchers say they could ultimately be a cheaper, safer alternative to lithium in electric cars and other energy applications.

records.title: Nucleotides act as ‘molecular glue’ and can sense their own abundance
records.description: Some nucleotides have been shown to control metabolism by ‘gluing’ proteins together. Could other small molecules made naturally by cells have similar capabilities?

records.title: AI avatars are reshaping society in China — the law is trying to catch up
records.description: Digital people are fulfilling roles from running hospitals to giving lectures to offering companionship.

records.title: Optical filter sorts light by its ‘quantum statistics’
records.description: A nanostructured gold surface can filter light depending on the tendency of its photons to arrive at a detector in pairs.

records.title: How naked mole rat queens stop rivals reproducing
records.description: The scent of a single chemical, made only by the queen, alters hormone production in other females.

records.title: Doctored data sets could trick AI agents
records.description: Researchers warn that ‘poisoned’ information can undermine the reliability of tools that analyse data autonomously.

records.title: Why there needs to be a global debate on inequality
records.description: Researchers have a responsibility to search for consensus on this crucial issue, both for future generations and the future of our planet.

records.title: A high-fat, low-carbohydrate diet can feed intestinal tumours
records.description: A ketogenic diet promotes tumour growth in the small intestine in susceptible mice. In people, diet advice might need to be tailored to individual cancer risks.

records.title: Daily briefing: The battery that could change everything
records.description: How sodium-ion batteries could change the world. Plus, the evolution of handedness with an ancient worm and how scientists are revealing the mysteries of the deep ocean.

records.title: Blue LEDs made from perovskite material shine bright thanks to hydrogen bonds
records.description: Blue light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are needed for high-definition displays with wide colour range. Efficient, stable and colour-saturated blue LEDs containing emitters made of perovskites have now been fabricated by adding isomeric molecules that generate a network of hydrogen bonds, stabilizing the octahedral structure of the perovskite crystal.

records.title: Biologists pinpoint how common virus triggers multiple sclerosis
records.description: A connection with Epstein–Barr virus has long been suspected, but the underlying mechanism was unclear until now.

records.title: Selectivity emerges from indiscriminate photoreduction
records.description: Super-potent photoreductants enable single electron transfer reactions with selectivity independent of substrate redox potentials, opening new pathways for coupling difficult-to-reduce organic molecules.

records.title: Modular in vivo antibody–ADC click to reverse drug resistance in tumours
records.description: In vivo ligation of clinically used therapeutic antibodies via bioorthogonal click chemistry to antibody–drug conjugates leads to enhanced antitumour activity in heterogeneous and treatment-resistant tumours.

records.title: A queen odour mediates reproductive suppression in a eusocial mammal
records.description: Naked mole-rat ( Heterocephalus glaber ) queens produce isopropyl myristate, a low-volatility ester that high-ranking animals detect and avoid, which alters prolactin and progesterone in other females to suppress reproduction and preserve eusocial hierarchy.

records.title: Highly fragmented European wetlands with uneven restoration needs
records.description: Satellite imagery and machine learning used for the mapping of six seminatural open wetland types and land-use disturbance in European countries shows that wetlands are highly fragmented and have uneven restoration needs.

records.title: Universal gates from braiding and fusing anyons on quantum hardware
records.description: A 54-qubit realization of non-Abelian S 3 topological order demonstrates that combining anyon braiding with fusion enables universal topological quantum computation.

records.title: Food systems transformation would reshape global agriculture
records.description: Scenario simulations using global economic models show that by 2050 the transformation of food systems towards healthy diets, improved productivity and halving of food waste result in a restructuring of global agriculture.

records.title: Quantum statistical plasmonic metacrystals
records.description: A new class of materials, quantum statistical plasmonic metacrystals, is described, which can selectively transmit different types of light based only on their quantum coherence, showing bands of allowed and forbidden photon statistics.

records.title: An ATPγS recycling strategy for practical biocatalytic thiophosphorylation
records.description: A new method for practical scaling up of enzymatic thiophosphorylation is described, making use of a two-kinase system along with recycling of the very expensive ATPγS, providing a pathway for thiophosphate-containing modalities in drug development.

records.title: Ammonia pressure controls colloidal metal nitride synthesis in molten salts
records.description: A molten salt, high-pressure synthesis method enables solution-based production of diverse refractory metal nitride nanocrystals, expanding access to technologically important nitride materials for advanced applications.

records.title: Scalable quasi-pure MOF membranes for energy-efficient gas separations
records.description: Scalable quasi-pure metal–organic framework membranes achieve near-intrinsic separation performance, enabling energy-efficient industrial gas separations with major cost reductions compared with distillation.

records.title: A Bayesian framework for longitudinal EHR and genetic discovery
records.description: A Bayesian generative framework that integrates longitudinal electronic health records with genetic data to identify latent disease signatures is presented.

records.title: Programming fracture resistance in metamaterials via elastic instabilities
records.description: Elastic instabilities in mechanical metamaterials can be harnessed to programme fracture behaviour, transforming instability from a failure mechanism into a design principle that increases fracture energy by up to tenfold.

records.title: Regression to the mean can explain saturation of geomagnetic storms
records.description: The saturation of geomagnetic activity with solar wind strength can be explained by a regression to the mean effect, suggesting that the impact of extreme geomagnetic storms can be twice as large as previously thought

records.title: Metabolite glues as a means of purine sensing and chemotherapeutic response
records.description: Purines can act as endogenous molecular glues in human cells by anchoring a rate-limiting enzyme in purine biosynthesis to its inhibitor, and modifying this mechanism could provide a way to improve the properties of thiopurine chemotherapeutic drugs.

records.title: Rising dust pollution across Europe in a changing climate
records.description: A database of daily dust metals in Europe is established and a machine learning model shows that transported dust intrusion events over the past decade are linked to changes in atmospheric circulation, while an ice core shows that the increase in dust since pre-industrial times is governed by increasing aridity in North Africa..

records.title: Rarely categorical, highly separable representations along the cortical hierarchy
records.description: Cortical circuits prioritize diversity over categorical structure, supporting a computational regime geared towards high-dimensional, highly separable neural representations.

records.title: People use fast and flat simulation to reason about new games
records.description: Large-scale behavioural studies show that people approach a new game systematically and adaptively rationally. A cognitive model called the ‘Intuitive Gamer’ offers insights into this process and may inform the design of more flexible AI systems.
