records.description: Large-scale behavioural studies show that people approach a new game systematically and adaptively rationally. A cognitive model called the ‘Intuitive Gamer’ offers insights into this process and may inform the design of more flexible AI systems.

records.title: Cell-type signatures of Alzheimer’s disease shared across population groups
records.description: Single-nucleus RNA-seq and ATAC-seq analyses on post-mortem brain samples from African American, Latin and white individuals identify cell-type-specific molecular signatures that are associated with cognitive impairment and/or Alzheimer’s disease across diverse population groups.

records.title: Ketogenic diet mediates intestinal tumorigenesis through lipids not ketones
records.description: A combination of different manipulations in mouse models of spontaneous intestinal adenoma formation dissects the roles of systemic and epithelial ketogenesis versus dietary lipids in ketogenic diet-mediated intestinal tumorigenesis, highlighting the need for nuanced consideration of dietary strategies for cancer prevention.

records.title: Fractional high-Chern insulator in twisted rhombohedral graphene
records.description: A rich variety of both integer and fractional high-Chern insulators are observed in a moiré system composed of Bernal bilayer graphene and rhombohedral tetralayer graphene.

records.title: An encyclopedia of human enhancer–gene regulatory interactions
records.description: An encyclopedia of more than 92 million enhancer–gene regulatory interactions created as part of the ENCODE4 project provides a valuable resource for future studies of gene regulation and human genetics.

records.title: Magnetic character of the low-energy enhancement in 70 Zn
records.description: The low-energy enhancement in the γ-ray strength function of 70 Zn is due to magnetic dipole transitions between nuclear states.

records.title: GPC3-specific dnTGFβRII-armoured CAR T cells for hepatocellular carcinoma
records.description: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells for antitumour therapy ‘armoured’ with a dominant-negative TGFβ receptor II show enhanced efficacy and tolerable safety in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma who have developed resistance or not responded to previous treatment.

records.title: Catalyst-free, microdroplet-mediated waste plastic conversion to diacids
records.description: A catalyst-free upcycling strategy based on in situ generation of hydroxyl radicals at microdroplet interfaces is described for efficient and scalable processing of polymers with minimal infrastructure, using only water and oxygen under mild conditions.

records.title: Graphene oxide-polydopamine membranes with controlled interlayer spacing
records.description: Polydopamine-pillared composite graphene oxide membranes with tunable and stable interlayer spacing, featuring controllable interlayer spacing, are capable of sieving hydrated rubidium and potassium ions and delivering continuous freshwater production at high levels.

records.title: Bird flu H5N1 in Australia: protect Australian species from bird flu virus
Academia should recognize community partnerships as having societal impact
The Enhanced Games and the normalization of doping: a public health concern
‘Dark comet’ unmasked by its mysterious motions
records.description: A celestial body thought to be an ordinary space rock turns out to have a comet-like tail.

records.title: Seeking an industry role after your PhD? Make sure your CV reflects that
records.description: A doctorate can open many doors. A CV tailored to your planned career path can help to unlock them.

records.title: Africa’s response to this Ebola outbreak shows how to shape global health
records.description: Countries elsewhere must learn from the continent’s example and combat disease outbreaks by working together, not by closing borders.

records.title: DNA-shredding CRISPR enzyme takes aim at cancer cells
records.description: A bacterial self-destruct mechanism has been repurposed as a potential therapy, selectively eliminating diseased cells — including tumour cells in mouse models of cancer.

records.title: My research on mice is causing me stress. How can I become more resilient?
records.description: A PhD student loves research, but not the realities of experimenting on animals. What are their options?

records.title: Four deep-sea technologies that could help detect deadly earthquakes and tsunamis
records.description: Deep-sea drilling ships, sea-floor sensors and repurposed Internet cables are helping scientists to study the last unmapped area on Earth.

records.title: Could this mysterious disappearing organ hold the key to longevity?
records.description: Researchers are racing to regrow the thymus, an ephemeral immune organ, in the hope that it will slow ageing.

records.title: Mathematics formula found on Maya wall rivals insights of ancient masters
records.description: Mathematical texts from a Maya site in Guatemala identify an astronomer called Sak Tahn Waax.

records.title: Daily briefing: Can regrowing the thymus slow down ageing?
records.description: Treatments to regrow the peculiar immune organ could also help to prevent cancer. Plus, a four-carbon sugar found in the stars and the name of an important Maya mathematician revealed.

records.title: RNA molecules with different destinies are processed through overlapping pathways
records.description: The protein complex that helps messenger RNA to leave the nucleus is remarkably similar to the one that facilitates the destruction of short, unwanted transcripts.

records.title: ‘Climate free fall’: why the biggest risk to our economies is yet to be recognized
records.description: Increasing instability of the ocean, ice and atmosphere threatens farming, finance and society. We all need to wake up to that fact.

records.title: Author Correction: OR7A10 GPCR engineering boosts CAR-NK therapy against solid tumours
Party pooper: grandparents’ COVID risk rose after grandchildren’s birthdays
records.description: Records from Denmark suggest that small family gatherings can be an important transmission point.

records.title: Tall and small trees are equally vulnerable to drought
records.description: The water-transport system of tropical giants called dipterocarps has evolved to defy the effects of gravity and resist water stress.

records.title: Rights for rivers and ice cream for all: top reads for the summer holidays
records.description: Ten Nature contributors share their current book obsessions.

records.title: How voluntary work can boost your career in science
records.description: Supporting charities can bring career benefits and provide valuable social connections.

records.title: The rise of evidence-based medicine and the ‘mavericks’ who championed it
records.description: An impeccably researched account describes how clinical trials have transformed health and social policy.

records.title: Epigenetic editing makes its mark
records.description: Researchers are rewriting the chemical tags on DNA and chromatin to tune gene expression.

records.title: This microbiologist endured a four-year court battle over COVID-19 tests
records.description: Linda Guamán wanted to serve her country, but became mired in a political controversy that led to her being arrested and facing years in prison.

records.title: Daily briefing: The rise of evidence-based medicine
records.description: How rigorous research has transformed health and social policy. Plus, a breakthrough for lab-grown sperm and the NSF plans to cut core science programmes to fund a White House initiative.

records.title: Daily briefing: Preprints are chock-full of authors’ private info
records.description: Passwords, to-do lists and even derogatory comments litter arXiv preprints. Plus, two huge planets that are lighter than candy floss and which ‘AI scientist’ might suit your lab.

records.title: Lab-grown sperm: scientists inch closer to fertility breakthrough
records.description: Sci-fi procedure generates immature human sperm from stem cells, nurturing them on a mouse’s kidney.

records.title: NSF plans cuts to core science programmes to fund White House initiative
records.description: A proposed clawback of already distributed research funds comes as the US agency struggles with a squeezed budget and a backlog of grant applications.

records.title: Found: the toxic killer that caused an ocean catastrophe
records.description: Scientists identify an alga species as the culprit behind the deaths of more than one million marine animals.

records.title: Pair of ‘super-puff’ planets are lighter than candyfloss
records.description: Two gas giants circling the same star are among the least dense planets ever found.

records.title: Graduating without a thesis: meet the people getting ‘practical’ PhDs in China
records.description: Nature spoke to three students from China’s first cohort of PhD candidates who are allowed to graduate with products instead of papers.

records.title: Daily briefing: Mutation lets octopuses make proteins with precision
records.description: A break in these octopuses’ protein-making machinery boosts their accuracy. Plus, a Nobel-prizewinner has left the United States for China and the effects of microgravity on the brain.

records.title: Whoops! Most arXiv papers contain information never meant to be shared
records.description: Passwords, GPS coordinates and private conversations have all been found in the metadata and source files of millions of preprint submissions.

records.title: ‘This time, it’s the other way around’: how Indonesia is reclaiming the science of human history
records.description: After a massive restructuring of its research ecosystem, Indonesia is taking the lead on its own palaeontological research.

records.title: Nukes in space? Orbital detector could sniff out warheads
records.description: A shoebox-sized detector satellite could identify the telltale signal of a hidden nuclear device — plus, how Indigenous plant knowledge is under threat.

records.title: I want to see a prison-to-PhD pipeline
records.description: Ryan Rising creates programmes that help people who have been incarcerated to access academic opportunities.

records.title: Regenerating people–nature relationships to counter biocultural erosion in the Amazon
records.description: Rebuilding the reciprocal care-oriented relationships between Amazonian Indigenous peoples and nature could address the predicted effects of climate change on biodiversity.

records.title: Nobel-winning chemist leaves US to direct AI materials lab in China
records.description: Omar Yaghi’s move comes amid cuts to US science and a campaign in China to recruit top international talent.

records.title: Volcanoes and wildfires contributed to increased stratospheric humidification
records.description: Observations from satellites and climate-model simulations show that moderate volcanic eruptions and extreme wildfires have humidified the stratosphere since 2005. The aerosol-mediated effects of these eruptions and fires explain about one-third of the observed stratospheric water-vapour trend, a contribution similar to that of surface warming.

records.title: Those who forget
records.description: Clarity of thought.

records.title: Ocean floor witnessed splitting apart for the first time — releasing lava
records.description: Scientists observed a mid-ocean ridge widen in real time, recording several metres of sea-floor motion and huge lava outflows.

records.title: Breast cancer driver genes found by screening chromosome aberrations in vivo
records.description: Cancer genomes are unstable, often experiencing gains or losses of whole chromosomes or chromosome arms — changes known as aneuploidies. Experiments in mouse models of breast cancer reveal that these instabilities harbour one or two prevalent genes that drive cancer and that bypass the need to accumulate aneuploidies; they also require an intact microenvironment to produce their effects.

records.title: Daily briefing: Mountain bongos still roam the forest
records.description: A breeding herd of critically endangered antelope offer hope for the species' future. Plus, the mysterious objects that washed up in Australia are ‘space balls’ and the role of native plants in our backyards.

records.title: Judicious use of LLMs could speed up progress in the social sciences
records.description: Large language models could advance experiments in the social sciences, but fundamental questions remain about how they should be used to support research.

records.title: Sea-floor spreading captured by undersea observatory
records.description: A sea-floor monitoring experiment observed oceanic crust being created between two tectonic plates — the first in situ measurement of this phenomenon.

records.description: Kathleen Fisher reveals the recipe for funding innovative science that she brings to the UK Advanced Research and Invention Agency.

records.title: Nuclear weapons lurking in space could be tracked down by satellites
records.description: A nuclear weapon orbiting Earth would emit neutrons through its interactions with the planet’s space radiation environment, and these could be detected by satellites.

records.title: Observation of Floquet rotational super-radiance
records.description: A Floquet regime of rotational super-radiance has been observed in a spatiotemporally modulated ring network of resonators.

records.title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery
records.description: A systematic evaluation shows that contemporary humanoid robots can perform laparoscopic surgical tasks through teleoperation, highlighting both their promise and key technical challenges before clinical deployment.

records.title: Single-phase gradient-solvation-electrolyte-stabilized Li metal batteries
records.description: A targeted ligand anti-solvent is incorporated into an anion-rich ether-based electrolyte and used to achieve lithium metal batteries with a long cycle life, high energy density and high capacity retention.

records.title: Non-genotoxic transplantation and in vivo selection through epitope editing
records.description: Epitope editing of KIT enables antibody-based, non-genotoxic conditioning that selectively enriches therapeutic BCL11A -edited haematopoietic stem/progenitor cells, supports durable engraftment, preserves clonal diversity and enhances induction of fetal haemoglobin, a therapeutic approach for conditions such as sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia.

records.title: Architecture of the 8 MDa Hdr–Vhu–Fwd super-assembly in class I methanogens
records.description: The structure of the Hdr–Vhu–Fwd super-assembly reveals a lineage-specific and modular 8 MDa complex with the ability to adapt to diverse anaerobic niches.

records.title: Reinforcement learning control of quantum error correction
records.description: By integrating reinforcement learning with quantum error correction, a quantum computer continuously self-calibrates during computation, achieving record logical error rates and enhanced resilience to drift.

records.title: Large language models can predict the results of social science experiments
records.description: Large language models can be used to estimate the results of social science experiments about as accurately as a group of human forecasters—even for experiments published after the models were trained—although they tended to overestimate effect sizes.

records.title: Ancient feeding-related neuropeptides regulate alloparenting in ants
records.description: Pharmacological screening and behavioural assays in ants identify two specific neuropeptides that have key and opposite effects in regulating brood care, and that link nutritional state to age-dependent changes in parenting behaviour.

records.title: Anatomy of a seafloor spreading event captured by in situ seismogeodesy
records.description: By combining hydroacoustic, direct-path ranging and bottom-pressure measurements, in situ observations of a rifting event at a segment of the Southeast Indian Ridge are reported, providing insight into seafloor spreading events on yearly timescales.

records.title: Computational approaches and the future of urban crime research
records.description: This Review examines the opportunities and challenges introduced by new datasets and computational techniques in urban crime research, and outlines future directions for leveraging these advances effectively.

records.title: Reconfigurable mmWave microchips co-integrating hBN switches on GaN
records.description: Radio-frequency switches made from two-dimensional layered hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) were co-integrated on gallium nitride (GaN) microchips to build programmable millimetre-wave (mmWave) monolithic microwave integrated circuits suitable for 6G hardware.

records.title: Air-permeable hydrogels through viscoelastic phase separation of aerogels
records.description: Viscoelastic phase separation is used to fabricate non-collapsible, air-rich networks in high-water-content hydrogels containing silica aerogel beads, allowing air to permeate through the material and enabling a tenfold increase in oxygen permeability over pristine hydrogels.

records.title: Verification of the Outer Space Treaty with cosmic protons
records.description: By observing the neutrons induced by spallation from protons in the inner Van Allen radiation belts using widely available sensor technologies, the detection of a thermonuclear weapon carried by a space satellite is possible.

records.title: Aneuploidy selects for the acquisition of driver genes in breast cancer
records.description: Screening of chromosome arm-level aneuploidies uncovers that these alterations select for specific basal-like breast cancer driver genes, including PLGRKT , an oncogene whose tumour-promoting activity is associated with highly stress-resistant mitochondria and enhanced detoxification of reactive oxygen species.

records.title: Intergenerational mobility fosters innovation in Europe
records.description: The EUROPE-IGM-ATLAS reveals spatiotemporal trends that characterize the changing geography of opportunity in Europe and its relationship with regional innovation.

records.title: An intrinsic cytoskeletal oscillator establishes neuronal polarity
records.description: The ARP2/3 complex works together with actomyosin in an oscillatory program at the soma to govern neuronal polarization.

records.title: The forest of knowledge under global change
records.description: The biocultural heritage of the Amazon, its plant species, plant services and cultures are at risk from climate change.

‘Humanizer’ tool can erase signs of AI-written text — alarming scientists

records.title: How to widen access to the critical minerals that the world needs
records.description: A patent pool and licensing architecture would enable more widespread use of key minerals than would decades of mining and refining investment alone.

records.title: Daily briefing: Three decades of Dolly
records.description: Look back at the thirty years of advances since the birth of Dolly the sheep. Plus, what the science says about staving off dementia and a call to preserve the Hubble space telescope.

records.title: Body-plan organizer in comb jellies hints at animal ancestry
records.description: Transplantation experiments in evolutionarily distinct animal groups reveal conserved mechanisms underlying tissue organization during development.

records.description: Collaboration in nature has often been overlooked in favour of competition, argues science journalist Rowan Hooper. Plus, what’s really happening with trust in science.

records.description: The National Natural Science Foundation of China says it will fund an extra 12,000 projects from this year.

records.description: The insects could explore underwater for up to three hours. Plus, fake cancer studies rake in the citations and how scientists can build trust by recognizing their biases.

records.description: Nature readers share their PhD time-management woes.

records.description: New leader of the National Academy of Sciences Neil Shubin warns: ‘a society that loses science loses the future’.

records.description: Electrodeposited self-assembled molecules improve perovskite solar cell stability and efficiency by forming dense, strongly anchored layers on indium tin oxide, enabling 26.8% laboratory-cell and 21.3% module efficiencies.

records.description: Science journalist Rowan Hooper joins us to talk about symbiosis and the importance of organisms working together.

records.title: Scientists should recognize their own political biases to build public trust
records.description: Public trust in science can’t be sustained by the support of narrow constituencies at one end of an ideological spectrum.

records.title: Plant membranes shuffle lipids around to stay firm under heat stress
records.description: High temperatures make cell membranes weak and leaky. Rice plants rapidly counteract this effect by adjusting membrane lipid content, enabling them to resist heatwaves.

records.title: Paper mill cancer studies get double the number of citations as genuine papers
records.description: Potentially fraudulent papers often cite each other and could be inflating the impact factor of journals in which they are published.

records.title: The complex truth about trust in science
records.description: Confidence in science has not collapsed, but scientists have urgent problems to address.

records.title: Six ways to put the public at the heart of science and policy
records.description: Trust in elite institutions is on the wane globally. Building public participation into research and government advice can turn the tide.

records.title: As transistors get smaller, electrodes must keep shrinking too
records.description: Direct imaging shows that the contacts through which current flows into atomically thin transistors can be scaled down to just a few nanometres in length.

records.title: Have people stopped trusting science? The data tell a surprising story
records.description: Some say there’s a global crisis of trust — but research reveals where the real problems lie.

records.title: Nanodiamonds made from tiny graphene triangles
records.description: Nanodiamonds can host atom-sized light emitters for quantum sensing and imaging, but making nanodiamonds that are small, crystalline and uniform has been difficult. A single-step process for making nanodiamonds only 3–4 nanometres in size uses planar carbon ‘nanographene’ molecules with hydrogen atoms on the edges, and can be adapted to generate fluorescent nanodiamonds.

records.title: Backreaction of stimulated Hawking radiation in an optical analogue
records.description: By using a fibre-optical analogue of the physics of black holes, theoretical and experimental evidence is presented for the process underpinning the generation of Hawking radiation and its backreaction onto the optical pump.

records.title: Harmonizing standards and resources for the medical genome
records.description: This Perspective examines the challenges and opportunities of genomic sequencing across multiple clinical applications, including genetic therapies, and calls for the establishment of new, centralized reference standards to improve consistency and accuracy in the field of precision medicine.

records.title: Towards the construction of a virtual yeast
records.description: A virtual yeast, an artificial intelligence-driven agent for modelling eukaryotic cellular behaviours, is described.

records.title: Isomeric multi-hydrogen-bonding enables blue perovskite LEDs
records.description: Hydrogen-bonding networks engineered with isomeric molecules enable stable, saturated blue perovskite LEDs with record external quantum efficiencies up to 22.0%, advancing high-performance full-colour display technologies.

records.title: A secreted endosymbiont protein essential for colonizing host cells
records.description: SyeA was present in the Buchnera ancestor, is secreted into the host cytoplasm, is homologous to secreted effectors of bacterial pathogens and is essential for Buchnera transmission.

records.title: Replication-stress-induced chromatin loops protect fork stability
records.description: Replication stress induces the formation of transient chromatin loops that enclose de novo heterochromatin-enriched stalled replication forks.

records.title: Identification of cross-stage, cross-species malaria CD8 + T cell antigens
records.description: An immunopeptidomics analysis identifies numerous Plasmodium T cell antigens that are conserved across malaria parasite species and expressed at several phases of the parasite’s life cycle, with possible applications in the development of a malaria vaccine.

records.title: Targeted enzyme discovery using metal-coordination mining
records.description: A methodology for mining protein structure databases on the basis of the distinct intrinsic structures of metal-binding active sites in enzymes enables the discovery of new families of radical halogenases.

records.title: Directly probing the carrier transfer length in 2D-material transistors
records.description: Cross-sectional scanning tunnelling microscopy shows a 2 nm carrier transfer length in bismuth-contacted monolayer MoS 2 transistors, defining metal-contact scaling limits for sub-10 nm 2D electronic devices.

records.title: Restoring cortical disinhibition improves Huntington’s disease phenotypes
records.description: In a mouse model of Huntington’s disease, targeted modulation of neuronal activity restores network function and improves motor deficits.

records.title: Tin perovskite transistors stabilized through volatile coordination
records.description: A volatile-assisted coordination strategy regulates surface defect chemistry and self-doping, thus stabilizing the stoichiometry of tin perovskite semiconductors, resulting in transistors that can maintain stable operation for a month at temperatures of 100 °C.

records.description: New high-precision neodymium isotope data measured on recently erupted lavas from the submarine Fani Maoré volcano in the Comoros archipelago allow the identification of heterogeneities dating back to Earth’s earliest history.

records.title: Steatosis shapes prognosis-defining liver metastasis heterogeneity in CRC
records.description: Liver steatosis increases formation of replacement liver metastases by increasing MYC stability through acetylation, which increases proline synthesis and collagen production.

records.title: Connecting single-cell transcriptomes to projectomes in the mouse visual cortex
records.description: In the mouse visual cortex, multimodal cell-type definitions, gene expression patterns and cell location predict long-range projection targets of excitatory neurons, linking transcriptomic identity with morphological, electrophysiological and circuit-level properties.

records.title: Dual tumour–myeloid targeting of glioblastoma with GPNMB CAR-T cells
records.description: Integrated multi-omic profiling of glioblastoma reveals GPNMB as a shared antigen in tumour cells and the surrounding microenvironment, and GPNMB-targeted chimeric antigen receptor T cells demonstrate therapeutic activity in vitro and in animal models.

records.title: Heat-triggered phospholipid flipping stabilizes plasma membrane fluidity
records.description: In rice, the P4-ATPase complex OsALA5–OsALIS2 rapidly stabilizes membrane fluidity in response to high temperature by flipping saturated phosphatidylcholines to the cytosolic leaflet of the plasma membrane.

records.title: TROP2 targeting reveals therapy-driven cell state dynamics in colorectal cancer
records.description: TROP2 marks poor-prognosis colorectal cancer cells with fetal-like, therapy-resistant states, and therapeutic targeting of TROP2 with antibody–drug conjugates in combination with chemotherapy enhances treatment efficacy by modulating tumour cell plasticity and overcoming resistance.

records.title: Aerosols and hydrocarbons in the atmosphere of a white dwarf planet
records.description: Transmission spectroscopy of the planet WD 1856 b, orbiting a white dwarf, with the James Webb Space Telescope reveals the presence of hydrocarbons and aerosols in its atmosphere, providing insight into its mass and heating history.

records.title: Moderate volcanic eruptions and extreme wildfires humidify the stratosphere
records.description: Observations and modelling show that volcanic eruptions and extreme wildfires have systematically increased stratospheric water vapour since 2005, revealing that these episodic aerosol perturbations are a previously overlooked driver of stratospheric water vapour variability.

records.title: N 4 -Acetylcytidine enhances synthetic mRNA translation yield and fidelity
records.description: Different RNA modifications elicit different translation elongation rates for in vitro transcribed mRNAs that result in disparate translation outputs and fidelity, as shown here for N 4 -acetylcytidine versus the industry standard for synthetic mRNAs, N 1 -methylpseudouridine.

records.title: Food web complexity underlies biodiversity effects on ecosystem functioning
records.description: Analyses of the relationship between taxon richness and multi-trophic ecosystem functioning across marine, lake, stream and soil ecosystems show that food web complexity underlies biodiversity effects on ecosystem functioning.

records.title: Competing programs shape cortical sensorimotor–association axis development
records.description: Multispecies evidence supports the multinodal induction–exclusion in network development model, in which sensorimotor-to-association patterning is governed by competing processes of induction and exclusion driven by two opposing transcriptomically defined programs.

records.title: Correcting congenital myasthenia-associated acetylcholine receptor defects
records.description: Cryogenic electron microscopy, chemical biology and electrophysiology are used to determine the structures and functional consequences of representative congenital myasthenic syndrome-associated mutant receptors with and without drugs, uncovering principles of pathogenesis and providing a framework for precision therapies.

records.title: Dendrite initiation and deflection in biaxially stressed solid electrolytes
records.description: By deflecting dendrite propagation, in-plane biaxial compression provided direct evidence that dendrite initiation occurs within the interior of garnet solid electrolytes during long-term cycling.

records.title: Urokodia sheds light on the origin of chelicerae and book gills of Chelicerata
records.description: Microtomography reconstructions and phylogenetic analyses of Urokodia aequalis from the Chengjiang biota of China provide an updated interpretation of the evolution of anatomical structures in chelicerates.

records.title: Casdatifan shows durable response linked to HIF-2α biology in kidney cancer
records.description: Monotherapy with the HIF-2α inhibitor casdatifan achieves meaningful, durable responses linked to HIF-2α biology with manageable safety in the treatment of individuals with clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

records.title: Child online safety needs more than social-media bans
Ebola preparedness must start with ecosystems and before humans show symptoms
Early television set impresses Nature editors — but will it catch on?
records.description: Nature reports a demonstration of a ‘televisor’, and the British Government makes a generous endowment, in our weekly dip into the magazine’s archive.

records.title: AI tools can speed up thinking, but evidence still comes from the lab bench
Can Rwanda sustain its rise in science and technology? Here’s what can help
records.description: An ambitious analysis challenges the view that a nation’s pursuit of economic growth alone can deliver long-term prosperity.

records.title: Retraction Note: NSD2 targeting reverses plasticity and drug resistance in prostate cancer
Daily briefing: How to brew a climate-friendly coffee
records.description: Researchers are racing to safeguard coffee from climate change. Plus, how ticks are making people allergic to meat and how AI tools can help neurodivergent students succeed in their science careers.

records.title: AI systems devise hypotheses and ways to test them
records.description: AI agents collaborate to generate biomedical hypotheses and analyse data, moving towards a laboratory discovery cycle with AI involved in every step.

records.title: Coffee is under threat: how scientists are fighting to save it from extinction
records.description: Coffee plants are critically endangered by climate change. Researchers are finding solutions to keep scientists supplied with their favourite discovery fuel.

records.title: Vaccination elicits HIV broadly neutralizing antibodies in primates
records.description: Germline-targeting vaccines can reproducibly elicit prespecified classes of broadly neutralizing antibodies to prespecified epitopes under endogenous conditions.

records.title: Enhanced B cell priming induces broadly neutralizing HIV-1 apex antibodies
records.description: A germline-targeted HIV-1 Env (CAP256.OPT4) increases the efficiency of V2 apex broadly neutralizing antibody precursor priming by 30–400-fold compared with wild-type HIV-1 Envs and induces neutralization breadth in more than 90% of rhesus macaques, including Asn130-containing viruses.

records.title: Audio long read: Is the peptide craze backed by science? The promise behind the hype
records.description: The market for unregulated peptides is huge. Has the hottest trend in wellness got ahead of the science?

records.title: Ozone erosion started decades before the ozone hole’s discovery
records.description: Depletion of the ozone layer has been traced mainly to the widespread use of industrial chlorofluorocarbon chemicals, but there might have been an additional culprit.

records.title: Trump has big AI and quantum ambitions: this scientist’s job is to make them reality
records.description: Darío Gil knows that researchers are sceptical of the massive US artificial-intelligence push — he’s asking them to keep an open mind.

records.title: Daily briefing: Editing the epigenome with CRISPR to treat disease
records.description: CRISPR’s next act, the new ‘world’s fastest computer’ and how to triumph in the metaphorical penalty shootout of life.

records.title: How one US scientist is adapting to life abroad after DOGE cuts
records.description: Sarah Weisberg is one of a number of scientists who have made the move to Europe for job security.

records.title: How AI can crack open the ‘hidden curriculum’ for neurodivergent students
records.description: Marisa Chrysochoou and Keivan Stassun argue that AI tools could help students to navigate academia’s unwritten rules.

records.title: What’s the human cost of US research turmoil? A new film finds out
records.description: Science is a complex, interconnected, deeply human enterprise involving hard grind — and funding cuts and grant delays have come as a sucker punch to many.

records.title: Dementia risk in middle-aged people linked to a blood protein
records.description: Those under 55 with relatively high levels of the molecule GDF15 had an elevated risk of developing dementia.

records.title: Briefing Chat: What tickling a chimpanzee can tell us about the evolution of speech
records.description: Nature staff discuss how apes share a rhythm of laughter, and how AI use might degrade skills in medicine and computer science.

records.title: The poetry of twilight and the awe-inspiring magic of eclipses: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: Daily briefing: Ovaries start a second job after menopause
records.description: The organs might begin a role in the immune system after egg production stops. Plus, precise gene-editing of human embryos and a game to terraform Mars.

records.title: The surprising career parallels between footballers and researchers
records.description: Sarah Blackford reflects on how early-career scientists and professional football players share similar motivations, pressures and challenges.

records.title: CRISPR’s next act: the companies editing the epigenome to treat disease
records.description: A handful of start-up firms are testing therapies that target specific epigenetic markers to treat everything from high cholesterol to a rare muscular disorder.

records.title: Inside the new political screening that’s stalling NIH grants
records.description: Mandatory reviews by top health officials and checks for 235 disfavoured terms have left hundreds of vetted grant applications in administrative limbo.

records.title: I study World Cup penalty shoot-outs: they say a lot about the psychology of performance under pressure
records.description: Football's most nail-biting feature can reveal ways for everyone to manage stressful situations better.

records.title: Europe’s record heatwave: does the continent have a new climate?
records.description: Nature asks researchers whether scorching summers are the new norm for London, Paris and Berlin.

records.title: Publisher Correction: In situ nanocrystal confinement for efficient blue perovskite LEDs
Daily briefing: Humans and great apes giggle in the same rhythms
records.description: The findings hint that vocal motor control might have evolved from a shared ancestor. Plus, sea turtles’ navigation skills are only so-so and what’s next for the International Space Station.

records.title: Oo oo, ha ha: why humans and great apes giggle alike when tickled
records.description: The rhythmic patterns of laughter found in apes and humans reveal that complex primate vocal control might have started evolving 15 million years ago.

records.title: US funding uncertainties threaten to sink key global oceanography projects
records.description: The United States has led the world in observing the oceans — but cuts and threats of cuts have researchers worried it is no longer a reliable partner.

records.title: China’s LineShine just topped the global supercomputer ranking: what you need to know
records.description: The supercomputer has an innovative chip design that allows it to carry out more than two quintillion calculations per second.

records.title: Can you terraform Mars? Try Nature ’s game
records.description: Once the realm of science fiction, the idea of making Mars habitable is gaining traction. Nature consulted with key scientists to develop this experimental adventure.

records.title: How long-term dietary cholesterol can slow down its own clearance by liver cells
records.description: Cholesterol carried by low-density lipoprotein (LDL) drives heart disease and is cleared by liver cells expressing the receptor LDLR. A cell-signalling mechanism has been discovered through which high cholesterol promotes the enzyme-mediated degradation of LDLR. Blocking this enzyme restores LDLR levels in liver cells, suggesting a new strategy for treating high cholesterol.

records.title: Electric fields probe the symmetry of the ‘heavy hydrogen’ nucleus
records.description: The response of the nucleus of a deuterium atom to electric fields shows no evidence of asymmetry, which is consistent with conventional theories of particle physics.

records.title: ‘Edited’ human embryos reveal secrets of our development — and fuel ethical debate
records.description: Ethical discussions are urgently needed as genome-editing science advances, some researchers say.

records.title: Base editing reveals an essential role for NANOG in human embryogenesis
records.description: Base editing of NANOG in human embryos reveals its essential role in epiblast pluripotency, showing that loss of NANOG disrupts pluripotent epiblast specification and instead cells differentiate towards primitive endoderm and trophectoderm, which highlights base editing as a precise, non-genotoxic tool for studying human development.

records.title: Ligand-enabled distal desaturative lactonization of aliphatic acids
records.description: A designed ligand enables palladium-catalysed remote γ-C( sp 3 )–H activation in aliphatic carboxylic acids, providing efficient access to valuable γ-lactones and bioactive molecules from simple feedstock chemicals.

records.title: Reply to: On the robustness of topological gap detection via transport
Daily briefing: Sperm whales have different dialects
records.description: Whales in different areas of the Mediterranean use varying patterns of clicks and pauses. Plus, a technique to make protein samples one billion times bigger and the science of grief.

records.title: ‘Us’ not ‘them’: scientists must use their skills to help stop polarization and division
records.description: Researchers who study what divides people also have the tools to explore strategies to unite them.

records.title: A hidden predictor of sudden cardiac death uncovered by deep learning
records.description: A machine-learning model trained on thousands of electrocardiogram recordings identifies a previously unrecognized group of at-risk people.

records.title: ‘Megacluster’ of genes enables bacteria to make potent antibiotic mixture
records.description: Soil bacteria make cocktails of molecules that synergistically inhibit the growth of microbial pathogens — suggesting a strategy for tackling antibiotic-resistant infections.

records.title: Antibiotic cocktail made by soil bacteria can kill superbugs
records.description: Four antibiotic compounds produced in Streptomyces bacteria attack multiple parts of an essential metabolic pathway.

records.title: Crude oil turns cheap porous membrane into a sieve to refine itself without heat
records.description: An inexpensive, porous polymer membrane helps to separate raw crude oil, without heat or selective coating. Heavy hydrocarbons self-assemble inside the pores to create channels that are likely to be less than 2 nanometres wide, enriching the resulting permeate mix into light, ‘naphtha range’ hydrocarbons with 30% less energy cost and carbon dioxide emissions than conventional distillation.

records.title: Addendum: Transmission of MPXV from fire-footed rope squirrels to sooty mangabeys
Long-sought chemical inhibitors of β-arrestin proteins
records.description: Proteins called β-arrestins regulate signalling through members of the G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) superfamily. Small molecules that bind directly to the β-arrestins and inhibit their activities are the first chemical tools to probe their biology, opening avenues for transducer-targeted, pathway-specific GPCR therapeutics.

records.title: Why science needs the humanities more than ever
records.description: From AI to biotechnology, today’s scientific breakthroughs raise ethical and social challenges that technical expertise alone cannot solve.

records.title: A global map of seagrass ecosystems
records.description: Combining satellite imagery and machine learning has created the first comprehensive map of seagrass meadows, in a boost for the conservation of these crucial ecosystems.

records.title: On the robustness of topological gap detection via transport
The mutational landscape of STING-induced immunity
records.description: A massively parallel assay systematically charts the sequence-function landscape of the STING signalling protein, and the findings define molecular principles that tune STING activity and show its functional potential across immune contexts.

records.title: Genetic technologies to enhance crop nutritional value under climate change
records.description: This Review reflects on the joint power of genetic technologies, including untapped CRISPR–Cas techniques to combat hidden hunger and improve crop resilience, and argues in favour of their combined use to overcome these societal challenges.

records.title: Dietary cholesterol activates a Ral-dependent pathway driving LDLR turnover
records.description: Chronic dietary cholesterol activates Ral GTPases, which promote LDLR internalization and lysosomal degradation through RalBP1–REPS1 and CTSA, thereby reducing cholesterol clearance, whereas CTSA inhibition restores LDLR function and may offer a therapeutic strategy for cardiovascular disease.

records.title: Global high-resolution mapping of seagrass to support conservation
records.description: Global high-resolution mapping shows widespread seagrass loss and degradation since 2019, with most meadows outside protected areas, highlighting urgent conservation and climate-policy needs.

records.title: Disparate privacy risks from medical AI
records.description: AI models for medical diagnostics are vulnerable to membership inference attacks.

records.title: Role of methanesulfonic acid in atmospheric particle nucleation and growth
records.description: Experiments carried out at atmospheric conditions show that methanesulfonic acid is an important driver of particle formation and growth in cold marine environments, with simulations indicating enhanced cloud condensation nuclei concentrations, especially in polar regions.

records.title: Small-molecule modulation of β-arrestins
records.description: Integrated pharmacological, biochemical, biophysical and structural analyses of small-molecule β-arrestin inhibitors show how they block β-arrestin engagement with activated GPCRs, revealing their mechanism of action and uncovering a previously unrecognized allosteric regulatory site.

records.title: Immunological mechanisms of mRNA vaccines for infectious diseases
records.description: A Review of the immunological mechanisms of mRNA–lipid-nanoparticle vaccines for infectious diseases discusses how the components of this vaccine platform can be modified to fine-tune immune responses against challenging pathogens.

records.title: Dietary cholesterol activates a Ral-dependent pathway driving LDLR turnover
records.description: Chronic dietary cholesterol activates Ral GTPases, which promote LDLR internalization and lysosomal degradation through RalBP1–REPS1 and CTSA, thereby reducing cholesterol clearance, whereas CTSA inhibition restores LDLR function and may offer a therapeutic strategy for cardiovascular disease.

records.title: Global high-resolution mapping of seagrass to support conservation
records.description: Global high-resolution mapping shows widespread seagrass loss and degradation since 2019, with most meadows outside protected areas, highlighting urgent conservation and climate-policy needs.

records.title: Disparate privacy risks from medical AI
records.description: AI models for medical diagnostics are vulnerable to membership inference attacks.

records.title: Role of methanesulfonic acid in atmospheric particle nucleation and growth
records.description: Experiments carried out at atmospheric conditions show that methanesulfonic acid is an important driver of particle formation and growth in cold marine environments, with simulations indicating enhanced cloud condensation nuclei concentrations, especially in polar regions.

records.title: Small-molecule modulation of β-arrestins
records.description: Integrated pharmacological, biochemical, biophysical and structural analyses of small-molecule β-arrestin inhibitors show how they block β-arrestin engagement with activated GPCRs, revealing their mechanism of action and uncovering a previously unrecognized allosteric regulatory site.

records.title: Immunological mechanisms of mRNA vaccines for infectious diseases
records.description: A Review of the immunological mechanisms of mRNA–lipid-nanoparticle vaccines for infectious diseases discusses how the components of this vaccine platform can be modified to fine-tune immune responses against challenging pathogens.

records.title: Optical cooling by interfacial charge transfer in 2D heterostructures
records.description: Optical cooling in two-dimensional semiconductor heterostructures is demonstrated through phonon-assisted interfacial charge transfer, enabling cryogen-free thermal management without stringent quantum-efficiency requirements.

records.title:
Detection of anisotropic cosmic structures on a gigaparsec
            scale
records.description:
Using the parameter-free Angular Distribution of Pairwise Distances for
                measuring directional correlations, evidence is found for coherent anisotropic
                structures extending over gigaparsec scales, challenging the assumption that the
                Universe becomes statistically isotropic on sufficiently large scales.

records.title: An ECG biomarker for sudden cardiac death discovered with deep learning
records.description: A deep-learning model trained on electrocardiogram (ECG) waveforms identifies an easily visible biomarker that predicts sudden cardiac death more accurately than the current clinical state of the art.

records.title: Epiblast diversification and blood formation in a human pregastrula
records.description: High-resolution spatial transcriptome analysis of a human embryo at Carnegie stage 6 reveals three distinct developmental trajectories from the epiblast towards amnion, primitive streak and axial mesoderm, and detects the initiation of haematopoiesis before gastrulation, originating from hypoblast rather than epiblast.

records.title: Fourier pixels for bidirectional light control
records.description: A versatile platform of miniaturized Fourier-optics-based diffractive elements enables multifunctional pixels that fully control and sense the amplitude, phase and polarization of optical wavefronts for advanced photonic applications.

records.title: Genetic diversity of late Neanderthals in northwestern Europe
records.description: Genetic sequencing of multiple late Neanderthals living less than 52,500 years ago provides an overview of genetic diversity and demonstrates that even low-coverage nuclear genome data can increase resolution of within-Neanderthal diversity.

records.title: Crude oil fractionation by means of mesoporous polyacrylonitrile membranes
records.description: Porous polyacrylonitrile membranes—typically used as non-selective support layers—can be used to achieve effective molecular refining of crude oil at steady state, enabling substantial reductions in energy consumption, cooling water, and CO 2 emissions compared with distillation processes.

records.title: GW250114 reveals signatures of post-merger black-hole horizon
records.description: The observation of a direct wave after the merger of two black holes reveals signatures associated with the remnant black-hole horizon, establishing an observational channel to directly measure frame-dragging effects in black-hole ergospheres and probe the horizon surface gravity.

records.title: Chiral laser gyroscopes breaking the lock-in limit
records.description: Ring laser gyroscope lock-in has been eliminated using spontaneous symmetry breaking in a He–Ne laser, enabling accurate near-zero rotation sensing without external components, improving miniaturization and precision.

records.title: Zero-shot design of drug-binding proteins via neural iterative selection−expansion
records.description: By pairing two neural networks in an iterative optimization algorithm, small-molecule binding proteins can be designed from scratch with high accuracy, affinity and success rates, showing promise for applications in drug delivery and sequestration.

records.title: Ductile alloys offering 100 MPa tensile strength at 2,400 °C
records.description: A boron-stabilized oxide-strengthened tantalum alloy combines exceptional room-temperature ductility with record ultrahigh-temperature strength, enabling load-bearing applications above 2,000 °C.

records.title: Alternate RNA decoding results in stable and abundant proteins in mammals
records.description: Alternate RNA decoding, an understudied process, leads to peptide sequence modifications that can have substantial functional effects on protein stability, tissue-specific proteomes and disease.

records.title: A Streptomyces megacluster encodes synergistic biotin-targeting antibiotics
records.description: In Streptomyces spp., a conserved biosynthetic gene megacluster produces an arsenal of distinct antimicrobials that converge on bacterial biotin biosynthesis as a naturally evolved combination therapy.

records.title: Nepal’s new science ministry must strengthen scientific capacity
Alternate RNA decoding results in stable and abundant proteins in mammals
records.description: Alternate RNA decoding, an understudied process, leads to peptide sequence modifications that can have substantial functional effects on protein stability, tissue-specific proteomes and disease.

records.title: A Streptomyces megacluster encodes synergistic biotin-targeting antibiotics
records.description: In Streptomyces spp., a conserved biosynthetic gene megacluster produces an arsenal of distinct antimicrobials that converge on bacterial biotin biosynthesis as a naturally evolved combination therapy.

records.title: Nepal’s new science ministry must strengthen scientific capacity
Academic success still assumes uninterrupted careers
The halo effect: how academic hierarchy undermines peer review and enables fraud
Do not leave fungi out of impact assessments
A 1970s patent that changed the course of commercial biotechnology
records.description: The scientific community awaits a patent for recombinant DNA technology, and experimentation with an anaesthetic from puffballs, in our weekly dip into Nature ’s archive.

records.title: Silicon Valley’s vision for global AI is flawed: each country needs its own blueprint
records.description: From energy grids to language performance, emerging economies are exposing the limits of today’s artificial-intelligence strategy as it expands globally.

records.title: Retraction Note: Sub-second periodicity in a fast radio burst
Europe as science superpower: what it will take to rival the US and China
records.description: Amid chaos in US science and geopolitical turmoil, Europe wants to position itself as a research haven — but questions about funding and innovation remain.

records.title: How should I respond to race-based exclusion in my lab?
records.description: A researcher in Europe feels left out of their team and held to different standards from their colleagues. How can they challenge exclusion without risking their position?

records.title: Daily briefing: NASA to launch satellite-rescue mission
records.description: The space agency will lift the orbit of a falling satellite by around 200 kilometres. Plus, Europe’s efforts to take on the US and China as a science superpower and the narcissism of bosses who want to nix remote working.

records.title: Europe must seize the moment to lead on free and open science
records.description: An under-appreciated research powerhouse, Europe has a responsibility to champion democratic science that is accessible to all the world’s research talent.

records.title: Making samples one billion times bigger lets simple microscopes pinpoint amino acids
records.description: Stretching protein samples in all directions pulls molecules farther apart, allowing them to be visualized using only light microscopy.

records.title: A spacecraft is falling to its doom — can NASA save it?
records.description: A successful rescue of the Swift space observatory could be a good omen for the Hubble Space Telescope.

records.title: The first ticking ‘nuclear clocks’ are here — what can they do?
records.description: Two research teams have created a new, long-awaited type of timekeeper.

records.title: Will AI spark a scientific renaissance — or a diffuse monoculture?
records.description: Artificial intelligence’s ability to enrich science will depend not only on model capability, but also on whether researchers, reviewers and funders reward originality over speed.

records.title: Forty years of high-temperature superconductivity
records.description: The first demonstration of superconductivity at 35 kelvin drove decades of materials research and introduced a puzzle about this strange state of matter.

records.title: Daily briefing: First-ever ‘nuclear’ clocks put atomic clocks in the shade
records.description: Two research teams have created a new, long-awaited type of timekeeper. Plus, how backlash has saved an ocean-monitoring network targeted by Trump and how our cultural heritage is put at risk by climate change.

records.title: Make science more reliable: study people as they go about their lives
records.description: Researchers have long discussed the replication crisis. Now it’s time to tackle another problem in the behavioural sciences: generalizability.

records.title: Isotopic evidence for a cold and distant origin of 3I/ATLAS
records.description: Carbon isotopic measurements of the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS reveal that it may have formed as long ago as 12 billion years and thus represents a preserved fragment of an ancient planetary system.

records.title: C-glycoside synthesis through radical cross-coupling of glycohydrazides
records.description: A platform for synthesis of C-aryl glycosides using glycosyl sulfonyl hydrazides as redox-neutral radical precursors for cross-coupling produces versatile and readily diversifiable building blocks, expanding practical access to carbohydrate-derived therapeutics and chemical tools.

records.title: Stereoretentive decarbonylative C( sp 3 )–C( sp 3 ) cross-coupling
records.description: A catalytic stereoretentive decarbonylation step is used to form a chiral alkylnickel intermediate from easily available chiral amino acid and α-hydroxy-acid derivatives, providing a straightforward approach to stereocontrolled C( sp 3 )–C( sp 3 ) bond formation.

records.title: A long-lived butterfly’s secret to graceful ageing
records.description: Species in the Heliconius genus are among the longest-lived butterflies, thanks to a diet of pollen.

records.title: Author Correction: Autophagic cell death restricts chromosomal instability during replicative crisis
Briefing Chat: Testosterone and sperm might get a boost from obesity drugs
records.description: Nature staff discuss preliminary data on the effects of GLP-1 drugs on male fertility, plus a two-year trial of a brain–computer interface.

records.title: Stem cells banish severe autoimmune disease for 15 years
records.description: Two people were the first to receive the therapy for a condition that damages the spinal cord and optic nerve.

records.title: Daily briefing: Human detritus remakes geology
records.description: What, exactly, is a rock? Plus, a stem-cell success for a severe autoimmune disease and evidence that ‘AI deskilling’ is real.

records.title: Clues to the sloth’s sloth found in its genome
records.description: Sequencing shows duplication of genes that affect mitochondria, the organelles that provide energy for cells.

records.title: It slices! It dices! Sashimi-Bot handles seafood with ease
records.description: Fillets of raw fish are irregular in shape and floppy in texture, but a robot with three arms has learnt how to manipulate a salmon loin.

records.title: Is AI ruining our skills? Early results are in — and they’re not good
records.description: Reliance on artificial-intelligence tools degrades the abilities of physicians and software engineers, studies show.

records.title: Brexit tore apart European science — now the research rifts are healing
records.description: The UK’s share of EU research funding is climbing, but lost networks will be harder to recover.

records.title: Cell transplant across the tree of life hints at how animals emerged
records.description: Embryonic ‘organizer cells’ can tell embryos of various phyla what kind of body to build.

records.title: Daily briefing: The brain builds a sentence neuron by neuron
records.description: Researchers have tracked the electrical activity of individual brain cells during conversation in real time. Plus, the history of GPS and a cross-species transplant that could reveal clues about the origin of animals.

records.title: Fiery data hint that controlled forest fires benefit human health
records.description: Analysis of wildfire in California suggests a net reduction in exposure to blaze-related air pollution.

records.title: The brain region that could provide a cognitive ‘reservoir’ in old age
records.description: Having a greater tissue volume in some parts of the cerebellum is linked to higher scores on cognitive tests.

records.title: DNA from hunter-gatherer teeth reveals secrets of ancient plague
records.description: Analysis shows evidence of deadly outbreaks 5,500 years ago — plus, a prototype dark-matter detector.

records.title: How the zebrafish brain weaves recent experiences into future decisions
records.description: Animals often use recent experience to guide future choices. Whole-brain imaging in larval zebrafish ( Danio rerio ) reveals a dedicated neural circuit that governs history-biased decisions: the thalamus maintains the most recent event as a stable pattern of neuronal activity, and the brainstem integrates recent experiences into a continuous signal that biases future action.

records.title: Freezing brain damage in its tracks: cooling drugs limit stroke injury in mice
records.description: A two-drug combination induces hypothermia in mice by lowering metabolism and dilating blood vessels.

records.title: Oceans in Asia smash heat records — what it means for extreme weather
records.description: Report shows region is particularly vulnerable to the effects of climate change.

records.title: Wah-ult in the vault
records.description: Relics of wonder.

records.title: Reconfigurable quantum computer juggles 98 qubits
records.description: A quantum computer based on trapped ions can connect any two quantum bits, reaching performance levels that conventional computers cannot match.

records.title: Reimagining machine vision with optical computing
records.description: A general-purpose artificial-intelligence vision system for use in image-sensing devices has been developed by embedding fundamentals of core computer-vision operations into a light-manipulating planar material called an optical metasurface. A prototype enables accurate, real-time perception and processing across diverse tasks, suggesting that this could be a solution for rapid, low-energy, on-device vision intelligence.

records.title: Navigating a crowded developing brain leaves neurons with broken DNA
records.description: As neurons migrate to their final destinations in the forming brain, their DNA gets damaged. The brain has evolved a fix, but there can be lasting consequences if repair fails.

records.title: The EU needs to back its ambition to end animal testing with cash
records.description: The European Union has declared that it wants to stop using animals in chemical safety testing. Its goal will need a timeline and a serious funding commitment.

records.title: Should nicotine be regulated like a narcotic? A Pacific nation makes the case
records.description: Existing global efforts to reduce harms caused by smoking have targeted tobacco smoking, but vapes containing nicotine are also harmful.

records.title: How the brain builds sentences, neuron by neuron
records.description: Neural maps reveal the specialized cells that produce speech.

records.title: Light-controlled microgripper punches above its weight
records.description: A microscale gripper that can be opened and closed using light can fit into tight spaces and perform tasks linked to clinical applications.

records.title: Daily briefing: The proteins that protect us from deadly mutations
records.description: Proteins that ‘buffer’ the effects of mutations could help to treat diseases such as cancers. Plus, goats can follow human voices and the battle over a key ocean observatory project in the United States.

records.title: The ancestors of eukaryotic cells contained a mix of genes from various microbes
records.description: Reconstruction of the ancestral gene repertoire of eukaryotic cells reveals traces of a series of close, long-term interactions with diverse microorganisms, and a role of viruses in gene exchange. The findings challenge the view that eukaryotic cells evolved from a simple merger of just two organisms.

records.title: Emergent decadal predictability in Antarctic contribution to sea-level rise
records.description: Although Antarctic ice loss projections diverge widely by 2100, this Perspective shows that present-day rates robustly predict mid-century sea level rise, providing a firm basis for near-term planning, while highlighting priorities for model development aimed at resolving longer-term sea level rise uncertainty.

records.title: These ‘master’ proteins protect us from deadly mutations — and could inspire new drugs
records.description: Biology has clever ways to mask the effects of potentially harmful gene mutations. Scientists are investigating how this ‘buffering’ works — and how to exploit it.

records.title: A distant brown dwarf coplanar to a warm Jupiter and a hot super-Earth
records.description: Analysis of long-term radial velocity data and transit time variations, induced by a super-Earth, a warm Jupiter and a brown dwarf in a coplanar orbit around the relatively young star TOI201.

records.title: Probing picometre-scale interlayer deformations via hyperbolic polaritons
records.description: A new polaritonic optical method that uses the mid-infrared out-of-plane hyperbolic polaritons mode is described and experimentally validated to allow the examination of picometre-scale interlayer deformations, providing a bridge between nanomechanics and photonics.

records.title: Optical fibre gripper for high-performance 3D micromanipulation
records.description: A miniature three-dimensional optical fibre gripper enables powerful, precise micromanipulation of particles and single cells in confined spaces, bridging the gap between optical and mechanical tweezers.

records.title: A prototype differential atom interferometer for fundamental physics
records.description: A prototype differential atom interferometer operates at the standard quantum limit with no excess noise beyond atom shot noise, achieving performance in line with the specifications for future long-baseline atom interferometers.

records.title: Structure of the pre-initiation complex explains CMGE biogenesis
records.description: Cryo-electron microscopy and biochemical reconstitution experiments in yeast provide insight into the assembly of the CMGE complex, a helicase that establishes bidirectional DNA replication in eukaryotic cells, and elucidate the role of the firing factor Sld2.

records.title: A 98-qubit trapped-ion quantum computer with all-to-all connectivity
records.description: A new quantum computer, Quantinuum Helios, which is a 98-qubit trapped-ion quantum processor built on the QCCD architecture, demonstrates performance well beyond classical capabilities and provides a path for scaling up quantum computing.

records.title: Fast formation to reinforce lithium-rich cathodes
records.description: Fast formation in lithium-ion batteries outperforms conventional slow formation, lowering costs and improving battery capacity, stability and cycle life, offering broader application to electrode systems.

records.title: Revealing competitive interfacial reactions in high-energy Li–S batteries
records.description: Visualization of concentration-driven phase segregation within high-concentration interfacial layers in the context of high-energy lithium–sulfur batteries using liquid-cell electrochemical transmission electron microscopy reveals competitive interfacial reactions under lean electrolyte conditions at different phase boundaries.

records.title: Molecular basis of polyadenylated RNA fate determination in the nucleus
records.description: Biochemical, structural and cell biological analyses reveal that UAP56 (DDX39B) assembles with a TREX-2–like module that redirects non-functional polyadenylated RNAs from export to degradation.

records.title: Rock weathering can counteract river CO 2 emissions induced by permafrost thaw
records.description: Permafrost thaw on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau increases rock-weathering rates while reducing river CO 2 emissions, suggesting geological carbon fluxes may eventually outpace thaw-driven emissions.

records.title: Cortical development dynamics across autism spectrum disorder mouse models
records.description: Using single-nucleus multi-omic sequencing, diverse autism spectrum disorder-linked gene mutations converge on transient, stage-specific disruptions in early brain development, and highlight sex-specific gene expression alterations.

records.title: A blastoporal organizer in a ctenophore
records.description: Experiments using the comb jelly Mnemiopsis leidyi and the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis reveal that the emergence of a core signalling pathway may have been a key innovation enabling the transition to multicellularity in animals.

records.title: Confined migration induces non-lethal DNA damage in developing neurons
records.description: The migration of neurons in developing cerebral and cerebellar cortices is accompanied by massive DNA double-strand breaks due to mechanostress during passage through narrow interstitial spaces.

records.title: Analysis of 173,303 exomes and genomes in the Pakistan Genome Resource
records.description: The Pakistan Genome Resource compiles biobank data from 173,303 individuals with high familial relatedness, broadening the catalogue of human genetic variation and establishing a population-specific genomic reference for Pakistan.

records.title: A mosaic of whole-body representations on the human precentral gyrus
records.description: A comprehensive map of the human motor cortex at single-neuron resolution is described.

records.title: Spatial distribution of the proteome in the human body and in cancers
records.description: A spatially resolved map of the human proteome across a variety of healthy tissues and cancers provides wide-ranging insights in developmental biology and oncology, and could aid the identification of therapeutic targets and development of treatments for cancer.

records.title: Towards conversational artificial intelligence for disease management
records.description: Advances to the artificial intelligence system AMIE enable it to manage disease across multiple visits while reasoning over a corpus of clinical guidelines and patient history, outperforming primary care physicians on management reasoning tasks.

records.title: Lethal plague outbreaks in Lake Baikal hunter-gatherers 5,500 years ago
records.description: Analyses of ancient DNA from hunter-gatherers near Lake Baikal in southeast Siberia around 5,500 years ago indicate that highly virulent Yersinia pestis emerged earlier than previously estimated, far from the next known cases of infection in Late Neolithic Europe.

records.title: Mapping the neuronal building blocks of human language with language models
records.description: Wide-scale recordings reveal neurons in the human brain that encode fundamental components of language such as the grammatical relationships between words, their parts of speech and the higher-order syntactic structure of phrases and sentences.

records.title: Towards autonomous medical artificial intelligence agents
records.description: A large language model artificial intelligence agent operating in a sandboxed electronic health record system can autonomously take patient histories, order tests, interpret findings, diagnose conditions and propose treatments, outperforming experienced clinicians while adhering to safety standards and clinical guidelines.

records.title: CHPO coordinates chilling recovery and nitrogen use in rice
records.description: A rice gene, CHPO , links chilling resilience with nitrogen-use efficiency, revealing a domestication-shaped regulatory mechanism that could guide breeding of climate-resilient, sustainable rice varieties.

records.title: Optical metasurfaces for general vision processing on the edge
records.description: By embedding core computer vision principles into a large-scale optical metasurface, an efficient vision processing system using far fewer parameters is demonstrated to outperform many digital models and enables deployment on edge devices.

records.title: Visualizing the impact of quenched disorder on 2D electron Wigner solids
records.description: A technique combining atomically resolved scanning tunnelling microscopy with neural-quantum-state quantum Monte Carlo simulation of disordered 2D electron Wigner solids establishes a powerful framework to enable the clear identification of two distinct defect-induced disorder regimes.

records.title: Cucurbituril-based anion-conducting membranes with supramolecular nanopores
records.description: A supramolecular strategy, in which uniform, dynamic nanopores are constructed, overcomes the limitations of limited structural control, mechanical fragility or demanding synthesis in nanoporous anion-conducting membranes, providing a versatile tool for molecularly engineering transport pathways.

records.title: Confirmation that bryozoan animals were present during the Cambrian explosion
records.description: Bryozoans are marine invertebrates that live in colonies and have long been considered absent from the Cambrian explosion — a rapid evolutionary event that began around 538 million years ago. Newly discovered fossils from the Cambrian period reveal that the bryozoan phylum had already diversified by this time.

records.title: ‘Hidden hero’ peptides guard crops against sudden cold
records.description: A protein signal remains silent under normal conditions but is activated under cold stress to protect developing pollen. This ‘on-demand’ resilience mechanism could enable the development of ‘climate smart’ crops that maintain high yields in good years and food security under climate stress.

records.title: When drug discovery fails: scientists share their frustrations with the process
records.description: In clinical trials, there are many times (and ways) a therapeutic can come up short.

records.title: Is the peptide craze backed by science? The promise behind the hype

records.title: Artificial intelligence shines a light on hidden global migration flows

records.title: Daily briefing: Ancient ground squirrels ate like ‘zombies of the Pleistocene’

records.title: Gen Z scepticism towards AI is a wake-up call — universities must take it seriously
records.description: The challenge for universities is not adopting artificial intelligence, but doing so in ways that the current generation of students can trust.

records.title: How I use AI to turn failed drugs into new medicines
records.description: By combining chemistry and biology with AI modelling, Layla Hosseini-Gerami is finding and reviving therapeutics with ‘huge potential’.

records.title: Doubting Thomas
