records.title: Light slows down carbon nanotubes in water
records.description: Water-suspended carbon nanotubes move more slowly in green light, suggesting that excited electrons in the tubes couple to the water through ‘quantum friction’.

records.title: Structural basis for chaperone-guided assembly of RNA-induced silencing complex
records.description: Structures of the AGO maturation complex reveal how chaperones and an RNA duplex drive assembly of the RNA-induced silencing complex.

records.title: SIRT7 regulates dosage compensation and safeguards the female X chromosome
records.description: SIRT7 safeguards X-chromosome integrity and dosage balance with autosomes.

records.title: A 5.3-million-year-old deep-sea whale necropolis in the Diamantina Zone
records.description: Researchers uncovered an enormous deep-sea accumulation of whale remains in the southeastern Indian Ocean, showing long-term, specialized ecosystems and an extensive fossil record that offers new insight into deep-ocean biodiversity and whale evolutionary history.

records.title: Whole-genome duplication shaped cell-type evolution in the vertebrate brain
records.description: Analyses of brain single-cell transcriptomes from human, mouse, lizard, lamprey and amphioxus reveal that duplicated genes (ohnologues) played a pivotal part in early vertebrate cell-type diversification.

records.title: In situ nanocrystal confinement for efficient blue perovskite LEDs
records.description: Efficient blue perovskite light-emitting diodes with an external quantum efficiency of 21.8% are achieved through in situ polymerization-driven nanocrystal confinement.

records.title: A prognostic human brain network for diffuse midline glioma
records.description: Tumour network mapping of diffuse midline glioma (DMG) defines a conserved and prognostically important brain network in children with DMG, consistent with the hypothesis that DMGs exploit otherwise healthy brain circuits to promote tumour growth.

records.title: Two-component exciton condensates in an electron–hole bilayer
records.description: Macroscopic quantum coherence arises in two-component exciton Bose–Einstein condensates within MoSe 2 /hBN/WSe 2 electron–hole bilayers, exhibiting distinct spin–valley polarized phases, quantum phase transitions under magnetic fields and stable condensate behaviour up to approximately 1.8 K.

records.title: Mutation-dependent responses to sleep and exercise in clonal haematopoiesis
records.description: Sleep and exercise can slow clonal haematopoiesis and limit mutant cell-driven atherosclerosis.

records.title: Efficient and accurate neural-field reconstruction using resistive memory
records.description: A co-optimized AI hardware–software system using resistive-memory computing improves energy efficiency and parallelism for sparse signal reconstruction in imaging and three-dimensional vision applications.

records.title: Gene ancestries reveal diverse microbial associations during eukaryogenesis
records.description: Phylogenomic reconstruction of the proteome of the last eukaryotic common ancestor sheds light on the origin of eukaryotes, indicating an important role of horizontal transfer of genes from diverse bacterial and viral donors.

records.title: Molecular glue degraders of HuR suppress BRAF-mutant colorectal cancer
records.description: Molecular glue degraders of the RNA-binding protein HuR have therapeutic potential for BRAF-mutant cancers.

records.title: Light-induced quantum friction of carbon nanotubes in water
records.description: Near-infrared fluorescent carbon nanotubes exhibit light-induced quantum friction in water, in which exciton interactions slow nanoscale motion and enable optical control of diffusion and fluid dynamics.

records.title: Lignin to adipic acid in a high-yield chemical and biological redox process
records.description: A chemical and biological redox process that resembles processes in petrochemical refining is used to convert lignin from poplar into a single, valuable bioproduct, adipic acid, in high yields.

records.title: Measurement of reactor neutrino oscillation with the first JUNO data
records.description: The first data of the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory deliver high-precision neutrino oscillation parameters, improving measurements and demonstrating readiness to determine neutrino mass ordering.

records.title: Mitochondria directly interact with the nuclear pore complex
records.description: Mitochondria interact directly with the nuclear pore complex via VDAC1–RANBP2 binding to sustain nuclear ATP levels.

records.title: A thalamus–brainstem attractor network drives history-biased decisions
records.description: Whole-brain, cellular-resolution imaging reveals a hierarchical thalamus–brainstem attractor network that encodes recent history and shapes behavioural bias in zebrafish.

records.title: Improved quantum processor logical error rates via correction and detection
records.description: Experimental demonstration of quantum error-correcting codes combined with error detection and post-selection applied to a trapped-ion quantum processor shows improvements in logical error rates ranging from 11× to 800× compared with several physical circuit baselines.

records.title: Deep learning four decades of human migration
records.description: A global annual migration-flow dataset (1990–2024) is produced using deep-learning models and diverse sources to estimate movements across 230 countries with improved temporal resolution, coverage and uncertainty estimates.

records.title: Amplified Arctic iceberg traffic reshapes benthic biodiversity
records.description: Accelerated Arctic glacier disintegration and a more dynamic sea ice cover are increasing iceberg-delivered dropstones in the deep ocean, reshaping seafloor habitats and extending cryospheric impacts far beyond glaciers.

records.title: Building user-driven climate adaptation products
records.description: A systematic review and analysis shows how user-centred design can be integrated into, and strengthen, co-production approaches for building user-driven climate adaptation products.

records.title: A first-in-class pulsatile FXR agonist for bile-acid-related liver diseases
records.description: Linafexor is a rapidly cleared FXR agonist designed to mimic natural bile acid signalling, achieving transient receptor activation with strong efficacy and reduced toxicity in preclinical and early clinical studies.

records.title: Diverse binding poses of agonistic neurotoxins on human Na v 1.6

records.description: Structures called plastoglobules organize the enzymes that turn nitrogen into compounds needed for plant growth, offering lessons for sustainable agriculture.

records.title: Ubiquitin tags detected on non-protein biomolecules using new method
records.description: An innovative method of mass spectrometry has detected the small protein ubiquitin on biomolecules other than proteins. In mouse liver, the energy-storing molecule glycogen has a large increase in ubiquitination — involving 1% of the liver’s total ubiquitin — during fasting, when glycogen is broken down.

records.title: Troubled waters: a plant protein senses when cells are running dry
records.description: How cells sense fluctuations in the availability of water has long been unclear. The protein SAM8 is now shown to undergo a process called phase separation in a way that depends on its hydration, thereby sensing cellular water availability and linking changes in water status to the regulation of gene expression.

records.title: The size of tropical vegetation gross primary production
A natural depsipeptide antibiotic binds the E-site of the bacterial ribosome
records.description: Improved fractionation strategies can identify antibiotics with previously unseen scaffolds and mechanisms, exemplified by manikomycin from Streptomyces rimosus , which acts by targeting the E-site of the bacterial large ribosomal subunit.

records.title: Earth’s east–west albedo symmetry
records.description: Analysis of a 25-year satellite record shows that Earth has a persistent east–west albedo symmetry split at 27° E, with clear-sky albedo, cloud radiative effect and open-ocean fraction exhibiting a triple symmetry around this meridian.

records.title: Relativistic electron acceleration at the bow shock of Jupiter and beyond
records.description: NASA’s Juno observations show relativistic electron acceleration at the bow shock of Jupiter and establish a universal scaling law linking shock size to maximum cosmic ray energy.

records.title: Acquired genetic and cell-state changes in IDH-mutant glioma progression
records.description: Longitudinal transcriptomic, chromatin and genomic analyses of the two types of IDH-mutant glioma reveal in detail how disease progression is influenced by interdependent genetic, epigenetic and microenvironmental factors.

records.title: Mining triggers extensive additional deforestation in sub-Saharan Africa
records.description: Extensive mining activity leads to large-scale deforestation of dense tropical forests across sub-Saharan Africa, driven particularly by key energy transition minerals such as cobalt.

records.title: Cold-induced peptide signalling secures pollen resilience and crop yield
records.description: A small-peptide signalling axis involving RGF family members controls resilience to cold stress in tomatoes and rice; modulating this pathway prevents cold-induced yield losses.

records.title: Teosinte alleles enhance nitrogen assimilation and seed protein in maize
records.description: Teosinte alleles enhance nitrogen assimilation and seed protein without lowering crop yield when expressed in modern maize, providing a powerful strategy for crop improvement to meet future population demands.

records.title: Cell-type-resolved genetic variation shapes inflammatory bowel disease risk
records.description: Single-cell mapping of cis -expression quantitative trait loci in inflammatory bowel disease revealed distal, enhancer-enriched variants detected at the cell-type level more frequently co-localize with genome-wide association study loci than those identified at the tissue level.

records.title: Plastoglobules compartmentalize nitrogen assimilation in maize
records.description: Chloroplast plastoglobules act as nitrogen-assimilation hubs in maize, with key enzymes enhancing nitrogen-use efficiency and offering new strategies for developing high-yield, sustainable crops.

records.title: Analysis of trade-offs of post-sorting plastic packaging
records.description: An analysis of post-sorting plastic packaging shows that target polymer purity is similar across source-separation and post-sorting pathways, but post-sorted plastics contain more contaminants that need to be removed before recyclate production.

records.title: Spermine is an endogenous iron chelator that inhibits ferroptosis
records.description: A non-canonical metabolic route for spermine synthesis mediated by ALDH18A1 limits iron availability and lipid peroxidation in hepatocellular carcinoma.

records.title: Chiral superfluorescence from perovskite superlattices at room temperature
records.description: Chiral perovskite superlattices exhibit room-temperature circularly polarized superfluorescence, with emission intensity and polarization controllable by weak magnetic fields.

records.title: Mechanophore cross-linking enhances ballistic energy dissipation of polymers
records.description: Embedding a small fraction of force-sensitive mechanophores as cross-links into common polymers enhances ballistic energy dissipation.

records.title: Commensal-derived acetylcholine enhances mucosal immune education
records.description: A diet–microbiome–host axis strengthens mucosal immune defences and reinforces host–microbiota mutualism.

records.title: Nuclear shell structure governs short-range nucleon pairing
records.description: The scattering of high-energy electrons from three different nuclei demonstrated that short-range-correlated pairing depends far more on the specific quantum orbitals occupied by nucleons than predicted by theoretical models.

records.title: High-pulse-energy integrated mode-locked laser using a Mamyshev oscillator
records.description: A Mamyshev oscillator mode-locked laser compactly integrated on a photonic-chip delivers nanojoule, femtosecond pulses.

records.title: LASER couples damage sensing to ESCRT assembly for lysosome repair
records.description: ATG8 conjugation on damaged lysosomes triggers rapid assembly of a protein complex containing TFG, which directs lysosomal membrane repair by recruiting ESCRT proteins to sites of damage.

records.title: High-pulse-energy integrated mode-locked laser using a Mamyshev oscillator
records.description: A Mamyshev oscillator mode-locked laser compactly integrated on a photonic-chip delivers nanojoule, femtosecond pulses.

records.title: LASER couples damage sensing to ESCRT assembly for lysosome repair
records.description: ATG8 conjugation on damaged lysosomes triggers rapid assembly of a protein complex containing TFG, which directs lysosomal membrane repair by recruiting ESCRT proteins to sites of damage.

records.title: Cooperation conflicts with equality when allocating public goods
records.description: Uniform sharing of public goods can boost cooperation in social networks, but often concentrates benefits among well-connected individuals, creating inequality despite greater collective success.

records.title: Enamel nanocrystal misorientation increased with meat-eating and agriculture
records.description: An analysis of enamel nanocrystal misorientation in primate and human teeth across three major dietary shifts in human evolution shows that misorientation increased with harder diets, suggesting that misorientation contributes to enamel’s resilience.

records.title: High-fidelity modular skeletons authenticate a Cambrian origin for Bryozoa
records.description: Exquisite early Cambrian fossils of Protomelission gatehousei and Dayingomelission hexaclitia preserve soft-tissue anatomy and skeletal microstructure, confirming that these taxa are definitively bryozoans and indicating a deeper origin for the Bryozoa than was first apparent.

records.title: Centromeric footprints preserve telomere integrity in ALT cancers
records.description: Centromeric DNA repeat insertions and CENP-A chromatin assembly are identified as genomic signatures that preserve telomere integrity in ALT cancer cells.

records.title: Queen cell architecture shapes honey bee queen development
records.description: Worker bee construction behaviour actively engineers a physicochemical niche that is crucial for queen development in honey bees.

records.title: Global plastics treaty must be built on a foundation of monitoring
Chemicals meant to be eco-friendly accumulate aloft
records.description: Large-scale measurements of atmospheric hydrofluoroolefins show that their levels are rising, but the implications are unclear.

records.title: Natural capital accounting needs a way to assess uncertainty

records.title: The future of science communication is not an article like this

records.title: Will AI ruin the social sciences — or revolutionize them?

records.title: Enantioselective hydrogen atom relay via non-covalent catalyst assembly

records.title: Smartphone camera takes users’ pulse passively during device use
records.description: A machine-learning system has been developed that can monitor heart rate using facial video clips that are captured passively by the user-facing camera during everyday smartphone use. records.description: High smoking rates and polluted air mean lung cancer cases are rising fastest in places such as China. Africa could soon head in the same direction.

records.title: Nests in an egg cell: structures of protein-storage units in oocytes
records.description: A fertilized egg’s first few divisions rely on proteins stored in fibrous structures. The ordered nature of these structures and clues about their function are revealed.

records.title: Peter H. Raven obituary: visionary botanist who transformed our understanding of plant diversity
records.description: As the leader of the Missouri Botanical Garden, he called global attention to the biodiversity crisis.

records.title: Nature is expanding Registered Reports to all the fields in which we publish
records.description: Registered Reports improve the credibility of scientific claims by rewarding big questions, sound methods and solid analyses. They need to become a standard tool in research.

records.title: Social‑media feeds are detoxified by a redesigned algorithm
records.description: A large-scale experiment tested the impact of changing the Bluesky feed-ranking algorithm on political content and perceptions during the 2024 US presidential election. By making feeds more representative of users, the ‘diversified extremity’ algorithm reduced exposure to polarizing content and made perceptions of social norms more accurate, without reducing user enjoyment.

records.title: Child sexual abuse enabled by digital technologies is widespread and under-reported
records.description: One in six Internet-using adolescents in parts of Africa and Asia faced technology-facilitated sexual abuse in 2020–21. As digital access expands globally, better protection is crucial.

records.title: We vibe-coded a custom AI poetry lab. Here’s how you can, too.

records.description: An open-source atlas generated by an AI tool called ESMFold2 vastly increases the known protein universe.

records.title: Hailstorms are predicted to hit harder with climate change
records.description: The global likelihood of damage from hailstorms is predicted to increase substantially by the end of the century, owing to increases in hailstone size as the climate warms. However, regional differences are expected, with greater increases in hailstone size and damage in mid-latitudes and reductions in the tropics and subtropics.

records.title: How the connection between lung cancer and the brain could lead to better treatments
records.description: The discovery that small cell lung cancer has several neuronal features is yielding biological insights that could ultimately save lives.

records.title: Five highlights from lung-cancer research
records.description: Treatment breakthroughs, improved screening approaches and other developments from recent studies.

records.title: Biobank analysis reveals more than 88,000 genetic associations with metabolic traits
records.description: An investigation of the Estonian Biobank and the UK Biobank has identified more than 88,000 associations between more than 8,000 genomic regions and metabolic traits. The combined size of the sample enabled the detection of many more associations than in previous efforts.

records.title: GDP and beyond: why treating nature as capital cannot save the planet

records.title: Daily briefing: The known protein universe just got a lot bigger

Human blood stem cells remember previous inflammation
records.description: Inflammatory stress is shown to reprogram a subset of human haematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). These inflammatory memory (HSC-iM) cells have reduced differentiation and pass on inflammation-related gene programs to their immune-cell progeny. HSC-iM cells accumulate with age, and cancer-associated mutations affect HSC-iM cells more than they do other HSCs in clonal blood disorders.

records.title: β-Arrestin condensates regulate G-protein-coupled receptor function
records.description: β-Arrestins, multifunctional adaptor proteins that regulate G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), form phase-separated condensates, suggesting that β-arrestin liquid–liquid phase separation organizes and diversifies GPCR signalling functions.

records.title: Human haematopoietic stem cells remember inflammatory stress
records.description: Using xenograft inflammation–recovery models and single-cell multiomics, a haematopoietic stem cell population after inflammatory stress is identified.

records.title: Darkness and body size shaped end-Cretaceous marine extinction patterns
records.description: Trait-based ecosystem modelling shows that impact-driven darkness and body-size-dependent extinction thresholds, rather than carbon-dioxide increase or acidification, drove most of the observed end-Cretaceous marine extinction patterns.

records.title: Sparse-to-dense coding transformation between hippocampal areas CA3 and CA1
records.description: The hippocampus exhibits a CA3-to-CA1 coding transformation that combines fast learning with an efficient, compressed neural code.

records.title: Technology mediation in child sexual exploitation and abuse in Africa and Asia
records.description: Enabling parental mediation of online activities and children’s knowledge of where to seek help after sexual harassment or assault is associated with higher rates of disclosure of technology-facilitated CSEA.

records.title: αKG-mediated carnitine synthesis drives DNA repair via histone acetylation
records.description: The metabolite αKG promotes carnitine synthesis and increases site-specific histone acetylation, thereby promoting homologous recombination-mediated DNA repair, which has potential implications for chemoresistant cancers.

records.title: Four ppm measurement of the antihydrogen ground-state hyperfine splitting
records.description: A measurement of the hyperfine splitting energy of the ground state of antihydrogen at 4 ppm precision reaches a point at which this result is sensitive to the internal structure of the antiproton.

records.title: Cellular water-potential sensing through biomolecular condensation

records.title: Distinct genetic architecture in the tails of complex traits

records.title: Universal transcriptomic hallmarks of mammalian ageing and mortality
records.description: Integration of gene expression data from multiple tissues across four mammalian species reveals conserved transcriptomic signatures of mammalian ageing and mortality and uncovers the modular architecture of ageing and mortality hallmarks.

records.title: Substrate selectivity of the human RNA m 5 C methyltransferase NSUN2
records.description: NSUN2 is an enzyme that adds a small chemical mark to RNA molecules and uniquely selects its targets based on specific sequence patterns and structural features.

records.title: Transcription factor codes patterning neuronal groundplans of the cerebrum

records.title: Genetic architecture of sugarcane traits in a polyploid genomics framework

records.title: Metamaterial-enhanced near-field radiative heat transfer

records.title: Monolithic three-dimensional integration of silicon transistors
records.description: Uniformly doped, ultrathin single-crystalline silicon nanomembranes can be vertically stacked at low temperature using a roll-transfer-printing process that is scalable to wafer scale and tolerant to substrate topology and surface roughness for constructing high-performance monolithic three-dimensional integrated circuits.

records.title: Temporary carbon dioxide removal to offset short-lived climate forcers
records.description: Temporary carbon dioxide removal can offset short-lived non-CO 2 climate forcers, providing a viable physical approach for crediting temporary carbon dioxide removal activities in industries in which non-CO 2 emissions dominate and direct emission reductions are difficult.

records.title: A direct black-hole mass measurement in a little red dot at high redshift
records.description: A direct, dynamical black-hole mass measurement in a strongly lensed little red dot at high redshift indicates that it is a massive black-hole seed caught in its earliest accretion phase.

records.title: Direct observation of the superallowed α-decay of 104 Te
records.description: Enhanced preformation of the α particle, a strongly bound system of two protons and two neutrons, in 104 Te causes it to be the fastest ground-state α-emitting nucleus known so far.

records.title: De novo design of miniproteins targeting GPCRs
records.description: De novo design, combined with a high-throughput receptor-diversion microscopy-based screen, complementary display methods and functional assays, enabled the development of G-protein-coupled receptor-binding miniprotein agonists and antagonists targeting receptors implicated in itch, pain, cancer, metabolic disease and migraine.

records.title: Nearly half of the world’s Nature Index chemistry research is now done in China
records.description: A breakdown of leading countries and institutions highlights China’s dominance in the field.

records.title: Red light therapy: the science behind the hype
records.description: From glowing red face masks to fibre optic needles, we explore the gap between commercial devices and the field of ‘photobiomodulation’.

records.title: AI ‘scientists’ promise to accelerate research — how do they work?
records.description: Systems generate hypotheses and ways to test them — plus, how mobile phones might one day be able to see around corners.

records.title: What China’s rise in chemistry means for the rest of the world
records.description: China now produces more than three times the United States’ chemistry output in the Nature Index, underscoring its rapidly growing influence in the field.

records.title: Author Correction: Inactivating SnRK1β1A promotes broad-spectrum disease resistance in rice
Monkeys that ‘draw’ reveal a neuronal population that encodes combinable actions
records.description: When faced with unfamiliar problems, humans and other animals must plan and execute action sequences that they might not have used before. In macaque monkeys, this ability is supported by a population of neurons in the brain’s frontal cortex that encode recombinable action units or ‘action symbols’.

records.title: Becoming a mother leaves long-lasting molecular memories
records.description: In mice, motherhood induces transcriptional changes in the brain that endure beyond short-term hormonal shifts. Postpartum stress disrupts these patterns.

records.title: Why are PFASs so hard to replace?
records.description: As the toxic legacy of ‘forever chemicals’ grows, researchers are racing to develop safer alternatives.

records.title: Tough peer-review process? Your paper might end up being more highly cited
records.description: An AI-led analysis of publicly available peer-review reports links requests for major revisions with papers that end up having high impact.

records.title: Daily briefing: Bogus citations will get you banned from arXiv
records.description: arXiv’s stance on AI-hallucinated references is a good start, but not tough enough, say some researchers. Plus, the brain’s code seems to be in constant flux and how to learn to love networking.

records.title: The brain’s code seems to be in constant flux. Neuroscientists are baffled
records.description: Neurons fire much more erratically than researchers thought. What does that mean for how the brain works?

records.title: The CAPTCHA protocol
records.description: Difficult choices.

records.title: Cities affect small and large storms differently
records.description: Analysis of a 23-year record of Texan storms reveals how urban landscapes affect storm rainfall — painting a more complex picture than had been realized.

records.title: Wearable robot boosts strength of children with spinal muscular atrophy
records.description: The device helps muscle recovery in those receiving gene therapy for the rare neuromuscular condition.

records.title: A guide to the Nature Index
records.description: A description of the terminology and methodology used in this supplement, and a guide to the functionality that is available free online at natureindex.com.

records.title: Too little or too much sleep is linked to faster ageing throughout the body
records.description: A multimodal analysis reveals a ‘U-shaped’ association between sleep duration and biological ageing across various organ systems, with too much or not enough sleep being linked with accelerated organ ageing. The study also shows that biological ageing differentially mediates the relationship between extremes in sleep duration and late-life depression.

records.title: Three scientists pushing chemistry in new directions
records.description: From improving battery technology to speeding up reaction times, these innovative scientists are making their mark.

records.title: NoTrue , Silence and Rubbish Communications : satirical journals give Chinese academics a pressure valve
records.description: Viral trend highlights frustration over the ‘credibility crisis’.

records.title: A conference taught me that scientists and journalists must work together to protect research
records.description: Science sleuth Lonni Besançon realizes that he has sometimes misunderstood what the media want from him and his researcher colleagues.

records.title: Quantum light source boosts attosecond science
records.description: Ionization experiment shows that quantum light can behave like a conventional laser that has a higher intensity.

records.title: Cusp-singularity-enhanced Coriolis effect for sensitive chip-scale gyroscopes
records.description: By using singularity physics to enable cubic-root scaling of frequency and phase modulations induced by the Coriolis effect to enhance the performance of chip-scale Coriolis vibratory gyroscopes, substantial improvements in signal-to-noise ratio and precision are demonstrated.

records.title: A pathogen lncRNA secreted into rice sequesters a host miRNA for virulence
records.description: A fungal long non-coding RNA from Magnaporthe oryzae translocates into rice cells to sequester a host microRNA that normally represses PKR1 , a negative immunity regulator, thereby facilitating infection and revealing a widespread RNA-based pathogen–host interaction mechanism.

records.description: Ionization experiment shows that quantum light can behave like a conventional laser that has a higher intensity.

records.title: Cusp-singularity-enhanced Coriolis effect for sensitive chip-scale gyroscopes
records.description: By using singularity physics to enable cubic-root scaling of frequency and phase modulations induced by the Coriolis effect to enhance the performance of chip-scale Coriolis vibratory gyroscopes, substantial improvements in signal-to-noise ratio and precision are demonstrated.

records.title: De novo design of quasisymmetric two-component protein cages
records.description: Researchers designed two-component proteins forming quasisymmetric cages via geometric frustration, enabling tunable virus-like assemblies for cargo delivery, cellular uptake and studying intracellular diffusion and protein localization.

records.title: Genetic analysis of circulating metabolic traits in 619,372 individuals
records.description: A genome-wide association study combining data from the Estonian Biobank and the UK Biobank identifies many common and low-frequency locus–metabolic trait associations, enabling the identification of putative causal links with disease outcomes.

records.title: Nonlinear atomic tunnelling boosted by bright squeezed vacuum
records.description: Bright squeezed vacuum light boosts nonlinear atomic tunnelling ionization more than 20-fold compared with coherent light, enabling quantum control of strong-field processes without increasing classical intensity.

records.title: Dopamine drives persistent remodelling of the maternal brain
records.description: Brain-wide transcriptomic profiling in mice reveals that reproductive experience remodels the maternal brain by altering dopamine dynamics in the dorsal hippocampal formation, causing dopamine-dependent histone post-translational modifications, and thereby changes in gene expression and behaviour.

records.title: Feature-specific threat coding in lateral septum guides defensive action
records.description: The populations of CRHR2-expressing neurons in the lateral septum of mice involved in threat-related behaviour in response to environmental challenges are defined.

records.title: A critical initialization for biological neural networks
records.description: Basic properties of symmetric random matrices can explain the emergence of macroscopic patterns in neural networks, suggesting that initialization conditions of connected neural populations may confer computational advantages across the mouse brain.

records.title: Neural representation of action symbols in primate frontal cortex
records.description: A drawing-like task designed to study compositional generalization identifies a specific neural population in the ventral premotor cortex in primates that encodes action symbols.

records.title: A deep-learning framework reveals whole-body perturbations at cell level
records.description: An analysis of diet-induced obesity using MouseMapper—a suite of foundation-model-based deep-learning algorithms—identifies structural alterations of the infraorbital branch of the trigeminal ganglia.

records.title: Advancing solar and wind penetration in China through energy complementarity
records.description: Using high-resolution satellite imagery combined with a deep-learning-based framework to build a national energy inventory enables a data-driven assessment of solar–wind complementarity strategies to reduce power variability and enhance renewable energy penetration across China.

records.title: Imaging hidden objects with consumer LiDAR via motion-induced sampling
records.description: Researchers enable hidden-object imaging on consumer LiDAR by fusing multiple frames with a motion-based model, achieving three-dimensional reconstruction, tracking and localization using low-cost, off-the-shelf smartphone sensors.

records.title: Design of one-component quasisymmetric protein nanocages
records.description: Quasisymmetry could arise from spontaneous symmetry breaking in a system of strongly interacting building blocks with programmed curvatures, and this principle, coupled with a design approach, can generate a rich array of quasisymmetric assemblies.

records.title: Divergent urban storm response to convective, frontal and tropical systems
records.description: Analysis of five types of warm-season storms in Texas using three-dimensional radar reflectivity data shows that urbanization can influence storm frequency, intensity, or vertical distribution, depending on the storm type.

records.title: Early fossil eukaryotes were benthic aerobes
records.description: Integrated palaeontological, sedimentological and geochemical analyses of ancient rocks from Australia show that early eukaryotes were largely restricted to oxygenated benthic habitats, probably possessed mitochondria by 1.75 billion years ago, and may have expanded into planktonic habitats much later, perhaps during the Neoproterozoic era.

records.title: A SAUR gene enhances maize drought resilience by promoting silk elongation
records.description: The Small Auxin Up RNA (SAUR) protein ZmSAUR72 in maize ( Zea mays ) promotes silk growth via regulation of H + -ATPase activity, and is a key determinant of the anthesis-silking interval and thus resilience to drought.

records.title: Mitochondrial l -2-hydroxyglutarate is a physiological signalling metabolite
records.description: l -2-Hydroxyglutarate is identified as a legitimate physiological signalling metabolite, and control of its levels is essential for postnatal growth and survival and correct renal development and function.

records.title: Spinal neuromotor rehabilitation using a portable isokinetic training robot
records.description: A lightweight and portable robot that administers isokinetic variable resistance training for juveniles with spinal muscular atrophy type II is shown to facilitate enduring neuromuscular recovery even after temporary exposure, helping patients perform sit-to-stand transitions.

records.title: Forest carbon protocols underestimate climate-driven carbon loss risks
records.description: The buffer pool designed to compensate for unintended carbon losses from the largest forest climate mitigation programme in the United States is too small when considering the impact of future climate change scenarios.

records.title: Astrocyte glucocorticoid receptor signalling restricts neuronal plasticity
records.description: Combined single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility sequencing analysis of mouse primary visual cortex across postnatal development reveals that the glucocorticoid receptor drives astrocyte maturation to limit neuronal plasticity.

records.title: High-fidelity identification of guest species in porous materials
records.description: A reconstruction method based on Gaussian-apodized single-sideband electron ptychography removes artefacts to enable the high-fidelity identification of guest species in porous materials.

records.title: AI might jeopardize the uncertainty required in science
Support academic institutions under attack
River oxygen levels are dropping around the world as Earth warms
records.description: Satellite data on more than 20,000 rivers reveals small but widespread decreases in dissolved oxygen.

records.title: France’s research-primate project goes against its own ethics panel
On the right track in the design of an early typewriter
records.description: A beautiful and ingenious machine hit the headlines 150 years ago, and a book explores bird migration in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: Airborne DNA can yield insights with the right techniques

records.title: Teams of AI agents boost speed of research
records.description: Systems can generate hypotheses, interpret data and suggest ways to develop medicines.

records.title: Why AI cannot do good science without humans
records.description: With the arrival of ‘AI scientists’, it’s as well to remember that human wisdom, empathy and sheer messiness are as much part of progress as are process and efficiency.

records.title: Could this synthetic egg bring back extinct birds? Researchers urge caution
records.description: Colossal Biosciences says its artificial egg has de-extinction and conservation potential.

records.title: The uncritical adoption of AI in science is alarming — we urgently need guard rails
records.description: Artificial intelligence is rapidly accelerating scientific output, but risks narrowing inquiry, weakening judgement and undermining how scientists are trained.

records.title: Researchers who use hallucinated references to face arXiv ban
records.description: The preprint server is the latest to impose stiff penalties on authors who contribute to AI ‘slop’ — but not everyone is convinced it’s the right approach.

records.title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
records.description: Co-Scientist is an AI system for structured scientific thinking and generates research hypotheses for experimental verification.

records.title: Do you hate or love AI? Take Nature’ s poll
records.description: The backlash against artificial intelligence is growing. Nature wants to know what its readers think about the impact on science.

records.title: Secrets of giant ancient jar in Laos unpacked at last
records.description: A receptacle on the ‘Plain of Jars’ was used as a repository for human bones for generations.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Microbiota-induced T cell plasticity enables immune-mediated tumour control
A step-by-step guide for scientists who hate conference networking
records.description: If the thought of ‘working’ a room packed with strangers fills you with dread, academic careers coach Caroline Dunne has some advice.

records.title: Criminals are made, not born: how when you live shapes whether you will break the law
records.description: An analysis of what makes young people more likely to commit crimes tears down the influential assumption that character is the main factor.

records.title: Daily briefing: Mouse eyes can photosynthesize after a plant-to-animal transplant
records.description: Photosynthetic machinery from spinach can help to soothe eye inflammation in mice. Plus, an Ebola outbreak has been declared a global health emergency and the science skills you might not know you have.

records.title: Ebola outbreak is a global health emergency: what happens next
records.description: The outbreak is only the third caused by the rare Bundibugyo virus, for which there are no approved vaccines or therapeutics.

records.title: Can the ‘steroid Olympics’ show the sporting community how to support athletes better?
records.description: The Enhanced Games, which permits the use of performance-enhancing drugs, exposes flaws in the sporting world.

records.title: Race begins to trial Ebola drugs amid current outbreak
records.description: Clinical trials for treatments against the Bundibugyo virus are ‘in a strong position’ to be launched quickly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda.

records.title: Birds get a bad rap: why we should look up to our feathered friends
records.description: Many avian species are threatened, but conservation efforts and birds’ high intelligence offer hope.

records.description: An event that champions performance-boosting substances poses risks to athletes’ health — and integrity. Anti-doping science must keep up.

records.description: Brandon Brown sees parallels between life as an academic and tending a citrus grove following his move to the country.

records.description: Health-evidence reviewers revisit screening for a common cancer, after decades of controversy.

records.description: An El Niño is coming, models say, but Nature spoke to researchers about when and how we’ll know its intensity.

records.description: More than 140,000 fake citations across four research repositories were identified in papers and preprints published in 2025 alone.

records.description: Between six and eight hours of sleep each day seems to be a ‘sweet spot’ for preventing disease. Plus, unexpected interbreeding between Denisovans and Homo erectus , and how the look of antibiotics could be driving antimicrobial resistance.

records.title: Immune cells in the blood drive brain ageing — blocking them improves memory
records.description: Old T cells secrete an enzyme that can impair cognitive function in mice.

records.title: Mental-health research is too often invisible — it is time to change that
records.description: Mental illness needs visibility more urgently than almost any other area of medicine and health care. A new award from Wellcome and Nature aims to raise its prominence.

records.title: Procrastination, productivity and inspiration: how research is like designing video games
records.description: After leaving academia, Bennett Foddy sees connections between games design, creativity and research, as he tells John Tregoning.

records.title: The hunt for the next antibiotics
records.description: To battle antibiotic resistance, researchers are leaving no stone unturned, looking at folk traditions and harnessing AI to find new antibiotics.

records.title: Red-light therapy is all the rage — does it work?
records.description: There are a multitude of red-light emitting consumer goods, but do they really do anything for your health? We look at the science behind the hype — plus, the increasing levels of obesity in lower-income countries.

records.title: Pristine Antarctic ice records the Solar System’s travels
records.description: Rare isotopes hint at when the Solar System entered the Local Interstellar Cloud.

records.title: Street sellers and private physicians fuel antibiotic overuse
records.description: Limited access to medical professionals and irresponsible prescribing practices are contributing to antimicrobial resistance in low-resource settings.

records.title: Old antibiotics are being revived to fight new threats
records.description: The last antimicrobial peptide was developed decades ago. Now, drug-resistant bacteria are forcing scientists to take a fresh look at this class of antibiotic.

records.title: Fast and furious: the gaseous outflows of quasars in the early Universe were extreme
records.description: Observations from the James Webb Space Telescope reveal that extremely fast, galaxy-scale outflows from luminous objects called quasars were much more frequent, and on average more powerful, about one billion years after the Big Bang than at later cosmic epochs. These outflows could easily escape their host galaxies and regulate the evolution of early massive galaxies.

records.title: Sleep linked to slower ageing: huge study pinpoints the right amount
records.description: Health outcomes were better in people who slept for between about six and eight hours a day.

records.title: Growth charts reveal how the brain’s ‘communication highways’ change throughout life
records.description: Studies of white matter — the tissue used for communication between brain regions — have revealed substantial changes in people with neurological diseases and disorders. The creation of white-matter brain charts enables individual deviations from the typical structure to be assessed using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain scans.

records.title: Can AI tools assess coding assignments?
records.description: Yulu Hou and her partner experimented with using ChatGPT to automate marking of undergraduate assignments. Here’s what they learnt.

records.description: Scientists are debating whether to limit biological AI software to ward off threats.

records.title: Why farm workers need protection from antimicrobial resistance
records.description: Antibiotic use in agriculture threatens the health of workers and their communities, but there are potential solutions.

records.title: Antibiotics look like any other drugs — and that’s a problem
records.description: Medical microbiologist Heiman Wertheim explains why the physical appearance and labelling of antibiotics matter when trying to limit resistance.

records.title: Daily briefing: Ice core is the longest-ever continuous record of Earth’s climate
records.description: Data from the 2.8-kilometre-deep core stretches back 1.2 million years. Plus, the cost of using AI tools in the lab and the greatest physics mysteries that still divide researchers.

records.title: Relics of the first stars spotted in a distant, ultra-faint galaxy
records.description: An observation of an ultra-faint galaxy, captured as it was shortly after the Big Bang, indicates the presence of material from the first generation of stars.

records.title: Targeted electron beam creates thousands of atomic crystal defects
records.description: An electron-beam technique that can precisely create thousands of atomic defects in a crystal could be used to build quantum devices.

records.title: Bee-inspired navigation robot pinpoints its home using a neural network
records.description: A simple machine-learning algorithm, inspired by honeybees’ visual memory and sense of direction, enables a flying robot to pinpoint its home location.

records.title: Six key developments in the fight against antimicrobial resistance
records.description: Antibiotics designed by artificial intelligence, immunotherapy for resistant infections and other highlights from studies and trials.

records.title: State media control shapes LLM behaviour by influencing training data
records.description: State control of the media is shown to alter the training data of large language models (LLMs) through its impact on the information environment. This has a substantial effect on the output of LLMs, with states rated more favourably in their own language when they have tighter media control.

records.title: Economic reform can save antibiotic innovation
records.description: Governments must create meaningful incentives for biopharmaceutical companies to develop antimicrobial products.

records.title: Antifungal resistance is growing – will new treatments turn the tables?
records.description: Trials of drugs to fight deadly resistant infections are advancing, but they might fall victim to overuse of agricultural fungicides just like their predecessors.

records.title: Are non-antibiotic drugs contributing to antimicrobial resistance?
records.description: Plans to address drug resistance typically focus on the use of antibiotics, but there are signs that compounds with incidental antibacterial effects might be part of the problem, too.

records.title: The futile beauty of flightless birds
records.description: Navigating by the stars.

records.title: Obesity has risen in all countries — but at a faster pace in poorer ones
records.description: Trajectories of obesity prevalence over the past 45 years reveal patterns of growth, plateau and decline that differ across high-, middle- and low-income countries.

records.title: At last, a pill that can prevent COVID after exposure to infected people
records.description: Drug arrives years after pandemic’s peak, but could still offer protection to vulnerable populations.

records.title: Protective maternal gut instincts
records.description: Pregnancy poses many challenges, including protecting against infection and increased nutritional demands. Pregnancy-associated gut changes offer some help.

records.title: An ultra-faint, chemically primitive galaxy forming in the reionization era
records.description: LAP1-B—an ultra-faint and tiny galaxy that formed in the reionization era and is strongly magnified by gravitational lensing—is chemically primitive and hosts very few stars in an otherwise dominant dark matter halo.

records.title: Adaptive cellular evolution in the intestine of hyperdiverse cichlid fishes
records.description: Single-cell transcriptomics combined with morphological and ecological data show that the rapid evolutionary radiation of cichlid fishes in Lake Tanganyika was accompanied by dietary specialization across multiple layers of biological organization.

records.title: Long-term editing of brain circuits using an engineered electrical synapse
records.description: Connexin proteins found in white perch fish were used to engineer synthetic electrical synapses, enabling precision circuit editing in mammals.

records.title: State media control influences large language models
records.description: Government-controlled media influences the output of large language models via their training data, and models queried in the languages of countries with lower media freedom show a stronger pro-regime valence than models queried in the languages of countries with higher media freedom.

records.title: Enhanced response of extreme compound events to cumulative CO 2 emissions
records.description: A new metric shows that compound climate extremes rise faster with cumulative CO 2 emissions than models project, implying higher risks and smaller remaining carbon budgets for the 1.5 °C and 2 °C targets.

records.title: Enamel proteins from six Homo erectus specimens across China
records.description: Palaeoproteomic analysis of ancient enamel proteins extracted from Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus specimens from the Zhoukoudian, Hexian and Sunjiadong sites in China suggests that they are a new genetic monogroup, and super-archaic introgression in Denisovans is likely to have originated from H. erectus .

records.title: Twenty-first century emergence of alpine fire in Central African mountains
records.description: A twenty-first century fire is shown to be the first to have affected a high-elevation region in the central African mountains in the past 12,000 years, and previous burning at mid-elevations highlights the potential role of humans in transforming Afromontane ecosystems.

records.title: Ecotypes of triple-negative breast cancer in response to chemotherapy
records.description: Treatment data for triple-negative breast cancer show the importance of macrophage subtypes and cancer-cell metaprograms for interferon signalling, HLA expression and cell cycle activity that are associated with a good response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

records.title: Gaussian boson sampling with 1,024 squeezed states in 8,176 modes
records.description: A programmable photonic quantum processor, Jiuzhang 4.0, incorporates 1,024 high-efficiency squeezed states into a hybrid spatial–temporal encoded 8,176-mode circuit.

records.title: Lineage and organ signals sequentially build organ intrinsic nervous systems
records.description: Systems-level analyses of organ intrinsic nervous systems reveal that these networks are initially configured by lineage-dependent programmes, and their architecture and molecular identity are refined by intra-organ specific local cues.

records.title: SNOR promotes translation restart after dormancy
records.description: High-resolution in situ cryo-electron tomography in Schizosaccharomyces pombe identifies SNOR protein, which binds to ribosomes during dormancy induced by glucose depletion, priming them for rapid reactivation of protein synthesis upon glucose repletion.

records.title: Mesoscale atomic engineering in a crystal lattice
records.description: Electron-beam control enables deterministic placement of tens of thousands of atomic defects in three-dimensional crystals, creating stable, programmable artificial matter for scalable quantum and nanoscale technologies.

records.title: Subspace communication in the hippocampal–retrosplenial axis
records.description: Hippocampal–neocortical communication reconfigures predetermined circuit motifs to flexibly encode experiences.

records.title: Large-scale discovery, analysis and design of protein energy landscapes
records.description: An analysis of 5,778 domains 28–64 amino acids in length reveals hidden variation in conformational fluctuations, even between sequences sharing the same fold and global folding stability.

records.title: Asymmetric splitting in dividing lipid-nucleotide multilamellar droplets
records.description: Structured liquid droplets exhibit asymmetric division in the absence of reconstituted protein machinery.

records.title: Sleep chart of biological ageing clocks in middle and late life
records.description: A cross-organ, multi-omics U-shaped relationship between sleep duration and biological ageing clocks highlights the potential of sleep optimization to promote healthy ageing, lower disease risk and extend longevity.

records.title: Developmental gene expression patterns driving species-specific cortical features
records.description: Machine learning analysis of cell-type-specific gene expression in mouse and human neocortex and human cortical organoids reveals human-specific cell-type and temporal variations in expression controlled by JUNB.

records.title: Obesity rise plateaus in developed nations and accelerates in developing nations
records.description: Global analysis of obesity trends from 1980 to 2024 in 200 countries and territories using data from 4,050 population-based studies reveals that framing obesity as a single global epidemic masks the highly varied dynamics across countries and age groups.

records.title: Eosinophils drive intestinal remodelling and innate defence in reproduction
records.description: From pregnancy until lactation, eosinophils accumulate in the small intestine where they regulate goblet cell fate and enhance innate defences against enteric pathogens.

records.title: Stereoelectronic manipulation of ligands for perovskite solar cells
records.description: By tuning the stereoelectronic properties of ligand adsorption topology to optimize the interfacial architecture and improve stability in perovskite solar cells, high certified power outputs of nearly 27% in the laboratory are demonstrated.

records.title: A synaptic locus of song learning
records.description: Combining a computational framework and optogenetic and chemogenetic manipulations within and downstream of the cortico-basal ganglia circuit identifies the specific cortico-basal ganglia synapses that drive the acquisition and expression of rapid vocal changes during juvenile song learning.

records.title: Stereoelectronic manipulation of ligands for perovskite solar cells
records.description: By tuning the stereoelectronic properties of ligand adsorption topology to optimize the interfacial architecture and improve stability in perovskite solar cells, high certified power outputs of nearly 27% in the laboratory are demonstrated.

records.title: A synaptic locus of song learning
records.description: Combining a computational framework and optogenetic and chemogenetic manipulations within and downstream of the cortico-basal ganglia circuit identifies the specific cortico-basal ganglia synapses that drive the acquisition and expression of rapid vocal changes during juvenile song learning.

records.title: An X-linked long non-coding RNA, PTCHD1-AS , and the core features of autism
records.description: PTCHD1-AS , which encodes a long non-coding RNA, is associated with the aetiology of autism spectrum disorder in humans through striatal molecular and circuit-level dysregulation.

records.title: White matter micro- and macrostructure brain charts for the human lifespan

records.description: Genomics and experimental data suggest that an evolutionary arms race between cholera-causing bacteria and their viral predators shapes the disease in humans.

records.description: Recent price hikes, usage limitations and unreliable outputs are causing some scientific researchers to think twice about using artificial intelligence.

records.description: Trust is no longer enough: secure data sharing requires international collaboration across institutions and governments.

records.description: Floating genetic material could give insights into ecosystem health, the presence of invasive species, and help researchers identify pathogens before they cause harm.

records.title: ‘Undruggable’ cancer proteins meet their match

records.description: Proposed UN progress indicators include greenhouse-gas emissions, life expectancy and children’s performance in reading and maths.

records.title: Three mental-health claims from RFK’s wellness movement: what scientists say

records.title: Matter of taste

records.title: A life in pictures: celebrating David Attenborough at 100
records.description: As the British naturalist marks a milestone birthday, we take a look at how his work has shaped science.

records.title: Daily briefing: David Attenborough at 100

records.title: Happy 100th birthday David Attenborough! Nature salutes you
records.description: The science communicator has raised awareness of the natural world and its myriad interconnections on which humans depend.

records.title: Trafficked pangolins can be traced to their source by DNA — even to a specific forest
records.description: A method reveals that some local wild-meat markets share the same supply chains as global smuggling operations.

records.title: There is no vaccine for deadly hantavirus: what that means for future outbreaks
records.description: Virologist Jay Hooper is developing a vaccine for the rare rodent virus behind an outbreak on a cruise ship.

records.title: Early-career researchers do more ‘disruptive’ science than veterans
records.description: Analysis of papers from millions of scientists shows that older researchers tend to stick with ideas from their past.

records.title: Why AI chatbots that follow human laws are hard to build
records.description: OpenAI is under investigation after a person accused of murder in Florida allegedly sought ChatGPT's advice to plan the crime.

records.description: The month’s most spectacular science images. Plus, the surprising activity in the unconscious brain.

records.title: My English skills are hurting my chances in academic publishing — how can I improve?
records.description: A non-fluent English speaker struggles to navigate language barriers in academic publishing.

records.title: Anaesthetized brains can still process podcasts
records.description: Neuronal recordings taken during surgery reveal that the brain can learn even when unconscious — plus, the electrical test that can determine a cup of coffee’s strength.

Author Correction: Multidimensional profiling of heterogeneity in supratentorial ependymomas

records.description: Plans for expansion.

records.title: The lights are out but someone’s home: sensory processing in anaesthetized human brains
records.description: Detailed neural recordings were made from a brain structure called the hippocampus in unconscious anaesthetized people. Neuronal activity responded to ‘oddballs’ in a series of auditory tones, encoded complex meaning-related properties of language and could even predict upcoming words in a heard phrase.

records.title: Towards disentangling human-induced drivers of precipitation trends from naturally occurring ones
records.description: Combining climate models with statistical learning allows an assessment of the relative contributions of different factors to trends in winter precipitation at mid-latitudes. Thermodynamic (non-circulation-related) effects are mostly consistent between models and observations, but whether circulation-related changes are forced or unforced remains unclear.

records.title: 25 years of chemistry that simply clicks
records.description: When the concept of ‘click’ chemistry — highly effective and specific reactions — was first reported, some dismissed it as a gimmick. But it has transformed many fields of research.

records.title: Revealed: the mysterious ‘dark’ proteins that might play a big role in biology
records.description: Thousands of dark proteins have been reclassified as peptideins and added to databases as a new category.

records.title: J. Craig Venter obituary: maverick biotechnologist who sequenced the human genome
records.description: The entrepreneur was also a pioneer of synthetic biology.

records.title: I’m burnt out and leaving academia. How do I finish my PhD?
records.description: Burnout is a systemic problem, but individuals can take steps to cope with it and pave a path forward.

records.title: Relativistic plasmas open a route to extreme optical fields
records.description: By precisely shaping the leading edge of ultrafast high-power laser pulses, bright ‘harmonic’ radiation has been generated with great efficiency from plasma oscillating at almost the speed of light. This long-sought regime removes a key barrier to the production of extremely intense electromagnetic fields for applications such as compact particle acceleration, attosecond science and strong-field physics.

records.title: TikTok’s algorithm systematically skewed to the right during the 2024 US elections
records.description: An audit of TikTok’s recommendation algorithm using hundreds of automated ‘bot’ accounts during the 2024 US presidential election finds that the ‘For You’ feed of the platform steered users towards Republican-aligned political content, regardless of their initial political leanings.

records.title: Even the unconscious brain can learn — and predict what you’ll say next
records.description: Neuronal recordings of people under anaesthesia show that their brains are processing words and sounds.

records.title: Daily briefing: Digital distractions are real — but you can rescue your attention span
records.description: What the science says about shrinking focus, plus a quantum ‘thermometer’ that can take a reading inside a cell and a celebrity-whale rescue that went very wrong.

records.title: Engineering resilient food systems in a warming world
records.description: Can synthetic biology provide food security in a changing climate?

records.title: In twisted graphene, some electrons are heavier than others
records.description: When two graphene layers are twisted at a ‘magic angle’, their electrons can behave as both heavy and light particles, depending on momentum.

records.title: Male sex hormone loss aids brain tumour growth
records.description: Depletion of sex hormones that enable male development induces neuroinflammation that disrupts hormonal signalling and immune responses against brain tumours.

records.title: Are microbes the future of pollution clean-up?
records.description: Synthetic biologists are engineering bacteria to feast on oil, plastic and toxic chemicals.

records.title: ‘Alternative COP’ must drive real, cooperative change in climate action
records.description: A new climate coalition to steer the transition away from fossil fuels is good news, but it must avoid undermining existing global scientific structures.

records.title: Explore a stunningly detailed map of the Universe in April's best science images
records.description: The month’s sharpest science shots, selected by Nature ’s photo team.

records.title: First AI tool to detect suspicious peer reviews rolled out by academic publisher
records.description: Artificial-intelligence tool spots copied peer reviews, helping to uncover fraud in academic publishing.

records.title: Are attention spans really shrinking? What the science says
records.description: Digital distractions are vying for people’s focus, but our underlying capacity to pay attention seems to be undiminished.

records.title: Nanoscale ‘conveyor belt’ teleports quantum state of electron
records.description: Mobile quantum bits, which can be shuttled to where they are needed in a circuit, have been used to perform a quantum process called state teleportation.

records.title: Two-qubit logic and teleportation with mobile spin qubits in silicon
records.description: A device architecture comprising silicon-based mobile qubits and the shuttling of two electron spins together demonstrates two-qubit gate fidelity of about 99% as well as quantum state teleportation between qubits separated by 320 nm.

records.title: Expanding the human proteome with microproteins and peptideins
records.description: A large-scale proteomics analysis of the dark proteome by the TransCODE Consortium reveals many translated non-canonical open reading frames to encode microproteins and peptideins.

records.title: RNA-triggered cell killing with CRISPR–Cas12a2
records.description: Cas12a2 enables RNA-triggered, sequence-specific killing of eukaryotic cells via widespread DNA shredding, allowing selective elimination of cells on the basis of gene expression, including virus-infected or mutation-bearing cells.

records.title: Pollinators support the nutrition and income of vulnerable communities
records.description: Quantification of links among insect pollinators, crop plants, nutrient intake and income of smallholder communities in Nepal show that pollinators substantially contribute to their income and micronutrient intake.

records.title: Electrocaloric effects across room temperature in multilayer capacitors
records.description: Multilayer capacitors comprising a solid solution of two electrocaloric materials PbSc 0.5 Ta 0.5 O 3 and PbMg 0.5 W 0.5 O 3 are shown to maintain high B-site order and latent heat without needing an energetically expensive anneal, enabling efficient refrigeration across room temperature.

records.title: Foreshock-induced slip transients set mainshock nucleation timing
records.description: Analysis of laboratory experiments using a rate-and-state-based Griffith-like rupture framework shows that foreshocks can regulate mainshock nucleation timing, with larger foreshocks generating higher transient sliding velocities and triggering a more rapid transition to dynamic rupture.

records.title: Non-invasive profiling of the tumour microenvironment with spatial ecotypes
records.description: Multimodal machine learning reveals that tumour microenvironments can be decomposed into spatially organized multicellular ecosystems, termed spatial ecotypes, that can be accessed non-invasively via liquid biopsy and used to profile individual cancers and target treatments.

records.title: Plasticity and language in the anaesthetized human hippocampus
records.description: In the hippocampus, complex processing of sensory stimuli occurs even in the unconscious state.

records.title: Genome-wide sweeps create ecological units in the human gut microbiome
records.description: Genome-wide selective sweeps commonly occur in the human gut microbiome and can spread across the world within decades to produce epidemic-like population structures.

records.title: Tree community resource economics control soil food web multifunctionality
records.description: Plant community properties affect ecosystem functioning via energy fluxes in food webs, with the leaf and root resource economics of dominant tree species controlling soil food web multifunctionality.

records.title: Prefrontal to ventral tegmental area dynamics drive contingency degradation
records.description: This work provides a mechanistic understanding of how certain prefrontal circuits in the rodent brain permit flexibility to selectively stop learned behaviours through interactions with core subcortical reward systems.

records.title: Steric hindrance of antibody binding in an Omicron spike fusion intermediate
records.description: The SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant escapes neutralization by antibodies targeting the pan-coronavirus epitope in a spike fusion intermediate via steric hindrance, but reducing the antibody size overcomes this barrier and expands its range of accessible targets.

records.title: Purcell-enhanced spin–phonon coupling with a single colour centre
records.description: The acoustic Purcell effect is observed by constructing a specially engineered, microwave-frequency nanomechanical resonator around a colour centre spin qubit in diamond.

records.title: Predicting temporal stability and resilience from resistance and recovery
records.description: New predictions for how temporal stability and resilience depend on their resistance and recovery components are explored.

records.title: HIV-1 signalling remodels nuclear pores to licence infection
records.description: HIV-1 capsid nuclear import at the nuclear pore complex is a bottleneck to resting T cell infection, but HIV-1 overcomes this by triggering receptor-mediated signalling during cell–cell spread to drive nuclear import and licence infection.

records.title: Specific expansion of motor cortical projections in a singing mouse
records.description: High-throughput barcoded neuroanatomy of two closely related rodent species with divergent vocalizations reveals differences in long-range projection motifs in the brain that may support these differences in vocal complexity.

records.title: Quantum coherent manipulation and readout of superconducting vortex states
records.description: Vortices trapped in superconducting granular aluminium films can behave as a quantum two-level system that can be manipulated and read out, suggesting that they could be used for future quantum technologies.

records.title: Imaging the flat bands of magic-angle graphene reshaped by interactions
records.description: Quantum twisting microscopy is used to directly image the interacting energy bands of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, allowing characterization of the dual nature of its electrons at the magic angle.

records.title: Deforestation-induced drying lowers Amazon climate threshold
records.description: The Amazon forest faces a near system-wide transition of 62−77% of the area under a combination of 1.5–1.9 °C global warming and 22−28% deforestation.

records.title: Molecular skeleton programming of premediators in sulfur electrochemistry
records.description: A potential premediator, 2-chloropyrimidine, could be a model material for molecular skeleton design enabling lithium–sulfur batteries to achieve a strong average capacity retention and help design functional molecules in broader organic chemical spaces.

records.title: A brain reward circuit inhibited by next-generation weight-loss drugs in mice
records.description: Humanized glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor (GLP1R) mouse models are used to investigate the neural circuitry through which small-molecule GLP1R agonists modulate feeding, with implications for how these orally delivered weight-loss drugs engage brain reward circuits.

records.title: Extreme galaxy-scale outflows are frequent among luminous early quasars
records.description: James Webb Space Telescope observations show powerful high-redshift quasar outflows, supporting quasar feedback as a key mechanism driving rapid star-formation quenching in early massive galaxies.

records.title: Androgen loss accelerates brain tumour growth via HPA axis activation
records.description: Androgens have distinct roles in the brain, acting as immune-based tumour suppressors through neuroinflammation and neuroendocrine mechanisms.

records.title: Two decades of PARP inhibitor synthetic lethality in cancer
records.description: The past two decades of PARP inhibitor synthetic lethality in cancer is explored.

records.title: Systematic partisan content skews in TikTok during the 2024 US elections
records.description: Audit experiments on TikTok show asymmetric partisan exposure that is not explained by observable engagement metrics, with Republican-leaning accounts receiving more aligned content and Democratic-leaning accounts more cross-partisan recommendations.

records.title: Multiplexed magnetic resonance imaging
records.description: A new approach to magnetic resonance imaging, ‘multiplexed magnetic resonance imaging’, is reported, which enables high-resolution simultaneous multiparametric mapping of multiple molecules in standard clinical settings.

records.title: To move beyond GDP, don’t ignore ecological economics
records.description: Sustainable development will only be achieved when governments base decisions on human skills and natural resources, not just gross domestic product.

records.title: NIH grant cuts disproportionately hit minority and female scientists
records.description: A survey reveals sharp divides in who bore the brunt of last year’s spree of grant cancellations by the Trump administration.

records.description: Research funding agencies are battling a wave of AI-assisted applications. Countermeasures should not entrench existing power structures.

records.description: Some clinicians are pushing to broaden testosterone use, but there is debate about its benefits and risks.

records.title: Quantum ‘thermometer’ takes temperatures inside living cancer cells

records.title: How much of the scientific literature is generated by AI?
records.description: Tools for reliably estimating what artificial intelligence is being used for are still lacking.

records.title: Daily briefing: Who needs testosterone therapy?
records.description: The benefits and risks of testosterone replacement for men and women. Plus, we hear from scientists in Iran and learn that US lawmakers have voted to reject Trump’s massive budget cuts.

records.title: How fertilizer shortages caused by the energy crisis threaten food security
records.description: Unless governments treat fertilizer production as strategic infrastructure, the world will keep lurching from energy shock to harvest failure.

records.title: A wispy wrapper for a chilly, Pluto-like world
records.description: Astronomers are puzzled by how a relatively small object manages to hang onto its atmosphere.
