European funder must increase capacity to meet the ambition of scientists
records.description: To avoid sabotaging science, the European Research Council needs more funding and structural change.

records.title: This organoid can menstruate — and shows how tissue can repair itself
records.description: Mini models of the uterus lining give insight into mystery of how it is shed without scarring.

records.title: Prestigious European science funder scraps stricter rules after researcher backlash
records.description: The tougher policy was introduced to curb submissions, but it drew criticism.

records.title: Blood test hints at breast-tumour response to treatment
records.description: A biomarker shows which people with certain types of breast cancer are more likely to respond to an immune-based therapy.

records.title: Forest pests hit trees hard as temperatures rise
records.description: Damage by certain insects and fungi tends to be greatest in US woodlands where maximum temperatures during the warmest months are increasing.

records.title: An electrifying test to find a good coffee
records.description: Technique determines roast level and strength by applying voltage to the brew.

records.title: Wild-meat consumption estimated across Central Africa
records.description: A regional analysis brought together data on wild-animal consumption by more than 12,000 households, to investigate trends and drivers of wild-meat use across Central Africa. The study found that consumption has increased over the past two decades, and that the increase was driven by demand from growing towns and cities.

records.title: ‘Make Pluto a planet again’? NASA chief revives debate that divides astronomers
records.description: Researchers respond to NASA head’s claim to be ready to “escalate” the issue of whether Pluto is a planet.

records.title: Long-lived immune cells show promise against cancer in world-first trial
records.description: Blood cancer goes into remission for some people treated with a type of T cell that acts like stem cells.

records.title: Genome pioneer Craig Venter dies: here’s how he transformed science
records.description: Venter redrew the boundaries of biology — sequencing DNA at unprecedented speed, engineering synthetic life and charting ocean microbes.

records.title: All life runs on 20 amino acids. These cells run key machinery on just 19
records.description: AI-guided redesign of protein alphabet in bacteria could unlock more ways to build synthetic organisms.

records.title: Daily briefing: ‘A true pioneer and maverick’, Craig Venter dead at 79
records.description: Craig Venter — who led a race to decode the human genome – has died, aged 79. Plus, how so many runners just broke the marathon world record.

records.title: US lawmakers vote to reject Trump’s massive science-budget cuts — but call for substantial decreases
records.description: A draft bill would preserve NASA’s overall funding but downsize the National Science Foundation’s budget by 20%.

records.title: Why preprint servers are increasing moderation — and what that means for researchers
records.description: Repositories are adapting in response to AI-generated content and junk science, leading some people to question how much moderation is too much.

records.title: ‘Beyond COP’ climate summit puts scientists at the centre of the action
records.description: Researchers presented ways for nations to phase out fossil fuels at an international meeting of countries ready to take action.

records.title: Why cows burp methane: new organelle discovered in gut microorganisms
records.description: The hydrogen-producing structure could inspire strategies to lower the amount of methane produced by grazing animals.

records.title: Scientists to return to Fukushima — this time to study disaster recovery
records.description: A new research centre could help to reassure the public that the region is safe.

records.title: How sewing can set you up for failure and success in science
records.description: Making a garment and designing an experiment require similar skills and creative thinking. Time to try a new hobby?

records.title: Saving sharks and rays, one catch at a time — in photos
records.description: Working alongside fishers in a biodiverse gulf in Greece, Roxani Naasan Aga-Spyridopoulou is focused on securing species’ future survival.

records.title: Continuously graded-doped SnO 2 for efficient n–i–p perovskite solar cells
records.description: A continuously graded-doped tin oxide electron transport layer improves the efficiency of n–i–p perovskite solar cells and mini-modules.

records.title: Immunity gets a boost from a surprising place — breakfast
records.description: Eating a meal could lead to T cells springing into action more quickly— plus, 40 years after Chornobyl, how future nuclear calamities can be avoided.

records.title: Engineered blood clots stop bleeding in seconds
records.description: Red blood cells have been modified to form strong clots that halt any bleeding almost instantly and then promote tissue regeneration.

records.title: Why you should ‘feed a cold’: eating primes immune cells for action
records.description: Infection-fighting T cells from people who have eaten recently can proliferate more quickly in response to threats.

records.title: Author Correction: Broadly stable atmospheric CO 2 and CH 4 levels over the past 3 million years
Competition between separated parental genomes in fertilized eggs aids development
records.description: In fertilized egg cells, the maternal and paternal genomes are enclosed in separate compartments called pronuclei. Experiments in mice reveal that this spatial separation enables parental competition for cytoplasmic factors, which helps to prevent the dysregulation of chemical modifications to DNA-packing proteins and contributes to healthy embryonic development.

records.title: Cephalopods deserve higher welfare standards in research
records.description: These highly sentient creatures have weak protections for their well-being. That must change.

records.title: Higher racial diversity in US business and law schools is linked to higher graduate salaries
records.description: Two comprehensive data sets concerning students who graduated from 141 business schools over 29 years and 200 law schools over 21 years show that higher racial diversity is associated with higher median salary at graduation. Policies that promote racial diversity seem likely to enhance education and benefit society overall.

records.title: Delivering an immune therapy into tumours instead of intravenously reduces adverse effects
records.description: In people with advanced skin cancer, injecting low doses of an anticancer immunotherapy directly into tumours, rather than administering high doses intravenously, reduced severe immune toxicity while preserving antitumour efficacy. Pre-existing antitumour immunity predicted clinical benefit most strongly, and profiling fresh tissue provided response biomarkers faster than conventional diagnostics did.

records.title: Daily briefing: Octopuses’ strange brains might teach us what intelligence really is
records.description: Cephalopods are very smart, but have brains that evolved very differently than vertebrates. Plus, detailed maps of olfactory receptors in mice transform what we know about smell.

records.title: Friendlier LLMs tell users what they want to hear — even when it is wrong
records.description: A large language model that is trained to respond in a warm manner is more likely to give incorrect information and reinforce conspiracy beliefs.

records.title: In the flesh
records.description: Cyberspace can’t fulfil every need.

records.title: A cell atlas charts the immune architecture of diabetic kidney disease
records.description: Single-cell gene-expression profiling and spatial mapping have revealed the immune microenvironments comprising aggregated immune cells called B cells in a subset of individuals who have accelerated disease progression.

records.description: Just like vertebrates, cephalopods — such as octopuses and squid — have elaborate brains. Neuroscientists are flocking to them for insights into how intelligence evolved.

records.description: A Pd-catalysed method enables regio- and diastereoselective C–H alkylation of diverse alkenes using carboxylic acids, expanding synthetic access to complex substituted alkenes.

records.description: Triplet excitons in OPVs can redissociate via the charge-transfer state into free carriers, reducing losses and improving efficiency, enabled by molecular design controlling singlet–triplet energetics through exciton delocalization.

records.title: Safety and efficacy of intratumoural anti-CTLA4 with intravenous anti-PD1
records.description: The phase 1b NIVIPIT trial shows that in combined therapy with intravenous nivolumab (anti-PD1), intratumoural administration of ipilimumab (anti-CTLA4) offers improved safety and greater efficacy compared with intravenous delivery.

records.title: Digital quantum magnetism on a trapped-ion quantum computer
records.description: Simulations performed using Quantinuum’s H2 trapped-ion quantum computer for observing thermalization on challenging timescales demonstrate the usefulness of digital quantum computers for investigating continuous-time dynamics in regimes that classical simulation methods find difficult.

records.title: Improving access to essential medicines via decision-aware machine learning
records.description: Nationwide deployment of a novel decision-aware machine learning framework as a decision support tool for the allocation of essential medicines in Sierra Leone resulted in improved access to essential healthcare in this resource-constrained setting.

records.title: Transdimensional anomalous Hall effect in rhombohedral thin graphite
records.description: The experimental observation of a fundamentally new type of anomalous Hall effect that couples both in-plane and out-of-plane orbital magnetizations in multilayer rhombohedral graphene is reported.

records.title: Vaccination generates broadly cross-neutralizing antibodies to the HIV Env apex
records.description: A vaccination strategy using heterologous HIV Env trimers covalently coupled to liposomes for multivalent display generates cross-neutralizing HIV serum antibody responses in non-human primates, mimicking infection-elicited apex-targeting broadly neutralizing antibodies.

records.title: Translation-dependent degradation of cas12 mRNA triggered by an anti-CRISPR
records.description: The anti-CRISPR protein AcrVA2 specifically interrupts Cas12a biogenesis by triggering co-translational mRNA degradation.

records.title: Engineering tough blood clots for rapid haemostasis and enhanced regeneration
records.description: Engineered blood clots using rapidly crosslinked red blood cells form within seconds, greatly improving toughness and adhesion while effectively stopping bleeding and enhancing tissue repair.

records.title: Cytoplasmic competition between separate parental pronuclei in zygotes
records.description: Drug-based and manipulation-based strategies provide evidence of pronuclear competition for finite cytoplasmic resources between separate parental pronuclei in zygotes, suggesting a cell biological mechanism for the cytoplasm-mediated remote parental interaction that regulates epigenetic marks.

records.title: Training language models to be warm can reduce accuracy and increase sycophancy
records.description: Experiments on five different language models show that training language models to produce warmer responses can undermine the accuracy of their output, especially when users express feelings of sadness.

records.title: Spatial atlas of diabetic kidney disease reveals a B cell-rich subgroup
records.description: A single-cell spatial atlas identifies a B cell-predominant microenvironment within the profibrotic tubular niche that marks a subset of patients with diabetic kidney disease with rapid progression.

records.title: Increase in wild animal consumption across Central Africa
records.description: Wild meat is a fundamental component of the diets of rural Central African populations, accounting for 20% of the recommended daily protein intake, compared with 13% and 6% for those living in towns and cities.

records.title: Demography and life histories across the Roman frontier in Germany 400–700 ce
records.description: Analysis of 258 ancient genomes from southern Germany reveals a major demographic shift during the late fifth century, yet family structures persisted from Late Roman times, demonstrating cultural continuity despite profound demographic reorganization.

records.title: Racial diversity in higher education is associated with higher student salaries
records.description: A longitudinal study shows that racial diversity in higher education is associated with higher student salaries at graduation, indicating that policies to increase or leverage racial diversity enhance human capital and benefit society.

records.title: Postprandial lipid metabolism durably enhances T cell immunity
records.description: Experiments in mice and humans show enhancement of T cell function following fasting and refeeding, caused by persistent immunometabolic reprogramming, with potential implications for nutritional interventions and adoptive cell therapy.

records.title: Intrinsic polar vortex crystals in A-site layer-ordered perovskites
records.description: A two-dimensional polar hedgehog lattice spontaneously forms in layer-ordered perovskites, showing stable topological ferroelectric states without external constraints and enabling new pathways for functional material design.

records.title: Evolutionary characterization of lung cancer metastasis
records.description: DNA-sequencing data from primary tumours and paired metastases from participants in the TRACERx lung study and PEACE autopsy programme are used to analyse the metastatic diversity of advanced non-small cell lung cancer and the seeding patterns that underpin it.

records.title: Submicrometre sampling of living cells by macrophages
records.description: Macrophages can sample antigens from living cells through a trogocytosis-like mechanism that routes ingested material away from degradation, a finding that delineates a previously unknown pathway for antigen presentation to CD8 T cells.

records.description: Eu-doped infinite-layer nickelate Sm 0.95− x Ca 0.05 EuNiO 2 exhibits a magnetic-field-induced re-entrant superconducting phase in the Eu-rich overdoped regime.

records.title: ‘Jumping genes’ help a bacterium that causes hospital infections to adapt quickly
records.description: Over the past three decades, mobile DNA sequences called transposable elements have proliferated throughout the genome of Enterococcus faecium , an important bacterium behind infections in hospitalized individuals. These ‘jumping genes’ can replicate rapidly, alter gene activity and seem to help E. faecium to alter its metabolism on clinical timescales.

records.description: Real-world data reveal that cooperation continually falls and rebounds. Motivation to cooperate must therefore be actively renewed rather than assumed to sustain itself.

records.description: Webs of star-shaped cells called astrocytes connect distant parts of the brain, allowing long-distance exchange of molecules.

records.description: A model of the early Solar System that cools too quickly to reach chemical equilibrium generates mineral regimes resembling important classes of meteorites.

records.title: Genomic roots of Indigenous Americans uncovered
records.description: A large and diverse collection of Indigenous American genomes uncovers extensive genetic diversity and a complex history of dispersals, continuity and adaptation across the Americas. The findings reveal the evolutionary processes that shaped Indigenous American populations and address the under-representation of these populations in global genomic research.

records.title: Caspase 5c amplifies Wnt via APC cleavage to promote intestinal homeostasis
records.description: CASP5 expression is restricted to the human intestinal epithelium, and the CASP5C isoform has a key role in promoting Wnt signalling, which is required for epithelial homeostasis, through binding to dishevelled and cleavage of APC to regulate β-catenin turnover.

records.title: Focal white matter lesions drive grey matter inflammation and synapse loss
records.description: A transient grey matter microgliosis is required for remyelination, the failure of which results in a chronic neuroinflammatory state seen in neurodegenerative disorders.

records.title: Dynamics of genetic and somatic trade-offs in ageing and mortality
records.description: Mapping DNA variants that modulate mortality using a starting population of 6,438 young mice defined 29 distinct loci that influence lifespan and mortality with divergent age- and sex-specific effects, as well as 30 loci that specifically couple body mass with longevity.

records.title: Astrocytes connect specific brain regions through plastic networks
records.description: Communication between distant brain regions is mediated by plastic networks of gap junction-coupled astrocytes.

records.title: Multicentre gene therapy for OTOF -related deafness followed up to 2.5 years
records.description: In a multicentre trial of AAV1-hOTOF gene therapy involving 42 participants aged 0.8–32.3 years with autosomal recessive deafness 9, treatment demonstrated safety, tolerability, and improved hearing and speech perception, with age and distortion product otoacoustic emissions associated with treatment outcomes.

records.title: Efficiency-optimized relativistic plasma harmonics for extreme fields
records.description: Tailoring relativistic laser–plasma interactions on femtosecond timescales unlocks a direct route to extreme field generation using a coherent harmonic focus.

records.title: Myosin forces remodel F-actin for mechanosensitive protein recognition
records.description: Structural studies demonstrate that myosin generates forces that cause structural changes in actin, modulating cooperative binding by α-catenin and thus signal transduction and intercellular communication via adhesion complexes.

records.title: Evaluating large language models for accuracy incentivizes hallucinations
records.description: Metrics such as accuracy systematically reward guessing over admitting uncertainty in large language models; reframing hallucination as an incentive problem opens a practical path towards more reliable language models.

records.title: Switchable 2D–3D display through a metasurface lenticular lens
records.description: A full-colour 2D–3D switchable light-field display powered by a metasurface lenticular lens is proposed that is a promising solution for next-generation display technologies in both consumer electronics and commercial applications.

records.title: Netrin1 blockade alleviates resistance to chemotherapy in pancreatic cancer
records.description: The Lap-NET1 phase 1b trial reports that combined netrin1 antibody (NP137) plus modified FOLFIRINOX therapy on patients with locally advanced pancreatic cancer was well tolerated and improved progression-free survival and overall survival via inhibition of epithelial–mesenchymal transition.

records.title: Non-equilibrium condensation of the first Solar System solids
records.description: A time-dependent model shows chondrite precursors formed by non-equilibrium condensation: cooling rate and pressure alone generate three mineral classes with increasing oxidation, matching enstatite, ordinary and carbonaceous chondrites without large redox variations in the solar nebula.

records.title: A pro-carcinogenic bacterial toxin binds claudin-4 to cleave E-cadherin
records.description: CRISPR screening shows that claudin-4 is a receptor for the pro-carcinogenic B. fragilis toxin on colonic epithelial cells, and that this interaction promotes cleavage of E-cadherin, leading to epithelial barrier disruption and inflammation.

records.title: Electronic origin of reorganization energy in interfacial electron transfer
records.description: By tuning graphene’s electronic density of states, the study shows electrode electronic structure—not just the electrolyte—dominates reorganization energy and thus controls outer-sphere electron-transfer rates at solid–liquid interfaces.

records.title: Glycerol-driven TNAP activation in thermogenesis and mineralization
records.description: Glycerol is an allosteric activator of tissue-nonspecific alkaline phosphatase (TNAP), activating the futile creatine cycle.

records.title: Decade-long warming accelerates antibiotic resistance in grassland soils
records.description: Decade-long warming increased soil antibiotic-resistance genes by about 24%, enriching resistant microbes and gene transfer, driven by selection for thermal tolerance and linked traits, with implications for public health.

records.title: Punctuated decline of human cooperation
records.description: Cooperation in group lending declines over time due to shifting behavioural motivations, briefly rebounds after loan restarts, then declines faster again, revealing systematic deviations from rational behaviour driving long-term cooperation loss.

records.title: Outplaying elite table tennis players with an autonomous robot
records.description: An autonomous robot system, Ace, combines event-based vision and reinforcement learning to compete with elite human table tennis players, highlighting the potential of physical AI agents to perform complex, real-time interactive tasks.

records.title: Phonon Hall viscosity and the intrinsic thermal Hall effect of α-RuCl 3
records.description: Ultrasonic measurements show phonon Hall viscosity drives an intrinsic thermal Hall effect in α-RuCl 3 , resolving its origin.

records.title: Ubiquitination of glycogen and metabolites in cells and tissues
records.description: Integration of ubiquitin clippases with sortase-based labelling and mass spectrometry reveals that a wide range of non-peptide molecules are ubiquitinated in vivo, and points to a potential role for ubiquitination in physiological glycogen breakdown.

records.title: Hybrid calculation of hadronic vacuum polarization in muon g − 2 to 0.48%
records.description: A new calculation for the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon using a hybrid approach combining experimental and lattice data in different energy ranges represents a validation of the standard model to 11 digits.

records.title: Structural basis of fungal β-1,3-glucan synthase inhibition by caspofungin
records.description: Insights into the structural basis of fungal β-1,3- d -glucan synthase inhibition by caspofungin lay the groundwork for the development of next-generation echinocandins with increased potency, broader antifungal spectrum, and reduced propensity for resistance.

records.title: Quadruple pegRNA enables programmable and efficient large genomic insertion
records.description: QuadPE—a quadruple paired prime editing guide RNA strategy—enables efficient and programmable insertion of large DNA fragments.

records.title: Ceramic-like strength and metallic toughness in a bulk metallic glass
records.description: Re–Co–Ta–B bulk metallic glasses have high strength, fracture toughness and thermal stability, combining traditionally exclusive properties of metals and ceramics.

records.description: Through flexibility, problem-solving and the generosity of colleagues, I shepherded students through fieldwork remotely.

records.title: Improving cancer survival rates will require hard policy choices
records.description: Integrated care and prevention strategies are key, but without careful planning — and sustainable funding — they risk falling short.

records.title: Molecular profiling of gene-edited cells reveals shared drug-resistance mechanisms
records.description: A platform for tracking the changes in gene expression and chromatin accessibility that follow interference with specific genes has been developed. The platform, called PerturbFate, was applied to skin-cancer cells and showed that different genetic perturbations associated with tumour resistance push cells into a shared dedifferentiated state.

records.title: Brain–machine interface reveals the origin of a widely used neural signal
records.description: A type of activity in the brain’s cortex, called high gamma, is widely used in studies of brain function, but its origin has long been debated. An experiment using a brain–machine interface now shows that high-gamma activity is generated mainly by synchronized neuronal inputs, rather than outputs, which has implications for the interpretation of neuroscientific studies.

records.title: AI models ‘subliminally’ transmit biases when training other systems
records.description: Using artificial-intelligence to teach other models can be cheaper and faster than building them from scratch, but this approach can introduce dangerous traits.

records.title: Global cancer rates are rising. How are countries reacting?
records.description: Denmark and South Korea stand out for their strong cancer strategies while England seeks to get back on track.

records.title: A guide to the Nature Index
records.description: A description of the terminology and methodology used in this supplement, and a guide to the functionality that is available free online at natureindex.com.

records.title: Therapeutic mitochondria transplants made more efficient with targeting tool
records.description: A system of protein binders directs energy-generating organelles to targeted cells, potentially improving ways to treat mitochondrial dysfunction.

records.title: Daily briefing: Youthifying 'mirror' brings back more vivid childhood memories
records.description: Looking at a childlike version of your face might help you see childhood memories more clearly. Plus, some AI disease-prediction models are trained on suspect data and how thermal imaging can reveal night-flying birds.

records.title: Bad influence: LLMs can transmit malicious traits using hidden signals
records.description: A large language model that is trained using AI outputs can inherit undesirable behaviours, even if they are not directly referenced in the training data.

records.title: A picture of health: gene-expression maps of the human liver from living donors
records.description: A high-resolution atlas of the healthy human liver has been assembled using gene-expression profiling and spatial mapping of cells in samples from living donors. The atlas reveals human-specific patterns of gene expression in different zones and uncovers spatially resolved adaptations in liver cells from individuals with the disease steatosis.

records.title: Can China’s Great Green Wall shape efforts to keep the world’s deserts at bay?
records.description: Grand anti-desertification schemes often fail when trees die and funding dries up — yet one project has broken the mould.

records.title: Early-onset cancer fuels calls for wider screening — but at what cost?
records.description: As some countries lower the screening age for breast, colorectal and other cancers, scientists warn that it could cause more harm than good.

records.title: Why more fossil fuels won’t fix the Iran energy crisis
records.description: Climate-friendly technologies are the best way to stymie rising inflation — and will get better and cheaper over time.

records.title: How effective is the personalized off-label use of targeted cancer treatment?
records.description: If general cancer treatment fails, a tumour-type-specific therapy might be tried for other cancers with genetic changes in the targeted pathway. How well does this work?

records.title: Dozens of AI disease-prediction models were trained on dubious data
records.description: The models are designed to predict someone’s risk of diabetes or stroke. A few might already have been used on patients.

records.title: Ozymandias undead
records.description: Nothing beside remains.

records.title: Landmark ancient-genome study shows surprise acceleration of human evolution
records.description: Data from more than 15,000 ancient people reveal natural selection of hundreds of genes linked to immunity, skin tone, behaviour and other traits.

records.title: Monolithic 3D integration of tantalum pentoxide nonlinear photonics
records.description: Monolithic three-dimensional (3D) integration of tantalum pentoxide on a lithium niobate substrate enables scalable, multifunctional photonic systems and the incorporation of nonlinear optics directly into existing and emerging photonics infrastructure.

records.title: Linear RAG scanning mediates editing of Igκ variable region repertoires
records.description: Studies explaining the secondary Igk recombination mechanism are described and Cer/Sis deletion and/or displacement is implicated as a developmental switch converting the rearrangement mechanisms from two-loop-based diffusional primary Igk into one-loop-based linear scanning secondary mechanisms.

records.title: Identifying the topographic signature of early Martian oceans
records.description: Shelves rather than shorelines may be better topographic indicators of oceans on Earth and Mars.

records.title: Brainwide blood volume reflects opposing neural populations
records.description: Combined functional ultrasound imaging and Neuropixels recording of mouse brains identify two neuronal populations with opposing arousal-related activity and distinct haemodynamic response functions, that occur throughout the brain.

records.title: Ancient DNA reveals pervasive directional selection across West Eurasia
records.description: Analysis of 15,836 ancient West Eurasian genomes reveals hundreds of instances of directional selection, showing that sustained changes in allele frequency were widespread, rather than being rare over this period as previously assumed.

records.title: Tumour promotion through the lens of evolution
records.description: This Review revisits tumour initiation and promotion in light of clonal diversity and the presence of cancer driver mutations in normal tissues, aiming to understand mechanisms that enable environmental and endogenous factors to expand tumorigenic clones.

records.title: Cytoplasmic lattices are megadalton storage complexes in mammalian oocytes
records.description: Structural studies of native mouse oocyte cytoplasmic lattices using cryo-electron microscopy reveal that they consist of PADI6 and subcortical maternal complex proteins plus cytoskeletal proteins, epigenetic regulators and ubiquitination factors.

records.title: mRNA vaccines engage unconventional pathways in CD8 + T cell priming
records.description: mRNA–lipid-nanoparticle vaccines do not require type 1 conventional dendritic (cDC1) cells or the WDFY4-dependent cross-presentation pathway for CD8 + T cell priming but, instead, engage both cDC1 and cDC2 cells redundantly.

records.title: Prospective evaluation of genomics-guided off-label treatment
records.description: Evaluation by the Drug Rediscovery Protocol of off-label use of 37 approved cancer drugs on 1,610 patients showed modest activities overall, although subgroups of responders suggest that off-label drug use could be beneficial in tandem with more stringent biomarker selection.

records.title: Cell-type-targeted mitochondrial transplantation rescues cell degeneration
records.description: MitoCatch is a cell-type-specific mitochondrion-targeting system that links mitochondria and the cell surface by protein binders and delivers mitochondria into the target cell.

records.title: A spatial atlas of the healthy human liver from live donors
records.description: A human spatial atlas of gene expression in liver based on live donors shows marked porto–central zonation of hepatocytes and non-parenchymal cells, and transcriptomic changes in early steatosis.

records.title: A mechanism for adaptive genome regulation in cancer
records.description: In this Perspective article, a theoretical framework for how the AP-1 family of transcription factors mediates cellular adaptation in cancer drug resistance is proposed.

records.title: Molecular basis for methylation-sensitive editing by Cas9
records.description: ThermoCas9, a genome-editing enzyme that is sensitive to the DNA methylation status of the target locus, is characterized and shows promise for targeting hypomethylated DNA regions in cancer cells.

records.title: Emergence of oncofetal plasticity is ubiquitous in early colorectal cancers
records.description: Metastasis-associated oncofetal cell states emerge at the earliest stages of colorectal cancer and spatial profiling shows stereotypic patterning of fibroblast subtypes resembling normal tissue architecture, resulting in distinct regional microenvironments that dictate the timing and positioning of oncofetal plasticity.

records.description: ThermoCas9, a genome-editing enzyme that is sensitive to the DNA methylation status of the target locus, is characterized and shows promise for targeting hypomethylated DNA regions in cancer cells.

records.title: Emergence of oncofetal plasticity is ubiquitous in early colorectal cancers
records.description: Metastasis-associated oncofetal cell states emerge at the earliest stages of colorectal cancer and spatial profiling shows stereotypic patterning of fibroblast subtypes resembling normal tissue architecture, resulting in distinct regional microenvironments that dictate the timing and positioning of oncofetal plasticity.

records.title: Template-driven scaffolding of SCF FBXO42 regulates PP2A degradation
records.description: The E3 ligase SCF FBXO42 degrades holoenzyme-free PP2Ac in complex with the coiled-coil protein CCDC6 to maintain cancer cell fitness

records.title: Continuously tunable coherent pulse generation in a semiconductor laser
records.description: A monolithic mode-locked semiconductor laser with a continuously and widely tunable repetition rate is achieved by using a microwave driving signal that induces a spatiotemporal gain modulation along the entire laser cavity.

records.title: The neural mechanisms supporting the rise and fall of maternal aggression
records.description: In mice, female aggression is governed by an amygdala–to–medial hypothalamus circuit that is strengthened during pregnancy and is dynamically amplified by oxytocin during lactation.

records.title: Language models transmit behavioural traits through hidden signals in data
records.description: During model distillation, large language models can subtly transmit traits unrelated to the training data.

records.title: Pixelated quantum-dot superlattice LEDs
records.description: Scalable fabrication of ordered perovskite quantum dot superlattices enables high-efficiency, ultrahigh-resolution LEDs and active-matrix displays with greatly improved brightness, stability and device lifetime.

records.title: 300-unit-per-second roll-to-roll manufacturing of visible metalenses
records.description: This work demonstrates industrial-scale roll-to-roll fabrication of high-efficiency visible metalenses using nanoimprinting and TiO 2 coating, achieving low cost, high throughput and uniform performance, enabling commercialization of metasurfaces.

records.title: Carbonyl swapping converts cyclic ketones to saturated heterocycles
records.description: A modular carbonyl replacement strategy converts common cyclic ketones into diverse saturated heterocycles, enabling efficient synthesis and late-stage diversification of bioactive molecules.

records.title: Imaging interface-controlled bulk oxygen spillover
records.description: In situ microscopic single-particle imaging demonstrates the significance of rationally engineered metal–support interfaces for activating the oxygen in bulk catalyst, helping elucidate reaction pathways in catalytic conversions.

records.title: Mapping convergent regulators of melanoma drug resistance by PerturbFate
records.description: PerturbFate is a high-throughput, cost-effective, single-cell platform that systematically profiles CRISPR interference perturbations to reveal common regulatory nodes and convergent phenotypic states across diverse genetic alterations linked to vemurafenib resistance in melanoma cells.

records.title: EBV strain interacts with host HLA to drive nasopharyngeal carcinoma risk
records.description: A genome-to-genome association study identifies host and viral risk factors that interact to drive nasopharyngeal carcinoma endemicity in southern China.

records.title: Composable neural emulators accelerate thermoelectric generator design
records.description: A composable neural network emulator is described for speeding up thermoelectric generator design, demonstrating the ability to predict generator performance with >99% accuracy while taking only 0.01% of the time compared with commercial finite-element solvers.

records.title: The striking history of safety matches
records.description: The quest to make fire-lighting less dangerous, and a proposal for smallest unit of information worth photocopying, in our weekly dip into Nature ’s archive.

records.title: Stop overlooking librarians’ expertise
Deep-sea mining mustn’t go ahead until there are baseline data
AI agents replicate human social dynamics in days
Marine heatwaves can supercharge cyclones
records.description: Storms that cross exceptionally warm ocean waters intensify more quickly and do more damage than storms that do not.

records.title: China discontinues prominent journal ranking list
Researchers: here’s how to audit your fragmented digital identity
records.description: Services that track researcher profiles can splinter people’s online identities — but there are ways to keep them consistent.

records.title: The air is full of DNA — here’s what scientists are using it for
records.description: Airborne genetic material can be used to paint a picture of ecosystem health, watch for invasive species and even identify humans.

records.title: Daily briefing: The air is full of DNA — here’s what it can teach us
records.description: Researchers are using airborne DNA to get snapshots of the make up of ecosystems. Plus, what scientists in Hungary think about the end of Viktor Orbán’s government and the penguins helping to monitor ‘forever chemicals’.

records.title: AI needs solid botanical data more than ever
records.description: An artificial-intelligence revolution in biotechnology won’t get far without human taxonomic expertise — and that’s under threat.

records.title: Stop the ‘space race’: space exploration must be a shared human endeavour
records.description: Although led by NASA, Artemis II wasn’t just a US achievement; the mission was a collaborative effort. Long may such cooperation continue.

records.title: NSF awards record number of coveted PhD fellowships in surprise move
records.description: Quantum science and AI research are big winners just a year after the US funding giant slashed its Graduate Research Fellowship Program awards in half.

records.title: What Orbán’s fall from power means for research
records.description: Hungary’s new leader has promised a ‘system change’ — but researchers say that rebuilding science will take more than a reversal of Victor Orbán’s laws.

records.title: Boycott of major AI conference exposes a growing US–China divide
records.description: China-based researchers make up more than half of all lead authors at NeurIPS.

records.title: Saving face: why facial scars are smaller than back scars
records.description: Facial wounds heal with less scarring than do comparable ones on the back. The reason relates to differences in the ability of cells to express collagen genes.

records.title: Polyclonal selection of immune checkpoint mutations in thyroid autoimmunity
records.description: Single-molecule DNA sequencing identifies recurrent somatic mutations in autoimmune B cells that may allow them to escape peripheral tolerance and cause autoimmune disease.

records.title: Autonomous closed-loop framework for reproducible perovskite solar cells
records.description: An autonomous closed-loop framework combining machine-learning-driven materials discovery with an automated manufacturing platform is introduced for the highly reproducible production of perovskite solar cells that demonstrate high power conversion and certified maximum power point tracking efficiencies.

records.title: Viruses allegedly stolen from high-security lab cause stir in Brazil
records.description: The missing samples — reported to include chikungunya and dengue viruses — have been recovered, but questions linger over motive.

records.title: 14 things our PhD supervisors got right and why it mattered
records.description: PhD students reflect on how their supervisors made a meaningful difference — from quiet acts of kindness to career-shaping guidance.

records.title: The ‘crazy rule-defying’ genes that determine sex
records.description: A gripping account reveals the workings of the remarkable chromosomes that specify male or female development.

records.title: The middle years of my life and career: balancing two experiments at once
records.description: When I found out that I was no longer eligible for an early-career grant, I took a moment to pause and reflect on my family life and my work.

records.title: Microbial hockey: bacteria can spin a ‘puck’ just by swimming
records.description: 3D-printed discs harness a previously overlooked feature of bacterial locomotion to power tiny motors.

records.title: Electric vehicles can ride to the grid’s rescue
records.description: Vehicle-to-grid technology, if installed properly, could allow vehicles to serve as back-up batteries.

records.title: Liquid or solid? Oobleck droplets are both
records.description: High-speed cameras can observe the strange behaviour of a cornstarch–water mixture.

records.title: Your nose contains multitudes — of long-lived immune cells
records.description: Nasal tissue harbours T cells that ‘remember’ a pathogen long after infection is past.

records.title: Daily briefing: A treatment to reverse cellular ageing is about to be tested in people
records.description: ‘Partial reprogramming’, which winds back a cell’s biological clock, could enter clinical trials later this year. Plus, a single DNA tweak can make female mice grow testes and why obesity drugs are more effective in some people than others.

records.title: One woman, three autoimmune diseases: CAR-T therapy vanquishes ultra-rare disease trio
records.description: Fourteen months after treatment with engineered immune cells, the recipient has no symptoms and doesn’t need to take medication.

records.title: Female mice grow testes after this single DNA tweak
records.description: Small changes in the non-coding part of the genome have a key role in sex determination.

records.title: Ambiphilic cross-coupling with aryl-bismuth reagents
records.description: This study shows that aryl-bismuth complexes can act as either nucleophiles or electrophiles in palladium-catalysed cross-coupling reactions, enabling synthetic flexibility in biaryl formation.

records.title: Should academic misconduct be catalogued? Proposed US database sparks debate
records.description: Repository would require US universities to register research fraud and workplace harassment.

records.title: How to thrive in science when you move abroad
records.description: Sonali Majumdar offers a toolkit to support international scientists, their supervisors and mentors.

records.title: I was with Artemis II’s scientists during the Moon fly-by. Here’s what I saw
records.description: Nature correspondent Alexandra Witze describes the joy and tension at mission control in Houston.

records.title: Almost half of traded wildlife carries disease-causing pathogens
records.description: More than 40% of traded mammalian species share at least one pathogen with humans, compared with only 6% of non-traded mammals.

records.title: Briefing Chat: The tongue trick that helps sunbirds suck
records.description: Nature staff discuss some of the week’s top science news.

records.title: Hidden human–virus interactions uncovered in DNA in blood and saliva
records.description: The abundance of viral DNA was measured in DNA sequenced from blood and saliva samples in biobanks, revealing strong correlations with age, sex and dozens of genetic variants. Genetic analyses indicate that a high abundance of latent Epstein–Barr virus is a causal risk factor for a blood cancer called Hodgkin’s lymphoma.

records.title: Genetics reveal why people respond differently to GLP-1 weight-loss drugs
records.description: Genetic variants in GLP1R and GIPR , which encode targets of GLP-1-based medications, offer insights into why responses to these drugs vary and who might face adverse effects.

records.description: A popular online game simulates life as an academic — and throws the challenges of being an early-career researcher into sharp relief.

records.title: Brain organoids are a transformative technology — but they need regulation
records.description: The potential benefits of organoids for fundamental research and medicine are huge. Efforts to establish proper boundaries for their use should be supported.

records.description: Forests that regrow on farmland are resilient and regain much of their lost biodiversity and species richness in 30 years — a finding with implications for conservation.

records.title: Immolation
records.description: Supply and demand.

records.title: Why obesity drugs work better for some people: these genes hold clues
records.description: Study of almost 28,000 people also identifies genetic variants that raise the risk of gastrointestinal side effects from GLP-1 medications.

records.title: High-precision measurement of the W boson’s mass lends weight to the standard model
records.description: The latest value for the mass of a fundamental particle called the W boson is consistent with the standard model of particle physics, challenging a previous anomalous result.

records.title: Real-life Pokémon professors wanted: why the media franchise is hiring academics
records.description: An appetite for scientists reflects evolution in how video-game companies think about design.

records.title: Daily briefing: AI spread information about an obviously made-up disease
records.description: AI chatbots informed users of the symptoms of ‘bixonimania’ after scientists published just two fake preprints. Plus, different psychedelics work in surprisingly similar ways and an influential report on the economic cost of climate change revisited.

records.title: Artemis II relied on European science: what that means for the region’s space ambitions
records.description: The Artemis II mission is a success for the European Space Agency, as well as for NASA. Will Europe crew its own lunar missions?

records.title: Tumour trap: engineered enhancer sequences enlisted to kill cancer cells
records.description: New cancer therapies are needed that do not harm healthy tissue. An engineered DNA sequence shows promise as one of the tools in a method to target brain tumour cells.

records.title: Mapping the maternal–fetal interface through pregnancy in high resolution
records.description: The placenta — a temporary organ of the offspring — attaches to the mother’s uterus, from which it taps a blood supply. A high-resolution map of individual cells at this junction now reveals some of the specific cell–cell interactions involved and pinpoints cell types that are vulnerable in common pregnancy complications.

records.title: Mini models of the human brain are revealing how this complex organ takes shape
records.description: Lab-grown organoids are turbo-charging the study of human brain development and disease.

records.title: High-precision calculation of the quark–gluon coupling from lattice QCD
records.description: Large-scale lattice quantum chromodynamics simulations enable a model-free, highly precise determination of the strong coupling constant α s , reducing theoretical uncertainty and improving precision tests of particle physics.

records.title: Engineered immunosuppressive dendritic cells protect against cardiac remodelling
records.description: Lesion-targeted immune modulation is a feasible strategy to control cardiac fibrosis, and engineered dendritic cells are a promising therapeutic platform for treating cardiac remodelling and heart failure.

records.title: Biodiversity resilience in a tropical rainforest
records.description: Assessment of how 16 taxonomic groups in a lowland tropical forest resist and recover from anthropogenic disturbance shows the potential of protecting naturally regenerating secondary forests to reverse biodiversity losses.

records.title: Protected quantum gates using qubit doublons in dynamical optical lattices
records.description: A purely geometric two-qubit SWAP gate can be realized by transiently populating qubit doublon states of fermionic atoms in a dynamical optical lattice.

records.title: Saturation editing of RNU4-2 reveals distinct dominant and recessive disorders
records.description: Saturation genome editing of RNU4-2 identifies the functional and clinical impact of variants across the entire gene and delineates variants that cause a new recessive neurodevelopmental disorder distinct from ReNU syndrome.

records.title: The importance of competition and facilitation for global tree diversity
records.description: Across 17 forest plots (2.7 million trees, 5,400 species), competition dominated overall, but facilitation was relatively stronger near the equator and declined towards higher latitudes, partly linked to temperature, legumes, mycorrhizal associations and canopy nursing effect.

records.title: DNA damage drives antigen diversification in Trypanosoma brucei
records.description: An in vitro toolkit for studying VSG diversification defines key molecular requirements underlying the formation of mosaic VSGs, providing an experimental framework for the exploration of antigen diversification in Trypanosoma brucei and in other pathogenic microorganisms.

records.title: High-fidelity collisional quantum gates with fermionic atoms
records.description: A robust composite pair-exchange gate based on controlled interactions of fermionic atoms in an optical superlattice demonstrates high fidelities and long Bell-state lifetimes, marking an important step towards a fully digital fermionic quantum computer.

records.title: Single-cell spatiotemporal dissection of the human maternal–fetal interface
records.description: A single-cell multiomic atlas of the human maternal–fetal interface across pregnancy reveals cell types, states and spatial niches, developmental tissue architectures and transcriptional programmes, and identifies cell types with roles in pre-eclampsia, spontaneous preterm birth and miscarriage.

records.title: High-precision measurement of the W boson mass with the CMS experiment
records.description: The CMS experiment at CERN reports one of the highest-precision measurements of the W boson mass, finding it in line with standard model predictions and at odds with recent anomalous measurements.

records.title: Genetic predictors of GLP1 receptor agonist weight loss and side effects
records.description: Identification of genetic variants associated with the efficacy and side effects of GLP1 medications could underpin development of precision medicine approaches in the treatment of obesity.

records.title: Mummified early Permian reptile reveals ancient amniote breathing apparatus
records.description: A mummified fossil of the early Permian reptile Captorhinus reveals the potential ancestral amniote breathing mechanism and its impact on terrestrial vertebrate evolution.

records.title: Clinical application of base editing for treating β-thalassaemia
records.description: A clinical phase 1 trial of a single infusion of CS-101, CD34 + cells modified using a transformer base editor to reactivate fetal haemoglobin production, led to early and enduring transfusion independence in patients with β-thalassaemia.

records.title: Asymmetric selection of a rice immune module and rebuild of disease resistance
records.description: Stacking XA48-mediated effector-triggered immunity with XA21-mediated pattern-triggered immunity in Oryza sativa japonica reconstitutes the broad-spectrum resistance from wild rice.

records.title: Metabolomics across scales: from single cells to population studies
records.description: This Perspective reviews the potential and the challenges of metabolomics approaches, encompassing both single-cell and population-scale metabolomics.

records.title: Multiomics and deep learning dissect regulatory syntax in human development
records.description: The Human Development Multiomic Atlas catalogues single-cell accessibility and gene expression data from human fetal cells across 12 organs, enabling the inference of syntactic rules for motifs that govern cell-type-specific transcription factor binding and chromatin accessibility during human development.

records.title: Population-scale repeat expansions elucidate disease risk and brain atrophy
records.description: Decreased brain volumes and increased NfL levels can be observed earlier than disease diagnosis in short-tandem-repeat-associated neurological diseases.

records.title: Satellite imagery reveals increasing volatility in human night-time activity
records.description: Daily satellite data reveal that Earth’s artificial lights at night are highly volatile, with frequent brightening and dimming between 2014 and 2022.

records.title: Superconductivity and electronic structures of nickelate thin film superstructures
records.description: Engineered Ruddlesden–Popper nickelate superstructures show that specific Fermi surface features enable ambient-pressure superconductivity, linking structural configuration, electronic structure and superconducting behaviour. .

records.title: Synthetic super-enhancers enable precision viral immunotherapy
records.description: Synthetic super-enhancers enable specific delivery of anticancer payloads, achieving tumour elimination after a single dose in a mouse model of aggressive glioblastoma.

records.title: AI and the human mind: only one is a black box
When page-renumbering causes outrage
records.description: The problem of page numbering in reprinted articles, and experiments to find the source of a typhoid outbreak, in our weekly dip into Nature ’s archive.

records.title: Representation without power in science isn’t equity
Don’t rush use of lymphatic surgery in Alzheimer’s disease
New drugs take aim at one of cancer’s deadliest mutations
records.description: Mutations in the KRAS protein were once deemed ‘undruggable’. Today, various approaches are in the pipeline.

records.title: First photos from Artemis II: see stunning ‘Earthset’ and more
records.description: Images snapped during a fly-by capture a solar eclipse and unprecedented details of the far side of the Moon.

records.title: Daily briefing: The Artemis II special
records.description: Nature correspondent Alexandra Witze takes over Nature Briefing for a special edition from mission control in Houston.

records.title: How DNA forensics is transforming studies of ancient manuscripts
records.description: Scientists are exposing the biological information hidden in ancient parchments without leaving a mark.

records.title: This method to reverse cellular ageing is about to be tested in humans
records.description: A burgeoning field is launching its first clinical trial to find out whether dialling back cell development can safely refresh aged tissues and organs.

records.title: Your brain on drugs: different psychedelics work in surprisingly similar ways
records.description: Hundreds of scans hint at how substances such as psilocybin, LSD and ayahuasca alter connections between key areas of the brain.

records.title: Scientists invented a fake disease. AI told people it was real
records.description: Bixonimania doesn’t exist except in a clutch of obviously bogus academic papers. So why did AI chatbots warn people about this fictional illness?

records.title: ‘Net zero’ isn’t madness: the staggering economic costs of climate change
records.description: The landmark Stern Review, published 20 years ago, laid bare the economic cost of climate inaction. A fracturing political consensus now risks accruing even heftier bills for future generations.

records.title: Engaging the head and the heart: why scientists turn to poetry
records.description: Some researchers use verse to visualize complex problems or translate the wonders of science for wider audiences.

records.title: ‘Yes, we can’: a blueprint for a clean economy and healthy society
records.description: As oil and gas markets face crisis, an influential economist sets out a path to a more efficient, prosperous and sustainable world.

records.title: Why the US needs a unified, mission-based strategy for health innovation
records.description: A goal-driven approach to medical research and development in the United States would address unmet medical needs, reduce costs and improve the reach of treatments.

records.title: Historic Artemis II Moon fly-by: Nature ’s live coverage as it happened

records.title: What Artemis II’s astronauts will look for on the Moon’s far side
records.description: Mission scientists spoke to Nature about the geological features they’re most excited about the crew observing.

records.title: Massive budget cuts for US science proposed again by Trump administration
records.description: The 2027 budget proposal would curb federal payments for scientific publishing and reduce funding for many US institutions.

records.title: Regular physical activity in midlife cuts risk of early death
records.description: Study of more than 11,000 women found that only a few hours of moderate-to-vigorous activity per week had a strong effect.

records.title: Artemis II is go: humans head to the Moon after half-century absence
records.description: We take a look at the mission’s aims and the science that’ll be happening along the way.

records.title: The Moon belongs to all of us — not just countries that can afford to reach it
records.description: As humanity blasts off into a new space race, we need a model of exploration that emphasizes stewardship of other worlds, not exploitation.

records.title: Why some cancer-fighting immune cells lose their strength inside tumours
records.description: Mitochondria are key to powering the immune defenders called dendritic cells.

records.title: These scientists chased a jet to learn more about ‘lean-burn’ contrails
records.description: In-flight experiment suggests lowering soot emissions might not reduce contrail formation — plus, what can be learnt from fakery in science.

records.title: These advanced solar cells have an antique source: old bullets
records.description: Lead recycled from centuries-old ammunition provides raw materials for perovskite solar cells.

records.title: Catalyst diverts course of industrial process to make valuable hydrocarbons
records.description: A catalyst with two cobalt components potentially opens the way to sustainable processes for manufacturing light olefins — key ingredients for making plastics and detergents.

records.title: Lift off! Artemis II mission sends humans to the Moon — opening a new era of exploration
records.description: The astronauts will fly by the far side of the Moon in the coming days, taking in views never seen by the human eye.

records.title: Super-potent opioids could be safer-than-expected alternatives to conventional painkillers
records.description: Modified nitazenes, opioids 1,000 times stronger than morphine, show remarkably few adverse effects in rodents, renewing the potential of these drugs for pain relief.

records.title: Is social media addictive? Why a formal diagnosis is still out of reach
records.description: Limited methods and a lack of guidance around diagnostic criteria mean that many scientists are reluctant to use the term addiction.

records.title: Struggling to focus on research when the world is ‘on fire’? Some ways to cope
records.description: Keeping up with distressing news is affecting some researchers’ mental health and their scientific work.

records.title: Hallucinated citations are polluting the scientific literature. What can be done?
records.description: Tens of thousands of publications from 2025 might include invalid references generated by AI, a Nature analysis suggests.

records.title: Daily briefing: The countdown to NASA’s Artemis II Moon mission launch
records.description: The science that NASA’s latest Moon mission will conduct, and why some researchers aren’t fussed about it. Plus, the status of the bird flu outbreak in US cows and what publishers can do about hallucinated citations in scientific literature.

records.title: Cutting aircraft soot emissions is not enough to curb contrail clouds
records.description: The contrail clouds formed by jet engines contribute to global warming. In-flight measurements of the particles emitted and contrails produced by a passenger jet show that contrails are formed through different mechanisms, depending on the soot-emission level and the fuel composition, potentially reshaping our understanding of the climate impact of aviation.

records.title: Half of social-science studies fail replication test in years-long project
records.description: Results from massive, ‘eagerly awaited’ initiative reinforce concerns about the credibility of science — but raise hope for solutions.

records.title: Pincer movement: fossil pushes origins of chelicerate arthropods back to the Cambrian period
records.description: Spiders and scorpions belong to a group called chelicerates, which are arthropods with pincers at the front of their head. Fossil evidence reveals how this group evolved.

records.title: ‘Replication games’ test the robustness of social-science studies
records.description: A large-scale assessment of the reproducibility and robustness of 110 articles published in leading economics and political-science journals finds that more than 85% were computationally reproducible, and 72% of statistically significant results remained significant and in the same direction in robustness checks. About 25% of the evaluated articles contained non‑trivial coding errors.

records.title: False hope
records.description: There’s something brewing.

records.title: More self-reflection in research can lead to better science
records.description: A package of papers looking at the social and behavioural sciences shows the value of researchers collaborating to further the cause of reproducible, replicable and robust findings.

records.title: Why science has a credibility problem — and how to address it
records.description: Psychologist Brian Nosek’s latest work indicates that many results in the social sciences don’t stand up to immediate scrutiny. But that’s the beginning of a conversation, not the end, he explains to Nature .

records.title: Huge meta-research project puts claims in social-science papers to the test
records.description: Three experts discuss lessons learnt from a large-scale dissection of the reproducibility, analytical robustness and replicability of published results.

records.title: 100 years of synthetic fuels
records.description: The Fischer–Tropsch synthesis shaped history by providing a way of making liquid fuels from coal. It is now causing a stir again as a route to sustainable fuels.

records.title: DNA damage burden causes selective CUX2 neuron loss in neuroinflammation
records.description: DNA damage burden and inadequate repair in CUX2 + cortical layer 2/3 excitatory neurons contributes to selective vulnerability in neuroinflammatory injury.

records.title: More self-reflection in research can lead to better science
records.description: A package of papers looking at the social and behavioural sciences shows the value of researchers collaborating to further the cause of reproducible, replicable and robust findings.

records.title: Why science has a credibility problem — and how to address it
records.description: Psychologist Brian Nosek’s latest work indicates that many results in the social sciences don’t stand up to immediate scrutiny. But that’s the beginning of a conversation, not the end, he explains to Nature .

records.title: Huge meta-research project puts claims in social-science papers to the test
records.description: Three experts discuss lessons learnt from a large-scale dissection of the reproducibility, analytical robustness and replicability of published results.

records.title: 100 years of synthetic fuels
records.description: The Fischer–Tropsch synthesis shaped history by providing a way of making liquid fuels from coal. It is now causing a stir again as a route to sustainable fuels.

records.title: DNA damage burden causes selective CUX2 neuron loss in neuroinflammation
records.description: DNA damage burden and inadequate repair in CUX2 + cortical layer 2/3 excitatory neurons contributes to selective vulnerability in neuroinflammatory injury.

records.title: Entanglement and electronic coherence in attosecond molecular photoionization
records.description: Dissociative ionization of H 2 molecules by the combination of a phase-locked attosecond laser pair and a few-cycle NIR laser shows that ion–photoelectron entanglement influences electronic coherence in H 2 + , allowing control over the degree of entanglement by varying the delay between the pulses.

records.title: The 1000 Chinese Pangenome empowers medical and population genetics
records.description: Development of the pangenome-informed genome assembly (PIGA) workflow enabled the generation of 1,116 diploid genome assemblies (55 de novo and 1,061 pangenome-informed), representing an extensive resource of medically relevant genic variations.

records.title: Gene regulatory landscape dissected by single-cell four-omics sequencing
records.description: Combining single-cell parallel profiling of genome conformation, histone modifications, chromatin accessibility and gene expression reveals dynamics and intranuclear spatial clustering of epigenome profiles, enabling sophisticated analysis of the regulatory landscape across cell types and tissues.

records.title: Developmental organization of sensory and sympathetic ganglia
records.description: Findings suggest that neural crest fate bias predominantly emerges within the neural tube, and that only a minor subset of delaminated progenitors retain multipotency to generate both sensory and sympathetic derivatives.

records.title: Dopaminergic mechanisms of dynamical social specialization
records.description: Longitudinal tracking of mice reveals that stable, specialized social roles emerge spontaneously within groups during a foraging task, with dopaminergic activity in the ventral tegmental area driving sex-divergent patterns of specialization.

records.title: A µ-opioid receptor superagonist analgesic with minimal adverse effects
records.description: N -desethyl-fluornitrazene is a µ-opioid receptor agonist derived from nitazenes that has supramaximal intrinsic efficacy that produces analgesia with minimal adverse effects in rodent models.

records.title: Moiré engineering of Cooper-pair density modulation states
records.description: Researchers created a moiré superlattice in Sb 2 Te 3 /FeTe bilayers, producing spatially modulated superconducting gaps directly imaged with Josephson scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy, tunable by replacing Sb 2 Te 3 with Bi 2 Te 3 .

records.title: Electric dipole moment drives the dynamics of the TNFR1 complex I signalosome
records.description: Long-range interactions mediated by protein electric dipole moments have a role in driving the assembly and disassembly of super-signalling complex I for promoting NF-κB signalling.

records.title: Evidence of the pair-instability gap from black-hole masses
records.description: LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA’s fourth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog shows evidence of a clear pair-instability gap in the distribution of binary black-hole secondary masses but is absent in the larger primary masses.

records.title: Expansion of outer cortical CUX2 neurons requires adaptations for DNA repair
records.description: The transcription factor ATF4 is shown to regulate double-stranded DNA repair within vulnerable CUX2 + upper-layer 2/3 cortical neurons, enabling their survival during development.

records.title: Structural modifications in strain-engineered bilayer nickelate thin films
records.description: Using multislice electron ptychography to directly measure the atomic-scale structural evolution of the nickelate La 3 Ni 2 O 7 under a range of biaxial strains, a theoretical framework is constructed for characterizing the impact of specific structural motifs for stabilizing superconductivity.

records.title: AhR inhibition promotes axon regeneration via a stress–growth switch
records.description: AhR functions as a neuronal brake on axon regeneration, integrating environmental sensing, protein homeostasis and metabolic signalling to control the balance between stress adaptation and axonal repair.

records.title: Substantial aircraft contrail formation at low soot emission levels
records.description: In-flight observations show that the use of lean-burn combustion succeeds in reducing soot emissions from aircraft—yet contrail ice crystals still form and nucleate on volatile particles.

records.title: Investigating the reproducibility of the social and behavioural sciences
records.description: A study of reproducibility in a stratified random sample of 600 papers published from 2009 to 2018 in 62 journals spanning the social and behavioural sciences finds higher reproducibility among more recent papers and papers from journals that require data sharing.

records.title: Stoichiometric FeTe is a superconductor
records.description: Analysis of FeTe films grown using molecular-beam epitaxy and annealed under a Te flux post-growth shows that stoichiometric FeTe is inherently a superconductor, contradicting the long-held view that it is an antiferromagnetic metal.

records.title: Investigating the analytical robustness of the social and behavioural sciences
records.description: When 100 social and behavioural science claims were examined, 34% of reanalyses closely matched the original results, with 74% reaching the same conclusion, revealing limited robustness of single-path analyses and the need to address analytical uncertainty.

records.title: Dual-symmetry-guided assembly of complex lattices
records.description: A dual-symmetry-guided strategy is used to assemble a broad class of complex Archimedean lattices and two-dimensional quasicrystalline structures, providing a general and experimentally accessible route to complex-symmetry materials.

records.title: A chelicera-bearing arthropod reveals the Cambrian origin of chelicerates
records.description: Megachelicerax cousteaui gen. et sp. nov. is a large soft-bodied arthropod from the middle Cambrian of Utah featuring massive three-segmented chelicerae, along with five pairs of pseudobiramous prosomal limbs with non-foliaceous exopodal rami, and plate-like lamellae-bearing opisthosomal appendages.

records.title: An enteric neuron ionotropic receptor regulates salt stress resistance
records.description: The I3 pharyngeal enteric neuron in Caenorhabditis elegans detects high-salt conditions, and the GLR-9 ionotropic salt receptor expressed specifically in I3 regulates genes related to salt stress resistance in distal tissues.

records.title: Deconstruction of a spino-brain–spinal cord circuit that drives chronic pain
records.description: In mice, a circuit between the spinal cord and various regions of the brain, centring on spinal-cord-projecting neurons in the rostral ventromedial medulla, has a key role in driving chronic pain.

records.title: General scales unlock AI evaluation with explanatory and predictive power
records.description: A fully automated methodology based on rubrics capturing a broad range of cognitive and intellectual demands is illustrated using LLMs and tasks, demonstrating a new way to evaluate the capabilities of AI systems and anticipate their performance.

records.title: Hydroxy-induced cobalt oxides for syngas to light olefins
records.description: A set of hydroxy promoters physically mixed with cobalt oxides for syngas to light olefins conversion using Fischer–Tropsch synthesis is shown to boost catalyst performance as well as simplifying the process and increasing sustainability.

records.title: Active dissociation of intracortical spiking and high gamma activity
records.description: A brain–machine interface is used in monkeys to investigate the biophysical underpinnings of cortical high gamma-band activity, a signal that is often studied in the context of many brain functions.

records.title: Reproducibility and robustness of economics and political science research
records.description: Robustness checks and reproduction of analyses with existing and updated data based on 110 articles in economics and political science journals with data and code-sharing requirements found high levels of robustness and reproducibility and determined that robustness was not dependent on author characteristics or data availability.

records.title: ‘Schrödinger’s carbon’: The misclassification of carbon capture and storage as standard mitigation
Bunny or bug?
records.description: A curious species of rabbit is detected in the lab, and bullfinches learn the art of primrose eating, in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: A solar system is born
records.description: Astronomers have spotted a second planet taking shape from the material orbiting a young star — only the second such example known.

records.title: A responsible authorship culture is needed — it is a collective responsibility
Author Correction: Signatures of ambient pressure superconductivity in thin film La 3 Ni 2 O 7
AI used in warfare needs a strong ethical framework
The hidden costs of ‘helpful’ AI
records.description: Even when artificial-intelligence tools aid individuals’ decision-making, they can quietly de-skill whole professions by narrowing how uncertainties and values are debated.

records.title: Artemis II mission is about to fly humans to the Moon — here’s the science they’ll do
records.description: Set to lift off this week, the NASA flight will take astronauts around the Moon for the first time in more than 50 years.

records.title: Author Correction: Phenome-wide analysis of copy number variants in 470,727 UK Biobank genomes
Daily briefing: Are boys really in crisis? What the science says
records.description: Concerns about boys are widespread, but evidence shows that worries are best understood in the context of all young people. Plus, the month’s best science images and a whole new way that vertebrates slurp.

records.description: The month’s sharpest science shots, selected by Nature ’s photo team.
