records.title: China is waging war on Alzheimer’s. What can its approach teach the rest of the world?
records.description: The country is facing a coming wave of dementia for its ageing population, and is investing in research into drugs, diagnostics and even surgery to prepare itself.

records.title: Daily briefing: COVID’s origins — what we do and don’t know
records.description: Most peer-reviewed evidence suggests an animal origin of SARS-CoV-2, but doesn’t indicate when or where the spillover occurred. Plus, how horses can make two sounds at once at the science jobs that might be overtaken by AI.

records.title: Scientists must step up to avert a nuclear breakout
records.description: The end of the US–Russia treaty to cap the number of nuclear weapons places the world at risk. Here’s what researchers can do.

records.title: Dynamic antigen expression and cytotoxic T cell resistance in HIV reservoir clones
records.description: Insights into the vulnerabilities of HIV-1 reservoir clones to potent, sustained cytotoxic T cell pressure are revealed.

records.title: From Victorian voyages to vanishing maps: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: Why every scientist needs a librarian
records.description: Librarians can be key research partners who help to scour the literature, manage data and make science open.

records.title: AI tools can design genomes. Will they upend how life evolves?
records.description: Breakthroughs in computing are supercharging a field of science dedicated to building synthetic organisms from scratch.

records.title: Iron Age mass grave reveals unprecedented violence against women and children
records.description: Women and children moving through Europe became victims of mass violence.

records.title: First-of-a-kind stem-cell therapies set for approval in Japan
records.description: Regenerative medicines are headed for people with Parkinson’s disease or severe heart failure — but researchers are concerned about minimal clinical-trial data.

records.title: Whistle while you whinny: researchers identify two sounds straight from the horse’s mouth
records.description: The ability to make two distinct sounds at once is shared with human beatboxers and throat singers.

records.title: Historically Black US universities chase top research ranking
records.description: Howard University is reaping the rewards of becoming the first such institution to reach ‘R1’ status.

records.title: This AI can improve your peer review — and make it more polite
records.description: A system of five models helps peer reviewers to write more constructive comments, but it is not yet known whether this strengthens the papers that are being reviewed.

records.title: How big is the ‘motherhood penalty’? In Denmark, it adds up to $120,000
records.description: An analysis documents the cumulative income hit mothers incur — as well as the extent to which state aid can offset the loss.

records.title: Music is not a universal language — but it can bring us together when words fail
records.description: Societies, animals and even machines have music in common. Our varied experiences of it might tell us about the origins of language.

records.title: Super-sticky feet help a robot to climb the walls
records.description: An adhesive inspired by the foot pads of geckos allows a robot to scale both smooth and rough vertical surfaces.

records.title: Briefing Chat: How hovering bumblebees keep their cool
records.description: Nature staff discuss some of the week’s top science news.

records.title: Publisher Correction: PtdIns(3,5)P 2 is an endogenous ligand of STING in innate immune signalling
Gel helps mini spinal cords to heal from injury
records.description: Complex 3D structures of cells called organoids could be used to test treatments for spinal-cord damage that can lead to paralysis.

records.title: Author Correction: Natural behaviour is learned through dopamine-mediated reinforcement
Runaway black hole leaves a trail of stars
records.description: The supermassive object broke away from a nearby galaxy and is now racing through the intergalactic medium.

records.title: Why do curling stones slide across ice the way they do?
records.description: After a century of study, physicists have theories — but they’re still not 100% sure.

records.title: Five ways increased militarization could change scientific careers
records.description: Scholars working on defence, conflict and science funding consider the impact on research careers and budgets, highlighting five broad trends.

records.title: Are obesity drugs causing a severe complication? What the science says
records.description: The United Kingdom and Brazil have issued warnings about a possible link between GLP-1 weight-loss drugs and pancreatic inflammation, but the connection is murky.

records.title: Daily briefing: ‘Universal’ vaccine protects mice from multiple pathogens
records.description: A nasal-spray activates the innate immune system to protect against both pathogens and allergens in mice. Plus, how bigger military budgets could change the course of global science and a blood test that could predict the onset of Alzheimer’s disease.

records.title: AI is threatening science jobs. Which ones are most at risk?
records.description: Data-analysis and modelling positions are already becoming obsolete, but hands-on experimentalists can breathe easy for now.

records.title: Biotech investor set to lead US National Science Foundation
records.description: If confirmed, Jim O’Neill would be the first non-scientist or non-engineer to lead the agency, which is a big funder of US basic research.

records.title: ‘An AlphaFold 4’ — scientists marvel at DeepMind drug spin-off’s exclusive new AI
records.description: Isomorphic Lab’s proprietary drug-discovery model is a major advance, but scientists developing open-source tools are left guessing how to achieve similar results.

records.title: Daily briefing: Automated robot ‘scientists’ spark debate over the future of lab work
records.description: AI-controlled robots could automate simple tasks, but scientists say lab work still needs a human touch. Plus, a glass tile that can store terabytes of data and how service-dog trainers are using science to boost graduation rates.

records.title: Blood test holds promise for predicting when Alzheimer’s symptoms will start
records.description: The Alzheimer’s ‘clock’ could make it easier to treat the disease early, before memory problems appear.

records.title: Academia’s parent trap: the struggles faced by researcher mothers
records.description: How effective is the sector at supporting early career scientists hoping to start a family, including those who face fertility challenges?

records.title: Science journalism on the ropes worldwide as US aid cuts bite
records.description: Federal freezes to foreign assistance are affecting grants for investigative reporters everywhere — but especially in poorer countries.

records.title: ‘Universal vaccine’ protects mice against multiple pathogens
records.description: An innovative approach supercharges the innate immune system to provide a first line of defence against respiratory infections.

records.title: Host control of persistent Epstein–Barr virus infection
records.description: Using blood-based genome sequence data, non-genetic and genetic factors associated with control of Epstein–Barr virus during persistent infection are reported.

records.title: Author Correction: BCL6 enables Ph + acute lymphoblastic leukaemia cells to survive BCR–ABL1 kinase inhibition
Host control of persistent Epstein–Barr virus infection
records.description: Using blood-based genome sequence data, non-genetic and genetic factors associated with control of Epstein–Barr virus during persistent infection are reported.

records.title: Author Correction: BCL6 enables Ph + acute lymphoblastic leukaemia cells to survive BCR–ABL1 kinase inhibition
This chunk of glass could store two million books for 10,000 years
records.description: Microsoft unveils a laser-modified glass that could store huge amounts of data for millennia — plus, a trial of mRNA vaccines to prevent a form of breast cancer recurring.

records.title: This giant virus hijacks cells’ protein-making machinery to multiply wildly
records.description: A virus that is big enough to be seen under an ordinary light microscope co-opts its host’s systems with the help of potentially purloined genes.

records.title: How ‘skull drains’ keep the brain safe from damage and pathogens
records.description: Veins in the skull can rearrange their borders to accommodate patrolling immune cells, a strange behaviour called ruffling.

records.title: Mid-cycle update
records.description: Code of conduct.

records.title: How do autistic people age — and what does it mean for their health?
records.description: Most research on autism focuses on younger people, but some studies suggest older adults face increased risks — and perhaps benefits.

records.title: Microsoft team creates ‘revolutionary’ data-storage system that lasts for millennia
records.description: Researchers use mini plasma explosions to encode the equivalent of two million books into a coaster-sized device. The method could preserve research data for millennia with minimal storage costs.

records.title: AI offers way to image and assess clinical cell samples
records.description: The use of artificial intelligence in the clinic to image slides of cells enables the rapid assessment of cellular characteristics that might help with diagnostic decisions.

records.title: Stereospecific alkyl–alkyl cross-coupling of boronic esters
records.description: Stereospecific coupling of boronic esters catalysed by a copper acetylide complex provides simplification of the synthesis of chiral building blocks for complex molecules.

records.title: Turning on the ‘for you’ feed on X shifted political opinions, but turning it off did not
records.description: A field experiment shows that turning on the algorithmic feed on the social-media platform X in 2023 shifted political opinions to the right, whereas turning it off had no effect on political attitudes. The algorithmic feed led users to follow more right-leaning accounts, which they continued following when the algorithm was off.

records.title: Personalized mRNA vaccine induces strong, durable immunity in hard-to-treat breast cancer
records.description: In an experimental trial, a personalized mRNA vaccine was tested in 14 individuals with an aggressive form of breast cancer. It trained immune cells to target cancer-specific mutant proteins, inducing strong, lasting immunity. Ten participants remained disease-free. Analysis of relapses revealed resistance mechanisms, offering essential insights for future therapies.

records.title: AI succeeds in diagnosing rare diseases
records.description: An artificial-intelligence system uses clinical data, genetic information and literature searches to suggest diagnoses and provides the underlying reasoning.

records.title: Chip-scale device efficiently boosts light signals
records.description: Optical-amplifier devices that boost light signals are workhorses of modern technology, but shrinking them onto microchips requires impractically high power. An amplifier architecture has been developed that recycles its own ‘pump’ energy to achieve high performance at power levels ten times lower than those of previous designs, making low-power, chip-scale optical amplification practical.

records.title: Laser-written glass tablets can preserve data for millennia
records.description: An archive system that encodes information in modified optical properties of glass could be a fast, efficient way to store huge quantities of data.

records.title: Will self-driving ‘robot labs’ replace biologists? Paper sparks debate
records.description: AI-driven autonomous robots are coming to biology laboratories, but researchers insist that human skills remain essential.

records.title: Malaria is hindered by repression of a cell-cycle protein
records.description: A genetic variant that quashes cyclin D3 expression might have been selected for in a population on an island where malaria was once endemic.

records.title: Oysters build reefs with optimal geometries
records.description: Some species, including oysters, shape their habitat. However, the relationship between the 3D properties of their habitat and demographic processes is unclear. Experiments with systematically varying habitat units shed light on how specific combinations of geometric attributes influence oyster establishment and survival under predation.

records.title: Why China and Europe should collaborate to ‘defossilize’ the world’s carbon
records.description: The world needs non-fossil sources of carbon. It’s a no-brainer for nations working towards this goal to join forces.

records.title: Gene editing treats a mouse model of a neurodevelopmental disorder
records.description: An approach that specifically targets a single nucleotide corrected behavioural abnormalities in an animal model of Snijders Blok–Campeau syndrome.

records.title: Daily briefing: What we know about autism and ageing — and what we don’t
records.description: More adults are being diagnosed with autism than ever before, but we know very little about how the condition affects ageing. Plus, how hovering bees keep their cool and a call for nanoscientists to tackle the reproducibility crisis.

records.title: Giant energy storage and dielectric performance in all-polymer nanocomposites
records.description: A high-temperature immiscible blend of two dipolar polymers that self-assemble into three-dimensional all-polymer nanocomposites allows markedly enhanced dielectric and energy storage performances over a broad temperature range.

records.title: Rising atmospheric CO 2 reduces nitrogen availability in boreal forests
records.description: Nitrogen isotope tree-ring chronologies show that rising atmospheric CO 2 has reduced nitrogen availability in boreal forests in Sweden, suggesting that elevated atmospheric CO 2 is causing oligotrophication in boreal forests.

records.title: The natural architecture of oyster reefs maximizes recruit survival
records.description: Survival of reef-building oysters peaks at specific combinations of fractal dimension and height that reduce predation, showing how optimal three-dimensional habitat geometry can guide more effective ecosystem restoration.

records.title: Accurate predictions of disordered protein ensembles with STARLING
records.description: The deep learning model STARLING can generate accurate ensembles of intrinsically disordered regions of proteins using only protein sequence as input.

records.title: Practical lithium–organic batteries enabled by an n-type conducting polymer
records.description: An n-type conducting polymer with excellent mixed ionic and electronic transport enables a practical lithium–organic battery that exhibits a wide operating temperature range and excellent safety.

records.title: Individualized mRNA vaccines evoke durable T cell immunity in adjuvant TNBC
records.description: In a phase 1 trial, personalized mRNA vaccines tailored to individual tumour mutations in triple-negative breast cancer induced robust, long-lasting T cell responses and improved prognosis.

records.title: Reduced cyclin D3 expression in erythroid cells protects against malaria
records.description: Population-level analyses and in vitro experiments show that a specific genetic variant of cyclin D3 inhibits the growth of the malaria-causing parasite Plasmodium falciparum in erythrocytes, and suggest that its high frequency in Sardinia was driven by past endemic malaria.

records.title: Single-cell and isoform-specific translational profiling of the mouse brain
records.description: Post-transcriptional regulation of mRNA translation was explored using Ribo-STAMP and single-cell RNA sequencing to reveal cell-type-specific and isoform-specific translation patterns across hippocampal neuronal and non-neuronal cell types, highlighting functional differences between CA1 and CA3.

records.title: Roles of microtubules and LIS1 in dynein transport machinery assembly
records.description: Cryo-electron microscopy suggests a model in which microtubules, rather than adaptors in the cytoplasm, act as the primary platform for dynein–dynactin assembly, while LIS1 stabilizes low-microtubule-affinity intermediates near the pre-assembled complexes.

records.title: In vivo base editing of Chd3 rescues behavioural abnormalities in mice
records.description: In vivo base editing of a causative mutation that leads to the neurodevelopmental disorder Snijders Blok–Campeau syndrome restores protein dosage and ameliorates molecular and behavioural deficits in a humanized mouse model of the condition.

records.title: RYK is a GPNMB receptor that drives MASH
records.description: MASH is driven by the secreted GPNMB ectodomain, which binds hepatocyte RYK to activate ERK1/2 and promote lipid uptake and lipogenic programs; blocking the GPNMB–RYK axis prevented and treated MASH in preclinical models.

records.title: Highly dynamic dural sinuses support meningeal immunity
records.description: Microscopic imaging and biochemical studies show that sinuses in mouse and human form a highly dynamic surface that regulates fluid movement and immune cell surveillance via RAMP1-dependent regulation of smooth muscle contraction and RAMP2-dependent regulation of the sinus endothelial barrier.

records.title: Laser writing in glass for dense, fast and efficient archival data storage
records.description: An optical archival storage technology based on femtosecond laser direct writing in glass addresses the practical demands of archival storage.

records.title: Integrated photonics enabling ultra-wideband fibre–wireless communication
records.description: An integrated photonics scheme is presented for the manufacture of communication systems supporting the use of fibre and wireless infrastructures simultaneously, addressing the long-standing bandwidth mismatch between the two domains and demonstrating ultrahigh data rates.

records.title: Clinical-grade autonomous cytopathology through whole-slide edge tomography
records.description: This study presents a clinical-grade autonomous pipeline combining high-resolution whole-slide tomography, edge computing and artificial intelligence, achieving high accuracy in cervical cytology and enabling scalable and objective diagnostics.

records.title: A roadmap for evaluating moral competence in large language models
records.description: This Perspective offers a roadmap for tackling the challenges of the facsimile problem, moral multidimensionality and moral pluralism in large language models.

records.title: Ancient co-option of LTR retrotransposons as yeast centromeres

records.title: Agouti integrates environmental cues to regulate paternal behaviour

records.title: An agentic system for rare disease diagnosis with traceable reasoning

records.title: Mucosal vaccination clears Clostridioides difficile colonization

records.title: Ancestry and somatic profile indicate acral melanoma origin and prognosis

records.title: Higher-dimensional Fermiology in bulk moiré metals

records.title: Cold-injection synthesis of highly emissive perovskite nanocrystals

records.title: The integrated stress response promotes immune evasion through lipocalin 2

records.description: A machine-learning method that reasons and adapts has been developed to solve one of the most time-consuming bottlenecks in battery development.

records.title: What my cave stay taught me about sensors
records.description: Five days isolated in complete darkness retunes the senses. Scientist Kiana Aran explains how sensors help to share the sensations with others.

records.title: A tumour-to-brain pathway hinders anticancer defences
records.description: Sensory neurons detect internal and external cues in organs and send this information to the brain. Lung cancer exploits this pathway to lessen immune responses.

records.title: Common genetic variants affect risk of a major cause of pregnancy loss
records.description: Genetic data from 139,416 human embryos were used to characterize chromosomal abnormalities, called aneuploidies, that underlie many cases of pregnancy loss. This approach revealed a relationship between aneuploidy and the exchange of DNA between chromosomes during female meiosis and egg formation, and identified common maternal genetic variants associated with meiotic errors.

records.title: Open-source AI tool beats giant LLMs in literature reviews — and gets citations right
records.description: Researchers can deploy the cheap and transparent model on their own computer system.

records.title: Particle collisions cast light on how matter forms from seemingly empty space
records.description: Fundamental particles called quarks can be created in quantum-correlated pairs. These correlations can be passed on to larger particles that form from the quarks.

records.title: How tumours trick the brain into shutting down cancer-fighting cells
records.description: Lung cancer in mice hijacks neurons to send a signal that subdues the immune system, study finds.

records.title: Eviction notice
records.description: Universal agreement.

records.title: Atlantic ocean currents defied the ice age
records.description: The state of the North Atlantic Ocean during the last ice age remains debated. A pair of independent geochemical measures shows that a cold, salty and dense deep-ocean current, known as the North Atlantic Deep Water, continued to form and remained relatively warm, instead of being close to freezing as was assumed previously.

records.title: Quantum computers will finally be useful: what’s behind the revolution
records.description: A string of surprising advances suggests usable quantum computers could be here in a decade.

records.title: Evolutionary insights into a skin fold
records.description: The formation of a skin fold named a rete ridge reveals how simple architectural changes reshape tissue mechanics and signalling routes to make a different type of skin structure.

records.title: Immune cells from the gut drive development of Parkinson’s disease in the brain
records.description: In ‘body-first’ Parkinson’s disease, misfolded proteins propagate from the gut’s nervous system to the brain. Immune-cell activity seems to play a key part in this spread.

records.title: Daily briefing: More than one-third of cancer cases are preventable
records.description: Nearly 40% of new cancer cases worldwide are linked to things we can change, such as smoking. Plus, the NIH is rolling back red tape on some types of human research and the unexpected success of ice skates.

records.title: A way to gauge the equity of ocean-related initiatives
records.description: Inequity is undermining the ocean’s contributions to people. The Ocean Equity Index is a tool to guide the development of more equitable ocean governance and management. The index can be used to assess and advance equity in ocean initiatives, projects and policies, thereby ensuring better outcomes for people and ecosystems.

records.title: How a protein repurposes vitamin B 12 as a light sensor
records.description: Intense, ultrashort X-ray pulses have been used to probe the extraordinary reactions that occur in a light-sensing receptor, resolving a biochemical conundrum.

records.title: AI could transform research assessment — and some academics are worried
records.description: Resistance to using the technology, despite its labour-saving potential, is particularly prevalent in research-intensive universities.

records.title: A universal concept for melting in mantle upwellings
records.description: The first melts generated in any solid-state mantle upwelling are kimberlitic CO 2 -rich silicate melts that form at about 250 km depth through oxidation of elemental carbon to CO 2 .

records.title: Atlas-guided discovery of transcription factors for T cell programming
records.description: A comprehensive atlas platform integrating transcriptional and epigenetic data enables more precise engineering of T cell states, accelerating the rational design of more effective cellular immunotherapies.

records.title: Regulatory grammar in human promoters uncovered by MPRA-based deep learning
records.description: PARM is a deep-learning model trained on data from massively parallel reporter assays to help predict promoter activity in different human cell types, design synthetic promoters and identify key features of regulatory promoter grammar.

records.title: Biofluid biomarkers in Alzheimer’s disease and other neurodegenerative dementias
records.description: Improved technologies facilitate the detection of molecules linked to neurodegenerative brain changes at very low concentrations in the blood, complementing the clinical evaluation of suspected neurodegenerative disease.

records.title: PtdIns(3,5)P 2 is an endogenous ligand of STING in innate immune signalling
records.description: Phosphatidylinositol 3,5-bisphosphate is a ligand of STING and, together with cGAMP, induces STING activation and innate immune responses.

records.title: Atmospheric H 2 variability over the past 1,100 years
records.description: Analysis of the atmospheric H 2 variability over the past millennium suggests that the sensitivity of H 2 to climate change should be considered in estimates of the radiative consequences of rising anthropogenic H 2 emissions.

records.title: Large-scale analogue quantum simulation using atom dot arrays
records.description: A new platform comprising large-scale 2D arrays of quantum dots patterned with sub-nanometre precision, with each quantum dot defined by tens of phosphorus atoms doped into silicon, allows for analogue simulation of quantum materials on arbitrary lattices.

records.title: Synthesizing scientific literature with retrieval-augmented language models
records.description: A specialized, open-source, retrieval-augmented language model is introduced for answering scientific queries and synthesizing literature, the responses of which are shown to be preferred by human evaluations over expert-written answers.

records.title: Discovery Learning predicts battery cycle life from minimal experiments
records.description: Discovery Learning, a machine learning approach integrating active learning, physics-guided learning and zero-shot learning into a human-like reasoning loop, is described for predicting the battery cycle life of new designs from minimal experiments, reducing prototyping requirements.

records.title: Bacterial immune activation via supramolecular assembly with phage triggers
records.description: An antiphage defence system has an activation mechanism that relies on the sensing of phage-encoded proteins that enforce geometry crucial to activation and are not typically present in non-infected cells.

records.title: Signatures of fractional charges via anyon–trions in twisted MoTe 2
records.description: Fractionally charged excitations at zero magnetic field in twisted MoTe 2 bilayers, a recently discovered fractional quantum anomalous Hall system, are observed via anyon-trions, excitonic complexes formed by binding a trion to a fractional charge.

records.title: A pore-forming antiphage defence is activated by oligomeric phage proteins
records.description: Bacteria use diverse defence systems against phages, including a 164-residue prophage-encoded protein, Rip1, which senses conserved phage assembly rings to form membrane pores that block virion maturation and trigger premature host cell death.

records.title: Imaging a terahertz superfluid plasmon in a two-dimensional superconductor
records.description: Terahertz microspectroscopic imaging at subgap millielectronvolt energies of a two-dimensional superfluid plasmon in few-layer Bi 2 Sr 2 CaCu 2 O 8+ x is demonstrated, allowing the spatial resolution of its deeply subdiffractive terahertz electrodynamics.

records.title: Parkinson’s disease as a somato-cognitive action network disorder
records.description: The substantia nigra and all Parkinson’s disease deep-brain stimulation targets are selectively connected to the somato-cognitive action network rather than to effector-specific motor regions.

records.title: Phenome-wide analysis of copy number variants in 470,727 UK Biobank genomes
records.description: A multiancestry phenome-wide analysis of copy number variants in the UK Biobank genomes increases power to detect genetic associations with complex traits across human populations.

records.title: Tumour–brain crosstalk restrains cancer immunity via a sensory–sympathetic axis
records.description: Mouse models demonstrate that vagal sensory neurons transmit signals from lung adenocarcinoma to the brain, increasing sympathetic efferent activity in the tumour microenvironment and thereby creating a immunologically permissive environment for tumour growth.

records.title: Contemporaneous mobile- and stagnant-lid tectonics on the Hadean Earth
records.description: Geochemical data from zircons show that subduction-like processes were operating contemporaneously with stagnant-lid-like processes at different locations as early as 4.4 billion years ago on the Hadean Earth.

records.title: Single-molecule dynamics of the TRiC chaperonin system in vivo
records.description: Single-particle tracking experiments in intact cells reveal dynamic co- and post-translational interactions of the TRiC–PFD chaperonin complex with client proteins during in vivo protein folding.

records.title: ZFTA–RELA ependymomas make itaconate to epigenetically drive fusion expression
records.description: The ZFTA – RELA fusion, an oncogene for ependymomas, promotes the production of itaconate, and its dependence on this metabolite represents a new therapeutic target for this cancer.

records.title: Spin-wave band-pass filters for 6G communication
records.description: A spin-wave ladder architecture based on single-crystal yttrium iron garnet requiring only one external magnetic bias for manufacturing tunable compact filters using modern micromachining fabrication methods is described, demonstrating applications in future communications systems.

records.title: Imaging the sub-moiré potential using an atomic single electron transistor
records.description: An atomic single electron transistor, which utilizes a single atomic defect in a van der Waals material as an ultrasensitive, high-resolution potential sensor, is used to image the electrostatic potential within a moiré unit cell.

records.title: Regulation of STING activation by phosphoinositide and cholesterol
records.description: Phosphatidylinositol phosphates together with cholesterol bind at the interface between STING dimers, directly promoting high-order oligomerization.

records.title: Cleavage of mRNAs by a minority of pachytene piRNAs improves sperm fitness
records.description: Most pachytene PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) have no biological function; however, a small population enhances sperm fitness, which has led to their persistence in mammalian evolution.

records.title: Resolving intervalley gaps and many-body resonances in moiré superconductors
records.description: This study of magic-angle twisted trilayer graphene moiré superconductors using scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy identifies two energy gaps that develop from many-body resonance in this highly tunable class of materials.

records.title: Activated ATF6α is a hepatic tumour driver restricting immunosurveillance
records.description: ATF6α activation in human and preclinical models of hepatocellular carcinoma is significantly associated with an aggressive tumour phenotype characterized by reduced survival, glycolytic reprogramming and local immunosuppression.

records.title: Rete ridges form via evolutionarily distinct mechanisms in mammalian skin
records.description: A spatial and single-cell transcriptomics study across multiple mammalian species identifies epidermal BMP signalling as a functional requirement for rete ridge formation, providing insight into mechanisms underlying hair density loss and wound healing.

records.title: Mosquito–capsid interactions contribute to flavivirus vector specificity
records.description: Systemic flavivirus dissemination in mosquitoes following initial infection requires protein–protein interactions within extracellular vesicles, which enable infectious particles to be transported through haemolymph and confer species specificity.

records.title: Integrated structural dynamics uncover a new B 12 photoreceptor activation mode
records.description: Spatiotemporal insight into photoactivation of the prototypical B 12 photoreceptor CarH is revealed across nine orders of magnitude in time, identifying a transient adduct that distinguishes it from thermally activated B 12 enzymes.

records.title: Efficient near-telomere-to-telomere assembly of nanopore simplex reads
records.description: A genome assembly method called hifiasm (ONT) allows the assembly of chromosomes from telomere to telomere without the need for ultra-long reads, and outperforms conventional methods on most evaluation metrics.

records.title: Measuring spin correlation between quarks during QCD confinement
records.description: The STAR experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider at Brookhaven National Laboratory demonstrates evidence of spin correlations in \(\Lambda \bar{\Lambda }\) hyperon pairs inherited from virtual spin-correlated strange quark–antiquark pairs during QCD confinement.

records.title: Chemical capture of diazo metabolites reveals biosynthetic hydrazone oxidation
records.description: An approach to discover reactive diazo-based metabolites by capture based on their reactivity coupled to mass spectrometry revealed two previously unknown diazo-containing compounds produced by the human lung pathogen Nocardia ninae using novel biosynthetic chemistry.

records.title: Embrace diverse PhD supervision styles — but enforce essential standards
Calling all scientists: Support your Iranian colleagues
A history of hocus pocus: witchcraft down the ages
records.description: A book about witches casts a spell, and arguments about whether blue-green algae should be called blue-green bacteria, in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: Who does academic consulting serve?
Many people have no mental imagery. What’s going on in their brains?
records.description: People with aphantasia are offering a window into consciousness.

records.title: The ‘bible for psychiatry’ is getting a rewrite: your guide to the next DSM
records.description: Could the next version of the DSM be a ‘living’ document that has more focus on the causes of mental illness?

records.title: The global plastics treaty can be saved — here’s how to break the deadlock
records.description: The stalled multinational effort to protect environmental and human health from plastic pollution is salvageable, with a revamped negotiation process.

records.title: More than one-third of cancer cases are preventable, massive study finds
records.description: Many cancers are linked to two modifiable habits: tobacco smoking and alcohol consumption.

records.title: Daily briefing: What people with no ‘mind’s eye’ can tell us about consciousness
records.description: How clearly you can picture mental images might influence your memory and creativity. Plus, cursive is making a comeback in schools and how to move the Global Plastics Treaty forward.

records.title: Author Correction: Increasingly negative tropical water–interannual CO 2 growth rate coupling
Now is not the time to defund human fetal tissue research
records.description: Hindering studies involving fetal tissue will impede the development of the alternatives intended to replace it, while slowing the search for new medicines.

records.title: I know science can’t fix the world — here’s why I do it anyway
records.description: The world faces energy shortages as fossil fuels are phased out. Research can’t go on as normal.

records.title: Ontogeny and transcriptional regulation of Thetis cells
records.description: A study of antigen-presenting cells called Thetis cells sheds light on their development and transcriptional regulation in mice, which has implications for the tolerance of gut microbiota and food antigens.

records.title: Daily briefing: Scientists delve into the smells of history
records.description: Researchers are working to reproduce the smells of heritage and history, from mummies to the Battle of Waterloo. Plus, the best science images of the month and whether we’ve already achieved ‘artificial general intelligence’.

records.title: Are health influencers making us sick?
records.description: Social media can help to raise awareness of health conditions — but the wealth of dubious information online might do more harm than good.

records.title: Does AI already have human-level intelligence? The evidence is clear
records.description: The vision of human-level machine intelligence laid out by Alan Turing in the 1950s is now a reality. Eyes unclouded by dread or hype will help us to prepare for what comes next.

records.title: How learning handwriting trains the brain: the science behind the cursive wars
records.description: Handwriting requirements were cut from school curricula around the world. Now it’s looping back, riding on a wave of evidence.

records.title: Don’t talk science, play science: translate your data into music to improve its reach
records.description: Data sonification helps researchers to build connections and communicate their science to a broader audience.

records.title: The number of China’s elite scientists who have been trained abroad is falling
records.description: A study that examines career histories of the country’s leading scholars reveals that the nation is turning inwards in its search for talent.

records.title: See the Sun expand and contract like a pufferfish — January’s best science images
records.description: The month’s sharpest science shots, selected by Nature ’s photo team.

records.title: OpenAI-backed firm to use ultrasound to read minds. Does the science stand up?
records.description: Spin-out Merge Labs aims to rival Elon Musk’s brain-chip company Neuralink. But researchers say the technology is still at an early stage.

records.title: Is the journal legitimate? Aletheia-Probe can help you decide
records.description: The open-source tool provides a one-stop shop to help you assess whether journals and conferences are trustworthy or predatory.

records.title: Author Correction: Albumin orchestrates a natural host defence mechanism against mucormycosis
Long-lived remote ion–ion entanglement for scalable quantum repeaters
records.description: Long-lived trapped-ion entanglement over 10 km of spooled fibre reaches the threshold where establishment exceeds loss, providing a critical building block for scalable quantum repeaters.

records.title: A broadly protective antibody targeting gammaherpesvirus gB
records.description: The antibody Fab5 cross-neutralizes gammaherpesviruses by binding to a conserved region in the membrane fusion protein gB on the virus; this region could form the basis for a herpesvirus vaccine.

records.title: Largest galaxy survey yet confirms that the Universe is not clumpy enough
records.description: The six-year results from the Dark Energy Survey highlight unresolved tensions in standard cosmological theory.

records.title: Publisher Correction: A domed pachycephalosaur from the early Cretaceous of Mongolia
Publisher Correction: Nanotyrannus and Tyrannosaurus coexisted at the close of the Cretaceous
Briefing Chat: What Brazilian centenarians could reveal about the science of ageing
records.description: Nature staff discuss some of the week’s top science news.

records.title: Light-powered bacteria become living chemical factories
records.description: Engineered Escherichia coli could open the door to more sustainable routes to new drugs and other chemicals.

records.title: This robot hand detaches and walks by itself
records.description: Six-fingered appendage can detach, crawl and manipulate objects

records.title: Can academia handle my religious faith?
records.description: Religious faith is a fundamental part of many academics’ identities, but some are nervous of talking about it at work.

records.title: How DeepMind’s genome AI could help solve rare-disease mysteries
records.description: Hackathons using AlphaGenome and other AI models are hunting down the genetic causes of devastating conditions that have evaded diagnosis.

records.title: China is betting on ‘optical’ computer chips — will they power AI?
records.description: Semiconductor chips that process light rather than electricity could boost processing speeds and reduce energy use.

records.title: Daily briefing: Why we enjoy things more when they’re hard to get
records.description: A key brain chemical is the reason we enjoy rewards more when they are difficult to achieve. Plus, genetics might play a bigger part in longevity than we thought and a holistic view of eating well.

records.title: Longevity is in the genes: half of lifespan is heritable
records.description: Understanding the genetic controls of ageing could lead to more therapies that forestall it.

records.title: Genetically engineered ‘stinkweed’ comes up roses for making seed oil
records.description: Field pennycress could become a valuable winter crop, with benefits for both carbon storage and farm profitability.

records.title: Still conscious? Brain marker signals when anaesthesia takes hold
records.description: De-synchronized electrical activity marks the loss of awareness.

records.title: ArXiv says submissions must be in English: are AI translators up for the job?
records.description: The preprint repository’s requirement could boost the use of large language models to translate scientific texts.

records.title: This AI has chemical expertise — and helps synthesize 35 new compounds
records.description: An open-source program enables researchers to bypass a major bottleneck in the process of chemical synthesis.

records.title: Daily briefing: Brain–immune crosstalk worsens the damage of heart attacks
records.description: Vagus nerve signalling causes damaging post-heart-attack inflammation. Plus, why birds decorate their nests with ‘tails’ and the health benefits of forest bathing.

records.title: 48 hours without lungs: artificial organ kept man alive until transplant
records.description: The external, artificial-lung system could be used to treat other people who are critically unwell and awaiting transplants.

records.title: Five ways to make the academic workplace happier and healthier this year
records.description: Despite attempts by many universities to modernize their policies on working conditions and misconduct, the academic system has pushed back. Here’s how to ensure lasting change.

records.title: Author Correction: Hunter-gatherer sea voyages extended to remotest Mediterranean islands
AI chatbots are infiltrating social-science surveys — and getting better at avoiding detection
records.description: A researcher has created a chatbot that is indistinguishable from human participants in online surveys. Some researchers fear that a workhorse of social science is now under threat.

records.title: A step towards building miniature human livers
records.description: Recapitulating the complexity of human organs in vitro would accelerate drug discovery and enable personalized treatments. By combining different types of liver cell from donor tissues, in vitro models of a liver region that mirror some of the organ’s main structures and functions can be assembled, getting closer to reproducing mini livers in vitro .

records.title: Scraps of viral DNA in biobank samples reveal secrets of Epstein–Barr virus
records.description: Viral DNA that is usually dismissed when sequencing the human genome could help to uncover useful information about complex diseases.

records.title: Alternative explanation for how celestial objects generate large-scale magnetic fields
records.description: Numerical simulations provide a mechanism that explains how celestial objects such as stars and galaxies can generate ordered, macroscopic magnetic fields. The mechanism arises from turbulence — chaotic changes in the pressure and velocity of fluid — and avoids a physical effect that hinders other proposed systems from explaining observed ordered fields.

records.title: Funding cuts could put research into emerging threats to lung health at risk
records.description: Wildfire smoke, spore-spread fungal diseases and microplastic are all on the rise, even as the US government slashes support for respiratory research and policy.

records.title: Treatments for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis are on the horizon
records.description: The life-threatening disease affects millions of people, but has no effective therapy. Drugs under development could target the condition before fibrosis becomes established.

records.title: Six highlights from lung-health research
records.description: Fibrosis survival, long COVID’s lasting toll and other highlights from lung studies.

records.title: Expert-level test is a head-scratcher for AI
records.description: Conventional benchmarks are becoming less effective at assessing AI performance, but a multi-disciplinary test has set AI systems a fresh challenge.

records.title: Wikipedia is needed now more than ever, 25 years on
records.description: The online encyclopedia is an antidote to an increasingly poisoned information ecosystem. Researchers should help to nourish it.

records.title: The surprisingly big health benefits of just a little exercise
records.description: ‘Exercise snacks’ and other forms of everyday movement can greatly reduce the risk of heart disease and death.

records.title: Pesticide cocktails negatively affect soil biodiversity
records.description: A much-needed assessment of the scale of the effects of pesticides on soil biodiversity in Europe will support regulation and conservation efforts.

records.title: Could the regenerative power of the lungs help to reverse disease?
records.description: The ability of the lungs to rebuild themselves has long been underappreciated, now researchers are raising the possibility that it could help to tackle chronic disease.

records.title: The unfortunate embossing of Subsector XZ-74
records.description: Presentation matters.

records.title: How ‘forest bathing’ keeps lungs healthy
records.description: Wooded environments release organic compounds that seem to improve respiratory health, but the magnitude and mechanism of the effect remains unclear.

records.title: A bendable AI chip for wearable technology
records.description: Co-optimized design and technology has resulted in cheap, flexible microchips that efficiently run neural-network tasks, as demonstrated in wearable health-care devices.

records.title: Daily briefing: The secrets of the centenarians
records.description: A study of people over 100 years old in Brazil is offering clues about the limits of human longevity. Plus, what might be producing mysterious ‘dark oxygen’ in the depths of the ocean and the big benefits of just a little exercise.

records.title: Technologies to give a clearer view of the lungs
records.description: From better screening to artificial-intelligence enhancements, pulmonologists are seeking better ways to spot fibrosis and other pulmonary maladies.

records.title: Damage from a heart attack comes from brain signals, mouse study suggests
records.description: The brain and vagus nerve play a key part in exacerbating tissue damage after a heart attack, but there are ways to block it.

records.title: Projected impacts of climate change on malaria in Africa
records.description: Projected impacts of climate change on malaria burden in Africa by 2050 highlight the urgent need for climate-resilient malaria control strategies and robust emergency response systems to safeguard progress towards malaria eradication.

records.title: Constraints on axion dark matter by distributed intercity quantum sensors
records.description: Amplification and optimal noise filtering in hyperpolarized noble-gas spins of observations from distributed intercity quantum sensors monitoring for unexpected transient rotations of polarized spins set parameter range constraints in the search for axion dark matter.

records.title: Could the regenerative power of the lungs help to reverse disease?
records.description: The ability of the lungs to rebuild themselves has long been underappreciated, now researchers are raising the possibility that it could help to tackle chronic disease.

records.description: Co-optimized design and technology has resulted in cheap, flexible microchips that efficiently run neural-network tasks, as demonstrated in wearable health-care devices.

records.description: A study of people over 100 years old in Brazil is offering clues about the limits of human longevity. Plus, what might be producing mysterious ‘dark oxygen’ in the depths of the ocean and the big benefits of just a little exercise.

records.title: Technologies to give a clearer view of the lungs
records.description: From better screening to artificial-intelligence enhancements, pulmonologists are seeking better ways to spot fibrosis and other pulmonary maladies.

records.title: Damage from a heart attack comes from brain signals, mouse study suggests
records.description: The brain and vagus nerve play a key part in exacerbating tissue damage after a heart attack, but there are ways to block it.

records.title: Projected impacts of climate change on malaria in Africa
records.description: Projected impacts of climate change on malaria burden in Africa by 2050 highlight the urgent need for climate-resilient malaria control strategies and robust emergency response systems to safeguard progress towards malaria eradication.

records.title: Constraints on axion dark matter by distributed intercity quantum sensors
records.description: Amplification and optimal noise filtering in hyperpolarized noble-gas spins of observations from distributed intercity quantum sensors monitoring for unexpected transient rotations of polarized spins set parameter range constraints in the search for axion dark matter.

records.title: Prethermalization by random multipolar driving on a 78-qubit processor
records.description: The existence of a long-lived, prethermal regime in many-body systems with tunable heating rates, driven by structured random protocols, is observed using a 78-qubit superconducting quantum processor.

records.title: Multimodal learning with next-token prediction for large multimodal models
records.description: Emu3 enables large-scale text, image and video learning based solely on next-token prediction, matching the generation and perception performance of task-specific methods, with implications for the development of scalable and unified multimodal intelligence systems.

records.title: Radiation-tolerant atomic-layer-scale RF system for spaceborne communication
records.description: Using a wafer-scale monolayer 2D MoS 2 process instead of conventional silicon-based devices to manufacture components of spaceborne communication systems demonstrates radiation tolerance, low bit error rate and long-term stability, even under much harsher radiation environments.

records.title: Accurate determination of the 3D atomic structure of amorphous materials
records.description: A quantitative framework for atomic electron tomography enables reliable determination of three-dimensional (3D) atomic coordinates and elemental identities in amorphous materials.

records.title: Intestinal macrophages modulate synucleinopathy along the gut–brain axis
records.description: Muscularis macrophages, housekeepers of enteric nervous system integrity and intestinal homeostasis, modulate α-synuclein pathology and neurodegeneration in models of Parkinson’s disease, and understanding the accompanying mechanisms could pave the way for early-stage biomarkers.

records.title: Cholinergic modulation of dopamine release drives effortful behaviour
records.description: In the nucleus accumbens, acetylcholine boosts dopamine release to promote effortful behaviour.

records.title: Optical control of integer and fractional Chern insulators
records.description: Optical control of integer and fractional Chern insulators is demonstrated by circularly polarized optical pumping in tMoTe 2 .

records.title: Environmentally driven immune imprinting protects against allergy
records.description: In a mouse model, environmental immunostimulation in early life led to cross-reactive adaptive immune memory and reduced type II immune responses to allergens, indicating a mechanistic relationship between environmental antigen exposure and subsequent allergy.

records.title: Population-scale sequencing resolves determinants of persistent EBV DNA
records.description: Population-scale WGS reveals genetic determinants of persistent EBV DNA, linking immune regulation—especially antigen processing and MHC class II variation—to EBV persistence and heterogeneous disease associations.

records.title: Pesticide residues alter taxonomic and functional biodiversity in soils
records.description: A wide survey of pesticide effects on soil biodiversity across 373 sites in Europe reveals that pesticide residues occur in 70% of sites and have major effects on soil biodiversity and functional ecology.

records.title: Lasing of a cavity-based X-ray source
records.description: Lasing with multi-pass gain is achieved in a diamond-based X-ray cavity at the European XFEL, opening a path to next-generation X-ray science.

records.title: Bandwidth-tuned Mott transition and superconductivity in moiré WSe 2
records.description: Tunable moiré WSe 2 bilayers realize Hubbard-model physics, exhibiting antiferromagnetism, strange metals and superconducting domes, offering a controllable platform to study high-transition-temperature superconductivity.

records.title: Human and bacterial genetic variation shape oral microbiomes and health
records.description: Human genetic loci that associate with composition of the oral microbiome are identified using saliva-derived DNA, where the same host genetics also shapes oral health and genetic variation in oral bacteria.

records.title: Frequency reproducibility of solid-state thorium-229 nuclear clocks
records.description: The nuclear clock transition of 229m Th in 229 Th:CaF 2 crystals is characterized as a function of doping concentration, temperature and time, demonstrating high reproducibility and identifying ideal operating characteristics of these crystals as nuclear clocks.

records.title: PAF15–PCNA exhaustion governs the strand-specific control of DNA replication
records.description: PCNA–PAF15 has a key role in determining replisome dynamics during genome replication and protecting against genome instability.

records.title: A Cambrian soft-bodied biota after the first Phanerozoic mass extinction
records.description: The Huayuan biota exhibits extraordinary biodiversity, illuminating the impact of the Phanerozoic mass extinction around 513 million years ago and offering critical insights into the transformation of global ecosystems in the early Cambrian.

records.title: An X-ray-emitting protocluster at z ≈ 5.7 reveals rapid structure growth
records.description: Discovery of a protocluster at z = 5.68, merely one billion years after the Big Bang, suggests that large-scale structure must have formed more rapidly in some regions of the early universe than previously thought.

records.title: Low-power integrated optical amplification through second-harmonic resonance
records.description: An integrated optical parametric amplifier on thin-film lithium niobate achieves more than 17 dB gain with less than 200 mW input power.

records.title: A prophage-encoded abortive infection protein preserves host and prophage spread
records.description: A Gifsy-1 prophage–encoded higher eukaryotes and prokaryotes nucleotide-binding protein, HepS, senses Siphoviridae infection, activates abortive defence by cleaving host transfer RNAs, blocks rival phages and avoids self-targeting via tail-tip variation.

records.title: Robust cytoplasmic partitioning by solving a cytoskeletal instability
records.description: The cytoplasm can be partitioned into distinct compartments by microtubule structures, which can be stabilized by distinct mechanisms in different species.

records.title: Advancing regulatory variant effect prediction with AlphaGenome
records.description: AlphaGenome, a deep learning model that inputs 1-Mb DNA sequence to predict functional genomic tracks at single-base resolution across diverse modalities, outperforms existing models in variant effect prediction and enables comprehensive genomic analysis.

records.title: A cavity-array microscope for parallel single-atom interfacing
records.description: A cavity-array microscope is realized using intra-cavity lenses to create a two-dimensional array of over 40 modes, each coupled to a single atom in free-space.

records.title: A cross-population compendium of gene–environment interactions
records.description: A large cross-population atlas of gene–environment interactions reveals how age, sex and lifestyle shape genetic effects, heritability, prediction accuracy and disease biology, with implications for personalized medicine and drug development.

records.title: Vacuum ultraviolet second-harmonic generation in NH 4 B 4 O 6 F crystal
records.description: The fluorooxoborate crystal NH 4 B 4 O 6 F shows promise as a nonlinear optical material for vacuum ultraviolet light sources through second-harmonic generation, demonstrating record output energy and efficiency resulting from optimized arrangements of fluorine-based units creating asymmetric sublattices.

records.title: Psychedelics elicit their effects by 5-HT 2A receptor-mediated G i signalling
records.description: Psychedelics and their non-hallucinogenic analogues were compared, revealing that serotonin 2A receptor (5-HT 2A R)-mediated G i signalling is essential for hallucinogenic effect, with the functional mechanisms underlying this providing insights for designing therapeutic drugs without hallucinogenic effects.

records.title: Limit of atomic-resolution-tomography reconstruction of amorphous nanoparticles
records.description: A simulation approach is used to ascertain the limitations on the structural and chemical information that atomic-resolution electron tomography can determine from noisy electron images.

records.title: Optofluidic three-dimensional microfabrication and nanofabrication
records.description: A strategy compatible with a broad range of materials by precisely manipulating optofluidic interactions within a confined 3D space to control the assembly of colloidal microparticles/nanoparticles is demonstrated, enabling the precise manufacture of complex microstructures/nanostructures.

records.title: Ferromagnet-like binary switching of a Stoner–Wohlfarth antiferromagnet
records.description: CrPS 4 , a 2D van der Waals A-type antiferromagnet, is shown to exhibit ideal characteristics of Stoner–Wohlfarth antiferromagnets, such as ferromagnet-like binary switching rather than layer-by-layer flipping as in other 2D A-type antiferromagnets.

records.title: The Ocean Equity Index
records.description: The Ocean Equity Index provides a systematic, twelve-criteria framework to assess and improve equity in ocean initiatives, projects and policies, producing structured data that guide evidence-based decisions and support more equitable outcomes for coastal communities and ecosystems.

records.title: A flexible digital compute-in-memory chip for edge intelligence
records.description: A flexible digital artificial intelligence chip with a compute-in-memory architecture is fabricated using a commercial low-temperature polycrystalline silicon thin-film transistor process and shows high accuracy in human daily activity monitoring using multimodal physiological signals.

records.title: Optical control over topological Chern number in moiré materials
records.description: Optical spin orientation of itinerant ferromagnets in twisted MoTe 2 homobilayers is demonstrated, enabling control of topological Chern numbers with circularly polarized light.

records.title: Disentangling multiple gas kinematic drivers in the Perseus galaxy cluster
records.description: Kinematic measurements of the Perseus galaxy cluster reveal two drivers of gas motions: a small-scale driver in the inner core associated with black-hole feedback and a large-scale driver in the outer core powered by mergers.

records.title: Holistic motor control of zebra finch song syllable sequences
records.description: A cortical premotor network in HVC, once initiated, can sustain and regulate the sequential production of zebra finch song syllables without major extrinsic inputs.

records.title: A benchmark of expert-level academic questions to assess AI capabilities
records.description: Humanity’s Last Exam, a multi-modal benchmark at the frontier of human knowledge, is designed to be an expert-level closed-ended academic benchmark with broad subject coverage.

records.title: GlycoRNA complexed with heparan sulfate regulates VEGF-A signalling
records.description: Heparan sulfate proteoglycans facilitate the assembly of clusters of glycoRNAs and cell surface RNA-binding proteins, which negatively modulate VEGF-A signalling and angiogenesis.

records.title: Pre-assembly of biomolecular condensate seeds drives RSV replication
records.description: Viral ribonucleoprotein–viral protein networks form pre-replication centres that nucleate viral factories and drive respiratory syncytial virus replication.

records.title: Structures of Ostα/β reveal a unique fold and bile acid transport mechanism
records.description: Cryogenic electron microscopy structures of human Ostα/β uncover a unique transport pathway featuring two substrate-binding sites connected by an amphipathic helix-gated conduit, and electrophysiological studies demonstrate voltage-sensitive, bidirectional transport, showing its efflux role in vivo.

records.title: Observation of a superfluid-to-insulator transition of bilayer excitons
records.description: Transition of superfluid to insulator is observed in the layer-imbalanced regime of bilayer magnetoexcitons.

records.title: Optical switching of a moiré Chern ferromagnet
records.description: Optical switching of a moiré Chern ferromagnet is demonstrated in twisted molybdenum ditelluride bilayers using continuous-wave circularly polarized light, paving the way for dissipationless spintronics and quantized Chern junction devices.

records.title: Vagal blood volume receptors compensate for haemorrhage and posture change
records.description: A vagal reflex to blood volume changes in the heart involves PIEZO2 and helps to stabilize blood pressure in an upright posture and after blood loss.

records.title: Structure and mechanism of the human bile acid transporter OSTα–OSTβ
records.description: Cryo-electron microscopy structures of the bile acid transporter OSTα–OSTβ, which has a key role in bile acid homeostasis, provide insight into its distinct architecture and mechanism of substrate translocation.

records.title: Author Correction: Relatively warm deep-water formation persisted in the Last Glacial Maximum
Volcanic personality: the man who recognized volcanoes as a planet-shaping force of nature
records.description: Remembering the life and work of the geologist George Poulett Scrope, and salmon stories in this week’s pick from the Nature archive.

records.title: Social-media bans: why corporate fines could backfire
Street-dog policy in India is barking up the wrong tree
Author Correction: Nutrient-sensing nuclear receptors coordinate autophagy
Spotting viral invaders in koala family trees
records.description: Genetic analyses of koala pedigrees help to suss out virus-induced genome changes that affect cancer risk and reproductive success.

records.title: African science needs to cut reliance on foreign donors
Daily briefing: The battle over the identity of the first animals
records.description: Scientists are locked in debate over whether sponges or jellies were the first animal lineage. Plus, the United Kingdom has lost its measles elimination status and a stick that could be the oldest known wooden tool.

records.title: What were the first animals? The fierce sponge–jelly battle that just won’t end
records.description: For almost two decades, scientists have debated whether sponges or comb jellies are the first animal lineage. Now some are calling for a more harmonious approach.

records.title: How to eat well and within Earth’s limits
records.description: Dietary change, supported by bold policies, is essential for a sustainable planet.

records.title: Sensors are transforming the world — work together to maximize their benefits
records.description: To get the most out of the sensing revolution, different disciplines need to be on the same wavelength. This is a priority for the Nature Portfolio’s newest journal, Nature Sensors .

records.title: Should professors be forced to retire?
records.description: Some universities are implementing a mandatory retirement age for academics. Will it help young researchers to get permanent positions?

records.title: Still working at 107: supercentenarian study probes genetics of extreme longevity
records.description: Scientists seek to understand the factors that have allowed people in Brazil to reach their 100th or even 110th birthdays despite facing adversities.

records.title: Defending endangered trees against climate change and hungry goats
records.description: Mohammed Amar manages conservation of imperilled flora in Socotra, a Yemeni island known as the Galápagos of the Indian Ocean.

records.title: Quantum spinning effect observed in a levitating magnet
records.description: A supercooled microscopic ferromagnet proves the existence of gyroscopic magnetic behaviour that has been long sought by physicists.

records.title: Audio long read: ‘I rarely get outside’ — scientists ditch fieldwork in the age of AI
records.description: In the wake of new computer-based methods, some ecologists fear their field is losing touch with nature.

records.title: Why do women like me get diagnosed with ADHD late?
records.description: Emily Bates was diagnosed with ADHD at the age of 34. She explores how the condition presents in women and why so many are diagnosed later in life.

records.title: Technology is changing how we write — and how we think about writing
records.description: An exploration of how writing systems, from ancient Chinese characters to modern alphabets, shape language, and whether users of ChatGPT can be said to be authors at all.

records.title: Daily briefing: Blister beetles hoodwink bees with floral smells
records.description: Beetle larvae are the first animal known to imitate the scent of a flower. Plus, a proposal for a new north-star number for climate progress and why Greenland is a unique hotspot for research.

records.title: As we breach 1.5 °C, we must replace temperature limits with clean-energy targets
records.description: Actionable goals are needed to guide the world towards what needs to happen most quickly: shifting economies to clean energy sources.

records.title: Exceeding 1.5 °C requires rethinking accountability in climate policy
records.description: A scientific foundation is required to establish nations’ responsibilities in a hotter ‘overshoot’ world.

records.title: Scalable and multiplexed recorders of gene regulation dynamics across weeks
records.description: An intracellular protein-based recorder called CytoTape is capable of tracking cell activities over weeks and at scale.

records.title: Marvellous microbes, memory and the multiverse: Books in brief
records.description: Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

records.title: Briefing Chat: The canny cow that can use tools, and how babies share their microbiomes
records.description: Nature staff discuss some of the week’s top science news.

records.title: Gladys Mae West obituary: mathematician who pioneered GPS technology
records.description: She made key contributions to US cold-war science despite facing huge barriers as a Black woman.

records.title: What a $1-billion pledge means for CERN’s ambitious supercollider plans
records.description: New director-general Mark Thomson discusses fundraising efforts and future priorities for Europe’s particle-physics laboratory.

records.title: Daily briefing: Why cancer might protect against Alzheimer’s disease
records.description: A protein made by cancer cells seems to break down the hallmark plaques of Alzheimer’s disease. Plus, our breath might reveal what’s going on in our gut and the controversy surrounding a US-funded hepatitis B vaccine trial in Guinea-Bissau.

records.title: Greenland is important for global research: what’s next for the island’s science?
records.description: Geopolitics made Greenland the unexpected focus of the world’s attention. But the territory has long been a unique region for science.

records.title: Guinea-Bissau suspends US-funded vaccine trial as African scientists question its motives
records.description: Officials at the US Department of Health and Human Services, which awarded funding for the controversial study, say it will proceed as planned.

records.title: Cause of vision loss discovered in overlooked genes
records.description: Non-protein-coding genes have been linked to a hereditary condition, retinitis pigmentosa, that causes progressive blindness.

records.description: Quantum superposition gets supersized — plus, US science after a year of Trump.

records.title: ADHD is on the rise, but why?
records.description: The more we learn, the less we seem to understand this condition.

Untangling the connection between dopamine and ADHD
records.description: Dopamine signals have long been a target for ADHD treatments. Now, researchers are learning how the neurotransmitter influences the condition.

records.title: Quantum effect observed for biggest objects yet
records.description: An experiment has broken the size record for an object exhibiting matter-wave interference — fuelling the debate about possible size constraints.

records.title: Six highlights from ADHD research
records.description: Key studies and trials examine genetic mutations, the impact on life expectancy, cognitive impairments and other aspects of this condition.

records.title: More than half of authors of leading research say funding is declining
records.description: Nature Index ‘Research Leaders’ survey also finds that scientists in North America and Europe are much more likely to say they intend to leave research.

records.title: Illuminating how the bird inner retina works without oxygen solves a 350-year-old structural mystery
records.description: Neurons in the bird eye’s inner retina lack a blood supply. Finding how these neurons function without oxygen reveals a role for an enigmatic eye structure.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Multiple oestradiol functions inhibit ferroptosis and acute kidney injury
Schrödinger’s cat just got bigger: quantum physicists create largest ever ‘superposition’
records.description: Record-breaking experiment shows that a cluster of thousands of atoms can act like a wave as well as a particle.

records.title: Is paracetamol in pregnancy a risk factor for ADHD?
records.description: A common pain reliever taken in pregnancy might raise the risk of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, according to research in the past decade. But proof of cause and effect remains elusive.

records.title: A variety of early hominin species shared the Afar region of Ethiopia
records.description: Fossils reveal that at least four types of hominin, including Paranthropus , were present in northern Ethiopia between 3 million and 2.4 million years ago.

records.title: ADHD treatments move beyond stimulants
records.description: Researchers are developing drugs to broaden the options on available therapies.

records.title: The rich stopped buying yachts the year time went on sale
records.description: Second thoughts.

records.title: Sending babies to nursery completely reshapes their microbiomes
records.description: Socializing at a young age helps to develop greater diversity in children’s microbiota, according to an analysis of baby-to-baby transmission of gut bacteria.

records.title: An eye-popping discovery: early vertebrates had four eyes rather than two
records.description: Eyes on a face’s front or side enable a brain to perceive images. Fossil evidence suggests that two light-sensitive organs on top of ancient vertebrate heads generated images, too.

records.title: Why ADHD goes undiagnosed in girls
records.description: Differences in how the condition presents in girls, and co-occurring psychiatric conditions, make detection more difficult.

records.title: AI and nuclear energy feature strongly in agenda-setting technologies for 2026
records.description: Nature ’s annual list of technologies to watch is a chance to celebrate progress and stimulate research into both opportunities and risks.

records.title: Hand stencils in Indonesian cave are world’s oldest known artworks
records.description: Rock art found in Indonesia dates to at least 67,800 years ago, representing the earliest known cave art made by humans. These findings provide insights into the movement and cultural lives of populations that contributed to the ancestry of Indigenous Australian and Papuan people.
